devanagari: ततो युद्धपरिश्रान्तं समरे चिन्तया स्थितम् । / रावणं चाग्रतो दृष्ट्वा युद्धाय समुपस्थितम् ॥1॥
iast: tato yuddhapariśrāntaṃ samare cintayā sthitam । / rāvaṇaṃ cāgrato dṛṣṭvā yuddhāya samupasthitam ॥1॥
sayIt: ta-TO yud-dha-pa-ri-SHRAAN-tum sa-ma-RAY chin-ta-YAA STHI-tum / RAA-va-num CHAA-gra-to drisht-VAA yud-DHAA-ya sa-mu-pa-STHI-tum
translation: Then — Rama stood on the field of battle, worn out by the fighting and sunk in troubled thought, and before him Ravana had come forward, arrayed and ready for war —
source: Aditya Hridayam 1, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: When exhaustion and worry hit you in the middle of a struggle, what do you usually reach for first?

translations.hi: तब — राम रणभूमि में युद्ध से थके, चिंता में डूबे खड़े थे, और उनके सामने रावण युद्ध के लिए तैयार आ खड़ा था —

devanagari: दैवतैश्च समागम्य द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो रणम् । / उपागम्याब्रवीद्राममगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः ॥2॥
iast: daivataiśca samāgamya draṣṭumabhyāgato raṇam । / upāgamyābravīdrāmamagastyo bhagavānṛṣiḥ ॥2॥
sayIt: dai-va-TAISH-cha sa-MAA-gam-ya DRASH-tum abh-YAA-ga-to RA-num / u-PAA-gam-yaa-bra-veed RAA-mum a-GAST-yo bha-ga-VAAN RI-shih
translation: The venerable sage Agastya, who had come together with the gods to watch the battle, approached Rama and spoke.
source: Aditya Hridayam 2, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Who in your life crosses the field toward you when you are struggling — and do you let them speak?

translations.hi: देवताओं के साथ युद्ध देखने आए पूज्य ऋषि अगस्त्य राम के पास आए और बोले।

devanagari: राम राम महाबाहो शृणु गुह्यं सनातनम् । / येन सर्वानरीन्वत्स समरे विजयिष्यसि ॥3॥
iast: rāma rāma mahābāho śṛṇu guhyaṃ sanātanam । / yena sarvānarīnvatsa samare vijayiṣyasi ॥3॥
sayIt: RAA-ma RAA-ma ma-haa-BAA-ho SHRI-nu GUH-yum sa-NAA-ta-num / YAY-na sar-VAAN a-REEN VAT-sa sa-ma-RAY vi-ja-YISH-ya-si
translation: Rama, Rama, mighty-armed one — hear the eternal secret, dear child, by which you will conquer all your enemies in battle.
source: Aditya Hridayam 3, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What old, patient wisdom have you not yet invited into your newest fight?

translations.hi: राम, राम, महाबाहु! वत्स, वह सनातन रहस्य सुनो जिससे तुम युद्ध में अपने सारे शत्रुओं को जीत लोगे।

devanagari: आदित्यहृदयं पुण्यं सर्वशत्रुविनाशनम् । / जयावहं जपेन्नित्यमक्षयं परमं शिवम् ॥4॥
iast: ādityahṛdayaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvaśatruvināśanam । / jayāvahaṃ japennityamakṣayaṃ paramaṃ śivam ॥4॥
sayIt: aa-DIT-ya-hri-da-yum PUN-yum sar-va-SHA-tru-vi-NAA-sha-num / ja-YAA-va-hum ja-PEN NIT-yum ak-SHA-yum PA-ra-mum SHI-vum
translation: It is the holy Aditya Hridayam, the Heart of the Sun — destroyer of all enemies, bringer of victory, imperishable, supremely auspicious; one should recite it constantly.
source: Aditya Hridayam 4, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What is one practice small enough to survive your worst day that you could actually do daily?

translations.hi: यह पवित्र आदित्यहृदय है — समस्त शत्रुओं का नाश करने वाला, विजय दिलाने वाला, अक्षय और परम कल्याणकारी; इसका नित्य जप करना चाहिए।

devanagari: सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् । / चिन्ताशोकप्रशमनं आयुर्वर्धनमुत्तमम् ॥5॥
iast: sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam । / cintāśokapraśamanaṃ āyurvardhanamuttamam ॥5॥
sayIt: sar-va-MAN-ga-la-MAAN-gal-yum sar-va-PAA-pa-pra-NAA-sha-num / chin-TAA-sho-ka-pra-SHA-ma-num AA-yur-VAR-dha-num UT-ta-mum
translation: It is the blessing within all blessings, the destroyer of all sin, the calmer of worry and grief, and the finest increaser of life.
source: Aditya Hridayam 5, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Which weighs on you more right now — worry about what may come, or grief over what has passed?

translations.hi: यह सब मंगलों का मंगल है, सारे पापों का नाश करने वाला, चिंता और शोक को शांत करने वाला, और आयु बढ़ाने वाला सर्वोत्तम उपाय।

devanagari: रश्मिमन्तं समुद्यन्तं देवासुरनमस्कृतम् । / पूजयस्व विवस्वन्तं भास्करं भुवनेश्वरम् ॥6॥
iast: raśmimantaṃ samudyantaṃ devāsuranamaskṛtam । / pūjayasva vivasvantaṃ bhāskaraṃ bhuvaneśvaram ॥6॥
sayIt: rash-mi-MAN-tum sa-mud-YAN-tum day-VAA-su-ra-na-mas-KRI-tum / poo-ja-YAS-va vi-vas-VAN-tum BHAAS-ka-rum bhu-va-NAYSH-va-rum
translation: Worship the rising sun crowned with rays, honoured by gods and asuras alike — Vivasvan, the maker of light, the lord of all the worlds.
source: Aditya Hridayam 6, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What in your day deserves a moment of reverence before you start fighting for anything?

translations.hi: किरणों से दमकते, उदय होते सूर्य की वंदना करो, जिन्हें देवता और असुर दोनों प्रणाम करते हैं — वे विवस्वान हैं, प्रकाश के स्रोत, समस्त लोकों के स्वामी।

devanagari: सर्वदेवात्मको ह्येष तेजस्वी रश्मिभावनः । / एष देवासुरगणाँल्लोकान् पाति गभस्तिभिः ॥7॥
iast: sarvadevātmako hyeṣa tejasvī raśmibhāvanaḥ । / eṣa devāsuragaṇām̐llokān pāti gabhastibhiḥ ॥7॥
sayIt: sar-va-day-VAAT-ma-ko HYAY-sha tay-JAS-vee rash-mi-BHAA-va-nah / AY-sha day-VAA-su-ra-ga-NAAM lo-KAAN PAA-ti ga-BHAS-ti-bhih
translation: For he is the self of all the gods, the brilliant one who nourishes all through his rays; with his beams he protects the hosts of gods and asuras and all the worlds.
source: Aditya Hridayam 7, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Where in your own practice do you already sense one light behind many names?

translations.hi: वे ही समस्त देवताओं की आत्मा हैं — तेजस्वी, अपनी किरणों से सबका पोषण करने वाले; अपने प्रकाश से वे देवों, असुरों और सारे लोकों की रक्षा करते हैं।

devanagari: एष ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च शिवः स्कन्दः प्रजापतिः । / महेन्द्रो धनदः कालो यमः सोमो ह्यपां पतिः ॥8॥
iast: eṣa brahmā ca viṣṇuśca śivaḥ skandaḥ prajāpatiḥ । / mahendro dhanadaḥ kālo yamaḥ somo hyapāṃ patiḥ ॥8॥
sayIt: AY-sha brah-MAA cha VISH-nush-cha SHI-vah SKAN-dah pra-JAA-pa-tih / ma-HAYN-dro DHA-na-dah KAA-lo YA-mah SO-mo hya-PAAM PA-tih
translation: He is Brahma and Vishnu and Shiva, Skanda and Prajapati; he is great Indra, the wealth-giver Kubera, Time, Yama, Soma, and Varuna, lord of the waters.
source: Aditya Hridayam 8, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Does it change your prayer to imagine every name you call landing in one and the same light?

translations.hi: वे ही ब्रह्मा हैं, विष्णु हैं, शिव हैं, स्कन्द और प्रजापति भी; वे ही महेन्द्र हैं, धन देने वाले कुबेर, काल, यम, सोम और जल के स्वामी वरुण।

devanagari: पितरो वसवः साध्या ह्यश्विनौ मरुतो मनुः । / वायुर्वह्निः प्रजाप्राण ऋतुकर्ता प्रभाकरः ॥9॥
iast: pitaro vasavaḥ sādhyā hyaśvinau maruto manuḥ । / vāyurvahniḥ prajāprāṇa ṛtukartā prabhākaraḥ ॥9॥
sayIt: pi-ta-RO VA-sa-vah SAADH-yaa hyash-vi-NOW ma-ru-TO MA-nuh / VAA-yur VAH-nih pra-jaa-PRAA-na ri-tu-kar-TAA pra-BHAA-ka-rah
translation: He is the ancestors, the Vasus, the Sadhyas, the two Ashvins, the Maruts and Manu; he is wind and fire, the life-breath of beings, the maker of the seasons, and the giver of light.
source: Aditya Hridayam 9, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Which everyday rhythm — breath, sunrise, the seasons — could you treat as sacred this week?

translations.hi: वे ही पितर हैं, वसु, साध्य, दोनों अश्विनीकुमार, मरुद्गण और मनु; वे ही वायु हैं, अग्नि हैं, प्राणियों के प्राण, ऋतुओं के रचयिता और प्रकाश के दाता प्रभाकर।

devanagari: आदित्यः सविता सूर्यः खगः पूषा गभस्तिमान् । / सुवर्णसदृशो भानुर्हिरण्यरेता दिवाकरः ॥10॥
iast: ādityaḥ savitā sūryaḥ khagaḥ pūṣā gabhastimān । / suvarṇasadṛśo bhānurhiraṇyaretā divākaraḥ ॥10॥
sayIt: aa-DIT-yah sa-vi-TAA SOOR-yah kha-GAH poo-SHAA ga-BHAS-ti-maan / su-VAR-na-sa-dri-sho BHAA-nur hi-RUN-ya-ray-taa di-VAA-ka-rah
translation: He is Aditya, son of Aditi; Savita the impeller; Surya; the sky-goer; Pushan the nourisher; the ray-crowned one; Bhanu, glowing like gold; the golden-seeded; the maker of the day.
source: Aditya Hridayam 10, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: If your roles were names — provider, starter, steady light — which one needs more of you today?

translations.hi: वे अदिति के पुत्र आदित्य हैं; प्रेरणा देने वाले सविता; सूर्य; आकाश में विचरने वाले खग; पोषण करने वाले पूषा; किरणधारी; सोने-से दमकते भानु; हिरण्यरेता; और दिन के रचयिता दिवाकर।

devanagari: भानुर्विश्वरेता / हरिदश्वः सहस्रार्चिः सप्तसप्तिर्मरीचिमान् । / तिमिरोन्मथनः शम्भुस्त्वष्टा मार्ताण्ड अंशुमान् ॥11॥
iast: bhānurviśvaretā / haridaśvaḥ sahasrārciḥ saptasaptirmarīcimān । / timironmathanaḥ śambhustvaṣṭā mārtāṇḍa aṃśumān ॥11॥
sayIt: ha-ri-DASH-vah sa-has-RAAR-chih sap-ta-SAP-tir ma-REE-chi-maan / ti-mi-RON-ma-tha-nah SHAM-bhus TVASH-taa maar-TAAN-da AN-shu-maan
translation: His horses gleam green-gold, his rays number a thousand, seven steeds draw him, and beams stream from him; he churns away the darkness — he is Shambhu, Tvashta, Martanda, the radiant one.
source: Aditya Hridayam 11, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What darkness in your routine could a single steady light slowly churn away?

translations.hi: उनके घोड़े हरित-स्वर्ण आभा वाले हैं, किरणें सहस्रों हैं, रथ में सात अश्व जुते हैं, और रश्मियाँ उनसे फूटती हैं; वे अंधकार का मंथन कर उसे मिटा देते हैं — वे ही शम्भु हैं, त्वष्टा हैं, मार्तण्ड हैं, अंशुमान हैं।

devanagari: मार्तण्ड / हिरण्यगर्भः शिशिरस्तपनो भास्करो रविः । / अग्निगर्भोऽदितेः पुत्रः शङ्खः शिशिरनाशनः ॥12॥
iast: mārtaṇḍa / hiraṇyagarbhaḥ śiśirastapano bhāskaro raviḥ । / agnigarbho'diteḥ putraḥ śaṅkhaḥ śiśiranāśanaḥ ॥12॥
sayIt: hi-RUN-ya-gar-bhah SHI-shi-ras ta-pa-NO BHAAS-ka-ro RA-vih / ag-ni-GAR-bho-di-tayh PUT-rah SHAN-khah shi-shi-ra-NAA-sha-nah
translation: He is Hiranyagarbha, the golden womb; the cool one and the burning one; the maker of light, Ravi; the one who carries fire within; the son of Aditi; Shankha; the destroyer of winter's cold.
source: Aditya Hridayam 12, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Can you hold two opposite duties — cooling one person, firing up another — without splitting in two?

translations.hi: वे हिरण्यगर्भ हैं — सुनहरा गर्भ; शीतल करने वाले भी और तपाने वाले भी; प्रकाश रचने वाले भास्कर, रवि; भीतर अग्नि धारण करने वाले; अदिति के पुत्र; शङ्ख; और शीत का नाश करने वाले।

devanagari: व्योमनाथस्तमोभेदी ऋग्यजुःसामपारगः । / घनवृष्टिरपां मित्रो विन्ध्यवीथी प्लवङ्गमः ॥13॥
iast: vyomanāthastamobhedī ṛgyajuḥsāmapāragaḥ । / ghanavṛṣṭirapāṃ mitro vindhyavīthī plavaṅgamaḥ ॥13॥
sayIt: vyo-ma-NAA-thas ta-mo-BHAY-dee rig-ya-juh-SAA-ma-PAA-ra-gah / gha-na-VRISH-tir a-PAAM MIT-ro vindh-ya-VEE-thee pla-VAN-ga-mah
translation: Lord of the sky, splitter of darkness, master of the Rig, Yajur and Sama Vedas; sender of heavy rain, friend of the waters, coursing swiftly along the Vindhya path of the heavens.
source: Aditya Hridayam 13, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Where could your knowledge become rain — something that actually lands on and feeds another person?

translations.hi: आकाश के स्वामी, अंधकार को चीरने वाले, ऋग्, यजुः और साम वेदों में पारंगत; घनघोर वर्षा के दाता, जल के मित्र, आकाश की विन्ध्य-वीथी पर तीव्र गति से चलने वाले।

devanagari: आतपी मण्डली मृत्युः पिङ्गलः सर्वतापनः । / कविर्विश्वो महातेजाः रक्तः सर्वभवोद्भवः ॥14॥
iast: ātapī maṇḍalī mṛtyuḥ piṅgalaḥ sarvatāpanaḥ । / kavirviśvo mahātejāḥ raktaḥ sarvabhavodbhavaḥ ॥14॥
sayIt: aa-ta-PEE man-da-LEE MRIT-yuh PIN-ga-lah sar-va-TAA-pa-nah / ka-vir-VISH-vo ma-haa-TAY-jaah RAK-tah sar-va-bha-VOD-bha-vah
translation: He blazes with heat, bears the orb, and is Death itself; tawny-gold, the scorcher of all; the seer-poet, the all, mighty in splendour, the crimson one, the origin of all becoming.
source: Aditya Hridayam 14, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What would change if you honoured endings as belonging to the same light that begins things?

translations.hi: वे तप्त तेज वाले हैं, मंडलधारी, स्वयं मृत्यु; पिंगल वर्ण, सबको तपाने वाले; क्रांतदर्शी कवि, स्वयं विश्व, महान तेजस्वी, रक्तिम, और समस्त सृष्टि के उद्गम।

devanagari: नक्षत्रग्रहताराणामधिपो विश्वभावनः । / तेजसामपि तेजस्वी द्वादशात्मन्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥15॥
iast: nakṣatragrahatārāṇāmadhipo viśvabhāvanaḥ । / tejasāmapi tejasvī dvādaśātmannamo'stu te ॥15॥
sayIt: nak-SHA-tra-gra-ha-taa-RAA-naam a-dhi-PO vish-va-BHAA-va-nah / tay-ja-SAAM a-pi tay-JAS-vee dvaa-da-SHAAT-man na-MO-stu tay
translation: Lord of the lunar mansions, the planets and the stars; bringer of the universe into being; radiance even of the radiant — O sun of twelve forms, homage be to you.
source: Aditya Hridayam 15, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What steady presence have you praised in the abstract but never actually thanked, face to face?

translations.hi: नक्षत्रों, ग्रहों और तारों के अधिपति, विश्व को अस्तित्व देने वाले, तेजस्वियों के भी तेज — हे द्वादश रूपों वाले आदित्य, आपको नमस्कार।

devanagari: नमः पूर्वाय गिरये पश्चिमायाद्रये नमः । / ज्योतिर्गणानां पतये दिनाधिपतये नमः ॥16॥
iast: namaḥ pūrvāya giraye paścimāyādraye namaḥ । / jyotirgaṇānāṃ pataye dinādhipataye namaḥ ॥16॥
sayIt: NA-mah poor-VAA-ya gi-ra-YAY pash-chi-MAA-yaad-ra-yay NA-mah / jyo-tir-ga-NAA-naam pa-ta-YAY di-NAA-dhi-pa-ta-yay NA-mah
translation: Homage to the mountain of the east, and homage to the mountain of the west; homage to the lord of the hosts of light, to the lord of the day.
source: Aditya Hridayam 16, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Do you close your days with the same care and respect you try to open them with?

translations.hi: उदय के पूर्व पर्वत को नमस्कार, अस्त के पश्चिम पर्वत को नमस्कार; ज्योतियों के गणों के स्वामी को, दिन के अधिपति को नमस्कार।

devanagari: जयाय जयभद्राय हर्यश्वाय नमो नमः । / नमो नमः सहस्रांशो आदित्याय नमो नमः ॥17॥
iast: jayāya jayabhadrāya haryaśvāya namo namaḥ । / namo namaḥ sahasrāṃśo ādityāya namo namaḥ ॥17॥
sayIt: ja-YAA-ya ja-ya-bha-DRAA-ya har-yash-VAA-ya na-MO NA-mah / na-MO NA-mah sa-has-RAAN-sho aa-dit-YAA-ya na-MO NA-mah
translation: Homage to victory and to the blessing that rides with victory; homage to the rider of the golden-green horses; homage again and again — O thousand-rayed one, homage, homage to Aditya.
source: Aditya Hridayam 17, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: When you last won at something, did the winning leave you and the people around you well?

translations.hi: जय को नमस्कार, जय के साथ चलने वाले कल्याण को नमस्कार; हरित-स्वर्ण अश्वों वाले को बार-बार नमस्कार; हे सहस्र किरणों वाले, आदित्य को बार-बार नमस्कार।

devanagari: नम उग्राय वीराय सारङ्गाय नमो नमः । / नमः पद्मप्रबोधाय मार्ताण्डाय नमो नमः ॥18॥
iast: nama ugrāya vīrāya sāraṅgāya namo namaḥ । / namaḥ padmaprabodhāya mārtāṇḍāya namo namaḥ ॥18॥
sayIt: NA-ma ug-RAA-ya vee-RAA-ya saa-ran-GAA-ya na-MO NA-mah / NA-mah pad-ma-pra-BO-dhaa-ya maar-taan-DAA-ya na-MO NA-mah
translation: Homage to the fierce one, to the hero, to the swift many-hued one, homage again and again; homage to the awakener of the lotus; homage, homage to Martanda.
source: Aditya Hridayam 18, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Which of your strengths could open something gently today instead of forcing it?

translations.hi: उग्र को नमस्कार, वीर को नमस्कार, सारंग को बार-बार नमस्कार; कमलों को जगाने वाले को नमस्कार; मार्तण्ड को बार-बार नमस्कार।

devanagari: मार्तण्डाय, प्रचण्डाय / ब्रह्मेशानाच्युतेशाय सूर्यायादित्यवर्चसे । / भास्वते सर्वभक्षाय रौद्राय वपुषे नमः ॥19॥
iast: mārtaṇḍāya, pracaṇḍāya / brahmeśānācyuteśāya sūryāyādityavarcase । / bhāsvate sarvabhakṣāya raudrāya vapuṣe namaḥ ॥19॥
sayIt: brah-MAY-shaa-naach-yu-TAY-shaa-ya soor-YAA-yaa-dit-ya-var-cha-say / BHAAS-va-tay sar-va-bhak-SHAA-ya rowd-RAA-ya va-pu-SHAY NA-mah
translation: Homage to the lord of Brahma, of Ishana and of Achyuta; to Surya, blazing with the splendour of Aditya; to the shining one, the devourer of all, the form filled with Rudra's awe.
source: Aditya Hridayam 19, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Can your reverence hold both halves — the light that feeds you and the fire that will take everything back?

translations.hi: ब्रह्मा, ईशान और अच्युत के भी स्वामी को नमस्कार; आदित्य के तेज से जगमगाते सूर्य को नमस्कार; प्रकाशमान, सबको अपने में समेट लेने वाले, रौद्र रूप को नमस्कार।

devanagari: तमोघ्नाय हिमघ्नाय शत्रुघ्नायामितात्मने । / कृतघ्नघ्नाय देवाय ज्योतिषां पतये नमः ॥20॥
iast: tamoghnāya himaghnāya śatrughnāyāmitātmane । / kṛtaghnaghnāya devāya jyotiṣāṃ pataye namaḥ ॥20॥
sayIt: ta-mo-GHNAA-ya hi-ma-GHNAA-ya sha-tru-GHNAA-yaa-mi-TAAT-ma-nay / kri-ta-ghna-GHNAA-ya day-VAA-ya jyo-ti-SHAAM pa-ta-YAY NA-mah
translation: Homage to the destroyer of darkness, the destroyer of frost, the destroyer of enemies — the one of measureless spirit; homage to the destroyer of ingratitude, the god who is lord of all lights.
source: Aditya Hridayam 20, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Whose past kindness to you deserves to be named and thanked before this week ends?

translations.hi: अंधकार के नाशक को नमस्कार, शीत के नाशक को, शत्रुओं के नाशक को — असीम आत्मा वाले को नमस्कार; कृतघ्नता का नाश करने वाले, ज्योतियों के स्वामी देव को नमस्कार।

devanagari: तप्तचामीकराभाय वह्नये विश्वकर्मणे । हरये विश्वकर्मणे / नमस्तमोऽभिनिघ्नाय रुचये लोकसाक्षिणे ॥21॥
iast: taptacāmīkarābhāya vahnaye viśvakarmaṇe । haraye viśvakarmaṇe / namastamo'bhinighnāya rucaye lokasākṣiṇe ॥21॥
sayIt: tap-ta-chaa-mee-ka-RAA-bhaa-ya vah-na-YAY vish-va-kar-ma-NAY / na-mas-ta-MO-bhi-nigh-NAA-ya ru-cha-YAY lo-ka-SAAK-shi-nay
translation: Homage to the one who glows like molten gold, to the fire, to the maker of all; homage to the striker-down of darkness, to the splendour, to the witness of the worlds.
source: Aditya Hridayam 21, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: How would today change if you lived it as though watched by a kind but unblinking witness?

translations.hi: तपे हुए सोने-सी आभा वाले को नमस्कार, अग्निरूप को, विश्व के रचयिता को; अंधकार को जड़ से मिटाने वाले, कांतिमान, लोकों के साक्षी को नमस्कार।

devanagari: नाशयत्येष वै भूतं तदेव सृजति प्रभुः । / पायत्येष तपत्येष वर्षत्येष गभस्तिभिः ॥22॥
iast: nāśayatyeṣa vai bhūtaṃ tadeva sṛjati prabhuḥ । / pāyatyeṣa tapatyeṣa varṣatyeṣa gabhastibhiḥ ॥22॥
sayIt: naa-sha-yat-YAY-sha vai BHOO-tum ta-DAY-va sri-JA-ti pra-BHUH / paa-yat-YAY-sha ta-pat-YAY-sha var-shat-YAY-sha ga-BHAS-ti-bhih
translation: It is this lord who dissolves all that exists and creates that very same again; with his rays he drinks up the waters, he blazes, and he pours them back down as rain.
source: Aditya Hridayam 22, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What recent loss of yours might be the first half of a cycle you cannot yet see?

translations.hi: यही प्रभु अस्तित्व को विलीन करते हैं और फिर उसी को रचते हैं; अपनी किरणों से वे जल पी जाते हैं, तपते हैं, और उसे वर्षा बनाकर बरसा देते हैं।

devanagari: एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति भूतेषु परिनिष्ठितः । / एष एवाग्निहोत्रं च फलं चैवाग्निहोत्रिणाम् ॥23॥
iast: eṣa supteṣu jāgarti bhūteṣu pariniṣṭhitaḥ । / eṣa evāgnihotraṃ ca phalaṃ caivāgnihotriṇām ॥23॥
sayIt: AY-sha sup-TAY-shu JAA-gar-ti bhoo-TAY-shu pa-ri-NISH-thi-tah / AY-sha ay-VAAG-ni-ho-trum cha PHA-lum chai-VAAG-ni-ho-tri-naam
translation: He stays awake within beings even while they sleep, fully established in them all; he is the fire-offering itself, and also the fruit that comes to those who offer it.
source: Aditya Hridayam 23, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What stays quietly awake in you through the night, and when did you last sit with it?

translations.hi: प्राणी सो जाते हैं, पर वे उनके भीतर जागते रहते हैं — सबमें प्रतिष्ठित; वे ही अग्निहोत्र यज्ञ हैं, और यज्ञ करने वालों को मिलने वाला फल भी।

devanagari: वेदाश्च क्रतवश्चैव क्रतूनां फलमेव च । / यानि कृत्यानि लोकेषु सर्व एष रविः प्रभुः ॥24॥
iast: vedāśca kratavaścaiva kratūnāṃ phalameva ca । / yāni kṛtyāni lokeṣu sarva eṣa raviḥ prabhuḥ ॥24॥
sayIt: vay-DAASH-cha kra-ta-VASH-chai-va kra-TOO-naam pha-la-MAY-va cha / YAA-ni KRIT-yaa-ni lo-KAY-shu SAR-va AY-sha RA-vih pra-BHUH
translation: The Vedas, the sacrifices, the fruit of the sacrifices, and every act performed in all the worlds — of all of this, Ravi the sun is the lord.
source: Aditya Hridayam 24, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: If your work and its results finally belong to something larger, how will you hold today's tasks?

translations.hi: वेद, यज्ञ, यज्ञों का फल, और लोकों में होने वाले सारे कर्म — इन सबके स्वामी यही रवि हैं।

devanagari: एनमापत्सु कृच्छ्रेषु कान्तारेषु भयेषु च । / कीर्तयन् पुरुषः कश्चिन्नावसीदति राघव ॥25॥
iast: enamāpatsu kṛcchreṣu kāntāreṣu bhayeṣu ca । / kīrtayan puruṣaḥ kaścinnāvasīdati rāghava ॥25॥
sayIt: AY-nam AA-pat-su KRICH-chray-shu kaan-TAA-ray-shu bha-YAY-shu cha / KEER-ta-yan PU-ru-shah KASH-chin naa-va-SEE-da-ti RAA-gha-va
translation: Whoever sings his praise in calamity, in hardship, in the trackless wilds and in fear — that person, O Raghava, does not sink.
source: Aditya Hridayam 25, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What is the thing you can still do in the middle of fear — your version of singing — that keeps you from sinking?

translations.hi: संकट में, कठिनाई में, बीहड़ रास्तों में और भय में जो भी इनका कीर्तन करता है, वह मनुष्य, हे राघव, कभी नहीं डूबता।

devanagari: पूजयस्वैनमेकाग्रो देवदेवं जगत्पतिम् । / एतत् त्रिगुणितं जप्त्वा युद्धेषु विजयिष्यसि ॥26॥
iast: pūjayasvainamekāgro devadevaṃ jagatpatim । / etat triguṇitaṃ japtvā yuddheṣu vijayiṣyasi ॥26॥
sayIt: poo-ja-yas-VAI-nam ay-KAA-gro day-va-DAY-vum ja-gat-PA-tim / AY-tat tri-GU-ni-tum JAP-tvaa yud-DHAY-shu vi-ja-YISH-ya-si
translation: Worship him with a single-pointed mind — the god of gods, the lord of the world; recite this three times through, and you will be victorious in your battles.
source: Aditya Hridayam 26, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Before your next hard thing, what could you repeat three times, slowly, with your whole attention?

translations.hi: एकाग्र मन से इनकी पूजा करो — ये देवों के देव, जगत के स्वामी हैं; इसका तीन बार जप करो, और तुम युद्धों में विजयी होगे।

devanagari: अस्मिन्क्षणे महाबाहो रावणं त्वं वधिष्यसि । / एवमुक्त्वा तदाऽगस्त्यो जगाम च यथागतम् ॥27॥
iast: asminkṣaṇe mahābāho rāvaṇaṃ tvaṃ vadhiṣyasi । / evamuktvā tadā'gastyo jagāma ca yathāgatam ॥27॥
sayIt: as-min KSHA-nay ma-haa-BAA-ho RAA-va-num tvum va-DHISH-ya-si / ay-vam UKT-vaa ta-DAA-gast-yo ja-GAA-ma cha ya-thaa-GA-tum
translation: "In this very moment, mighty-armed one, you will slay Ravana." Having spoken thus, Agastya then departed just as he had come.
source: Aditya Hridayam 27, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Once you have received good guidance, can you let the guide leave and still act on it?

translations.hi: "इसी क्षण, हे महाबाहु, तुम रावण का वध करोगे।" इतना कहकर अगस्त्य जैसे आए थे, वैसे ही लौट गए।

devanagari: एतच्छ्रुत्वा महातेजा नष्टशोकोऽभवत्तदा । / धारयामास सुप्रीतो राघवः प्रयतात्मवान् ॥28॥
iast: etacchrutvā mahātejā naṣṭaśoko'bhavattadā । / dhārayāmāsa suprīto rāghavaḥ prayatātmavān ॥28॥
sayIt: ay-tach-CHRUT-vaa ma-haa-TAY-jaa nash-ta-SHO-ko-bha-vat ta-DAA / dhaa-ra-yaa-MAA-sa su-PREE-to RAA-gha-vah pra-ya-TAAT-ma-vaan
translation: When he had heard this, the mighty Raghava's grief fell away; deeply gladdened and with a collected mind, he took the hymn to heart.
source: Aditya Hridayam 28, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: When did a few remembered words last change your state before your situation changed?

translations.hi: यह सुनते ही महातेजस्वी राघव का शोक मिट गया; गहरे प्रसन्न और संयत मन से उन्होंने इस स्तोत्र को हृदय में धारण कर लिया।

devanagari: आदित्यं प्रेक्ष्य जप्त्वा तु परं हर्षमवाप्तवान् । / त्रिराचम्य शुचिर्भूत्वा धनुरादाय वीर्यवान् ॥29॥
iast: ādityaṃ prekṣya japtvā tu paraṃ harṣamavāptavān । / trirācamya śucirbhūtvā dhanurādāya vīryavān ॥29॥
sayIt: aa-DIT-yum PRAYK-shya JAP-tvaa tu PA-rum HAR-sham a-VAAP-ta-vaan / trir-AA-cham-ya shu-chir-BHOOT-vaa dha-nur-aa-DAA-ya VEER-ya-vaan
translation: Gazing at the sun, he recited it and was filled with the highest joy; then, sipping water three times and made pure, the mighty one took up his bow.
source: Aditya Hridayam 29, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: What tiny act of preparation marks, for you, the line between worrying and acting?

translations.hi: सूर्य की ओर देखकर उन्होंने जप किया और परम हर्ष पाया; फिर तीन बार आचमन कर, शुद्ध होकर, उस वीर ने अपना धनुष उठा लिया।

devanagari: रावणं प्रेक्ष्य हृष्टात्मा युद्धाय समुपागमत् । / सर्व यत्नेन महता वधे तस्य धृतोऽभवत् ॥30॥
iast: rāvaṇaṃ prekṣya hṛṣṭātmā yuddhāya samupāgamat । / sarva yatnena mahatā vadhe tasya dhṛto'bhavat ॥30॥
sayIt: RAA-va-num PRAYK-shya hrish-TAAT-maa yud-DHAA-ya sa-mu-PAA-ga-mat / SAR-va YAT-nay-na ma-ha-TAA va-DHAY TAS-ya dhri-TO-bha-vat
translation: Beholding Ravana, his spirit exultant, he advanced to battle; with all his great effort he set himself firmly on Ravana's destruction.
source: Aditya Hridayam 30, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: Which situation are you seeing with tired eyes that might look different after ten quiet minutes?

translations.hi: रावण को देखकर उनका मन उल्लास से भर उठा, और वे युद्ध के लिए आगे बढ़े; अपने पूरे महान प्रयत्न के साथ वे उसके वध का दृढ़ निश्चय कर चुके थे।

devanagari: अथ रविरवदन्निरीक्ष्य रामं / मुदितमनाः परमं प्रहृष्यमाणः । / निशिचरपतिसङ्क्षयं विदित्वा / सुरगणमध्यगतो वचस्त्वरेति ॥31॥
iast: atha raviravadannirīkṣya rāmaṃ / muditamanāḥ paramaṃ prahṛṣyamāṇaḥ । / niśicarapatisaṅkṣayaṃ viditvā / suragaṇamadhyagato vacastvareti ॥31॥
sayIt: A-tha RA-vir a-va-dan ni-REEK-shya RAA-mum / mu-di-ta-ma-NAAH PA-ra-mum pra-hrish-ya-MAA-nah / ni-shi-cha-ra-pa-ti-SANK-sha-yum vi-DIT-vaa / su-ra-ga-na-madh-ya-ga-TO va-chas TVA-ray-ti
translation: Then the Sun himself, standing amid the host of gods, looked upon Rama with a gladdened mind and, rejoicing greatly — knowing the destruction of the lord of the night-rangers was at hand — spoke the word: "Make haste."
source: Aditya Hridayam 31, Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/adityahriday.itx
reflection: If the moment you prepared for is finally here, what are you still waiting for?

translations.hi: तब देवताओं के बीच खड़े स्वयं सूर्य ने प्रसन्न मन से राम को देखा और, निशाचरों के स्वामी का अंत निकट जानकर, अत्यंत हर्षित होकर एक शब्द कहा — "त्वरा करो।"

devanagari: भज गोविन्दं भज गोविन्दं / गोविन्दं भज मूढमते । / सम्प्राप्ते सन्निहिते काले / नहि नहि रक्षति डुकृङ्करणे ॥1॥
iast: bhaja govindaṃ bhaja govindaṃ / govindaṃ bhaja mūḍhamate । / samprāpte sannihite kāle / nahi nahi rakṣati ḍukṛṅkaraṇe ॥1॥
sayIt: BHA-ja go-VIN-dum BHA-ja go-VIN-dum / go-VIN-dum BHA-ja MOO-dha-ma-tay / sam-PRAAP-tay SAN-ni-hi-tay KAA-lay / na-hi na-hi RAK-sha-ti du-krin-KA-ra-nay
translation: Sing to Govinda, sing to Govinda, sing to Govinda, you deluded mind — when the appointed hour has drawn near, the grammar rule "ḍukṛñ karaṇe" will not save you, no, it will not.
source: Bhaja Govindam 1 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: If the deadline of your life were suddenly visible, which of today's preoccupations would still deserve the day?

translations.hi: गोविन्द को भजो, गोविन्द को भजो, हे मोहग्रस्त बुद्धि, गोविन्द को भजो — जब नियत घड़ी सिर पर आ पहुँचे, तब व्याकरण का सूत्र "डुकृञ् करणे" तुम्हें नहीं बचाएगा, नहीं बचाएगा।

devanagari: मूढ जहीहि धनागमतृष्णां / कुरु सद्बुद्धिं मनसि वितृष्णाम् । / यल्लभसे निजकर्मोपात्तं / वित्तं तेन विनोदय चित्तम् ॥2॥
iast: mūḍha jahīhi dhanāgamatṛṣṇāṃ / kuru sadbuddhiṃ manasi vitṛṣṇām । / yallabhase nijakarmopāttaṃ / vittaṃ tena vinodaya cittam ॥2॥
sayIt: MOO-dha ja-HEE-hi dha-NAA-ga-ma-TRISH-naam / ku-ru sad-BUD-dhim MA-na-si vi-TRISH-naam / yal-LA-bha-say ni-ja-kar-MO-paat-tum / VIT-tum TAY-na vi-NO-da-ya CHIT-tum
translation: Fool, give up the thirst for gathering wealth; free the mind of craving and turn it to honest thought. Let the wealth your own work brings you be what contents your heart.
source: Bhaja Govindam 2 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Would what you earned honestly this month feel like enough if you stopped measuring it against what others have?

translations.hi: मूर्ख मन, धन बटोरने की प्यास छोड़; तृष्णा से मुक्त होकर मन में सद्बुद्धि जगा। अपने कर्म से जो धन सहज मिले, उसी से चित्त को प्रसन्न रख।

devanagari: नारीस्तनभरनाभीदेशं / दृष्ट्वा मा गा मोहावेशम् । / एतन्मांसवसादिविकारं / मनसि विचिन्तय वारं वारम् ॥3॥
iast: nārīstanabharanābhīdeśaṃ / dṛṣṭvā mā gā mohāveśam । / etanmāṃsavasādivikāraṃ / manasi vicintaya vāraṃ vāram ॥3॥
sayIt: naa-ree-STA-na-bha-ra-NAA-bhee-DAY-shum / DRISHT-vaa maa gaa mo-HAA-vay-shum / ay-tan-MAAM-sa-va-SAA-di-vi-KAA-rum / MA-na-si vi-CHIN-ta-ya VAA-rum VAA-rum
translation: Seeing the swell of a woman's breast and waist, do not fall into a rush of infatuation. It is a modification of flesh, fat, and the rest — turn this over in the mind again and again.
source: Bhaja Govindam 3 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: When desire rises today, can you notice the story your mind adds to what the eye actually saw?

translations.hi: स्त्री के तन के उभारों को देखकर मोह के आवेश में मत बह जाओ। यह मांस, वसा आदि का ही विकार है — मन में बार-बार यही विचार करो।

devanagari: नलिनीदलगतजलमतितरलं / तद्वज्जीवितमतिशयचपलम् । / विद्धि व्याध्यभिमानग्रस्तं / लोकं शोकहतं च समस्तम् ॥4॥
iast: nalinīdalagatajalamatitaralaṃ / tadvajjīvitamatiśayacapalam । / viddhi vyādhyabhimānagrastaṃ / lokaṃ śokahataṃ ca samastam ॥4॥
sayIt: na-li-NEE-da-la-GA-ta-JA-lam a-ti-TA-ra-lum / TAD-vaj JEE-vi-tam a-ti-SHA-ya-CHA-pa-lum / VID-dhi VYAA-dhya-bhi-MAA-na-GRAS-tum / LO-kum SHO-ka-ha-tum cha sa-MAS-tum
translation: Water resting on a lotus leaf trembles and slides; life is every bit as unsteady. Know the whole world to be in the grip of disease and self-importance, and struck through with grief.
source: Bhaja Govindam 4 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: If you took today as a drop already sliding, what would you stop postponing?

translations.hi: कमल के पत्ते पर ठहरा पानी काँपता-फिसलता रहता है; जीवन भी उतना ही चंचल है। जान लो कि सारा संसार रोग और अभिमान से जकड़ा हुआ है, और शोक से आहत है।

devanagari: यावद्वित्तोपार्जनसक्त / स्तावन्निजपरिवारो रक्तः । / पश्चाज्जीवति जर्जरदेहे / वार्तां कोऽपि न पृच्छति गेहे ॥5॥
iast: yāvadvittopārjanasakta / stāvannijaparivāro raktaḥ । / paścājjīvati jarjaradehe / vārtāṃ ko'pi na pṛcchati gehe ॥5॥
sayIt: YAA-vad vit-TO-paar-ja-na-SAK-tas / TAA-van ni-ja-pa-ri-VAA-ro RAK-tah / pash-CHAAJ JEE-va-ti JAR-ja-ra-DAY-hay / VAAR-taam KO-pi na PRICH-cha-ti GAY-hay
translation: As long as you are fit to earn, your own family stays fond of you. Later, when you live on in a worn-out body, no one at home so much as asks how you are.
source: Bhaja Govindam 5 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which of your relationships would hold steady if you had nothing left to provide?

translations.hi: जब तक तुम कमाने में समर्थ हो, तब तक अपना परिवार अनुरक्त रहता है। बाद में, जब जर्जर देह में जीते हो, तो घर में कोई हालचाल तक नहीं पूछता।

devanagari: यावत्पवनो निवसति देहे / तावत्पृच्छति कुशलं गेहे । / गतवति वायौ देहापाये / भार्या बिभ्यति तस्मिन्काये ॥6॥
iast: yāvatpavano nivasati dehe / tāvatpṛcchati kuśalaṃ gehe । / gatavati vāyau dehāpāye / bhāryā bibhyati tasminkāye ॥6॥
sayIt: YAA-vat PA-va-no ni-VA-sa-ti DAY-hay / TAA-vat PRICH-cha-ti ku-SHA-lum GAY-hay / GA-ta-va-ti VAA-yow day-HAA-paa-yay / BHAAR-yaa BIBH-ya-ti TAS-min KAA-yay
translation: As long as breath lives in the body, those at home ask after your welfare. When the breath departs and the body fails, even the wife dreads that same body.
source: Bhaja Govindam 6 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: If what your loved ones cherish in you is not finally this body, what is it — and are you tending that?

translations.hi: जब तक देह में प्राण बसते हैं, तब तक घर में सब कुशल पूछते हैं। प्राण-वायु के निकलते ही, देह के ढह जाने पर, उसी काया से पत्नी तक डरती है।

devanagari: बालस्तावत्क्रीडासक्तः / तरुणस्तावत्तरुणीसक्तः । / वृद्धस्तावच्चिन्तासक्तः / परमे ब्रह्मणि कोऽपि न सक्तः ॥7॥
iast: bālastāvatkrīḍāsaktaḥ / taruṇastāvattaruṇīsaktaḥ । / vṛddhastāvaccintāsaktaḥ / parame brahmaṇi ko'pi na saktaḥ ॥7॥
sayIt: BAA-las TAA-vat kree-DAA-sak-tah / ta-RU-nas TAA-vat ta-ru-NEE-sak-tah / VRID-dhas TAA-vach chin-TAA-sak-tah / pa-RA-may BRAH-ma-ni KO-pi na SAK-tah
translation: The child is absorbed in play, the youth absorbed in a young woman, the old man absorbed in worry — and no one, at any age, is absorbed in the supreme Brahman.
source: Bhaja Govindam 7 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: What is the absorbing concern of your current stage of life, and what is it quietly crowding out?

translations.hi: बालक खेल में आसक्त है, युवक युवती में, वृद्ध चिन्ता में — पर परम ब्रह्म में आसक्त कोई नहीं।

devanagari: का ते कान्ता कस्ते पुत्रः / संसारोऽयमतीव विचित्रः । / कस्य त्वं कः कुत आयात / स्तत्त्वं चिन्तय तदिह भ्रातः ॥8॥
iast: kā te kāntā kaste putraḥ / saṃsāro'yamatīva vicitraḥ । / kasya tvaṃ kaḥ kuta āyāta / stattvaṃ cintaya tadiha bhrātaḥ ॥8॥
sayIt: kaa tay KAAN-taa KAS-tay PUT-rah / sam-SAA-ro-yam a-TEE-va vi-CHIT-rah / KAS-ya tvum kah KU-ta aa-YAA-tas / TAT-tvum CHIN-ta-ya TA-di-ha BHRAA-tah
translation: Who is your wife? Who is your son? Exceedingly strange is this round of the world. Whose are you? Who are you? From where have you come? Brother, ponder that truth here and now.
source: Bhaja Govindam 8 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Before any of your roles existed — spouse, parent, child, professional — who were you?

translations.hi: कौन तुम्हारी पत्नी, कौन तुम्हारा पुत्र? यह संसार अत्यन्त विचित्र है। तुम किसके हो? कौन हो? कहाँ से आए हो? भाई, यहीं-अभी उस तत्त्व का विचार करो।

devanagari: सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं / निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम् । / निर्मोहत्वे निश्चलतत्त्वं / निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः ॥9॥
iast: satsaṅgatve nissaṅgatvaṃ / nissaṅgatve nirmohatvam । / nirmohatve niścalatattvaṃ / niścalatattve jīvanmuktiḥ ॥9॥
sayIt: sat-SUNG-gat-vay nis-SUNG-gat-vum / nis-SUNG-gat-vay nir-MO-hat-vum / nir-MO-hat-vay nish-cha-la-TAT-tvum / nish-cha-la-TAT-tvay jee-van-MUK-tih
translation: From the company of the good comes freedom from clinging; from non-clinging, freedom from delusion; from freedom from delusion, the unwavering real; and in the unwavering real, liberation while still alive.
source: Bhaja Govindam 9 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Whose company reliably leaves you calmer and clearer — and how much of your week does that person actually get?

translations.hi: सत्संग से निःसंगता आती है; निःसंगता से निर्मोहता; निर्मोहता से निश्चल तत्त्व का बोध; और निश्चल तत्त्व में जीते-जी मुक्ति।

devanagari: वयसि गते कः कामविकारः / शुष्के नीरे कः कासारः । / क्षीणे वित्ते कः परिवारः / ज्ञाते तत्त्वे कः संसारः ॥10॥
iast: vayasi gate kaḥ kāmavikāraḥ / śuṣke nīre kaḥ kāsāraḥ । / kṣīṇe vitte kaḥ parivāraḥ / jñāte tattve kaḥ saṃsāraḥ ॥10॥
sayIt: VA-ya-si GA-tay kah KAA-ma-vi-KAA-rah / SHUSH-kay NEE-ray kah kaa-SAA-rah / KSHEE-nay VIT-tay kah pa-ri-VAA-rah / GYAA-tay TAT-tvay kah sam-SAA-rah
translation: When youth is gone, where is the surge of desire? When the water has dried, where is the lake? When wealth is spent, where is the retinue? And when the truth is known, where is saṃsāra?
source: Bhaja Govindam 10 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which solid-seeming certainty of your life exists only while its conditions last?

translations.hi: यौवन बीत जाए तो काम-विकार कहाँ? पानी सूख जाए तो सरोवर कहाँ? धन चुक जाए तो परिजनों की भीड़ कहाँ? और तत्त्व जान लिया जाए तो संसार कहाँ?

devanagari: मा कुरु धनजनयौवनगर्वं / हरति निमेषात्कालः सर्वम् । / मायामयमिदमखिलं हित्वा बुध्वा / ब्रह्मपदं त्वं प्रविश विदित्वा ॥11॥
iast: mā kuru dhanajanayauvanagarvaṃ / harati nimeṣātkālaḥ sarvam । / māyāmayamidamakhilaṃ hitvā budhvā / brahmapadaṃ tvaṃ praviśa viditvā ॥11॥
sayIt: maa KU-ru DHA-na-JA-na-YOW-va-na-GAR-vum / HA-ra-ti ni-MAY-shaat KAA-lah SAR-vum / maa-YAA-ma-yam i-dam a-khi-LUM hit-VAA / BRAH-ma-pa-dum tvum pra-VI-sha vi-dit-VAA
translation: Do not take pride in wealth, followers, or youth; time snatches all of it in the blink of an eye. Let go of this whole māyā-made show, know the truth of it, and enter the state of Brahman.
source: Bhaja Govindam 11 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Of your three quiet supports — money, people, youth — which one are you treating as a permanent possession?

translations.hi: धन, परिजन या यौवन का गर्व मत करो; काल पलक झपकते सब हर लेता है। इस पूरे मायामय प्रपंच को छोड़कर, उसका तत्त्व जानकर, तुम ब्रह्मपद में प्रवेश करो।

devanagari: दिनयामिन्यौ सायं प्रातः / शिशिरवसन्तौ पुनरायातः । / कालः क्रीडति गच्छत्यायु / स्तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशावायुः ॥12॥
iast: dinayāminyau sāyaṃ prātaḥ / śiśiravasantau punarāyātaḥ । / kālaḥ krīḍati gacchatyāyu / stadapi na muñcatyāśāvāyuḥ ॥12॥
sayIt: di-na-yaa-MIN-yow SAA-yum PRAA-tah / SHI-shi-ra-va-SAN-tow pu-na-raa-YAA-tah / KAA-lah KREE-da-ti gach-chat-YAA-yus / TA-da-pi na moon-chat-YAA-shaa-VAA-yuh
translation: Day and night, dusk and dawn, winter and spring come round again and again. Time plays, and the lifespan drains away — and even so, the gusting wind of hope does not let go.
source: Bhaja Govindam 12 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which of this year's passing seasons carried something away while you were busy planning for later?

translations.hi: दिन और रात, साँझ और सवेरा, शिशिर और वसन्त बार-बार लौट आते हैं। काल खेलता है, आयु बीतती जाती है — फिर भी आशा की हवा पीछा नहीं छोड़ती।

devanagari: का ते कान्ता धनगतचिन्ता / वातुल किं तव नास्ति नियन्ता । / त्रिजगति सज्जनसङ्गतिरेका / भवति भवार्णवतरणे नौका ॥13॥
iast: kā te kāntā dhanagatacintā / vātula kiṃ tava nāsti niyantā । / trijagati sajjanasaṅgatirekā / bhavati bhavārṇavataraṇe naukā ॥13॥
sayIt: kaa tay KAAN-taa DHA-na-ga-ta-CHIN-taa / VAA-tu-la kim TA-va NAAS-ti ni-YAN-taa / tri-JA-ga-ti SAJ-ja-na-SUNG-ga-ti-RAY-kaa / BHA-va-ti bha-VAAR-na-va-TA-ra-nay NOW-kaa
translation: What to you is a beloved, what this brooding sunk in wealth, you wind-tossed one? Is there no one to rein you in? In all three worlds, only the company of the good is a boat for crossing the ocean of becoming.
source: Bhaja Govindam 13 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Who in your life has real standing to rein you in — and do you let them use it?

translations.hi: हे वायु-से उड़ते चित्त वाले, कौन तुम्हारी प्रिया, कैसी यह धन में धँसी चिन्ता? क्या तुम्हें थामने वाला कोई नहीं? तीनों लोकों में केवल सज्जनों का संग ही भवसागर पार कराने वाली नौका है।

devanagari: जटिलो मुण्डी लुञ्छितकेशः / काषायाम्बरबहुकृतवेषः । / पश्यन्नपि च न पश्यति मूढो / ह्युदरनिमित्तं बहुकृतवेषः ॥14॥
iast: jaṭilo muṇḍī luñchitakeśaḥ / kāṣāyāmbarabahukṛtaveṣaḥ । / paśyannapi ca na paśyati mūḍho / hyudaranimittaṃ bahukṛtaveṣaḥ ॥14॥
sayIt: JA-ti-lo MOON-dee LOON-chi-ta-KAY-shah / kaa-SHAA-yaam-ba-ra-BA-hu-kri-ta-VAY-shah / PASH-yan-na-pi cha na PASH-ya-ti MOO-dho / HYU-da-ra-ni-MIT-tum BA-hu-kri-ta-VAY-shah
translation: One wears matted locks, one a shaven head, one hair plucked out, another ochre robes — costume upon costume. The fool sees and yet does not see: all this dressing-up is for the belly's sake.
source: Bhaja Govindam 14 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Where does your own practice have a costume — something visible you maintain in place of the seeing it was meant to serve?

translations.hi: कोई जटाधारी, कोई मुण्डित, कोई केश नुचवाए, कोई गेरुए वस्त्रों में — वेश पर वेश। मूढ़ देखकर भी नहीं देखता: यह सारा स्वांग तो पेट के लिए रचा गया है।

devanagari: अङ्गं गलितं पलितं मुण्डं / दशनविहीनं जातं तुण्डम् । / वृद्धो याति गृहीत्वा दण्डं / तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशापिण्डम् ॥15॥
iast: aṅgaṃ galitaṃ palitaṃ muṇḍaṃ / daśanavihīnaṃ jātaṃ tuṇḍam । / vṛddho yāti gṛhītvā daṇḍaṃ / tadapi na muñcatyāśāpiṇḍam ॥15॥
sayIt: UNG-gum GA-li-tum PA-li-tum MOON-dum / DA-sha-na-vi-HEE-num JAA-tum TOON-dum / VRID-dho YAA-ti gri-HEET-vaa DUN-dum / TA-da-pi na moon-chat-YAA-shaa-PIN-dum
translation: The limbs have withered, the head has greyed, the mouth is left without teeth; the old man walks leaning on a staff — and even then the thick knot of hope does not let him go.
source: Bhaja Govindam 15 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: If your desires will not retire when your body does, which one deserves to be set down now?

translations.hi: अंग ढल गए, सिर के बाल पक गए, मुँह दाँतों से ख़ाली हो गया; वृद्ध लाठी थामे चलता है — फिर भी आशा का पिण्ड उसे नहीं छोड़ता।

devanagari: अग्रे वह्निः पृष्ठे भानुः / रात्रौ चुबुकसमर्पितजानुः । / करतलभिक्षस्तरुतलवास / स्तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशापाशः ॥16॥
iast: agre vahniḥ pṛṣṭhe bhānuḥ / rātrau cubukasamarpitajānuḥ । / karatalabhikṣastarutalavāsa / stadapi na muñcatyāśāpāśaḥ ॥16॥
sayIt: AG-ray VAH-nih PRISH-thay BHAA-nuh / RAAT-row chu-BU-ka-sa-MAR-pi-ta-JAA-nuh / KA-ra-ta-la-BHIK-shas ta-ru-ta-la-VAA-sas / TA-da-pi na moon-chat-YAA-shaa-PAA-shah
translation: Fire in front, the sun at his back, knees hugged to the chin through the night; alms in the cupped palm, a tree for a dwelling — and even so, the noose of hope does not release him.
source: Bhaja Govindam 16 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: What have you given up outwardly while keeping your inner grip on it fully intact?

translations.hi: आगे अलाव, पीठ पर धूप, रात में ठोड़ी घुटनों में दबाए; हथेली ही भिक्षा-पात्र, पेड़ के नीचे वास — इतने पर भी आशा का फंदा नहीं छूटता।

devanagari: कुरुते गङ्गासागरगमनं / व्रतपरिपालनमथवा दानम् । / ज्ञानविहीनः सर्वमतेन / मुक्तिं न भजति जन्मशतेन ॥17॥
iast: kurute gaṅgāsāgaragamanaṃ / vrataparipālanamathavā dānam । / jñānavihīnaḥ sarvamatena / muktiṃ na bhajati janmaśatena ॥17॥
sayIt: ku-ru-TAY gun-GAA-saa-GA-ra-GA-ma-num / VRA-ta-pa-ri-PAA-la-nam a-tha-VAA DAA-num / GYAA-na-vi-HEE-nah SAR-va-ma-TAY-na / MUK-tim na BHA-ja-ti JAN-ma-sha-TAY-na
translation: One may journey to where the Ganga meets the sea, keep every vow, or give in charity; yet without knowledge — so runs the reckoning of every school — one does not attain liberation even in a hundred births.
source: Bhaja Govindam 17 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which part of your practice is running on autopilot — doing the act without remembering what it is for?

translations.hi: कोई गंगासागर की यात्रा कर ले, व्रतों का पालन करे या दान दे; पर ज्ञान के बिना — ऐसा सब मतों का कहना है — सौ जन्मों में भी मुक्ति नहीं मिलती।

devanagari: सुरमंदिरतरुमूलनिवासः / शय्या भूतलमजिनं वासः । / सर्वपरिग्रहभोगत्यागः / कस्य सुखं न करोति विरागः ॥18॥
iast: suramaṃdiratarumūlanivāsaḥ / śayyā bhūtalamajinaṃ vāsaḥ । / sarvaparigrahabhogatyāgaḥ / kasya sukhaṃ na karoti virāgaḥ ॥18॥
sayIt: su-ra-MUN-di-ra-TA-ru-MOO-la-ni-VAA-sah / SHAY-yaa BHOO-ta-lam A-ji-num VAA-sah / SAR-va-pa-ri-GRA-ha-BHO-ga-TYAA-gah / KAS-ya SU-khum na ka-RO-ti vi-RAA-gah
translation: A home in a temple of the gods or at the foot of a tree, the bare earth for a bed, a deerskin for clothing, every possession and every pleasure given up — whom would such dispassion not make happy?
source: Bhaja Govindam 18 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: What could you stop maintaining this week and feel lighter for it, not poorer?

translations.hi: देव-मन्दिर या पेड़ के नीचे वास, धरती ही शय्या, मृगचर्म ही वस्त्र, सारे संग्रह और भोग का त्याग — ऐसा वैराग्य किसे सुखी न कर दे?

devanagari: योगरतो वा भोगरतो वा / सङ्गरतो वा सङ्गविहीनः । / यस्य ब्रह्मणि रमते चित्तं / नन्दति नन्दति नन्दत्येव ॥19॥
iast: yogarato vā bhogarato vā / saṅgarato vā saṅgavihīnaḥ । / yasya brahmaṇi ramate cittaṃ / nandati nandati nandatyeva ॥19॥
sayIt: YO-ga-ra-to vaa BHO-ga-ra-to vaa / SUNG-ga-ra-to vaa SUNG-ga-vi-HEE-nah / YAS-ya BRAH-ma-ni ra-MA-tay CHIT-tum / NAN-da-ti NAN-da-ti NAN-dat-YAY-va
translation: Absorbed in yoga or absorbed in enjoyment, delighting in company or free of all company — the one whose mind comes to rest in Brahman rejoices, rejoices, simply rejoices.
source: Bhaja Govindam 19 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Where does your mind go to rest when nothing is demanding it — and does that place actually feed you?

translations.hi: कोई योग में रत हो या भोग में, संग में रमा हो या संग से रहित — जिसका चित्त ब्रह्म में रमता है, वही आनन्दित होता है, आनन्दित होता है, बस आनन्दित होता है।

devanagari: भगवद्गीता किञ्चिदधीता / गङ्गाजललवकणिका पीता । / सकृदपि येन मुरारिसमर्चा / क्रियते तस्य यमेन न चर्चा ॥20॥
iast: bhagavadgītā kiñcidadhītā / gaṅgājalalavakaṇikā pītā । / sakṛdapi yena murārisamarcā / kriyate tasya yamena na carcā ॥20॥
sayIt: BHA-ga-vad-GEE-taa KIN-chid a-DHEE-taa / gun-GAA-ja-la-LA-va-KA-ni-kaa PEE-taa / sa-KRI-da-pi YAY-na mu-RAA-ri-sa-MAR-chaa / kri-YA-tay TAS-ya ya-MAY-na na CHAR-chaa
translation: A little of the Bhagavad Gita studied, a single droplet of Ganga water sipped, worship offered to Murari even once — with such a person Yama has no case to argue.
source: Bhaja Govindam 20 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: What is the smallest sincere act of practice you could actually do today — and will you do it?

translations.hi: थोड़ी-सी भगवद्गीता पढ़ ली, गंगाजल की एक बूँद पी ली, एक बार भी मुरारि की सच्ची पूजा कर ली — ऐसे जन से यमराज का कोई विवाद नहीं रहता।

devanagari: पुनरपि जननं पुनरपि मरणं / पुनरपि जननीजठरे शयनम् । / इह संसारे बहुदुस्तारे / कृपयाऽपारे पाहि मुरारे ॥21॥
iast: punarapi jananaṃ punarapi maraṇaṃ / punarapi jananījaṭhare śayanam । / iha saṃsāre bahudustāre / kṛpayā'pāre pāhi murāre ॥21॥
sayIt: pu-na-RA-pi JA-na-num pu-na-RA-pi MA-ra-num / pu-na-RA-pi JA-na-nee-JA-tha-ray SHA-ya-num / i-ha sam-SAA-ray BA-hu-dus-TAA-ray / kri-pa-YAA-paa-ray PAA-hi mu-RAA-ray
translation: Birth once again, death once again, once again the lying in a mother's womb. This saṃsāra is so hard to ford — Murari, protect me by your boundless compassion.
source: Bhaja Govindam 21 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which pattern do you keep getting reborn into — and have you ever sincerely asked for help crossing it?

translations.hi: फिर जन्म, फिर मृत्यु, फिर माता के गर्भ में शयन। यह संसार पार करना बहुत कठिन है — हे मुरारे, अपनी अपार कृपा से मेरी रक्षा करो।

devanagari: रथ्याचर्पटविरचितकन्थः / पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितपन्थः । / योगी योगनियोजितचित्तो / रमते बालोन्मत्तवदेव ॥22॥
iast: rathyācarpaṭaviracitakanthaḥ / puṇyāpuṇyavivarjitapanthaḥ । / yogī yoganiyojitacitto / ramate bālonmattavadeva ॥22॥
sayIt: rath-YAA-char-PA-ta-vi-RA-chi-ta-KAN-thah / poon-YAA-poon-ya-vi-VAR-ji-ta-PAN-thah / YO-gee YO-ga-ni-YO-ji-ta-CHIT-to / ra-MA-tay BAA-lon-MAT-ta-va-DAY-va
translation: His patched wrap stitched from rags picked off the road, his path beyond merit and demerit alike, the yogi whose mind is yoked in yoga delights like a child, like one gone mad.
source: Bhaja Govindam 22 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: When did you last do something wholeheartedly with no ledger of gain, merit, or image running underneath?

translations.hi: राह में पड़े चिथड़ों से सिली गुदड़ी ओढ़े, पुण्य और पाप दोनों से परे चलता हुआ, योग में जुते चित्त वाला योगी बालक-सा, उन्मत्त-सा आनन्द में रमता है।

devanagari: कस्त्वं कोऽहं कुत आयातः / का मे जननी को मे तातः । / इति परिभावय सर्वमसारम् / विश्वं त्यक्त्वा स्वप्नविचारम् ॥23॥
iast: kastvaṃ ko'haṃ kuta āyātaḥ / kā me jananī ko me tātaḥ । / iti paribhāvaya sarvamasāram / viśvaṃ tyaktvā svapnavicāram ॥23॥
sayIt: KAS-tvum KO-hum KU-ta aa-YAA-tah / kaa may JA-na-nee ko may TAA-tah / I-ti pa-ri-BHAA-va-ya SAR-vam a-SAA-rum / VISH-vum tyakt-VAA SVAP-na-vi-CHAA-rum
translation: Who are you? Who am I? From where have I come? Who is my mother, who my father? Ponder it all this way, see it as pithless, and let go of the world — it is the stuff of a dream.
source: Bhaja Govindam 23 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Strip away your name, family, and history for one quiet moment — what remains that still says "I"?

translations.hi: तुम कौन हो? मैं कौन हूँ? कहाँ से आया हूँ? कौन मेरी माता, कौन मेरे पिता? इस प्रकार विचार करो, सबको निःसार जानो, और स्वप्न-सरीखे इस विश्व का आग्रह छोड़ दो।

devanagari: त्वयि मयि चान्यत्रैको विष्णु / र्व्यर्थं कुप्यसि मय्यसहिष्णुः । / भव समचित्तः सर्वत्र त्वं / वाञ्छस्यचिराद्यदि विष्णुत्वम् ॥24॥
iast: tvayi mayi cānyatraiko viṣṇu / rvyarthaṃ kupyasi mayyasahiṣṇuḥ । / bhava samacittaḥ sarvatra tvaṃ / vāñchasyacirādyadi viṣṇutvam ॥24॥
sayIt: TVA-yi MA-yi chaan-yat-RAI-ko VISH-nuh / VYAR-thum KUP-ya-si may-ya-sa-HISH-nuh / BHA-va SA-ma-CHIT-tah sar-VAT-ra tvum / VAAN-chas-ya-chi-RAAD YA-di VISH-nut-vum
translation: In you, in me, and everywhere else there is one Vishnu only. Your impatience and your anger at me are pointless. If you would soon reach the state of Vishnu, be even-minded toward all.
source: Bhaja Govindam 24 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: The person who most annoys you today — can you pause once and consider what looks out from behind their eyes?

translations.hi: तुझमें, मुझमें और अन्यत्र सर्वत्र एक ही विष्णु हैं। मुझ पर असहिष्णु होकर व्यर्थ ही क्रोध करते हो। यदि शीघ्र विष्णुत्व पाना चाहते हो, तो सर्वत्र समचित्त बनो।

devanagari: शत्रौ मित्रे पुत्रे बन्धौ / मा कुरु यत्नं विग्रहसन्धौ । / सर्वस्मिन्नपि पश्यात्मानं / सर्वत्रोत्सृज भेदाज्ञानम् ॥25॥
iast: śatrau mitre putre bandhau / mā kuru yatnaṃ vigrahasandhau । / sarvasminnapi paśyātmānaṃ / sarvatrotsṛja bhedājñānam ॥25॥
sayIt: SHAT-row MIT-ray PUT-ray BAN-dhow / maa KU-ru YAT-num vig-RA-ha-SAN-dhow / sar-VAS-min-na-pi pash-YAAT-maa-num / sar-vat-ROT-sri-ja bhay-daa-GYAA-num
translation: Toward enemy and friend, toward son and kinsman, spend no effort on feud or on alliance. See your own Self in every single one, and everywhere cast off the ignorance that divides.
source: Bhaja Govindam 25 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which relationship are you managing like a treaty negotiation instead of simply meeting the person?

translations.hi: शत्रु हो या मित्र, पुत्र हो या बन्धु — झगड़ने या पाटने की जोड़-तोड़ में शक्ति मत लगाओ। हर एक में अपने ही आत्मा को देखो, और भेद के अज्ञान को सर्वत्र त्याग दो।

devanagari: कामं क्रोधं लोभं मोहं / त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मानं भावय कोऽहम् । पश्यति सोऽहम् / आत्मज्ञानविहीना मूढा / स्ते पच्यन्ते नरकनिगूढाः ॥26॥
iast: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ lobhaṃ mohaṃ / tyaktvā''tmānaṃ bhāvaya ko'ham । paśyati so'ham / ātmajñānavihīnā mūḍhā / ste pacyante narakanigūḍhāḥ ॥26॥
sayIt: KAA-mum KRO-dhum LO-bhum MO-hum / tyakt-VAAT-maa-num BHAA-va-ya KO-hum / AAT-ma-GYAA-na-vi-HEE-naa MOO-dhaas / tay pach-YAN-tay NA-ra-ka-ni-GOO-dhaah
translation: Setting aside desire, anger, greed, and delusion, turn to yourself and ponder: "Who am I?" Those without knowledge of the Self are fools who stew, sunk out of sight in hell.
source: Bhaja Govindam 26 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which of the four — wanting, anger, greed, delusion — most often answers for you before your real self can speak?

translations.hi: काम, क्रोध, लोभ और मोह को छोड़कर अपने भीतर विचार करो — "मैं कौन हूँ?" आत्मज्ञान से रहित मूढ़ नरक में डूबे हुए पकते-तपते हैं।

devanagari: गेयं गीतानामसहस्रं / ध्येयं श्रीपतिरूपमजस्रम् । / नेयं सज्जनसङ्गे चित्तं / देयं दीनजनाय च वित्तम् ॥27॥
iast: geyaṃ gītānāmasahasraṃ / dhyeyaṃ śrīpatirūpamajasram । / neyaṃ sajjanasaṅge cittaṃ / deyaṃ dīnajanāya ca vittam ॥27॥
sayIt: GAY-yum gee-TAA-naa-ma-sa-HAS-rum / DHYAY-yum SHREE-pa-ti-ROO-pam a-JAS-rum / NAY-yum SAJ-ja-na-SUNG-gay CHIT-tum / DAY-yum DEE-na-ja-NAA-ya cha VIT-tum
translation: To be sung: the Gita and the thousand Names. To be held in mind without break: the form of the Lord of Shri. To be led into the company of the good: the mind. To be given to those in need: your wealth.
source: Bhaja Govindam 27 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Of the four — singing, remembering, keeping good company, giving — which one is missing from your ordinary day?

translations.hi: गाने योग्य है गीता और सहस्रनाम; निरन्तर ध्यान करने योग्य है श्रीपति का रूप; चित्त को ले जाना है सज्जनों के संग में; और धन देना है दीन-दुखियों को।

devanagari: सुखतः क्रियते रामाभोगः / पश्चाद्धन्त शरीरे रोगः । / यद्यपि लोके मरणं शरणं / तदपि न मुञ्चति पापाचरणम् ॥28॥
iast: sukhataḥ kriyate rāmābhogaḥ / paścāddhanta śarīre rogaḥ । / yadyapi loke maraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ / tadapi na muñcati pāpācaraṇam ॥28॥
sayIt: su-kha-TAH kri-YA-tay raa-MAA-bho-gah / pash-CHAAD HAN-ta sha-REE-ray RO-gah / YAD-ya-pi LO-kay MA-ra-num SHA-ra-num / TA-da-pi na MOON-cha-ti paa-PAA-cha-ra-num
translation: For pleasure one takes one's enjoyment of a woman; afterwards — alas — disease in the body. And though in this world death is the final refuge of all, still one does not give up the ways of sin.
source: Bhaja Govindam 28 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which habit are you continuing even though you can already see its bill arriving?

translations.hi: सुख मानकर देह-भोग किया जाता है; पीछे — हाय — शरीर में रोग। यद्यपि इस लोक में अन्ततः मरण ही सबकी शरण है, फिर भी मनुष्य पाप का आचरण नहीं छोड़ता।

devanagari: अर्थमनर्थं भावय नित्यं / नास्तिततः सुखलेशः सत्यम् । / पुत्रादपि धनभाजां भीतिः / सर्वत्रैषा विहिता रीतिः ॥29॥
iast: arthamanarthaṃ bhāvaya nityaṃ / nāsti tataḥ sukhaleśaḥ satyam । / putrādapi dhanabhājāṃ bhītiḥ / sarvatraiṣā vihitā rītiḥ ॥29॥
sayIt: AR-tham a-NAR-thum BHAA-va-ya NIT-yum / NAAS-ti TA-tah su-kha-LAY-shah SAT-yum / put-RAA-da-pi DHA-na-BHAA-jaam BHEE-tih / sar-vat-RAI-shaa VI-hi-taa REE-tih
translation: See wealth for the misfortune it is, and hold that thought daily; the truth is that not a sliver of happiness comes from it. Those who hold riches fear even their own son — everywhere, this is the settled way of things.
source: Bhaja Govindam 29 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: What do you own that has quietly turned from something you use into something you guard?

translations.hi: धन को अनर्थ जानकर नित्य विचार करो; सच यह है कि उससे सुख का लेश भी नहीं मिलता। धनवानों को अपने पुत्र तक से भय रहता है — सर्वत्र यही रीति चली आई है।

devanagari: प्राणायामं प्रत्याहारं / नित्यानित्य विवेकविचारम् । / जाप्यसमेतसमाधिविधानं / कुर्ववधानं महदवधानम् ॥30॥
iast: prāṇāyāmaṃ pratyāhāraṃ / nityānitya vivekavicāram । / jāpyasametasamādhividhānaṃ / kurvavadhānaṃ mahadavadhānam ॥30॥
sayIt: praa-naa-YAA-mum prat-YAA-haa-rum / nit-YAA-NIT-ya vi-VAY-ka-vi-CHAA-rum / JAAP-ya-sa-MAY-ta-sa-MAA-dhi-vi-DHAA-num / KUR-va-va-DHAA-num MA-ha-da-va-DHAA-num
translation: Regulation of the breath, the drawing-in of the senses, the discerning inquiry into what lasts and what passes, japa, and the discipline of absorption joined with it — practise these with attention, with the greatest attention.
source: Bhaja Govindam 30 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Which part of your practice gets your full attention, and which gets only your leftover minutes?

translations.hi: प्राणायाम, प्रत्याहार, नित्य और अनित्य का विवेक-विचार, जप सहित समाधि का विधान — इनका अभ्यास सावधानी से करो, बड़ी सावधानी से।

devanagari: गुरुचरणाम्बुजनिर्भरभक्तः / संसारादचिराद्भव मुक्तः । / सेन्द्रियमानसनियमादेवं / द्रक्ष्यसि निजहृदयस्थं देवम् ॥31॥
iast: gurucaraṇāmbujanirbharabhaktaḥ / saṃsārādacirādbhava muktaḥ । / sendriyamānasaniyamādevaṃ / drakṣyasi nijahṛdayasthaṃ devam ॥31॥
sayIt: gu-ru-cha-ra-NAAM-bu-ja-NIR-bha-ra-BHAK-tah / sam-saa-RAAD a-chi-RAAD BHA-va MUK-tah / SEN-dri-ya-MAA-na-sa-NI-ya-MAA-day-vum / DRAK-shya-si NI-ja-hri-da-YAS-thum DAY-vum
translation: Rest your devotion wholly on the lotus feet of the guru, and be free of saṃsāra before long. With the senses and the mind reined in this way, you will see the God who dwells in your own heart.
source: Bhaja Govindam 31 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: Where in your life do you accept guidance completely — and what does that trust make possible that willpower alone never did?

translations.hi: गुरु के चरण-कमलों में अनन्य भक्ति रखो, और शीघ्र ही संसार से मुक्त हो जाओ। इस प्रकार इन्द्रियों और मन के संयम से, तुम अपने ही हृदय में विराजमान देव के दर्शन करोगे।

devanagari: मूढः कश्चन वैयाकरणो / डुःकृङ्करणाध्ययनधुरीणः । / श्रीमच्छङ्करभगवच्छिष्यै / र्बोधित आसीच्छोधितकरणः ॥32॥
iast: mūḍhaḥ kaścana vaiyākaraṇo / ḍuḥkṛṅkaraṇādhyayanadhurīṇaḥ । / śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavacchiṣyai / rbodhita āsīcchodhitakaraṇaḥ ॥32॥
sayIt: MOO-dhah KASH-cha-na vai-YAA-ka-ra-no / duh-krin-KA-ra-NAADH-ya-ya-na-dhu-REE-nah / SHREE-mach-CHUNG-ka-ra-BHA-ga-vach-CHISH-yair / BO-dhi-ta aa-SEECH-cho-dhi-ta-KA-ra-nah
translation: A certain deluded grammarian, harnessed like a draught-ox to his drills on "ḍukṛñ karaṇe", was awakened by the disciples of the revered Shankara — and his faculties were made clean.
source: Bhaja Govindam 32 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: What are you diligently perfecting that might be the wrong thing to perfect?

translations.hi: कोई मोहग्रस्त वैयाकरण, "डुकृञ् करणे" की रटन्त में बैल-सा जुता हुआ, पूज्य शंकर भगवान के शिष्यों द्वारा प्रबोधित हुआ — और उसकी बुद्धि-इन्द्रियाँ शुद्ध हो गईं।

devanagari: भज गोविन्दं भज गोविन्दं / गोविन्दं भज मूढमते । / नामस्मरणादन्यमुपायं / नहि पश्यामो भवाब्धितरणे ॥33॥
iast: bhaja govindaṃ bhaja govindaṃ / govindaṃ bhaja mūḍhamate । / nāmasmaraṇādanyamupāyaṃ / nahi paśyāmo bhavābdhitaraṇe ॥33॥
sayIt: BHA-ja go-VIN-dum BHA-ja go-VIN-dum / go-VIN-dum BHA-ja MOO-dha-ma-tay / NAA-ma-sma-ra-NAAD AN-yam u-PAA-yum / na-hi pash-YAA-mo bha-VAAB-dhi-TA-ra-nay
translation: Sing to Govinda, sing to Govinda, sing to Govinda, you deluded mind. Other than remembrance of the Name, we see no means at all for crossing the ocean of becoming.
source: Bhaja Govindam 33 (attributed to Adi Shankaracharya and his disciples), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_vishhnu/bhajagovindam.itx
reflection: If you could keep only one practice — one name, one remembering — what would it be?

translations.hi: गोविन्द को भजो, गोविन्द को भजो, हे मोहग्रस्त बुद्धि, गोविन्द को भजो। नाम-स्मरण के सिवा भवसागर पार करने का कोई और उपाय हमें नहीं दिखता।

devanagari: जय हनुमान ज्ञान गुन सागर । / जय कपीस तिहुँ लोक उजागर
iast: jaya hanumāna jñāna guna sāgara । / jaya kapīsa tihum̐ loka ujāgara
sayIt: JA-ya ha-nu-MAA-na GYAA-na GU-na SAA-ga-ra / JA-ya ka-PEE-sa ti-HOON LO-ka u-JAA-ga-ra
translation: Victory to Hanuman, ocean of wisdom and virtue; victory to the lord of the monkeys, who lights up the three worlds.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 1, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: If someone hailed you today, would you rather it be for your strength or your character — and why?

translations.hi: हनुमान की जय, जो ज्ञान और गुणों के सागर हैं; कपियों के स्वामी की जय, जो तीनों लोकों को उजागर करते हैं।

devanagari: राम दूत अतुलित बल धामा । / अंजनिपुत्र पवनसुत नामा
iast: rāma dūta atulita bala dhāmā । / aṃjaniputra pavanasuta nāmā
sayIt: RAA-ma DOO-ta a-TU-li-ta BA-la DHAA-maa / an-ja-ni-PU-tra pa-va-na-SU-ta NAA-maa
translation: Messenger of Rama, abode of immeasurable strength; you are known as Anjani's son and the Son of the Wind.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 2, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Whose work gives your own strength its purpose?

translations.hi: आप राम के दूत और अतुलनीय बल के धाम हैं; अंजनी-पुत्र और पवनसुत — इन्हीं नामों से आप जाने जाते हैं।

devanagari: महाबीर बिक्रम बजरंगी । / कुमति निवार सुमति के संगी
iast: mahābīra bikrama bajaraṃgī । / kumati nivāra sumati ke saṃgī
sayIt: ma-haa-BEE-ra BI-kra-ma ba-ja-RUN-gee / KU-ma-ti ni-VAA-ra SU-ma-ti kay SUN-gee
translation: Great hero, mighty in valour, with limbs strong as the thunderbolt; you drive away wrong thinking and are the companion of good sense.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 3, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Which crooked thought would you most like driven out today, and what good sense could take its place?

translations.hi: आप महावीर हैं, पराक्रमी हैं, वज्र-जैसे अंगों वाले बजरंगी हैं; आप कुबुद्धि को दूर करते हैं और सुबुद्धि के साथी हैं।

devanagari: कंचन बरन बिराज सुबेसा । / कानन कुंडल कुंचित केसा
iast: kaṃcana barana birāja subesā । / kānana kuṃḍala kuṃcita kesā
sayIt: KUN-cha-na BA-ra-na bi-RAA-ja su-BAY-saa / KAA-na-na KUN-da-la KUN-chi-ta KAY-saa
translation: Golden-hued, you shine in beautiful attire, with earrings in your ears and curling hair.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 4, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: When you close your eyes to pray or reflect, what image actually holds your attention?

translations.hi: आपका रंग सोने-जैसा है, आप सुंदर वेश में सुशोभित हैं; कानों में कुंडल हैं और बाल घुँघराले हैं।

devanagari: हाथ बज्र औ ध्वजा बिराजै । / काँधे मूँज जनेऊ साजै
iast: hātha bajra au dhvajā birājai । / kām̐dhe mūm̐ja janeū sājai
sayIt: HAA-tha BUJ-ra au dhva-JAA bi-RAA-jai / KAAN-dhay MOON-ja ja-nay-OO SAA-jai
translation: In your hands shine the vajra-mace and the banner; the sacred thread of munja grass adorns your shoulder.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 5, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: What are the visible signs in your life of what you have committed yourself to?

translations.hi: आपके हाथों में वज्र (गदा) और ध्वजा शोभा देते हैं; कंधे पर मूँज का जनेऊ सजा है।

devanagari: संकर सुवन केसरीनंदन । / तेज प्रताप महा जग बंदन
iast: saṃkara suvana kesarīnaṃdana । / teja pratāpa mahā jaga baṃdana
sayIt: SUN-ka-ra SU-va-na kay-sa-ree-NUN-da-na / TAY-ja pra-TAA-pa ma-HAA JA-ga BUN-da-na
translation: Son of Shankara, delight of Kesari; your radiance and majesty are great, and the whole world venerates you.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 6, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Which of your roots — family or beyond — most explains the strength you carry?

translations.hi: आप शंकर के सुवन और केसरी के नंदन हैं; आपका तेज और प्रताप महान है, सारा जगत आपकी वंदना करता है।

devanagari: विद्यावान गुनी अति चातुर । / राम काज करिबे को आतुर
iast: vidyāvāna gunī ati cātura । / rāma kāja karibe ko ātura
sayIt: vid-yaa-VAA-na gu-NEE A-ti CHAA-tu-ra / RAA-ma KAA-ja ka-ri-BAY ko AA-tu-ra
translation: Learned, virtuous, supremely clever — and ever eager to do Rama's work.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 7, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Your skills are real — but whose work are they eager to do?

translations.hi: आप विद्यावान हैं, गुणी हैं, अत्यंत चतुर हैं — और राम का काम करने के लिए सदा आतुर रहते हैं।

devanagari: प्रभु चरित्र सुनिबे को रसिया । / राम लखन सीता मन बसिया
iast: prabhu caritra sunibe ko rasiyā । / rāma lakhana sītā mana basiyā
sayIt: PRA-bhu cha-RI-tra su-ni-BAY ko ra-si-YAA / RAA-ma LA-kha-na SEE-taa MA-na ba-si-YAA
translation: You delight in hearing the Lord's story; Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita dwell in your heart.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 8, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: What do you most love listening to — and is it something you would want living in your heart?

translations.hi: आप प्रभु की कथा सुनने के रसिया हैं; राम, लखन और सीता आपके मन में बसते हैं।

devanagari: सूक्ष्म रूप धरि सियहिं दिखावा । / बिकट रूप धरि लंक जरावा
iast: sūkṣma rūpa dhari siyahiṃ dikhāvā । / bikaṭa rūpa dhari laṃka jarāvā
sayIt: SOOK-shma ROO-pa DHA-ri si-ya-HIN di-KHAA-vaa / BI-ka-ta ROO-pa DHA-ri LUN-ka ja-RAA-vaa
translation: Taking a minute form, you appeared before Sita; taking a fearsome form, you burned Lanka.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 9, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Does today call for your smallest, gentlest self or your fiercest one — and can you tell the difference?

translations.hi: सूक्ष्म रूप धारण करके आपने सीता को दर्शन दिया; विकट रूप धारण करके लंका जला दी।

devanagari: भीम रूप धरि असुर सँहारे । / रामचंद्र के काज सँवारे
iast: bhīma rūpa dhari asura sam̐hāre । / rāmacaṃdra ke kāja sam̐vāre
sayIt: BHEE-ma ROO-pa DHA-ri A-su-ra sun-HAA-ray / raa-ma-CHUN-dra kay KAA-ja sun-VAA-ray
translation: Taking a colossal form, you destroyed the demons and brought Ramachandra's tasks to completion.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 10, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: When you finish something difficult today, will it be left truly set in order — and for whom?

translations.hi: भीम रूप धारण करके आपने असुरों का संहार किया और रामचंद्र के काज सँवारे।

devanagari: लाय सजीवन लखन जियाये । / श्रीरघुबीर हरषि उर लाये
iast: lāya sajīvana lakhana jiyāye । / śrīraghubīra haraṣi ura lāye
sayIt: LAA-ya sa-JEE-va-na LA-kha-na ji-YAA-yay / shree-ra-ghu-BEE-ra HA-ra-shi U-ra LAA-yay
translation: You brought the sanjivani herb and restored Lakshmana to life; overjoyed, Sri Raghubira clasped you to his heart.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 11, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Who in your life would you cross a mountain for tonight, without being asked twice?

translations.hi: आप संजीवनी लाए और लखन को जिला दिया; श्रीरघुवीर ने हर्षित होकर आपको हृदय से लगा लिया।

devanagari: रघुपति कीन्ही बहुत बड़ाई । / तुम मम प्रिय भरतहि सम भाई
iast: raghupati kīnhī bahuta baṛāī । / tuma mama priya bharatahi sama bhāī
sayIt: ra-ghu-PA-ti KEEN-hee ba-HU-ta ba-DAA-ee / TU-ma MA-ma PRI-ya bha-ra-ta-hi SA-ma BHAA-ee
translation: Raghupati praised you greatly: "You are as dear to me as my brother Bharata."
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 12, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Whose faithful presence in your life deserves to be named family out loud?

translations.hi: रघुपति ने आपकी बहुत बड़ाई की: "तुम मुझे भरत के समान प्रिय भाई हो।"

devanagari: सहस बदन तुम्हरो जस गावैं । / अस कहि श्रीपति कंठ लगावैं
iast: sahasa badana tumharo jasa gāvaiṃ । / asa kahi śrīpati kaṃṭha lagāvaiṃ
sayIt: SA-ha-sa BA-da-na TUM-ha-ro JA-sa GAA-vain / A-sa KA-hi SHREE-pa-ti KUN-tha la-GAA-vain
translation: "May the thousand-mouthed serpent sing your glory" — so saying, the Lord of Shri drew you into his embrace.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 13, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: When words run out, what simple gesture could carry your gratitude instead?

translations.hi: "सहस्र मुखों वाला शेष तुम्हारा यश गाए" — ऐसा कहकर श्रीपति (राम) आपको कंठ से लगा लेते हैं।

devanagari: सनकादिक ब्रह्मादि मुनीसा । / नारद सारद सहित अहीसा
iast: sanakādika brahmādi munīsā । / nārada sārada sahita ahīsā
sayIt: sa-na-KAA-di-ka brah-MAA-di mu-NEE-saa / NAA-ra-da SAA-ra-da SA-hi-ta a-HEE-saa
translation: Sanaka and the sages, Brahma and the lords among ascetics, Narada, Sharada, and the king of serpents — all sing your praise.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 14, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Have you ever admired something so much that describing it felt impossible — and what did you do then?

translations.hi: सनक आदि ऋषि, ब्रह्मा आदि मुनीश्वर, नारद, शारदा (सरस्वती) और शेषनाग — सभी आपका यश गाते हैं।

devanagari: जम कुबेर दिगपाल जहाँ ते । / कबि कोबिद कहि सके कहाँ ते
iast: jama kubera digapāla jahām̐ te । / kabi kobida kahi sake kahām̐ te
sayIt: JA-ma ku-BAY-ra di-ga-PAA-la ja-HAAN tay / KA-bi KO-bi-da KA-hi SA-kay ka-HAAN tay
translation: Where even Yama, Kubera, and the guardians of the quarters fall short, from where could poets and scholars tell your glory in full?
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 15, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Is there love in your life you have stopped trying to put into words — and is that a loss or an offering?

translations.hi: यम, कुबेर और दिक्पाल जहाँ आपका यश नहीं कह पाते, वहाँ कवि और विद्वान उसे कहाँ से कह सकते हैं?

devanagari: तुम उपकार सुग्रीवहिं कीन्हा । / राम मिलाय राज पद दीन्हा
iast: tuma upakāra sugrīvahiṃ kīnhā । / rāma milāya rāja pada dīnhā
sayIt: TU-ma u-pa-KAA-ra su-gree-va-HIN KEEN-haa / RAA-ma mi-LAA-ya RAA-ja PA-da DEEN-haa
translation: You did Sugriva a great kindness: you brought him to Rama and restored him to his royal throne.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 16, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Who around you needs not your rescue but one honest introduction you could make?

translations.hi: आपने सुग्रीव पर उपकार किया: उन्हें राम से मिलाया और राज-पद दिलाया।

devanagari: तुम्हरो मंत्र बिभीषन माना । / लंकेस्वर भए सब जग जाना
iast: tumharo maṃtra bibhīṣana mānā । / laṃkesvara bhae saba jaga jānā
sayIt: TUM-ha-ro MUN-tra bi-BHEE-sha-na MAA-naa / lun-KAYS-va-ra BHA-ay SA-ba JA-ga JAA-naa
translation: Vibhishana followed your counsel and became lord of Lanka — the whole world knows it.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 17, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Is your advice trustworthy enough that someone could rebuild a life on it?

translations.hi: आपकी मंत्रणा विभीषण ने मानी और वे लंकेश्वर बने — यह सारा जग जानता है।

devanagari: जुग सहस्र जोजन पर भानू । / लील्यो ताहि मधुर फल जानू
iast: juga sahasra jojana para bhānū । / līlyo tāhi madhura phala jānū
sayIt: JU-ga sa-HAS-ra JO-ja-na PA-ra BHAA-noo / LEE-lyo TAA-hi MA-dhu-ra PHA-la JAA-noo
translation: The sun, thousands upon thousands of yojanas away — you swallowed it, taking it for a sweet fruit.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 18, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: What have you filed under "impossible" that a bolder younger you would simply have leapt for?

translations.hi: सहस्रों योजन दूर स्थित सूर्य को आपने मीठा फल समझकर निगल लिया।

devanagari: प्रभु मुद्रिका मेलि मुख माहीं । / जलधि लाँघि गये अचरज नाहीं
iast: prabhu mudrikā meli mukha māhīṃ । / jaladhi lām̐ghi gaye acaraja nāhīṃ
sayIt: PRA-bhu mu-DRI-kaa MAY-li MU-kha maa-HEEN / ja-la-DHI LAAN-ghi GA-yay a-cha-RA-ja naa-HEEN
translation: Placing the Lord's ring in your mouth, you leapt across the ocean — and no wonder in that.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 19, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: What token of trust do you carry that could make your own ocean feel crossable?

translations.hi: प्रभु की मुद्रिका मुख में रखकर आप समुद्र लाँघ गए — इसमें कोई अचरज नहीं।

devanagari: दुर्गम काज जगत के जेते । / सुगम अनुग्रह तुम्हरे तेते
iast: durgama kāja jagata ke jete । / sugama anugraha tumhare tete
sayIt: DUR-ga-ma KAA-ja ja-GA-ta kay JAY-tay / SU-ga-ma a-nu-GRA-ha tum-HA-ray TAY-tay
translation: However many impossible tasks there are in the world, by your grace that many become easy.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 20, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: Which task feels impassable today — and how would you approach it if you trusted it could become simple?

translations.hi: जगत में जितने भी दुर्गम काज हैं, आपके अनुग्रह से वे सब सुगम हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: राम दुआरे तुम रखवारे । / होत न आज्ञा बिनु पैसारे
iast: rāma duāre tuma rakhavāre । / hota na ājñā binu paisāre
sayIt: RAA-ma du-AA-ray tum rakh-WAA-ray / HO-ta na AAG-yaa BI-nu pai-SAA-ray
translation: You are the guardian at Rama's door; without your permission no one gains entry.
source: Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 21, Tulsidas (Awadhi, public domain original), via sanskritdocuments.org, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_hanumaana/hanuman40.itx
reflection: What door in your life deserves a faithful guardian rather than a forced entry?

translations.hi: राम के द्वार पर तुम रखवाले हो; तुम्हारी आज्ञा के बिना किसी का प्रवेश नहीं होता।

devanagari: सब सुख लहै तुम्हारी सरना । / तुम रच्छक काहू को डर ना
