reflection: When did you last prove you had truly listened by saying it back?

translations.hi: यम ने उसे वह अग्नि बताई जो लोकों का आदि है — कौन-सी ईंटें, कितनी, और किस क्रम से। और नचिकेता ने जो सुना था, ठीक वैसा ही दोहरा दिया। तब प्रसन्न होकर मृत्यु ने फिर कहा।

devanagari: तमब्रवीत् प्रीयमाणो महात्मा / वरं तवेहाद्य ददामि भूयः । / तवैव नाम्ना भविताऽयमग्निः / सृङ्कां चेमामनेकरूपां गृहाण ॥1.1.16॥
iast: tamabravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā / varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ । / tavaiva nāmnā bhavitā'yamagniḥ / sṛṅkāṃ cemāmanekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa ॥1.1.16॥
sayIt: tum ab-ra-VEET pree-ya-MAA-no ma-HAAT-maa / VA-rum ta-VAY-haad-ya da-DAA-mi BHOO-yah / ta-VY-va NAAM-naa bha-vi-TAA-yum AG-nih / srin-KAAM chay-MAAM a-nay-ka-ROO-paam gri-HAA-na
translation: Pleased with him, the great soul said: "I give you a further boon here today — this fire shall be known by your name alone. And take this many-formed garland as well."
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What have you learned carefully enough that you could teach it back without losing anything?

translations.hi: प्रसन्न होकर उस महात्मा ने कहा: "आज यहीं मैं तुम्हें एक और वर देता हूँ — यह अग्नि अब तुम्हारे ही नाम से जानी जाएगी। और यह अनेक रूपों वाली माला भी स्वीकार करो।"

devanagari: त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रिभिरेत्य सन्धिं / त्रिकर्मकृत्तरति जन्ममृत्यू । / ब्रह्मजज्ञं देवमीड्यं विदित्वा / निचाय्येमाँ शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥1.1.17॥
iast: triṇāciketastribhiretya sandhiṃ / trikarmakṛttarati janmamṛtyū । / brahmajajñaṃ devamīḍyaṃ viditvā / nicāyyemām̐ śāntimatyantameti ॥1.1.17॥
sayIt: tri-NAA-chi-kay-tus TRI-bhir AYT-ya SUN-dhim / tri-KAR-ma-krit TA-ra-ti jun-ma-mrit-YOO / brah-ma-ja-GYUM day-vum EED-yum vi-dit-VAA / ni-CHAAY-yay-MAAM SHAAN-tim ut-YUN-tum AY-ti
translation: Whoever kindles the Nachiketa fire three times, joined with the three, doing the threefold work, crosses over birth and death; knowing the praiseworthy, radiant knower born of Brahman, and beholding him closely, one attains this unending peace.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which practice in your life do you understand but not yet do — or do but not yet understand?

translations.hi: जो नाचिकेत अग्नि को तीन बार प्रज्वलित करता है, तीनों से जुड़कर तीन कर्म करता है, वह जन्म-मृत्यु के पार जाता है; ब्रह्म से उत्पन्न, स्तुति-योग्य, प्रकाशमान ज्ञाता को जानकर और भीतर निकट से देखकर वह इस अनंत शांति को पा लेता है।

devanagari: त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रयमेतद्विदित्वा / य एवं विद्वाँश्चिनुते नाचिकेतम् । / स मृत्युपाशान् पुरतः प्रणोद्य / शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके ॥1.1.18॥
iast: triṇāciketastrayametadviditvā / ya evaṃ vidvām̐ścinute nāciketam । / sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya / śokātigo modate svargaloke ॥1.1.18॥
sayIt: tri-NAA-chi-kay-tus TRA-yum AY-tud vi-dit-VAA / ya AY-vum vid-VAAMSH-chi-noo-tay NAA-chi-kay-tum / sa mrit-yoo-PAA-shaan poo-ra-TAH pra-NOD-ya / sho-KAA-ti-go MO-da-tay svar-ga-LO-kay
translation: The one who knows this triad and, so knowing, piles up the Nachiketa fire, throws off the snares of death even beforehand and, gone beyond sorrow, rejoices in the heavenly world.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.18, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which snare — craving, aversion, or an old habit — loosens a little the moment you name it?

translations.hi: जो इस त्रयी को जानकर, इसी ज्ञान के साथ नाचिकेत अग्नि का चयन करता है, वह अंत आने से पहले ही मृत्यु के पाशों को झटक देता है और शोक के पार जाकर स्वर्गलोक में आनंदित होता है।

devanagari: एष तेऽग्निर्नचिकेतः स्वर्ग्यो / यमवृणीथा द्वितीयेन वरेण । / एतमग्निं तवैव प्रवक्ष्यन्ति जनासः / तृतीयं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व ॥1.1.19॥
iast: eṣa te'gnirnaciketaḥ svargyo / yamavṛṇīthā dvitīyena vareṇa । / etamagniṃ tavaiva pravakṣyanti janāsaḥ / tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva ॥1.1.19॥
sayIt: AY-sha TAY-gnir na-chi-KAY-tah SVAR-gyo / yum a-vri-NEE-thaa dvi-TEE-yay-na va-RAY-na / AY-tum ug-NIM ta-VYE-va pra-VAKSH-yan-ti ja-NAA-sah / tri-TEE-yum va-RUM na-chi-KAY-to vri-NEESH-va
translation: This, Nachiketa, is your heaven-winning fire, which you chose with your second boon. People in time to come will call this fire yours alone. Now choose your third boon, Nachiketa.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If one question of yours were guaranteed a true answer, which would you actually ask?

translations.hi: नचिकेता, यह रही तुम्हारी स्वर्ग तक ले जाने वाली अग्नि, जो तुमने दूसरे वर से माँगी थी। आने वाले लोग इस अग्नि को तुम्हारे ही नाम से पुकारेंगे। अब, नचिकेता, तीसरा वर माँगो।

devanagari: येयं प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्ये- / ऽस्तीत्येके नायमस्तीति चैके । / एतद्विद्यामनुशिष्टस्त्वयाऽहं / वराणामेष वरस्तृतीयः ॥1.1.20॥
iast: yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye- / 'stītyeke nāyamastīti caike । / etadvidyāmanuśiṣṭastvayā'haṃ / varāṇāmeṣa varastṛtīyaḥ ॥1.1.20॥
sayIt: YAY-yum PRAY-tay vi-chi-kit-SAA ma-NOOSH-yay / steet-YAY-kay NAA-yum as-TEE-ti CHYE-kay / AY-tud-vid-YAAM a-noo-SHISH-tas tva-YAA-hum / va-RAA-naam AY-sha va-RAS tri-TEE-yah
translation: There is this doubt about a man who has died: some say "he still is," and others, "he is not." I would know this, taught by you. Of all the boons, this is the third.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.20, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which question do you keep postponing because easier questions are always available?

translations.hi: मरे हुए मनुष्य के बारे में जो यह संदेह है — कुछ कहते हैं "वह रहता है", कुछ कहते हैं "नहीं रहता" — आपसे शिक्षा पाकर मैं यही जानना चाहता हूँ। वरों में यह तीसरा वर है।

devanagari: देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं पुरा / न हि सुविज्ञेयमणुरेष धर्मः । / अन्यं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व / मा मोपरोत्सीरति मा सृजैनम् ॥1.1.21॥
iast: devairatrāpi vicikitsitaṃ purā / na hi suvijñeyamaṇureṣa dharmaḥ । / anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva / mā moparotsīrati mā sṛjainam ॥1.1.21॥
sayIt: day-VYE-rut-RAA-pi vi-chi-kit-si-TUM poo-RAA / na hi soo-vig-YAY-yum a-NOOR AY-sha DHAR-mah / UN-yum va-RUM na-chi-KAY-to vri-NEESH-va / maa MO-pa-ROT-seer A-ti maa sri-JYE-num
translation: Even the gods, long ago, had doubts about this — it is not easy to understand, so subtle is this truth. Choose another boon, Nachiketa. Do not hold me to this; release me from it.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.21, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When someone calls a truth too subtle for you, how do you decide whether to defer or to persist?

translations.hi: इस विषय में तो देवताओं को भी पहले संदेह रहा है; यह सहज में समझ नहीं आता — यह धर्म अत्यंत सूक्ष्म है। नचिकेता, कोई और वर माँग लो। मुझ पर दबाव मत डालो; इस वर से मुझे छोड़ दो।

devanagari: देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं किल / त्वं च मृत्यो यन्न सुज्ञेयमात्थ । / वक्ता चास्य त्वादृगन्यो न लभ्यो / नान्यो वरस्तुल्य एतस्य कश्चित् ॥1.1.22॥
iast: devairatrāpi vicikitsitaṃ kila / tvaṃ ca mṛtyo yanna sujñeyamāttha । / vaktā cāsya tvādṛganyo na labhyo / nānyo varastulya etasya kaścit ॥1.1.22॥
sayIt: day-VYE-rut-RAA-pi vi-chi-kit-si-TUM KI-la / tvum cha MRIT-yo yun na soog-YAY-yum AAT-tha / vak-TAA CHAAS-ya TVAA-drig UN-yo na LUB-hyo / NAAN-yo va-RAS TOOL-ya ay-TAS-ya KASH-chit
translation: Even the gods, you say, had doubts here — and you, O Death, say it is not easily known. But no other teacher of this can be found who is your equal, and no other boon is equal to this one at all.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.22, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When you finally stand before someone who truly knows, do you soften your question or sharpen it?

translations.hi: आप ही कहते हैं कि देवताओं तक को इसमें संदेह रहा, और हे मृत्यु, आप ही कहते हैं कि यह सहज में जाना नहीं जाता। पर इसे बताने वाला आप-जैसा दूसरा कोई मिल नहीं सकता, और इस वर के बराबर दूसरा कोई वर है ही नहीं।

devanagari: शतायुषः पुत्रपौत्रान्वृणीष्वा / बहून्पशून् हस्तिहिरण्यमश्वान् । / भूमेर्महदायतनं वृणीष्व / स्वयं च जीव शरदो यावदिच्छसि ॥1.1.23॥
iast: śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrānvṛṇīṣvā / bahūnpaśūn hastihiraṇyamaśvān । / bhūmermahadāyatanaṃ vṛṇīṣva / svayaṃ ca jīva śarado yāvadicchasi ॥1.1.23॥
sayIt: sha-TAA-yoo-shah POO-tra-pow-TRAAN vri-NEESH-vaa / ba-HOON pa-SHOON HAS-ti-hi-RUN-yum ash-VAAN / BHOO-mayr ma-ha-DAA-ya-ta-num vri-NEESH-va / sva-YUM cha JEE-va sha-ra-DO YAA-va-DICH-cha-si
translation: Choose sons and grandsons who will live a hundred years; choose herds of cattle, elephants, gold, and horses. Choose a vast expanse of earth, and yourself live as many autumns as you wish.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.23, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If you were offered everything except the answer, would you notice what was missing?

translations.hi: सौ-सौ वर्ष जीने वाले पुत्र-पौत्र माँग लो; ढेरों पशु, हाथी, सोना और घोड़े माँग लो। धरती का विशाल विस्तार माँग लो, और स्वयं जितनी शरदें चाहो, जी लो।

devanagari: एतत्तुल्यं यदि मन्यसे वरं / वृणीष्व वित्तं चिरजीविकां च । / महाभूमौ नचिकेतस्त्वमेधि / कामानां त्वा कामभाजं करोमि ॥1.1.24॥
iast: etattulyaṃ yadi manyase varaṃ / vṛṇīṣva vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca । / mahābhūmau naciketastvamedhi / kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi ॥1.1.24॥
sayIt: AY-tut-TOOL-yum YA-di MUN-ya-say va-RUM / vri-NEESH-va VIT-tum chi-ra-JEE-vi-kaam cha / ma-HAA-BHOO-mow na-chi-KAY-tas tvum AY-dhi / kaa-MAA-naam tvaa KAA-ma-BHAA-jum ka-RO-mi
translation: If you think any boon equal to that one, choose wealth and long life. Be a king, Nachiketa, over the wide earth — and I will make you the enjoyer of every desire.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.24, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which of your desires would still feel worth having the day after it was granted?

translations.hi: अगर इसके बराबर कोई और वर लगे, तो धन और लंबा जीवन माँग लो। विशाल पृथ्वी पर राजा बनो, नचिकेता — मैं तुम्हें हर कामना का भोक्ता बना दूँगा।

devanagari: ये ये कामा दुर्लभा मर्त्यलोके / सर्वान् कामाँश्छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व । / इमा रामाः सरथाः सतूर्या / न हीदृशा लम्भनीया मनुष्यैः । / आभिर्मत्प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व / नचिकेतो मरणं माऽनुप्राक्षीः ॥1.1.25॥
iast: ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke / sarvān kāmām̐śchandataḥ prārthayasva । / imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā / na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ । / ābhirmatprattābhiḥ paricārayasva / naciketo maraṇaṃ mā'nuprākṣīḥ ॥1.1.25॥
sayIt: yay yay kaa-MAA door-la-BHAA MART-ya-LO-kay / sar-VAAN kaa-MAANSH chun-da-TAH PRAAR-tha-yas-va / i-MAA raa-MAAH sa-ra-THAAH sa-TOOR-yaa / na HEE-dri-shaa lum-bha-NEE-yaa ma-noosh-YIGH / AA-bhir mat-prat-TAA-bhih pa-ri-CHAA-ra-yas-va / na-chi-KAY-to ma-ra-NUM MAA-noo-PRAAK-sheeh
translation: Whatever desires are hard to win in the mortal world — ask for them all at your pleasure. These lovely women with their chariots and their music — the like of them no mortal can win. I give them; let them attend you. But Nachiketa — do not ask me about dying.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.25, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What is being offered to you right now chiefly to keep you from asking something?

translations.hi: मर्त्यलोक में जो-जो कामनाएँ दुर्लभ हैं, वे सब इच्छा भर माँग लो। ये रथों और वाद्यों समेत सुंदरियाँ — ऐसी मनुष्यों को मिल ही नहीं सकतीं। मैं इन्हें देता हूँ; इनसे सेवा करा लो। पर नचिकेता — मृत्यु के बारे में मत पूछो।

devanagari: श्वोभावा मर्त्यस्य यदन्तकैतत् / सर्वेंद्रियाणां जरयंति तेजः । / अपि सर्वं जीवितमल्पमेव / तवैव वाहास्तव नृत्यगीते ॥1.1.26॥
iast: śvobhāvā martyasya yadantakaitat / sarveṃdriyāṇāṃ jarayaṃti tejaḥ । / api sarvaṃ jīvitamalpameva / tavaiva vāhāstava nṛtyagīte ॥1.1.26॥
sayIt: SHVO-bhaa-vaa MART-yas-ya ya-dun-ta-KYE-tat / sar-VAYN-dri-yaa-naam ja-ra-YUN-ti TAY-jah / A-pi SAR-vum JEE-vi-tum AL-pa-MAY-va / ta-VYE-va vaa-HAAS ta-va NRIT-ya-GEE-tay
translation: Things of a day, O Ender! They wear out the fire of all a mortal's senses. And even the whole of a life is brief. Keep your chariots for yourself; keep your dance and song.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.26, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which pleasure in your life is quietly wearing out the very capacity it depends on?

translations.hi: हे अंतक, ये सब तो कल तक की चीज़ें हैं! ये मरणशील मनुष्य की सारी इंद्रियों का तेज घिस डालती हैं। और तो और, पूरा जीवन भी थोड़ा ही है। रथ आपके पास ही रहें; नृत्य और गीत भी आपके ही।

devanagari: न वित्तेन तर्पणीयो मनुष्यो / लप्स्यामहे वित्तमद्राक्ष्म चेत्त्वा । / जीविष्यामो यावदीशिष्यसि त्वं / वरस्तु मे वरणीयः स एव ॥1.1.27॥
iast: na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo / lapsyāmahe vittamadrākṣma cettvā । / jīviṣyāmo yāvadīśiṣyasi tvaṃ / varastu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva ॥1.1.27॥
sayIt: na vit-TAY-na tar-pa-NEE-yo ma-NOOSH-yo / lap-SYAA-ma-hay VIT-tum ad-RAAKSH-ma chayt tvaa / jee-vish-YAA-mo YAA-va-DEE-shish-ya-si tvum / va-RAS too may va-ra-NEE-yah sa AY-va
translation: No human being can ever be satisfied by wealth. And now that we have seen you, wealth will come to us anyway; we will live only as long as you decree. The boon worth choosing is still that one alone.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.27, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What amount, named honestly, would finally be enough for you — and what does your answer reveal?

translations.hi: मनुष्य धन से कभी तृप्त नहीं होता। और अब जब आपके दर्शन हो गए, तो धन तो मिल ही जाएगा; जिएँगे भी उतना ही, जितना आप ठहराएँगे। इसलिए माँगने योग्य वर तो वही एक है।

devanagari: अजीर्यताममृतानामुपेत्य / जीर्यन्मर्त्यः क्वधःस्थः प्रजानन् । / अभिध्यायन् वर्णरतिप्रमोदान् / अतिदीर्घे जीविते को रमेत ॥1.1.28॥
iast: ajīryatāmamṛtānāmupetya / jīryanmartyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan । / abhidhyāyan varṇaratipramodān / atidīrghe jīvite ko rameta ॥1.1.28॥
sayIt: a-jeer-ya-TAAM a-mri-TAA-naam oo-PAYT-ya / JEER-yun MART-yah kva-DHAH-sthah pra-JAA-nun / a-bhi-DHYAA-yun VAR-na-RA-ti-pra-mo-DAAN / a-ti-DEER-ghay JEE-vi-tay ko ra-MAY-ta
translation: Having come into the presence of the unaging immortals, what aging mortal down here on earth, who understands — who has weighed the pleasures of beauty and delight — could take joy in an over-long life?
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.28, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If you were granted more time, what question would still be waiting for you at the end of it?

translations.hi: अजर अमरों के पास पहुँचकर, नीचे धरती पर रहने वाला कौन-सा बूढ़ा होता हुआ मरणशील मनुष्य — जो यह समझ चुका हो, जो रूप और रति के सुखों को परख चुका हो — बहुत लंबे जीवन में रस ले सकेगा?

devanagari: यस्मिन्निदं विचिकित्सन्ति मृत्यो / यत्साम्पराये महति ब्रूहि नस्तत् । / योऽयं वरो गूढमनुप्रविष्टो / नान्यं तस्मान्नचिकेता वृणीते ॥1.1.29॥
iast: yasminnidaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo / yatsāmparāye mahati brūhi nastat । / yo'yaṃ varo gūḍhamanupraviṣṭo / nānyaṃ tasmānnaciketā vṛṇīte ॥1.1.29॥
sayIt: yas-MIN-ni-DUM vi-chi-kit-SUN-ti MRIT-yo / yat saam-pa-RAA-yay MA-ha-ti BROO-hi nas tat / YO-yum va-RO GOO-dhum a-noo-pra-VISH-to / NAAN-yum tas-MAAN na-chi-KAY-taa vri-NEE-tay
translation: That over which they doubt, O Death — what lies in the great passing hence — tell us that. This boon, which has entered the hidden depth — Nachiketa chooses no other boon than that.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.1.29, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What would it take for you to hold a single question this steadily?

translations.hi: हे मृत्यु, जिस विषय में लोग संदेह करते हैं — उस महान प्रयाण में क्या है — वही हमें बताइए। जो वर गूढ़ रहस्य में उतर गया है, उसके सिवा नचिकेता कोई और वर नहीं माँगता।

devanagari: अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेय- / स्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषँ सिनीतः । / तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु / भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते ॥1.2.1॥
iast: anyacchreyo'nyadutaiva preya- / ste ubhe nānārthe puruṣam̐ sinītaḥ । / tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu / bhavati hīyate'rthādya u preyo vṛṇīte ॥1.2.1॥
sayIt: an-yuch-CHRAY-yo an-ya-doo-TAI-va PRAY-yas / tay oo-BHAY naa-NAAR-thay poo-roo-SHUM si-NEE-tah / ta-YOH SHRAY-ya aa-da-DAA-nas-ya SAA-dhoo / BHA-va-ti HEE-ya-tay ar-THAAD ya oo PRAY-yo vri-NEE-tay
translation: The good is one thing, the pleasant quite another; both bind a person, though to different ends. It goes well for the one who takes the good; whoever chooses the pleasant falls away from the goal.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which choice in front of you today are you calling good when it is only comfortable?

translations.hi: श्रेय एक चीज़ है और प्रेय बिलकुल दूसरी; दोनों मनुष्य को बाँधती हैं, पर दोनों की मंज़िलें अलग हैं। जो श्रेय को अपनाता है उसका भला होता है; जो प्रेय चुनता है, वह लक्ष्य से ही चूक जाता है।

devanagari: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः / तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः । / श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते / प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥1.2.2॥
iast: śreyaśca preyaśca manuṣyametaḥ / tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ । / śreyo hi dhīro'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte / preyo mando yogakṣemādvṛṇīte ॥1.2.2॥
sayIt: SHRAY-yash-cha PRAY-yash-cha ma-noosh-ya-MAY-tah / tau sum-pa-REET-ya vi-vi-NUK-ti DHEE-rah / SHRAY-yo hi DHEE-ro a-bhi PRAY-ya-so vri-NEE-tay / PRAY-yo MUN-do yo-ga-kshay-MAAD vri-NEE-tay
translation: Both the good and the pleasant come to a person. The wise one walks all the way around them, tells them apart, and chooses the good over the pleasant; the dull one chooses the pleasant for the sake of getting and keeping.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What decision are you about to make that you have not yet walked all the way around?

translations.hi: श्रेय और प्रेय — दोनों मनुष्य के सामने आते हैं। धीर व्यक्ति उन्हें चारों ओर से परखकर अलग-अलग पहचान लेता है और प्रेय के ऊपर श्रेय को चुनता है; मंदबुद्धि पाने-सँजोने की ख़ातिर प्रेय चुन लेता है।

devanagari: स त्वं प्रियान्प्रियरूपांश्च कामान् / अभिध्यायन्नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः । / नैतां सृङ्कां वित्तमयीमवाप्तो / यस्यां मज्जन्ति बहवो मनुष्याः ॥1.2.3॥
iast: sa tvaṃ priyānpriyarūpāṃśca kāmān / abhidhyāyannaciketo'tyasrākṣīḥ । / naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīmavāpto / yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ ॥1.2.3॥
sayIt: sa tvum pri-YAAN pri-ya-ROO-paansh-cha KAA-maan / a-bhi-DHYAA-yan na-chi-KAY-to at-yas-RAAK-sheeh / NAI-taam SRIN-kaam vit-ta-ma-YEE-ma-VAAP-to / YAS-yaam MUJ-jan-ti BA-ha-vo ma-noosh-YAAH
translation: You, Nachiketas, have looked desires full in the face — the dear things, the delightful shapes — and let them pass. You have not taken up that necklace of wealth in which so many people sink.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which temptation have you examined closely enough to have earned the right to refuse it?

translations.hi: हे नचिकेता, तुमने कामनाओं को — प्रिय चीज़ों और उनके लुभावने रूपों को — सीधे आँख भर देखा और जाने दिया। तुमने धन की वह माला नहीं पहनी जिसमें कितने ही लोग डूब जाते हैं।

devanagari: दूरमेते विपरीते विषूची / अविद्या या च विद्येति ज्ञाता । / विद्याभीप्सिनं नचिकेतसं मन्ये / न त्वा कामा बहवोऽलोलुपन्त ॥1.2.4॥
iast: dūramete viparīte viṣūcī / avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā । / vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye / na tvā kāmā bahavo'lolupanta ॥1.2.4॥
sayIt: DOO-ra-may-tay vi-pa-REE-tay vi-SHOO-chee / a-VID-yaa yaa cha VID-yay-ti GYAA-taa / vid-yaa-BHEEP-si-num na-chi-KAY-ta-sum MUN-yay / na tvaa KAA-maa BA-ha-vo a-lo-loo-PUN-ta
translation: Wide apart and pointing opposite ways run these two, known as ignorance and knowledge. I judge you, Nachiketas, one who longs for knowledge — the many desires could not drag you off course.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What tempted you recently and failed — and what does that failure tell you about your direction?

translations.hi: ये दोनों — जिन्हें अविद्या और विद्या कहा जाता है — दूर-दूर हैं और उल्टी दिशाओं में ले जाती हैं। मैं तुम्हें, नचिकेता, विद्या का सच्चा चाहने वाला मानता हूँ — इतनी सारी कामनाएँ भी तुम्हें डिगा नहीं पाईं।

devanagari: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः / स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः । / दन्द्रम्यमाणाः परियन्ति मूढा / अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥1.2.5॥
iast: avidyāyāmantare vartamānāḥ / svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃmanyamānāḥ । / dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā / andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ ॥1.2.5॥
sayIt: a-vid-YAA-yaam AN-ta-ray var-ta-MAA-naah / SVA-yum DHEE-raah pan-di-tum-MUN-ya-MAA-naah / dun-drum-ya-MAA-naah pa-ri-YUN-ti MOO-dhaa / an-DHAY-nai-va nee-ya-MAA-naa ya-THAAN-dhaah
translation: Dwelling in the very midst of ignorance, yet thinking themselves wise and learned, the deluded stagger round and round in circles — like the blind led by the blind.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Where are you most confident, and when did you last let that confidence be examined by someone who could prove it wrong?

translations.hi: अज्ञान के बीचोबीच रहते हुए भी खुद को धीर और पंडित मानने वाले मूढ़ ठोकरें खाते गोल-गोल घूमते रहते हैं — जैसे अंधे के हाथ में अंधों की डोर।

devanagari: न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालं / प्रमाद्यन्तं वित्तमोहेन मूढम् । / अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी / पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे ॥1.2.6॥
iast: na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ / pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham । / ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī / punaḥ punarvaśamāpadyate me ॥1.2.6॥
sayIt: na saam-pa-RAA-yah pra-ti-BHAA-ti BAA-lum / pra-maad-YUN-tum vit-ta-MO-hay-na MOO-dhum / a-YUM LO-ko NAAS-ti PA-ra i-ti MAA-nee / PU-nah PU-nar va-sha-MAA-pud-ya-tay may
translation: The way beyond never dawns on the childish one, heedless and befooled by the glamour of wealth. "This world is all there is; there is no other" — thinking so, he falls under my sway again and again.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which of your daily certainties exists only because you have never looked past what money can measure?

translations.hi: जो नासमझ धन के मोह में लापरवाह है, उसे परलोक की राह सूझती ही नहीं। "बस यही लोक है, और कोई नहीं" — ऐसा मानने वाला बार-बार मेरे (मृत्यु के) वश में आता है।

devanagari: श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्यः / शृण्वन्तोऽपि बहवो यं न विद्युः । / आश्चर्यो वक्ता कुशलोऽस्य लब्धा / आश्चर्यो ज्ञाता कुशलानुशिष्टः ॥1.2.7॥
iast: śravaṇāyāpi bahubhiryo na labhyaḥ / śṛṇvanto'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ । / āścaryo vaktā kuśalo'sya labdhā / āścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ ॥1.2.7॥
sayIt: shra-va-NAA-yaa-pi ba-hu-BHIR yo na LABH-yah / shrin-VUN-to-pi BA-ha-vo yum na vid-YOOH / aash-CHAR-yo vak-TAA ku-SHA-lo-sya lab-DHAA / aash-CHAR-yo GYAA-taa ku-sha-LAA-nu-SHISH-tah
translation: Many never even get the chance to hear of this Self; many, even hearing, do not know it. A wonder is the one who can teach it, skilled the one who attains it; a wonder the knower, taught by the skilled.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Who in your life can actually speak of these things from experience — and when did you last truly listen to them?

translations.hi: बहुतों को तो यह सुनने तक को नहीं मिलता; बहुत सुनकर भी इसे नहीं जान पाते। इसका कहने वाला अद्भुत है, पाने वाला कुशल; और कुशल गुरु से सीखा हुआ जानने वाला भी अद्भुत ही है।

devanagari: न नरेणावरेण प्रोक्त एष / सुविज्ञेयो बहुधा चिन्त्यमानः । / अनन्यप्रोक्ते गतिरत्र नास्ति / अणीयान् ह्यतर्क्यमणुप्रमाणात् ॥1.2.8॥
iast: na nareṇāvareṇa prokta eṣa / suvijñeyo bahudhā cintyamānaḥ । / ananyaprokte gatiratra nāsti / aṇīyān hyatarkyamaṇupramāṇāt ॥1.2.8॥
sayIt: na na-RAY-naa-va-RAY-na PROK-ta AY-sha / su-vig-YAY-yo ba-hu-DHAA chint-ya-MAA-nah / a-nan-ya-PROK-tay ga-ti-RUT-ra NAAS-ti / a-NEE-yaan hya-TARK-yum a-nu-pra-MAA-naat
translation: Taught by a lesser man, this Self is not easily understood — it just gets thought about in too many ways. When one who is not other than it teaches it, there is no more wandering; for it is subtler than the subtlest measure, beyond the reach of argument.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Are you collecting opinions about the deepest things, or sitting with someone who actually knows?

translations.hi: किसी साधारण व्यक्ति के बताने से यह आत्मा ठीक से समझ में नहीं आता — लोग इसे तरह-तरह से सोचते भर रह जाते हैं। जब वह सिखाता है जो इससे अलग नहीं, तब भटकाव नहीं रहता; क्योंकि यह सूक्ष्म से भी सूक्ष्म है, तर्क की पहुँच से परे।

devanagari: नैषा तर्केण मतिरापनेया / प्रोक्तान्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ । / यां त्वमापः सत्यधृतिर्बतासि / त्वादृङ्नो भूयान्नचिकेतः प्रष्टा ॥1.2.9॥
iast: naiṣā tarkeṇa matirāpaneyā / proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha । / yāṃ tvamāpaḥ satyadhṛtirbatāsi / tvādṛṅno bhūyānnaciketaḥ praṣṭā ॥1.2.9॥
sayIt: NAI-shaa tar-KAY-na ma-ti-RAA-pa-NAY-yaa / prok-TAAN-yay-NAI-va su-gyaa-NAA-ya PRAYSH-tha / yaam tvum AA-pah sat-ya-DHRI-tir ba-TAA-si / tvaa-DRIN-no BHOO-yaan na-chi-KAY-tah PRASH-taa
translation: This understanding cannot be reached by argument, dearest — only when taught by another does it become true knowing. And you have grasped it; steadfast in truth you are indeed. May we have more questioners like you, Nachiketa!
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When you ask your real questions, do you ask to win, or to be changed?

translations.hi: प्रिय, यह समझ तर्क से हाथ नहीं आती — किसी (जानने वाले) दूसरे के सिखाने पर ही यह सच्चा ज्ञान बनती है। और तुमने इसे पा लिया; तुम्हारी निष्ठा सचमुच सच्ची है। काश, नचिकेता, हमें तुम जैसे और प्रश्न पूछने वाले मिलें!

devanagari: जानाम्यहं शेवधिरित्यनित्यं / न ह्यध्रुवैः प्राप्यते हि ध्रुवं तत् । / ततो मया नाचिकेतश्चितोऽग्निः / अनित्यैर्द्रव्यैः प्राप्तवानस्मि नित्यम् ॥1.2.10॥
iast: jānāmyahaṃ śevadhirityanityaṃ / na hyadhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvaṃ tat । / tato mayā nāciketaścito'gniḥ / anityairdravyaiḥ prāptavānasmi nityam ॥1.2.10॥
sayIt: jaa-NAAM-ya-hum SHAY-va-dhir it-ya-NIT-yum / na hya-dhru-VAIH PRAAP-ya-tay hi dhru-VUM tat / TA-to ma-YAA naa-chi-KAY-tash-chi-TO-gnih / a-nit-YAIR drav-YAIH praap-ta-VAAN-as-mi NIT-yum
translation: "I know that the treasure won by rites is impermanent, for the constant is never gained through inconstant things. Even so I laid the Nachiketa fire, and with impermanent materials I have won what endures."
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which of your most solid achievements is really a long-lasting arrangement of impermanent parts?

translations.hi: "मैं जानता हूँ कि कर्म से मिलने वाला खजाना अनित्य है — अस्थिर साधनों से स्थिर वस्तु नहीं मिलती। फिर भी मैंने नाचिकेत अग्नि का चयन किया, और अनित्य सामग्री से वह पा लिया जो टिकाऊ है।"

devanagari: कामस्याप्तिं जगतः प्रतिष्ठां / क्रतोरानन्त्यमभयस्य पारम् । / स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा / धृत्या धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ॥1.2.11॥
iast: kāmasyāptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ / kratorānantyamabhayasya pāram । / stomamahadurugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā / dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo'tyasrākṣīḥ ॥1.2.11॥
sayIt: kaa-MAS-yaap-tim JA-ga-tah pra-tish-THAAM / kra-to-RAA-nant-yum a-bha-YAS-ya PAA-rum / sto-ma-ma-ha-DU-ru-GAA-yum pra-tish-THAAM DRISHT-vaa / DHRIT-yaa DHEE-ro na-chi-KAY-to at-yas-RAAK-sheeh
translation: The fulfilment of every desire, the foundation of the world, the endless reward of rites, the far shore beyond fear, greatness sung in praise, the wide way, a firm standing — you saw all of it, Nachiketa, and with steady wisdom you let it go.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What is the best offer in front of you right now that you would need real steadiness to refuse for something truer?

translations.hi: हर कामना की पूर्ति, संसार की प्रतिष्ठा, यज्ञ-फल की अनन्तता, निर्भयता का पार, स्तुति से मिली महिमा, दूर तक फैला मार्ग, दृढ़ स्थिति — यह सब देखकर भी, नचिकेता, तुमने धीरता से इसे जाने दिया।

devanagari: तं दुर्दर्शं गूढमनुप्रविष्टं / गुहाहितं गह्वरेष्ठं पुराणम् । / अध्यात्मयोगाधिगमेन देवं / मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति ॥1.2.12॥
iast: taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍhamanupraviṣṭaṃ / guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam । / adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ / matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti ॥1.2.12॥
sayIt: tum dur-DAR-shum GOO-dham-a-nu-pra-VISH-tum / gu-HAA-hi-tum gah-va-RAY-shtum pu-RAA-num / adh-YAAT-ma-yo-GAA-dhi-ga-MAY-na DAY-vum / mat-VAA DHEE-ro har-sha-SHO-kau ja-HAA-ti
translation: Hard to see, hidden deep, seated in the cave of the heart, dwelling in the depths, ancient — realizing that radiant one through the yoga of the inner self, the wise one leaves both elation and grief behind.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What remains of you when neither today's good news nor its bad news is allowed to define the hour?

translations.hi: जिसे देखना कठिन है, जो गहरे छिपा है, हृदय की गुफा में बसा, अतल में ठहरा, पुरातन — उस देव को अध्यात्म-योग से जानकर धीर पुरुष हर्ष और शोक दोनों पीछे छोड़ देता है।

devanagari: एतच्छ्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः / प्रवृह्य धर्म्यमणुमेतमाप्य । / स मोदते मोदनीयँ हि लब्ध्वा / विवृतँ सद्म नचिकेतसं मन्ये ॥1.2.13॥
iast: etacchrutvā samparigṛhya martyaḥ / pravṛhya dharmyamaṇumetamāpya । / sa modate modanīyam̐ hi labdhvā / vivṛtam̐ sadma naciketasaṃ manye ॥1.2.13॥
sayIt: ay-tach-CHRUT-vaa sum-pa-ri-GRIH-ya MART-yah / pra-VRIH-ya DHARM-yum a-NUM ay-ta-MAAP-ya / sa MO-da-tay mo-da-NEE-yum hi labdh-VAA / vi-VRI-tum SAD-ma na-chi-KAY-ta-sum MAN-yay
translation: Hearing this and taking it fully to heart, a mortal draws out this subtle essence of dharma and, attaining it, rejoices — for he has gained what is truly worth rejoicing in. I see the house standing wide open for Nachiketa.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What teaching have you heard and even agreed with, but never yet pulled the living pith from?

translations.hi: यह सुनकर, इसे पूरी तरह हृदय में धारण कर, मरणशील मनुष्य धर्म के इस सूक्ष्म तत्व को खींच निकालता है और उसे पाकर आनन्दित होता है — क्योंकि उसने वही पाया है जो सचमुच आनन्द के योग्य है। मुझे दिखता है, नचिकेता के लिए वह भवन खुला पड़ा है।

devanagari: अन्यत्र धर्मादन्यत्राधर्मा- / दन्यत्रास्मात्कृताकृतात् । / अन्यत्र भूताच्च भव्याच्च / यत्तत्पश्यसि तद्वद ॥1.2.14॥
iast: anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmā- / danyatrāsmātkṛtākṛtāt । / anyatra bhūtācca bhavyācca / yattatpaśyasi tadvada ॥1.2.14॥
sayIt: an-YUT-ra dhar-MAAD an-YUT-raa-dhar-MAAD / an-YUT-raas-MAAT kri-TAA-kri-TAAT / an-YUT-ra bhoo-TAACH-cha bhav-YAACH-cha / yat tat PASH-ya-si tad VA-da
translation: "Other than dharma, other than adharma, other than this whole realm of the done and the not-done, other than what has been and what is to come — what you see as That, tell me."
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If your deepest question tonight could not be about right and wrong, past or future, what would you ask?

translations.hi: "धर्म से अलग, अधर्म से अलग, किए और न-किए के इस पूरे दायरे से अलग, जो हो चुका और जो होने वाला है उससे भी अलग — जो तुम्हें 'वह' दिखता है, वही मुझे बताओ।"

devanagari: सर्वे वेदा यत्पदमामनन्ति / तपाँसि सर्वाणि च यद्वदन्ति । / यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति / तत्ते पदँ संग्रहेण ब्रवीम्योमित्येतत् ॥1.2.15॥
iast: sarve vedā yatpadamāmananti / tapām̐si sarvāṇi ca yadvadanti । / yadicchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti / tatte padam̐ saṃgraheṇa bravīmyomityetat ॥1.2.15॥
sayIt: SAR-vay VAY-daa yat pa-da-MAA-ma-nun-ti / ta-PAAM-si sar-VAA-ni cha yad va-DUN-ti / ya-dich-CHHUN-to brah-ma-CHAR-yum cha-RUN-ti / tat tay pa-DUM sun-gra-HAY-na bra-VEE-myo-mit-YAY-tat
translation: The goal all the Vedas proclaim, that all austerities speak of, desiring which seekers live the disciplined life — that goal I tell you in one word: it is Om.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If everything you are seeking had to be gathered into a single word, what word would you find yourself saying?

translations.hi: जिस पद की घोषणा सारे वेद करते हैं, सारे तप जिसकी बात करते हैं, जिसकी चाह में साधक ब्रह्मचर्य का जीवन जीते हैं — वह पद मैं तुम्हें संक्षेप में कहता हूँ: वह है ॐ।

devanagari: एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं परम् । / एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत् ॥1.2.16॥
iast: etaddhyevākṣaraṃ brahma etaddhyevākṣaraṃ param । / etaddhyevākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yadicchati tasya tat ॥1.2.16॥
sayIt: ay-tudd-HYAY-vaak-sha-rum BRAH-ma / ay-tudd-HYAY-vaak-sha-rum PA-rum / ay-tudd-HYAY-vaak-sha-rum GYAAT-vaa / yo ya-DICH-chha-ti TAS-ya tat
translation: This syllable truly is Brahman; this syllable truly is the supreme. Knowing this very syllable, whatever one desires, that is theirs.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What are you actually asking of your practice — and what would you ask if you trusted it completely?

translations.hi: यही अक्षर ब्रह्म है; यही अक्षर परम है। इसी अक्षर को जानकर जो जो चाहता है, वह उसका हो जाता है।

devanagari: एतदालम्बनँ श्रेष्ठमेतदालम्बनं परम् । / एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥1.2.17॥
iast: etadālambanam̐ śreṣṭhametadālambanaṃ param । / etadālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate ॥1.2.17॥
sayIt: ay-ta-DAA-lum-ba-num SHRAYSH-thum / ay-ta-DAA-lum-ba-num PA-rum / ay-ta-DAA-lum-ba-num GYAAT-vaa / brah-ma-LO-kay ma-HEE-ya-tay
translation: This support is the best; this support is the supreme. Knowing this support, one is exalted in the world of Brahman.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When your mind slips today, what will you give it to hold — and will that handhold bear real weight?

translations.hi: यही आलम्बन सबसे श्रेष्ठ है; यही आलम्बन परम है। इस आलम्बन को जानकर मनुष्य ब्रह्मलोक में महिमा पाता है।

devanagari: न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन् / नायं कुतश्चिन्न बभूव कश्चित् । / अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो / न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥1.2.18॥
iast: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin / nāyaṃ kutaścinna babhūva kaścit । / ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo / na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ॥1.2.18॥
sayIt: na JAA-ya-tay mri-YA-tay vaa vi-PASH-chin / NAA-yum ku-tush-CHIN-na ba-BHOO-va KASH-chit / A-jo NIT-yah SHAASH-va-TO-yum pu-RAA-no / na HUN-ya-tay hun-ya-MAA-nay sha-REE-ray
translation: The knower is not born, nor does it die; it did not arise from anything, nor did anything arise to become it. Unborn, constant, everlasting, primordial — it is not slain when the body is slain.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.18, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When you fear an ending, what exactly do you believe will end?

translations.hi: यह चेतन ज्ञाता न जन्म लेता है, न मरता है; न यह कहीं से आया, न कुछ और इसका रूप बना। अजन्मा, नित्य, शाश्वत, पुरातन — शरीर के मारे जाने पर भी यह नहीं मारा जाता।

devanagari: हन्ता चेन्मन्यते हन्तुँ हतश्चेन्मन्यते हतम् । / उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायँ हन्ति न हन्यते ॥1.2.19॥
iast: hantā cenmanyate hantum̐ hataścenmanyate hatam । / ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyam̐ hanti na hanyate ॥1.2.19॥
sayIt: hun-TAA chen MUN-ya-tay HUN-tum / ha-TASH-chen MUN-ya-tay ha-TUM / u-BHAU tau na vi-jaa-NEE-to / NAA-yum HUN-ti na HUN-ya-tay
translation: If the slayer thinks "I slay," and the slain thinks "I am slain," neither of them understands: this one neither slays nor is slain.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What in you has watched every change you have ever gone through without itself changing?

translations.hi: यदि मारने वाला सोचता है "मैंने मारा," और मारा गया सोचता है "मैं मारा गया," तो दोनों ही नहीं समझते: यह आत्मा न मारता है, न मारा जाता है।

devanagari: अणोरणीयान्महतो महीया- / नात्माऽस्य जन्तोर्निहितो गुहायाम् । / तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको / धातुप्रसादान्महिमानमात्मनः ॥1.2.20॥
iast: aṇoraṇīyānmahato mahīyā- / nātmā'sya jantornihito guhāyām । / tamakratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko / dhātuprasādānmahimānamātmanaḥ ॥1.2.20॥
sayIt: a-NO-ra-NEE-yaan ma-ha-TO ma-HEE-yaan / aat-MAAS-ya jun-TOR ni-hi-TO gu-HAA-yaam / tum-AK-ra-tuh PASH-ya-ti vee-ta-SHO-ko / dhaa-tu-pra-SAA-daan ma-hi-MAA-num aat-MA-nah
translation: Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, the Self is lodged in the hidden heart of every creature. One free of willed craving beholds that majesty of the Self through the settling-clear of mind and senses — and his grief is gone.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.20, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If for one hour you wanted nothing at all, what might become visible?

translations.hi: सूक्ष्म से सूक्ष्मतर, महान से महत्तर — यह आत्मा हर प्राणी के हृदय की गुफा में बसा है। जो कामना-रहित है, वह मन और इन्द्रियों के निर्मल हो जाने पर आत्मा की उस महिमा को देखता है — और उसका शोक जाता रहता है।

devanagari: आसीनो दूरं व्रजति शयानो याति सर्वतः । / कस्तं मदामदं देवं मदन्यो ज्ञातुमर्हति ॥1.2.21॥
iast: āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ । / kastaṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ madanyo jñātumarhati ॥1.2.21॥
sayIt: aa-SEE-no DOO-rum VRA-ja-ti / sha-YAA-no YAA-ti sar-va-TAH / kas-TUM ma-DAA-ma-dum DAY-vum / ma-DUN-yo GYAA-tum AR-ha-ti
translation: Sitting, it travels far; lying still, it goes everywhere. Who but I can know that radiant one, who is joy and yet beyond joy?
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.21, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Where were you rushing today that the deepest part of you had already arrived?

translations.hi: बैठा-बैठा यह दूर तक चला जाता है; लेटे-लेटे सब जगह पहुँच जाता है। उस देव को — जो आनन्दमय भी है और आनन्द से परे भी — मेरे सिवा और कौन जान सकता है?

devanagari: अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् । / महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥1.2.22॥
iast: aśarīram̐ śarīreṣvanavastheṣvavasthitam । / mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ॥1.2.22॥
sayIt: a-sha-REE-rum sha-ree-RAYSH-va-na-VUS-thaysh-va-vus-thi-TUM / ma-HAAN-tum vi-BHUM aat-MAA-num / mat-VAA DHEE-ro na SHO-cha-ti
translation: Bodiless within bodies, stable within the unstable — realizing the Self as the great and pervading one, the wise person does not grieve.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.22, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: In the middle of whatever is shaking right now, what are you taking yourself to be — the shaken thing, or the steady one within it?

translations.hi: शरीरों के भीतर अशरीरी, अस्थिरों के बीच स्थिर — आत्मा को महान और सर्वव्यापी जानकर धीर पुरुष शोक नहीं करता।

devanagari: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो / न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । / यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यः / तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूँ स्वाम् ॥1.2.23॥
iast: nāyamātmā pravacanena labhyo / na medhayā na bahunā śrutena । / yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ / tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūm̐ svām ॥1.2.23॥
sayIt: naa-ya-MAAT-maa pra-va-cha-NAY-na LABH-yo / na may-dha-YAA na ba-hu-NAA shru-TAY-na / ya-may-VAI-sha vri-NU-tay TAY-na LABH-yah / tas-YAI-sha AAT-maa vi-vri-NU-tay ta-NOOM svaam
translation: This Self is not attained by discourse, nor by intellect, nor by much hearing. Whom this very Self chooses, by him it is attained — to him this Self unveils its own form.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.23, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Today, will you approach the Self as a subject to be mastered, or as someone to be met?

translations.hi: यह आत्मा न प्रवचन से मिलता है, न बुद्धि से, न बहुत सुनने से। जिसे यह स्वयं चुनता है, उसी को मिलता है — उसी के आगे यह आत्मा अपना स्वरूप खोल देता है।

devanagari: नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः । / नाशान्तमानसो वाऽपि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात् ॥1.2.24॥
iast: nāvirato duścaritānnāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ । / nāśāntamānaso vā'pi prajñānenainamāpnuyāt ॥1.2.24॥
sayIt: NAA-vi-ra-to dush-cha-ri-TAAN / naa-SHAAN-to naa-sa-MAA-hi-tah / naa-SHAAN-ta-maa-na-SO VAA-pi / prug-YAA-nay-NAI-nam AAP-nu-yaat
translation: One who has not turned from wrong conduct, who is not stilled, not collected, whose mind is not at peace — such a one cannot reach this Self even by keen intelligence.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.24, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Of the four gates — conduct, calm, focus, a settled mind — which one are you quietly trying to skip?

translations.hi: जिसने बुरे आचरण से मुँह नहीं मोड़ा, जो शांत नहीं, एकाग्र नहीं, जिसका मन ठहरा नहीं — वह तीखी बुद्धि के बल पर भी इस आत्मा को नहीं पा सकता।

devanagari: यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः । / मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः ॥1.2.25॥
iast: yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ । / mṛtyuryasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ ॥1.2.25॥
sayIt: YAS-ya BRAH-ma cha KSHUT-rum cha / u-BHAY BHA-va-ta O-da-nah / mrit-YUR yas-YO-pa-say-cha-num / ka it-THAA VAY-da YUT-ra sah
translation: For That, the priestly power and the warrior power are both just the rice of its meal, and death itself is the sauce poured over — who can truly know where it is?
source: Katha Upanishad 1.2.25, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What towering power in your world would look small if you could see what it, too, is a meal for?

translations.hi: उसके लिए ब्राह्मण-शक्ति और क्षत्रिय-शक्ति दोनों मानो भात हैं, और मृत्यु उस पर परोसा हुआ रसा — कौन सचमुच जान सकता है कि वह कहाँ है?

devanagari: ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके / गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे । / छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति / पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः ॥1.3.1॥
iast: ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke / guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe । / chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti / pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ ॥1.3.1॥
sayIt: RI-tum pi-BAN-tow soo-KRI-tas-ya LO-kay / goo-HAAM pra-VISH-tow PA-ra-may pa-RAAR-dhay / chaa-YAA-ta-pow BRAH-ma-vi-do va-DAN-ti / pun-CHAAG-na-yo yay cha tri-naa-chi-KAY-taah
translation: Two there are, drinking the fruit of good action in this world, entered into the secret cave, in the highest place of the supreme. Knowers of Brahman call them shadow and sunlight — as do the keepers of the five fires, and those who have thrice kindled the Nachiketa fire.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: In the middle of today's busyness, can you sense the still companion in you who watches while you act?

translations.hi: दो हैं, जो इस लोक में सुकर्मों का फल पीते हैं, हृदय की गुप्त गुफा में, परम के सर्वोच्च स्थान में प्रविष्ट। ब्रह्म को जानने वाले उन्हें छाया और धूप कहते हैं — और पाँच अग्नियाँ रखने वाले गृहस्थ भी, और वे भी जिन्होंने तीन बार नाचिकेत अग्नि जलाई है।

devanagari: यः सेतुरीजानानामक्षरं ब्रह्म यत् परम् । / अभयं तितीर्षतां पारं [https://puranastudy.000space.com/pur_index15/nachiketa.htm नाचिकेतँ] शकेमहि ॥1.3.2॥
iast: yaḥ seturījānānāmakṣaraṃ brahma yat param । / abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketam̐ śakemahi ॥1.3.2॥
sayIt: yah say-too-ree-jaa-naa-NAAM AK-sha-rum BRAH-ma yat PA-rum / a-BHA-yum ti-teer-sha-TAAM PAA-rum NAA-chi-kay-tum sha-KAY-ma-hi
translation: May we be able to master the Nachiketa fire — the bridge for those who offer sacrifice — and the imperishable, the supreme Brahman, the fearless far shore for those who long to cross.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When you imagine being genuinely unafraid, what shore are you standing on?

translations.hi: जो यज्ञ करने वालों के लिए सेतु है, उस नाचिकेत अग्नि को — और उस अविनाशी, परम ब्रह्म को — साध पाने की शक्ति हममें हो, जो पार जाने की इच्छा रखने वालों के लिए अभय किनारा है।

devanagari: आत्मानँ रथिनं विद्धि शरीरँ रथमेव तु । / बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥1.3.3॥
iast: ātmānam̐ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīram̐ rathameva tu । / buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca ॥1.3.3॥
sayIt: aat-MAA-num RA-thi-num VID-dhi sha-REE-rum RA-tha-may-va too / BOOD-dhim too SAA-ra-thim VID-dhi MA-nah pra-GRA-ha-may-va cha
translation: Know the self as the rider in the chariot and the body as simply the chariot; know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If your body is the chariot and your intellect the driver, who chose the road you took today?

translations.hi: आत्मा को रथ में बैठा स्वामी जानो और शरीर को केवल रथ; बुद्धि को सारथी समझो, और मन को लगाम।

devanagari: इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयाँ स्तेषु गोचरान् । / आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥1.3.4॥
iast: indriyāṇi hayānāhurviṣayām̐ steṣu gocarān । / ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ ॥1.3.4॥
sayIt: in-dri-YAA-ni ha-YAA-naa-hoor vi-sha-YAAM STAY-shoo go-cha-RAAN / aat-MAYN-dri-ya-ma-no-YOOK-tum bhok-TAYT-yaa-hoor ma-nee-SHI-nah
translation: The senses, they say, are the horses, and sense-objects the roads they range over. The self joined to body, senses and mind — that, the wise say, is the experiencer.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which of your five horses pulls the hardest, and down which road?

translations.hi: इंद्रियाँ, कहते हैं, घोड़े हैं, और उनके विषय वे रास्ते जिन पर वे दौड़ते हैं। शरीर, इंद्रियों और मन से जुड़ा आत्मा — उसे ही ज्ञानी 'भोक्ता' कहते हैं।

devanagari: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । / तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥1.3.5॥
iast: yastvavijñānavānbhavatyayuktena manasā sadā । / tasyendriyāṇyavaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ ॥1.3.5॥
sayIt: yas-tva-vig-YAA-na-vaan bha-vat-ya-yook-TAY-na ma-na-SAA sa-DAA / tas-yen-dri-YAAN-ya-vash-YAA-ni doosh-TAASH-vaa i-va saa-ra-THAYH
translation: But whoever lacks understanding, whose mind is never reined in — his senses run beyond control, like the vicious horses of a charioteer.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Where in your day do the horses, not the driver, decide the route?

translations.hi: पर जिसमें विवेक नहीं और जिसका मन कभी लगाम में नहीं रहता, उसकी इंद्रियाँ बेकाबू हो जाती हैं — जैसे सारथी के दुष्ट घोड़े।

devanagari: यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । / तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥1.3.6॥
iast: yastu vijñānavānbhavati yuktena manasā sadā । / tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ ॥1.3.6॥
sayIt: yas-too vig-YAA-na-vaan BHA-va-ti yook-TAY-na ma-na-SAA sa-DAA / tas-yen-dri-YAA-ni VASH-yaa-ni sad-ASH-vaa i-va saa-ra-THAYH
translation: But whoever has understanding, whose mind is always held like reins in hand — his senses obey, like the good horses of a charioteer.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which one rein — sleep, food, the phone — could you quietly take back in hand this week?

translations.hi: पर जिसमें विवेक है और जिसका मन सदा जुता रहता है, उसकी इंद्रियाँ वश में रहती हैं — जैसे सारथी के अच्छे घोड़े।

devanagari: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्यमनस्कः सदाऽशुचिः । / न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति ॥1.3.7॥
iast: yastvavijñānavānbhavatyamanaskaḥ sadā'śuciḥ । / na sa tatpadamāpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati ॥1.3.7॥
sayIt: yas-tva-vig-YAA-na-vaan bha-vat-ya-ma-NAS-kah sa-DAA-shoo-chih / na sa tat-pa-dum AAP-no-ti sam-SAA-rum chaa-dhi-GACH-chha-ti
translation: Whoever lacks understanding, is unmindful and ever impure, does not reach that goal — he comes back again into samsara.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What does "going in circles" look like in your own life right now?

translations.hi: जिसमें विवेक नहीं, जिसका मन साधन नहीं बनता और जो सदा अशुद्ध रहता है, वह उस पद तक नहीं पहुँचता — वह संसार के चक्कर में लौटता रहता है।

devanagari: यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः । / स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते ॥1.3.8॥
iast: yastu vijñānavānbhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ । / sa tu tatpadamāpnoti yasmādbhūyo na jāyate ॥1.3.8॥
sayIt: yas-too vig-YAA-na-vaan BHA-va-ti sa-ma-NAS-kah sa-DAA SHOO-chih / sa too tat-pa-dum AAP-no-ti yas-MAAD BHOO-yo na JAA-ya-tay
translation: But whoever has understanding, is mindful and ever pure, reaches that place from which he is not born again.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What would "keeping the inner life clean" mean for you today, concretely?

translations.hi: पर जिसमें विवेक है, जिसका मन साधन बना है और जो सदा शुद्ध है, वह उस पद को पा लेता है जहाँ से फिर जन्म नहीं होता।

devanagari: विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनः प्रग्रहवान्नरः । / सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥1.3.9॥
iast: vijñānasārathiryastu manaḥ pragrahavānnaraḥ । / so'dhvanaḥ pāramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ॥1.3.9॥
sayIt: vig-yaa-na-SAA-ra-thir yas-too MA-nah pra-gra-ha-VAAN NA-rah / so-DHVA-nah PAA-ram AAP-no-ti tad-VISH-noh pa-ra-mum pa-DUM
translation: The man whose charioteer is discernment, who holds the mind's reins firmly, reaches the end of the road — that supreme abode of Vishnu.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If your attention had a destination this year, where is it actually driving?

translations.hi: जिस मनुष्य का सारथी विवेक है और जो मन की लगाम थामे रहता है, वह यात्रा के पार पहुँचता है — विष्णु के उस परम पद तक।

devanagari: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः । / मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान्परः ॥1.3.10॥
iast: indriyebhyaḥ parā hyarthā arthebhyaśca paraṃ manaḥ । / manasastu parā buddhirbuddherātmā mahānparaḥ ॥1.3.10॥
sayIt: in-dri-YAYBH-yah pa-RAA hyar-THAA ar-THAYBH-yash-cha PA-rum MA-nah / ma-na-SAS-too pa-RAA BOOD-dhir bood-DHAY-raat-MAA ma-HAAN pa-RAH
translation: Beyond the senses stand their objects; beyond the objects, the mind; beyond the mind, the intellect; and beyond the intellect, the great Self.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What is one level more inward than the thing currently gripping you?

translations.hi: इंद्रियों से परे उनके विषय हैं; विषयों से परे मन; मन से परे बुद्धि; और बुद्धि से भी परे महान आत्मा।

devanagari: महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः । / पुरुषान्न परं किंचित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः ॥1.3.11॥
iast: mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ । / puruṣānna paraṃ kiṃcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ ॥1.3.11॥
sayIt: ma-ha-TAH pa-ra-mav-YAK-tum av-yak-TAAT poo-roo-SHAH pa-RAH / poo-roo-SHAAN-na pa-RUM KIN-chit saa KAASH-thaa saa pa-RAA ga-TIH
translation: Beyond the great is the unmanifest; beyond the unmanifest, the Person. Beyond the Person there is nothing — that is the summit, that the supreme goal.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When you imagine your search finally ending, what are you standing before?

translations.hi: महान से परे अव्यक्त है; अव्यक्त से परे पुरुष। पुरुष से परे कुछ भी नहीं — वही पराकाष्ठा है, वही परम गति।

devanagari: एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽऽत्मा न प्रकाशते । / दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः ॥1.3.12॥
iast: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho''tmā na prakāśate । / dṛśyate tvagryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ ॥1.3.12॥
sayIt: AY-sha sar-VAY-shoo bhoo-TAY-shoo GOO-dhaat-maa na pra-KAA-sha-tay / drish-YA-tay tvag-rya-YAA boodh-YAA sooksh-ma-YAA sooksh-ma-dar-SHI-bhih
translation: This Self lies hidden in all beings and does not shine forth; yet subtle seers behold it with a keen and subtle intellect.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What might you already be looking at every day without seeing?

translations.hi: यह आत्मा सब प्राणियों में छिपा है और स्वयं प्रकट नहीं होता; पर सूक्ष्म देखने वाले उसे तीक्ष्ण और सूक्ष्म बुद्धि से देख लेते हैं।

devanagari: यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञस्तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञान आत्मनि । / ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेत्तद्यच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि ॥1.3.13॥
iast: yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñastadyacchejjñāna ātmani । / jñānamātmani mahati niyacchettadyacchecchānta ātmani ॥1.3.13॥
sayIt: yach-CHAYD VAANG ma-na-SEE PRAAG-yas tad-yach-CHAYJ GYAA-na AAT-ma-ni / GYAA-nam AAT-ma-ni ma-HA-ti ni-yach-CHAYT tad-yach-CHAYCH CHAAN-ta AAT-ma-ni
translation: Let the wise one merge speech into mind, mind into the knowing self, that knowing into the great Self, and the great into the Self of peace.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which outermost layer — speech, perhaps — could you quiet first tonight?

translations.hi: बुद्धिमान वाणी को मन में समेटे, मन को ज्ञानरूप आत्मा में, उस ज्ञान को महान आत्मा में, और महान को शांत आत्मा में विलीन कर दे।

devanagari: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत / प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत । / क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया / दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥1.3.14॥
iast: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata / prāpya varānnibodhata । / kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā / durgaṃ pathastatkavayo vadanti ॥1.3.14॥
sayIt: ut-TISH-tha-ta JAA-gra-ta / PRAAP-ya va-RAAN ni-BO-dha-ta / KSHOO-ras-ya DHAA-raa ni-shi-TAA doo-rat-ya-YAA / DOOR-gum pa-thas-tat KA-va-yo va-DUN-ti
translation: Arise! Awake! Approach the excellent ones and learn. Sharp as a razor's whetted edge, hard to cross — a difficult path, declare the poets.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What have you been waiting to wake up for, and who are the "excellent ones" you could learn it from?

translations.hi: उठो! जागो! श्रेष्ठ जनों के पास जाकर जानो। छुरे की तीखी धार जैसा दुर्गम है यह मार्ग — कठिन पथ, ऐसा ज्ञानी कहते हैं।

devanagari: अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं / तथाऽरसं नित्यमगन्धवच्च यत् । / अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं / निचाय्य तन्मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुच्यते ॥1.3.15॥
iast: aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayaṃ / tathā'rasaṃ nityamagandhavacca yat । / anādyanantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ / nicāyya tanmṛtyumukhāt pramucyate ॥1.3.15॥
sayIt: a-SHAB-dum as-PAR-shum a-ROO-pum av-ya-YUM / ta-THAA-ra-sum NIT-yum a-GUN-dha-vach-cha yat / a-NAAD-ya-NUN-tum ma-ha-TAH pa-RUM dhroo-VUM / ni-CHAAY-ya tan mrit-yoo-moo-KHAAT pra-MOOCH-ya-tay
translation: Discerning that which is soundless, touchless, formless, undecaying — likewise tasteless, eternal, scentless, without beginning or end, beyond the great, unwavering — one is freed from the mouth of death.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What in your experience has never changed, no matter what else did?

translations.hi: जो शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस और गंध से रहित है — अविनाशी, नित्य, अनादि, अनंत, महत से परे और अचल — उसे जानकर मनुष्य मृत्यु के मुख से छूट जाता है।

devanagari: नाचिकेतमुपाख्यानं मृत्युप्रोक्तँ सनातनम् । / उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥1.3.16॥
iast: nāciketamupākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktam̐ sanātanam । / uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate ॥1.3.16॥
sayIt: naa-chi-KAY-tum oo-PAAKH-yaa-num mrit-yoo-PROK-tum sa-naa-TA-num / OOKT-vaa SHROOT-vaa cha may-DHAA-vee brah-ma-LO-kay ma-HEE-ya-tay
translation: Telling or hearing this ancient tale of Nachiketa, spoken by Death, the wise one is exalted in the world of Brahman.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which teaching have you heard often but never yet told to someone else?

translations.hi: मृत्यु के कहे इस सनातन नचिकेता-आख्यान को जो बुद्धिमान सुनाता या सुनता है, वह ब्रह्मलोक में महिमा पाता है।

devanagari: य इमं परमं गुह्यं श्रावयेद् ब्रह्मसंसदि । / प्रयतः श्राद्धकाले वा तदानन्त्याय कल्पते । / तदानन्त्याय कल्पत इति ॥1.3.17॥
iast: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi । / prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tadānantyāya kalpate । / tadānantyāya kalpata iti ॥1.3.17॥
sayIt: ya i-MUM pa-ra-MUM GOOH-yum SHRAA-va-yayd brah-ma-sum-SA-di / pra-ya-TAH SHRAAD-dha-kaa-lay vaa ta-daa-NUNT-yaa-ya KAL-pa-tay / ta-daa-NUNT-yaa-ya KAL-pa-ta i-ti
translation: Whoever, purified, has this supreme secret recited in an assembly of knowers of Brahman, or at the time of shraddha — it readies him for the endless; it readies him for the endless.
source: Katha Upanishad 1.3.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What would it mean to treat a teaching as something you owe to the next hearer?

translations.hi: जो पवित्र होकर इस परम रहस्य को ब्रह्मज्ञों की सभा में या श्राद्ध के समय सुनाता है, वह अनंत का अधिकारी बनता है — वह अनंत का अधिकारी बनता है।

devanagari: पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भू- / स्तस्मात्पराङ्पश्यति नान्तरात्मन् । / कश्चिद्धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्ष- / दावृत्तचक्षुरमृतत्वमिच्छन् ॥2.1.1॥
iast: parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayambhū- / stasmātparāṅpaśyati nāntarātman । / kaściddhīraḥ pratyagātmānamaikṣa- / dāvṛttacakṣuramṛtatvamicchan ॥2.1.1॥
sayIt: pa-RAAN-chi KHAA-ni vya-TRI-nut sva-yum-BHOOS / TAS-maat pa-RAANG PASH-ya-ti NAAN-ta-RAAT-mun / KASH-chid DHEE-rah prat-yug-AAT-maa-num IKE-shud / aa-VRIT-ta-CHUK-shoor am-rit-UT-vum ICH-chhun
translation: The Self-existent pierced the openings of the senses outward, so a person looks out, not in toward the inner self. Some rare, steady one, longing for the deathless, turned the gaze around and saw the Self within.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If your senses open outward by design, what one minute today could you spend looking back at the looker?

translations.hi: स्वयंभू ने इंद्रियों के द्वार बाहर की ओर छेदे, इसलिए मनुष्य बाहर देखता है, भीतर की आत्मा को नहीं। कोई विरला धीर पुरुष, अमरता की चाह में, दृष्टि को मोड़कर भीतर बसी आत्मा को देख लेता है।

devanagari: पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बाला- / स्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् । / अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा / ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते ॥2.1.2॥
iast: parācaḥ kāmānanuyanti bālā- / ste mṛtyoryanti vitatasya pāśam । / atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā / dhruvamadhruveṣviha na prārthayante ॥2.1.2॥
sayIt: pa-RAA-chah KAA-maan a-noo-YUN-ti BAA-laas / tay mrit-YOR YUN-ti vi-ta-TUS-ya PAA-shum / A-tha DHEE-raa am-rit-UT-vum vi-dit-VAA / dhroo-VUM a-dhroo-VAYSH-vi-ha na PRAAR-tha-yun-tay
translation: The childish follow desires that face outward, and they walk into the wide-flung snare of death. But the wise, having known the deathless, do not seek the constant among the inconstant things of this world.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which fleeting thing in your life are you currently asking to be permanent?

translations.hi: नासमझ लोग बाहर की ओर मुँह किए भोगों के पीछे चलते हैं और मृत्यु के फैले हुए जाल में जा पड़ते हैं। पर धीर पुरुष, अमरता को जानकर, इस संसार की अस्थिर चीज़ों में स्थिर को नहीं खोजते।

devanagari: येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान् स्पर्शाँश्च मैथुनान् । / एतेनैव विजानाति किमत्र परिशिष्यते । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.3॥
iast: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśām̐śca maithunān । / etenaiva vijānāti kimatra pariśiṣyate । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.3॥
sayIt: YAY-na ROO-pum RA-sum GUN-dhum SHUB-daan spar-SHAAMSH-cha my-thoo-NAAN / ay-tay-NY-va vi-jaa-NAA-ti KIM UT-ra pa-ri-SHISH-ya-tay / ay-TUD VY TUT
translation: It is through this alone that one knows form, taste, smell, sounds, touches, and the pleasures of union. What, then, is left over that it could not know? This, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: The next time you taste something today, can you notice the knowing itself and not just the taste?

translations.hi: रूप, रस, गंध, शब्द, स्पर्श और मिलन के सुख — इन सबको जीव इसी के द्वारा जानता है। फिर ऐसा क्या बचता है जिसे यह न जान सके? यही, सचमुच, वह है।

devanagari: स्वप्नान्तं जागरितान्तं चोभौ येनानुपश्यति । / महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥2.1.4॥
iast: svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati । / mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ॥2.1.4॥
sayIt: svap-NAAN-tum jaa-ga-ri-TAAN-tum CHO-bhow yay-NAA-noo-PASH-ya-ti / ma-HAAN-tum VI-bhoom aat-MAA-num mut-VAA DHEE-ro na SHO-cha-ti
translation: That by which one sees both what happens in dream and what happens in waking — knowing it as the great, all-pervading Self, the wise one grieves no more.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What in you is present both in your dreams and in this waking moment?

translations.hi: जिसके द्वारा जीव स्वप्न और जागरण — दोनों अवस्थाओं को देखता है, उसे महान, सर्वव्यापी आत्मा जानकर धीर पुरुष शोक नहीं करता।

devanagari: य इमं मध्वदं वेद आत्मानं जीवमन्तिकात् । / ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.5॥
iast: ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvamantikāt । / īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.5॥
sayIt: ya i-MUM madh-VA-dum VAY-da aat-MAA-num JEE-vum an-ti-KAAT / ee-SHAA-num bhoo-ta-BHAV-yas-ya na TA-to vi-joo-GOOP-sa-tay / ay-TAD-vye tat
translation: Whoever knows this honey-eater — the self, the living one, nearer than near — as the lord of what was and what will be, no longer shrinks away in fear. This, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If the one in you tasting this very moment is also the lord of your past and future, what is left to hide from?

translations.hi: जो इस मधु के भोक्ता को — इस जीव को, इस आत्मा को, जो इतना निकट है — भूत और भविष्य का स्वामी जान लेता है, वह फिर डरकर नहीं सिकुड़ता। यही तो वह है।

devanagari: यः पूर्वं तपसो जातमद्भ्यः पूर्वमजायत । / गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तं यो भूतेभिर्व्यपश्यत । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.6॥
iast: yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātamadbhyaḥ pūrvamajāyata । / guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhirvyapaśyata । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.6॥
