sayIt: yah POOR-vum TA-pa-so JAA-tum ad-BHYAH POOR-vum a-JAA-ya-ta / goo-HAAM pra-VISH-ya tish-THAN-tum yo bhoo-TAY-bhir vya-PASH-ya-ta / ay-TAD-vye tat
translation: The one born of old from the heat of creation, born before the waters, who entered the cave of the heart and abides there, gazing out through all beings — this, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What changes in an ordinary afternoon if the oldest presence in the universe is keeping watch from inside your chest?

translations.hi: जो सृष्टि के तप से पहले-पहल जन्मा, जल से भी पहले जन्मा, जो हृदय की गुफा में प्रवेश कर वहीं ठहरा है और सब प्राणियों के भीतर से झाँकता है — यही तो वह है।

devanagari: या प्राणेन संभवत्यदितिर्देवतामयी । / गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तीं या भूतेभिर्व्यजायत । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.7॥
iast: yā prāṇena saṃbhavatyaditirdevatāmayī । / guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhirvyajāyata । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.7॥
sayIt: yaa praa-NAY-na sam-BHA-vat-ya-di-tir day-va-taa-MA-yee / goo-HAAM pra-VISH-ya tish-than-TEEM yaa bhoo-TAY-bhir vya-JAA-ya-ta / ay-TAD-vye tat
translation: Aditi, made of all the gods, who arises as the breath of life, who entered the cave of the heart and abides there, born again through all beings — this, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Through how many different doorways — breath, fire, mother, sky — have you glimpsed the same one room?

translations.hi: सब देवताओं से बनी अदिति, जो प्राण के साथ प्रकट होती हैं, जो हृदय की गुफा में प्रवेश कर वहीं विराजी हैं और प्राणियों में फिर-फिर जन्म लेती हैं — यही तो वह है।

devanagari: अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः । / दिवे दिवे ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.8॥
iast: araṇyornihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ । / dive dive īḍyo jāgṛvadbhirhaviṣmadbhirmanuṣyebhiragniḥ । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.8॥
sayIt: a-run-YOR ni-hi-TO jaa-ta-VAY-daa GAR-bha i-va soo-BHRI-to gar-bhi-NEE-bhih / di-VAY di-VAY EED-yo jaa-gri-VAD-bhir ha-vish-MAD-bhir ma-noosh-YAY-bhir AG-nih / ay-TAD-vye tat
translation: Like a child carried with care by an expectant mother, the fire that knows all beings lies hidden in the two fire-sticks — to be honored day after day by wakeful people bearing offerings. This, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which small fire of yours deserves to be tended today as carefully as an expectant mother carries her child?

translations.hi: जैसे गर्भवती स्त्रियाँ गर्भ को सँभालकर धारण करती हैं, वैसे ही दो अरणियों में छिपा है जातवेदा अग्नि — जागते हुए, हवि लिए मनुष्यों द्वारा दिन-प्रतिदिन वंदनीय। यही तो वह है।

devanagari: यतश्चोदेति सूर्योऽस्तं यत्र च गच्छति । / तं देवाः सर्वेऽर्पितास्तदु नात्येति कश्चन । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.9॥
iast: yataścodeti sūryo'staṃ yatra ca gacchati । / taṃ devāḥ sarve'rpitāstadu nātyeti kaścana । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.9॥
sayIt: ya-tush-cho-DAY-ti SOOR-yo-stum YAT-ra cha GACH-chha-ti / tum DAY-vaah sar-VAYR-pi-taas ta-doo NAAT-yay-ti KASH-cha-na / ay-TAD-vye tat
translation: That from which the sun rises and into which it sets — on it all the gods are fixed, and none whatsoever goes beyond it. This, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What would you build your days around if you took seriously that nothing — not even the sun — goes beyond That?

translations.hi: जिससे सूर्य उगता है और जिसमें अस्त होता है — उसी पर सारे देवता टिके हैं, और उसके पार कोई भी नहीं जाता। यही तो वह है।

devanagari: यदेवेह तदमुत्र यदमुत्र तदन्विह । / मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥2.1.10॥
iast: yadeveha tadamutra yadamutra tadanviha । / mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati ॥2.1.10॥
sayIt: ya-day-VAY-ha ta-da-MOO-tra ya-da-MOO-tra ta-DAN-vi-ha / mrit-YOH sa mrit-yoom-AAP-no-ti ya i-HA naa-NAY-va PASH-ya-ti
translation: What is here is exactly there; what is there is also here. From death to death goes the one who sees difference here.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Where did you draw a hard line today between the sacred over there and the ordinary right here?

translations.hi: जो यहाँ है वही वहाँ है; जो वहाँ है वही यहाँ भी। जो यहाँ अनेक-सा देखता है, वह मृत्यु से मृत्यु को प्राप्त होता है।

devanagari: मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं नेह नानाऽस्ति किंचन । / मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥2.1.11॥
iast: manasaivedamāptavyaṃ neha nānā'sti kiṃcana । / mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati ॥2.1.11॥
sayIt: ma-na-SYE-vay-dum aap-TAV-yum NAY-ha NAA-naas-ti KIM-cha-na / mrit-YOH sa MRIT-yoom GACH-chha-ti ya i-HA naa-NAY-va PASH-ya-ti
translation: By the mind alone is this to be reached; there is no plurality here at all. From death to death goes the one who sees plurality here.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What might become visible if you spent ten quiet minutes polishing the instrument instead of feeding it more sights?

translations.hi: मन से ही यह पाया जाना है; यहाँ अनेकता कुछ भी नहीं है। जो यहाँ अनेक-सा देखता है, वह मृत्यु से मृत्यु को जाता है।

devanagari: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो मध्य आत्मनि तिष्ठति । / ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.12॥
iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati । / īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.12॥
sayIt: an-goosh-tha-MAA-trah poo-roo-SHO MAD-hya AAT-ma-ni TISH-tha-ti / ee-SHAA-num bhoo-ta-BHAV-yas-ya na TA-to vi-joo-GOOP-sa-tay / ay-TAD-vye tat
translation: A person the size of a thumb dwells at the center of the body; knowing him as lord of what was and what will be, one no longer shrinks away in fear. This, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Can you sit for one minute with the thought that what rules past and future rests quietly at the center of your own body?

translations.hi: अँगूठे भर का पुरुष देह के मध्य में बसा है; उसे भूत और भविष्य का स्वामी जानकर मनुष्य फिर डरकर नहीं सिकुड़ता। यही तो वह है।

devanagari: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ज्योतिरिवाधूमकः । / ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.1.13॥
iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotirivādhūmakaḥ । / īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ । / etadvai tat ॥2.1.13॥
sayIt: an-goosh-tha-MAA-trah poo-roo-SHO JYO-tir i-vaa-DHOO-ma-kah / ee-SHAA-no bhoo-ta-BHAV-yas-ya sa ay-VAAD-ya sa oo SHVAH / ay-TAD-vye tat
translation: The thumb-sized person is like a flame without smoke — lord of what was and what will be, he alone is today, and he tomorrow too. This, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What in you will be exactly the same tomorrow as it is today, and can you rest there now?

translations.hi: अँगूठे भर का पुरुष धुएँ-रहित लौ जैसा है — भूत और भविष्य का स्वामी; वही आज है, और वही कल भी। यही तो वह है।

devanagari: यथोदकं दुर्गे वृष्टं पर्वतेषु विधावति । / एवं धर्मान् पृथक् पश्यंस्तानेवानुविधावति ॥2.1.14॥
iast: yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati । / evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃstānevānuvidhāvati ॥2.1.14॥
sayIt: ya-tho-DA-kum DOOR-gay VRISH-tum par-va-TAY-shoo vi-DHAA-va-ti / AY-vum dhar-MAAN pri-THAK pash-yums-taa-nay-VAA-noo-vi-DHAA-va-ti
translation: As rain fallen on a rugged ridge scatters and runs down the mountainsides, so one who sees things as separate runs scattering after them.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Down how many separate slopes is your attention running right now?

translations.hi: जैसे ऊबड़-खाबड़ ऊँची भूमि पर बरसा पानी पहाड़ों की ढलानों पर बिखरकर भागता है, वैसे ही जो चीज़ों को अलग-अलग देखता है, वह उन्हीं के पीछे बिखरकर भागता है।

devanagari: यथोदकं शुद्धे शुद्धमासिक्तं तादृगेव भवति । / एवं मुनेर्विजानत आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥2.1.15॥
iast: yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddhamāsiktaṃ tādṛgeva bhavati । / evaṃ munervijānata ātmā bhavati gautama ॥2.1.15॥
sayIt: ya-tho-DA-kum SHOOD-dhay SHOOD-dham aa-SIK-tum taa-DRIG-ay-va BHA-va-ti / AY-vum moo-NAYR vi-JAA-na-ta AAT-maa BHA-va-ti GOW-ta-ma
translation: As pure water poured into pure water becomes just the same, so, Gautama, becomes the self of the sage who knows.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.1.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When your mind is at its clearest, what seam can you still find between yourself and the stillness you pour into?

translations.hi: जैसे शुद्ध पानी में उड़ेला हुआ शुद्ध पानी वैसा ही हो जाता है, वैसे ही, हे गौतम, जानने वाले मुनि की आत्मा हो जाती है।

devanagari: पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः । / अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.2.1॥
iast: puramekādaśadvāramajasyāvakracetasaḥ । / anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaśca vimucyate । / etadvai tat ॥2.2.1॥
sayIt: PU-ram ay-KAA-da-sha-DVAA-ram a-JAS-yaa-VAK-ra-CHAY-ta-sah / a-noosh-THAA-ya na SHO-cha-ti vi-MOOK-tash-cha vi-MOOCH-ya-tay / ay-TAD vai TAT
translation: The unborn one of unswerving awareness has a city of eleven gates. Contemplating its ruler, one grieves no more — and, set free, is free for good. This indeed is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If your body is a city you govern rather than a cell you are locked in, how will you walk through it today?

translations.hi: अजन्मा और कभी न टेढ़ी होने वाली चेतना वाले उस आत्मा का ग्यारह द्वारों वाला एक नगर है। उस स्वामी का ध्यान करने वाला फिर शोक नहीं करता, और मुक्त होकर सदा के लिए मुक्त हो जाता है। यही तो वह है।

devanagari: हँसः शुचिषद्वसुरान्तरिक्षसद्- / होता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् । / नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसद् / अब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत् ॥2.2.2॥
iast: ham̐saḥ śuciṣadvasurāntarikṣasad- / hotā vediṣadatithirduroṇasat । / nṛṣadvarasadṛtasadvyomasad / abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ॥2.2.2॥
sayIt: HUM-sah SHU-chi-shud va-su-RAAN-ta-rik-sha-sud / HO-taa VAY-di-shud A-ti-thir du-RO-na-sut / NRI-shud VA-ra-sud RI-ta-sud VYO-ma-sud / ub-JAA go-JAA ri-ta-JAA ad-ri-JAA RI-tum bri-HUT
translation: The swan seated in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the priest at the altar, the guest in the house; dwelling in man, in the best, in truth, in space — born of water, born of earth, born of the rite, born of the mountain — this is Rita, the vast Truth.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which ordinary seat of your day — desk, kitchen, bus — could you treat today as one more place the swan is sitting?

translations.hi: प्रकाश में बैठा हंस, अन्तरिक्ष में वसु, वेदी पर बैठा होता, घर में अतिथि; मनुष्यों में, श्रेष्ठों में, ऋत में, आकाश में बसा हुआ; जल से जन्मा, पृथ्वी से, यज्ञ से, पर्वत से जन्मा — वही है ऋत, विराट सत्य।

devanagari: ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयत्यपानं प्रत्यगस्यति । / मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते ॥2.2.3॥
iast: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇamunnayatyapānaṃ pratyagasyati । / madhye vāmanamāsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate ॥2.2.3॥
sayIt: OORD-vum PRAA-nam-un-na-yat-ya-PAA-num prat-yag-AS-ya-ti / MUD-yay VAA-ma-nam-aa-SEE-num VISH-vay DAY-vaa u-PAA-sa-tay
translation: He leads the out-breath upward and casts the in-breath downward; the dwarf seated in the middle — all the gods worship him.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: For the next three breaths, can you watch for the one who is breathing them?

translations.hi: वह प्राण को ऊपर ले जाता है और अपान को भीतर-नीचे फेंकता है; बीच में बैठे उस वामन की — उस छोटे-से विराजमान की — सब देवता उपासना करते हैं।

devanagari: अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः । / देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.2.4॥
iast: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ । / dehādvimucyamānasya kimatra pariśiṣyate । / etadvai tat ॥2.2.4॥
sayIt: AS-ya vis-rum-sa-MAA-nus-ya sha-REE-rus-thus-ya DAY-hi-nah / day-HAAD-vi-much-ya-MAA-nus-ya kim-AT-ra pa-ri-SHISH-ya-tay / ay-tud-VYE tut
translation: When this embodied one that dwells in the body comes loose and is freed from the body, what remains here? This indeed is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: If everything that can be taken from you were set aside for a moment, what do you sense would still be here?

translations.hi: शरीर में बसा यह देही जब ढीला पड़कर शरीर से मुक्त हो जाता है, तब यहाँ बचता क्या है? यही तो है वह।

devanagari: न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन । / इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ ॥2.2.5॥
iast: na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana । / itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminnetāvupāśritau ॥2.2.5॥
sayIt: na PRAA-nay-na NAA-paa-nay-na MART-yo JEE-va-ti KASH-cha-na / i-ta-RAY-na too JEE-vun-ti yus-min-nay-TAAV-u-paash-ri-TOW
translation: Not by the out-breath nor by the in-breath does any mortal live; they live by another, on which both breaths depend.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Right now, without changing your breath, can you sense what it is resting on?

translations.hi: कोई भी मरणशील न प्राण से जीता है न अपान से; सब उस दूसरे के बल पर जीते हैं, जिस पर ये दोनों साँसें टिकी हैं।

devanagari: हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् । / यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥2.2.6॥
iast: hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam । / yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama ॥2.2.6॥
sayIt: HUN-ta ta i-DUM pra-VUK-shyaa-mi GOOH-yum BRAH-ma sa-naa-TA-num / ya-THAA cha MA-ra-num PRAAP-ya AAT-maa BHA-va-ti GOW-ta-ma
translation: Come, I shall tell you this hidden, eternal Brahman — and how the self fares, Gautama, when it comes to death.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which question of yours are you finally ready to hear answered honestly?

translations.hi: अच्छा, मैं तुम्हें यह गुप्त, सनातन ब्रह्म बताता हूँ — और यह भी, गौतम, कि मृत्यु आने पर आत्मा का क्या होता है।

devanagari: योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः । / स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम् ॥2.2.7॥
iast: yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ । / sthāṇumanye'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam ॥2.2.7॥
sayIt: YO-nim-un-YAY pra-pud-YUN-tay sha-ree-rut-VAA-ya DAY-hi-nah / STHAA-num-un-YAY-nu-sum-YUN-ti ya-thaa-KAR-ma ya-thaa-SHROO-tum
translation: Some embodied beings enter a womb, to take a body; others pass into the unmoving — each according to their deeds, according to what they have learned.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What are you doing and learning today that you would be content to be carried forward by?

translations.hi: कुछ देही शरीर धारण करने के लिए गर्भ में प्रवेश करते हैं; कुछ स्थाणु — अचल रूपों — में चले जाते हैं; जैसा जिसका कर्म, जैसा जिसका ज्ञान।

devanagari: य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः । / तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते । / तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.2.8॥
iast: ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ । / tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate । / tasmim̐llokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana । / etadvai tat ॥2.2.8॥
sayIt: ya AY-sha soop-TAY-shu JAA-gar-ti KAA-mum KAA-mum PU-ru-sho nir-mi-MAA-nah / ta-DAY-va SHOOK-rum tud-BRAH-ma ta-day-VAAM-ri-tum-OOCH-ya-tay / tus-MIL-lo-kaah shri-TAAH SAR-vay ta-du NAAT-yay-ti KASH-cha-na / ay-tud-VYE tut
translation: The person who stays awake in those who sleep, shaping desire after desire — that indeed is the Pure, that is Brahman, that alone is called the Immortal. On it all the worlds rest; none whatever goes beyond it. This indeed is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Tonight, as you fall asleep, can you notice the one who will keep watch?

translations.hi: जो सोते हुओं में जागता रहता है — कामना-पर-कामना गढ़ता हुआ पुरुष — वही शुद्ध है, वही ब्रह्म है, वही अमृत कहलाता है। उसी पर सारे लोक टिके हैं; उसके पार कोई नहीं जाता। यही तो है वह।

devanagari: अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो / रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव । / एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा / रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥2.2.9॥
iast: agniryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo / rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva । / ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā / rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ॥2.2.9॥
sayIt: AG-nir-ya-THYE-ko BHU-va-num pra-VISH-to / ROO-pum ROO-pum pra-ti-ROO-po ba-BHOO-va / AY-kus-ta-THAA sar-va-bhoo-TAAN-ta-RAAT-maa / ROO-pum ROO-pum pra-ti-ROO-po ba-HISH-cha
translation: As the one fire, having entered the world, takes a shape to match every shape, so the one inner Self of all beings matches the shape of everything it enters — and stands outside them all.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Where today did one thing wear many shapes in front of you?

translations.hi: जैसे एक ही अग्नि जगत में प्रवेश करके हर रूप के अनुरूप रूप धर लेती है, वैसे ही समस्त प्राणियों का एक अन्तरात्मा हर रूप के अनुरूप हो जाता है — और उन सबके बाहर भी है।

devanagari: वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो / रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव । / एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा / रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥2.2.10॥
iast: vāyuryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo / rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva । / ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā / rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ॥2.2.10॥
sayIt: VAA-yur-ya-THYE-ko BHU-va-num pra-VISH-to / ROO-pum ROO-pum pra-ti-ROO-po ba-BHOO-va / AY-kus-ta-THAA sar-va-bhoo-TAAN-ta-RAAT-maa / ROO-pum ROO-pum pra-ti-ROO-po ba-HISH-cha
translation: As the one air, having entered the world, takes a shape to match every shape, so the one inner Self of all beings matches the shape of everything it enters — and stands outside them all.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What in your day, like air, is present in every shape yet belongs to none of them?

translations.hi: जैसे एक ही वायु जगत में प्रवेश करके हर रूप के अनुरूप रूप धर लेती है, वैसे ही समस्त प्राणियों का एक अन्तरात्मा हर रूप के अनुरूप हो जाता है — और उन सबके बाहर भी है।

devanagari: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुः / न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः । / एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा / न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥2.2.11॥
iast: sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣuḥ / na lipyate cākṣuṣairbāhyadoṣaiḥ । / ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā / na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ ॥2.2.11॥
sayIt: SOOR-yo ya-THAA sar-va-LO-kus-ya CHUK-shuh / na LIP-ya-tay chaak-shu-SHIRE baah-ya-DO-shy-hee / AY-kus-ta-THAA sar-va-bhoo-TAAN-ta-RAAT-maa / na LIP-ya-tay lo-ka-DUH-khay-na BAAH-yah
translation: As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the outer flaws that eyes see, so the one inner Self of all beings is not stained by the world's sorrow — it stands outside it.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: The next time sorrow visits, can you also notice the light it is appearing in?

translations.hi: जैसे सूर्य — सारे जगत की आँख — आँखों से दिखने वाले बाहरी दोषों से लिप्त नहीं होता, वैसे ही समस्त प्राणियों का एक अन्तरात्मा जगत के दुःख से लिप्त नहीं होता — वह उसके बाहर है।

devanagari: एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा / एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति । / तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीराः / तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम् ॥2.2.12॥
iast: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā / ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti । / tamātmasthaṃ ye'nupaśyanti dhīrāḥ / teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ॥2.2.12॥
sayIt: AY-ko va-SHEE sar-va-bhoo-TAAN-ta-RAAT-maa / AY-kum ROO-pum ba-hu-DHAA yah ka-RO-ti / tum-aat-mus-THUM yay-nu-PASH-yun-ti DHEE-raah / TAY-shaam SU-khum SHAASH-va-tum NAY-ta-ray-shaam
translation: The one ruler, the inner Self of all beings, who makes his one form manifold — the wise who see him abiding in themselves, theirs is lasting happiness; it belongs to no one else.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Where are you still expecting lasting happiness from something that changes?

translations.hi: एक वशी — सबका स्वामी — समस्त प्राणियों का अन्तरात्मा, जो अपने एक रूप को अनेक कर देता है; जो धीर उसे अपने भीतर बसा देखते हैं, स्थायी सुख उन्हीं का है — औरों का नहीं।

devanagari: नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानाम् / एको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् । / तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीराः / तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम् ॥2.2.13॥
iast: nityo'nityānāṃ cetanaścetanānām / eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān । / tamātmasthaṃ ye'nupaśyanti dhīrāḥ / teṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ॥2.2.13॥
sayIt: NIT-yo-nit-YAA-naam CHAY-ta-nash-chay-ta-NAA-naam / AY-ko ba-HOO-naam yo vi-da-DHAA-ti KAA-maan / tum-aat-mus-THUM yay-nu-PASH-yun-ti DHEE-raah / TAY-shaam SHAAN-tih shaash-va-TEE NAY-ta-ray-shaam
translation: The eternal among things that pass, the conscious among the conscious, the One among the many who provides for their desires — the wise who see him abiding in themselves, theirs is lasting peace; it belongs to no one else.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What would change today if you treated peace as something to see, not something to arrange?

translations.hi: अनित्यों के बीच नित्य, चेतनों के बीच चेतन, अनेकों के बीच वह एक — जो सबकी कामनाएँ पूरी करता है; जो धीर उसे अपने भीतर बसा देखते हैं, शाश्वत शान्ति उन्हीं की है — औरों की नहीं।

devanagari: तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम् । / कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा ॥2.2.14॥
iast: tadetaditi manyante'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham । / kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyāṃ kimu bhāti vibhāti vā ॥2.2.14॥
sayIt: tud-AY-tud-I-ti mun-YUN-tay-nir-DAYSH-yum PA-ra-mum su-KHUM / ka-THUM nu tud-vi-jaa-NEE-yaam ki-mu BHAA-ti vi-BHAA-ti vaa
translation: "This is That" — so they sense the highest joy, which cannot be pointed out. How then shall I know it? Does it shine of itself, or does it shine by reflection?
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What is one question you have been decorating instead of asking plainly?

translations.hi: "यह है वह" — ऐसा वे उस परम सुख को अनुभव करते हैं, जिसकी ओर उँगली नहीं उठ सकती। पर मैं उसे जानूँ कैसे? क्या वह स्वयं चमकता है, या प्रतिबिम्ब की तरह चमकता है?

devanagari: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं / नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । / तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं / तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥2.2.15॥
iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ / nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto'yamagniḥ । / tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ / tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ॥2.2.15॥
sayIt: na TAT-ra SOOR-yo BHAA-ti na chan-dra-TAA-ra-kum / NAY-maa VID-yu-to BHAAN-ti ku-TO-ya-MAG-nih / ta-MAY-va BHAAN-tum a-nu-BHAA-ti SAR-vum / TAS-ya BHAA-saa SAR-va-mi-dum vi-BHAA-ti
translation: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine — how then could this fire? Everything shines only after him who shines; by his light all this becomes light.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.2.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When evening comes, which of today's lights — screen, lamp, sun — reminded you of the light they all borrow?

translations.hi: वहाँ न सूर्य चमकता है, न चन्द्र-तारे; ये बिजलियाँ भी वहाँ नहीं चमकतीं — फिर इस अग्नि की क्या बिसात? सब कुछ उसी के चमकने के पीछे-पीछे चमकता है; उसी के प्रकाश से यह सब प्रकाशित है।

devanagari: ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः । / तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते । / तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । / एतद्वै तत् ॥2.3.1॥
iast: ūrdhvamūlo'vākśākha eṣo'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ । / tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate । / tasmim̐llokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana । / etadvai tat ॥2.3.1॥
sayIt: oor-dhva-MOO-lo vaak-SHAA-kha AY-shosh-VUT-thah sa-NAA-ta-nah / ta-DAY-va SHOOK-rum tud-BRUH-ma ta-day-VAAM-ri-tum-OOCH-ya-tay / tas-MIL-lo-kaah shri-TAAH SAR-vay TA-doo NAAT-yay-ti KASH-cha-na / ay-tud-VY TUT
translation: Roots above, branches below stands this everlasting aśvattha tree. That is the bright one, that is Brahman, that alone is called the immortal. All the worlds rest in it, and nothing goes beyond it. This, truly, is That.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When you look at something ordinary today — a meal, a face, a tree — can you sense the unseen root it grows from?

translations.hi: जड़ें ऊपर, शाखाएँ नीचे — ऐसा है यह सनातन अश्वत्थ वृक्ष। वही शुद्ध तेज है, वही ब्रह्म है, वही अमृत कहलाता है। सारे लोक उसी के आश्रय में टिके हैं; उसके पार कोई नहीं जाता। यही, सचमुच, वह है।

devanagari: यदिदं किं च जगत् सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम् । / महद्भयं वज्रमुद्यतं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥2.3.2॥
iast: yadidaṃ kiṃ ca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam । / mahadbhayaṃ vajramudyataṃ ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥2.3.2॥
sayIt: ya-DI-dum KIM cha JA-gat SAR-vum PRAA-na AY-ja-ti NIH-sri-tum / ma-hud-BHA-yum VUJ-rum-OOD-ya-tum ya ay-TUD-vi-door am-ri-TAAS-tay bha-VUN-ti
translation: All this — whatever this whole world is — has come forth from the life-force and trembles within it. A great awe it is, a thunderbolt raised. Those who know this become immortal.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Does it change how you move through today to think of the world's order — sunrise, breath, heartbeat — as held rather than automatic?

translations.hi: यह सारा जगत — जो कुछ भी है — प्राण से निकला है और उसी के भीतर काँपता-चलता है। वह महान भय है, उठा हुआ वज्र है। जो इसे जान लेते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः । / भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः ॥2.3.3॥
iast: bhayādasyāgnistapati bhayāttapati sūryaḥ । / bhayādindraśca vāyuśca mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ ॥2.3.3॥
sayIt: bha-YAAD as-YAAG-nis TA-pa-ti bha-YAAT TA-pa-ti SOOR-yah / bha-YAAD IN-drush-cha VAA-yoosh-cha MRIT-yoor DHAA-va-ti PUN-cha-mah
translation: From fear of him fire burns; from fear the sun gives heat; from fear Indra and the wind — and Death, the fifth of them — run to their tasks.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What feels all-powerful in your life right now — and what would change if you saw that it, too, is answerable?

translations.hi: उसके भय से अग्नि जलती है; भय से सूर्य तपता है; भय से इन्द्र और वायु, और पाँचवाँ मृत्यु — सब अपने-अपने काम में दौड़ते हैं।

devanagari: इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्षरीरस्य विस्रसः । / ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते ॥2.3.4॥
iast: iha cedaśakadboddhuṃ prākṣarīrasya visrasaḥ । / tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate ॥2.3.4॥
sayIt: i-ha CHAY-da-sha-kud BOD-dhoom praa-ksha-REE-rus-ya VIS-ra-sah / TA-tah sar-GAY-shoo lo-KAY-shoo sha-ree-rut-VAA-ya KUL-pa-tay
translation: If one can come to know it here, before the body loosens and falls away, one is freed; if not, one is made ready for a body again in the worlds of creation.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What understanding are you postponing as if its season were guaranteed to come again?

translations.hi: यदि यहीं, शरीर के ढीले पड़कर गिरने से पहले, कोई उसे जान सके, तो वह मुक्त है; न जान सके, तो सृष्टि के लोकों में फिर किसी शरीर के लिए तैयार होता है।

devanagari: यथाऽऽदर्शे तथाऽऽत्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके । / यथाऽप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके / छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके ॥2.3.5॥
iast: yathā''darśe tathā''tmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke । / yathā'psu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke / chāyātapayoriva brahmaloke ॥2.3.5॥
sayIt: ya-thaa-DAR-shay ta-THAAT-ma-ni ya-thaa SVAP-nay ta-thaa pi-tri-LO-kay / ya-THAAP-su pa-REE-va da-DRI-shay ta-thaa gan-dhar-va-LO-kay / chhaa-yaa-TA-pa-yor-i-va brah-ma-LO-kay
translation: As in a mirror, so is the Self seen in one's own being; as in a dream, so in the world of the ancestors; as a thing glimpsed wavering in water, so in the world of the gandharvas; as sharply as shadow and sunlight, so in the world of Brahma.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Where in your life are you waiting for a clearer view that is actually available right where you stand?

translations.hi: जैसे दर्पण में, वैसे अपने भीतर आत्मा दिखती है; जैसे स्वप्न में, वैसे पितृलोक में; जैसे पानी में झिलमिलाती छवि, वैसे गन्धर्वलोक में; और जैसे छाया और धूप — उतनी स्पष्ट — वैसे ब्रह्मलोक में।

devanagari: इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावमुदयास्तमयौ च यत् । / पृथगुत्पद्यमानानां मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥2.3.6॥
iast: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvamudayāstamayau ca yat । / pṛthagutpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ॥2.3.6॥
sayIt: in-dri-YAA-naam pri-thag-BHAA-vum u-da-YAAS-ta-ma-yow cha yat / pri-thag ut-pad-ya-maa-NAA-naam MAT-vaa DHEE-ro na SHO-cha-ti
translation: Knowing that the senses arise separately — each distinct from the Self — and that rising and setting belong to them, the wise one does not grieve.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which passing state — a mood, an ache, a craving — are you currently treating as if it were you?

translations.hi: यह जानकर कि इन्द्रियाँ अलग-अलग उत्पन्न होती हैं — हर एक आत्मा से भिन्न है — और उदय-अस्त उन्हीं का स्वभाव है, धीर पुरुष शोक नहीं करता।

devanagari: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् । / सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम् ॥2.3.7॥
iast: indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvamuttamam । / sattvādadhi mahānātmā mahato'vyaktamuttamam ॥2.3.7॥
sayIt: in-dri-YAYBH-yah PA-rum MA-no MA-na-sah SAT-vum UT-ta-mum / sat-VAAD A-dhi ma-HAAN AAT-maa ma-HA-to VYAK-tum UT-ta-mum
translation: Beyond the senses is the mind; above the mind, the intellect; above the intellect, the great Self; and beyond the great, the unmanifest.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When you trace one of today's reactions inward — sense, mind, judgment — how far back can you follow it?

translations.hi: इन्द्रियों से परे मन है; मन से ऊपर बुद्धि; बुद्धि से ऊपर महान् आत्मा — महत्; और महत् से भी परे अव्यक्त।

devanagari: अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च । / यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति ॥2.3.8॥
iast: avyaktāttu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako'liṅga eva ca । / yaṃ jñātvā mucyate janturamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ॥2.3.8॥
sayIt: av-yak-TAAT too PA-rah POO-roo-sho vyaa-PA-ko LIN-ga AY-va cha / yum GYAAT-vaa MOOCH-ya-tay JAN-toor am-ri-TAT-vum cha GACH-chha-ti
translation: But beyond the unmanifest is the Person — all-pervading and bearing no mark. Knowing him, a being is freed and reaches immortality.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What would change today if the highest thing you can conceive of were also the nearest?

translations.hi: पर अव्यक्त से भी परे पुरुष है — सर्वव्यापी और चिह्न-रहित। उसे जानकर जीव मुक्त हो जाता है और अमरत्व पाता है।

devanagari: न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य / न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् । / हृदा मनीषा मनसाऽभिक्लृप्तो / य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥2.3.9॥
iast: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpamasya / na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam । / hṛdā manīṣā manasā'bhiklṛpto / ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥2.3.9॥
sayIt: na sum-DRI-shay TISH-tha-ti ROO-pum AS-ya / na chak-shoo-SHAA PASH-ya-ti kash-cha-NYE-num / hri-DAA ma-NEE-shaa ma-na-SAA-bhi-KLRIP-to / ya AY-tad VI-door am-ri-TAAS-tay bha-VAN-ti
translation: His form does not stand within sight; no one sees him with the eye. He is revealed by the heart, by insight, by the mind. Those who know this become immortal.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What do you know to be real that you have never once seen with your eyes?

translations.hi: उसका रूप आँखों के सामने नहीं ठहरता; कोई उसे नेत्रों से नहीं देखता। हृदय, मनीषा और मन से ही वह प्रकट होता है। जो यह जानते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह । / बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टते तामाहुः परमां गतिम् ॥2.3.10॥
iast: yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha । / buddhiśca na viceṣṭate tāmāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim ॥2.3.10॥
sayIt: ya-DAA pun-chaa-va-TISH-thun-tay gyaa-NAA-ni ma-na-SAA SA-ha / BOOD-dhish-cha na vi-CHESH-ta-tay taam-AA-hooh pa-ra-MAAM GA-tim
translation: When the five senses of knowing stand still together with the mind, and the intellect does not stir — that, they say, is the highest state.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What is the longest your attention stood genuinely still today, and what set it moving again?

translations.hi: जब पाँचों ज्ञानेन्द्रियाँ मन के साथ ठहर जाती हैं, और बुद्धि भी नहीं चलती — उसी को परम गति कहते हैं।

devanagari: तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिरामिन्द्रियधारणाम् । / अप्रमत्तस्तदा भवति योगो हि प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥2.3.11॥
iast: tāṃ yogamiti manyante sthirāmindriyadhāraṇām । / apramattastadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau ॥2.3.11॥
sayIt: taam YO-gum I-ti man-YAN-tay sthi-RAAM in-dri-ya-dhaa-ra-NAAM / a-pra-MAT-tas ta-DAA BHA-va-ti YO-go hi pra-bha-VAAP-ya-yow
translation: That steady holding of the senses is what they call yoga. Then one becomes vigilant — for yoga can arise, and it can slip away.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: When practice goes well, do you guard it — or relax your grip and assume it will stay?

translations.hi: इन्द्रियों की उसी स्थिर धारणा को योग कहते हैं। तब साधक सजग हो जाता है — क्योंकि योग उपजता भी है और छूट भी जाता है।

devanagari: नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा । / अस्तीति ब्रुवतोऽन्यत्र कथं तदुपलभ्यते ॥2.3.12॥
iast: naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā । / astīti bruvato'nyatra kathaṃ tadupalabhyate ॥2.3.12॥
sayIt: NYE-va VAA-chaa na ma-na-SAA PRAAP-tum SHAK-yo na chak-shoo-SHAA / as-TEE-ti broo-va-TON-yat-ra KA-thum tad u-pa-LABH-ya-tay
translation: Not by speech, not by mind, not by the eye can it be reached. How can it be apprehended except from one who says: it is?
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Is there a truth you currently hold only on trust, waiting to be verified by your own experience?

translations.hi: न वाणी से, न मन से, न आँख से वह पाया जा सकता है। "वह है" — ऐसा कहने वाले से अलग, उसे कैसे पकड़ा जाए?

devanagari: अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धव्यस्तत्त्वभावेन चोभयोः । / अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धस्य तत्त्वभावः प्रसीदति ॥2.3.13॥
iast: astītyevopalabdhavyastattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ । / astītyevopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati ॥2.3.13॥
sayIt: as-TEET-yay-vo-pa-lub-DHAV-yas tat-tva-BHAA-vay-na cho-bha-YOH / as-TEET-yay-vo-pa-LUB-dhas-ya tat-tva-BHAA-vah pra-SEE-da-ti
translation: It should be grasped simply as "it is," and then in its real nature — in both ways. For one who has grasped it as "it is," its real nature dawns.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What are you demanding full proof of up front, when the seeing might only come after the staying?

translations.hi: पहले उसे सीधे "वह है" — इस रूप में पकड़ना चाहिए, फिर उसके तत्त्व-भाव में — दोनों प्रकार से। जिसने "वह है" कहकर उसे पकड़ लिया, उस पर उसका असली स्वरूप स्वयं खुलता है।

devanagari: यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः । / अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते ॥2.3.14॥
iast: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye'sya hṛdi śritāḥ । / atha martyo'mṛto bhavatyatra brahma samaśnute ॥2.3.14॥
sayIt: ya-DAA SAR-vay pra-MOOCH-yan-tay KAA-maa YAYS-ya HRI-di shri-TAAH / A-tha MART-yo-MRI-to BHA-vat-yat-ra BRAH-ma sa-MASH-noo-tay
translation: When all the desires lodged in the heart are released, then a mortal becomes immortal; here itself, one attains Brahman.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which single desire, if it quietly released its grip on your heart, would leave you most free today?

translations.hi: जब हृदय में बसी सारी कामनाएँ छूट जाती हैं, तब मरणधर्मा अमर हो जाता है; यहीं, इसी जीवन में, वह ब्रह्म को पा लेता है।

devanagari: यथा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः । / अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम् ॥2.3.15॥
iast: yathā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ । / atha martyo'mṛto bhavatyetāvaddhyanuśāsanam ॥2.3.15॥
sayIt: ya-THAA SAR-vay pra-BHID-yan-tay hri-da-yas-YAY-ha gran-tha-YAH / A-tha MART-yo-MRI-to BHA-vat-yay-TAA-vad dhya-nu-SHAA-sa-num
translation: When all the knots of the heart are cut through, here in this life, then a mortal becomes immortal. This much is the whole teaching.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Which knot — which "I am this" — feels most tightly tied in you right now?

translations.hi: जब यहाँ — इसी जीवन में — हृदय की सारी गाँठें कट जाती हैं, तब मरणधर्मा अमर हो जाता है। बस इतना ही अनुशासन है — यही पूरी शिक्षा है।

devanagari: शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्य- / स्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका । / तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति / विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवन्ति ॥2.3.16॥
iast: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍya- / stāsāṃ mūrdhānamabhiniḥsṛtaikā । / tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti / viṣvaṅṅanyā utkramaṇe bhavanti ॥2.3.16॥
sayIt: SHA-tum CHYE-kaa cha hri-da-YAS-ya NAAD-yas / TAA-saam moor-DHAA-num a-bhi-nih-sri-TYE-kaa / ta-YOR-dhvum AA-yan am-ri-TAT-vum AY-ti / vish-VANG an-YAA ut-kra-ma-NAY bha-VAN-ti
translation: A hundred and one are the channels of the heart. One of them rises to the crown of the head: passing upward by it, one reaches immortality. The others lead out in every direction.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What in your daily life is already moving upward — toward clarity rather than scatter?

translations.hi: हृदय की एक सौ एक नाड़ियाँ हैं। उनमें से एक सिर के शिखर तक जाती है: उससे ऊपर की ओर जाने वाला अमरत्व पाता है। शेष नाड़ियाँ अलग-अलग दिशाओं में निकलती हैं।

devanagari: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा / सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः । / तं स्वाच्छरीरात्प्रवृहेन्मुञ्जादिवेषीकां धैर्येण । / तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतमिति ॥2.3.17॥
iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo'ntarātmā / sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ । / taṃ svāccharīrātpravṛhenmuñjādiveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa । / taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtaṃ taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtamiti ॥2.3.17॥
sayIt: an-goosh-tha-MAA-trah POO-roo-shon-ta-RAAT-maa / sa-DAA ja-NAA-naam hri-da-YAY sum-ni-VISH-tah / tum svaach-chha-REE-raat pra-vri-HAYN moon-JAAD i-vay-SHEE-kaam DHAIR-yay-na / tum vid-yaach-CHOOK-rum am-RI-tum tum vid-yaach-CHOOK-rum am-RI-tum I-ti
translation: The Person the size of a thumb, the inner Self, is seated forever in the heart of beings. With steadiness one should draw him out from one's own body, as a reed-stalk is drawn from muñja grass. Him one should know as the pure, the immortal — him one should know as the pure, the immortal.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What gives you the patience to keep separating what you are from what you merely wear?

translations.hi: अँगूठे भर का पुरुष, अन्तरात्मा, सदा प्राणियों के हृदय में बसा है। धैर्य के साथ उसे अपने शरीर से वैसे ही अलग निकालना चाहिए जैसे मूँज घास से सींक निकाली जाती है। उसे ही शुद्ध, अमृत जानो — उसे ही शुद्ध, अमृत जानो।

devanagari: मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा / विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम् । / ब्रह्मप्राप्तो विरजोऽभूद्विमृत्यु- / रन्योऽप्येवं यो विदध्यात्ममेव ॥2.3.18॥
iast: mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo'tha labdhvā / vidyāmetāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam । / brahmaprāpto virajo'bhūdvimṛtyu- / ranyo'pyevaṃ yo vidadhyātmameva ॥2.3.18॥
sayIt: mrit-yoo-PROK-taam na-chi-KAY-to-tha LUB-dhvaa / vid-YAAM ay-TAAM yo-ga-vi-DHIM cha KRITS-num / brah-ma-PRAAP-to vi-ra-JO-bhood vi-MRIT-yoor / an-YO-pyay-vum yo vi-dadh-YAAT-mum AY-va
translation: Nachiketa, having received this knowledge declared by Death, and the whole method of yoga, attained Brahman — free of taint, free of death. So will anyone else who knows, in this way, that which concerns the Self.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.18, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: What would change if you treated Nachiketa's story not as legend but as precedent?

translations.hi: मृत्यु के कहे इस ज्ञान और योग की पूरी विधि को पाकर नचिकेता ब्रह्म को प्राप्त हुआ — निर्मल और मृत्यु से मुक्त। और जो कोई भी अध्यात्म को इसी तरह जान लेता है, उसकी भी यही गति है।

devanagari: सह नाववतु । / सह नौ भुनक्तु । / सह वीर्यं करवावहै । / तेजस्विनावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै ॥2.3.19॥
iast: saha nāvavatu । / saha nau bhunaktu । / saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai । / tejasvināvadhītamastu mā vidviṣāvahai ॥2.3.19॥
sayIt: SA-ha NAA-va-va-too / SA-ha now bhoo-NAK-too / SA-ha VEER-yum ka-ra-VAA-va-high / tay-jas-VI-naa-va-DHEE-tum AS-too maa vid-vi-SHAA-va-high
translation: May that One protect us both. May it nourish us both. May we work together with vigor. May what we study be filled with light. May we never hate one another.
source: Katha Upanishad 2.3.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Who is on the other side of your learning right now, and what would it take to study as allies?

translations.hi: वह हम दोनों की रक्षा करे। हम दोनों का पालन करे। हम दोनों मिलकर पूरी शक्ति से काम करें। हमारा पढ़ा हुआ तेजस्वी हो। हम आपस में कभी द्वेष न करें।

devanagari: ॐ सह नाववतु । / सह नौ भुनक्तु । / सहवीर्यं करवावहै । / तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु । / मा विद्विषावहै ॥ / ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥
iast: oṃ saha nāvavatu । / saha nau bhunaktu । / sahavīryaṃ karavāvahai । / tejasvi nāvadhītamastu । / mā vidviṣāvahai ॥ / oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ ॥
sayIt: om SA-ha NAA-va-va-too / SA-ha now bhoo-NUK-too / sa-ha-VEER-yum ka-ra-VAA-va-high / tay-JUS-vi naa-va-DHEE-tum-US-too / maa vid-vi-SHAA-va-high / om SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih
translation: Om. May that One protect us both — teacher and student. May it nourish us both. May we work together with vigour; may what we study be radiant with light; may we never resent one another. Om — peace, peace, peace.
source: Katha Upanishad, shanti mantra, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80
reflection: Who is learning or working alongside you right now, and what would change if you began by praying for you both?

translations.hi: ॐ। वे हम दोनों — गुरु और शिष्य — की रक्षा करें। हम दोनों का पोषण करें। हम दोनों मिलकर पूरी शक्ति से काम करें। हमारा पढ़ा हुआ तेजस्वी हो। हम आपस में कभी द्वेष न करें। ॐ शान्ति, शान्ति, शान्ति।

devanagari: ॐ केनेषितं पतति प्रेषितं मनः / केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः । / केनेषितां वाचमिमां वदन्ति / चक्षुः श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ॥1.1॥
iast: oṃ keneṣitaṃ patati preṣitaṃ manaḥ / kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ । / keneṣitāṃ vācamimāṃ vadanti / cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ka u devo yunakti ॥1.1॥
sayIt: om kay-NAY-shi-tum PA-ta-ti PRAY-shi-tum MA-nah / KAY-na PRAA-nah pra-tha-MAH PRY-ti yook-TAH / kay-NAY-shi-taam VAA-cha-mi-MAAM va-DAN-ti / CHUK-shooh SHRO-trum ka oo DAY-vo yoo-NUK-ti
translation: Sent forth by whom does the mind alight on its objects? Yoked by whom does the first breath move? Willed by whom is this speech that people speak? And what god joins the eye and the ear to their work?
source: Kena Upanishad 1.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you notice a thought arising today, can you ask what it is that notices?

translations.hi: किसकी प्रेरणा से भेजा हुआ मन अपने विषयों पर जा गिरता है? किसके जोतने से पहला प्राण चलता है? किसकी इच्छा से लोग यह वाणी बोलते हैं? और आँख और कान को कौन देवता उनके काम में जोड़ता है?

devanagari: श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रं मनसो मनो यद्वाचो ह वाचं / स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः चक्षुषश्चक्षुः | / अतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥1.2॥
iast: śrotrasya śrotraṃ manaso mano yadvāco ha vācaṃ / sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ cakṣuṣaścakṣuḥ । / atimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ॥1.2॥
sayIt: SHRO-tras-ya SHRO-trum MA-na-so MA-no yad-VAA-cho ha VAA-chum / sa oo PRAA-nas-ya PRAA-nah CHUK-shoo-shush CHUK-shooh / a-ti-MOOCH-ya DHEE-raah prayt-YAAS-maal lo-KAAD am-ri-TAA bha-VAN-ti
translation: The ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech behind speech — that is also the breath of the breath, the eye of the eye. Freeing themselves from these instruments, the wise pass beyond this world and become immortal.
source: Kena Upanishad 1.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: As you listen to someone today, can you also notice what is doing the listening?

translations.hi: जो कान का कान है, मन का मन, वाणी की वाणी — वही प्राण का प्राण है और आँख की आँख। इन उपकरणों को ही अपना स्वरूप मानना छोड़कर धीर जन इस लोक से आगे निकलकर अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: न तत्र चक्षुर्गच्छति न वाग्गच्छति नो मनः । / न विद्मो न विजानीमो यथैतदनुशिष्यात् ॥1.3॥
iast: na tatra cakṣurgacchati na vāggacchati no manaḥ । / na vidmo na vijānīmo yathaitadanuśiṣyāt ॥1.3॥
sayIt: na TAT-ra CHUK-shoor GUCH-cha-ti na VAAG GUCH-cha-ti NO MA-nah / na VID-mo na vi-jaa-NEE-mo ya-THY-tud a-noo-shish-YAAT
translation: The eye does not travel there, nor speech, nor the mind. We do not know it, we do not understand — how would one even teach it?
source: Kena Upanishad 1.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What do you know most surely in your life that you have never been able to put into words?

translations.hi: वहाँ न आँख पहुँचती है, न वाणी, न मन। हम उसे जानते नहीं, समझते भी नहीं — उसे सिखाया भी कैसे जाए?

devanagari: अन्यदेव तद्विदितादथो अविदितादधि । / इति शुश्रुम पूर्वेषां ये नस्तद्व्याचचक्षिरे ॥1.4॥
iast: anyadeva tadviditādatho aviditādadhi । / iti śuśruma pūrveṣāṃ ye nastadvyācacakṣire ॥1.4॥
sayIt: AN-ya-DAY-va tad-vi-di-TAAD-a-tho a-vi-di-TAAD-a-dhi / I-ti SHOO-shroo-ma poor-VAY-shaam YAY nas tad vyaa-cha-CHUK-shi-ray
translation: It is other than the known, and beyond the unknown as well — so we have heard from the ancients who explained it to us.
source: Kena Upanishad 1.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Whose handed-down guidance are you standing on, and when did you last acknowledge it?

translations.hi: वह ज्ञात से अलग है, और अज्ञात से भी परे — ऐसा हमने उन पूर्वजों से सुना है जिन्होंने हमें उसे समझाया।

devanagari: यद्वाचाऽनभ्युदितं येन वागभ्युद्यते । / तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥1.5॥
iast: yadvācā'nabhyuditaṃ yena vāgabhyudyate । / tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥1.5॥
sayIt: yad-VAA-chaa-nab-hyoo-di-tum YAY-na VAAG ab-HYOOD-ya-tay / tad AY-va BRAH-ma tvum VID-dhi NAY-dum yad-i-dum-oo-PAA-sa-tay
translation: That which is not uttered by speech, that by which speech itself is uttered — know that alone as Brahman, not this that people worship here.
source: Kena Upanishad 1.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Before you speak today, can you sense the silent capacity that lets the words come at all?

translations.hi: जो वाणी से कहा नहीं जाता, जिसके बल पर वाणी कही जाती है — उसी को ब्रह्म जानो; उसे नहीं, जिसकी लोग यहाँ उपासना करते हैं।

devanagari: यन्मनसा न मनुते येनाहुर्मनो मतम् । / तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥1.6॥
iast: yanmanasā na manute yenāhurmano matam । / tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥1.6॥
sayIt: yan MA-na-saa na ma-NOO-tay yay-NAA-hoor MA-no MA-tum / tad AY-va BRAH-ma tvum VID-dhi NAY-dum yad-i-dum-oo-PAA-sa-tay
translation: That which one cannot think with the mind, but by which, the wise say, the mind itself is thought — know that alone as Brahman, not this that people worship here.
source: Kena Upanishad 1.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Can you catch the difference between your next thought and the awareness that knows it?

translations.hi: जिसे मन से सोचा नहीं जा सकता, पर जिसके बल पर — ज्ञानी कहते हैं — मन स्वयं जाना जाता है, उसी को ब्रह्म जानो; उसे नहीं, जिसकी लोग यहाँ उपासना करते हैं।

devanagari: यच्चक्षुषा न पश्यति येन चक्षूँषि पश्यति । / तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥1.7॥
iast: yaccakṣuṣā na paśyati yena cakṣūm̐ṣi paśyati । / tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥1.7॥
sayIt: yach CHUK-shoo-shaa na PASH-ya-ti YAY-na chuk-SHOOM-shi PASH-ya-ti / tad AY-va BRAH-ma tvum VID-dhi NAY-dum yad-i-dum-oo-PAA-sa-tay
translation: That which the eye cannot see, but by which the eyes themselves see — know that alone as Brahman, not this that people worship here.
source: Kena Upanishad 1.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When something beautiful catches your eye today, can you notice the seeing as well as the seen?

translations.hi: जिसे आँख देख नहीं सकती, पर जिसके बल पर आँखें देखती हैं — उसी को ब्रह्म जानो; उसे नहीं, जिसकी लोग यहाँ उपासना करते हैं।

devanagari: यच्छ्रोत्रेण न शृणोति येन श्रोत्रमिदं श्रुतम् । / तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥1.8॥
iast: yacchrotreṇa na śṛṇoti yena śrotramidaṃ śrutam । / tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥1.8॥
sayIt: yach-CHRO-tray-na na shri-NO-ti YAY-na SHRO-tram i-dum SHROO-tum / tad AY-va BRAH-ma tvum VID-dhi NAY-dum yad-i-dum-oo-PAA-sa-tay
translation: That which one cannot hear with the ear, but by which this ear itself is heard — know that alone as Brahman, not this that people worship here.
source: Kena Upanishad 1.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: In the next silence you meet, what is it that hears the silence?

translations.hi: जिसे कान से सुना नहीं जा सकता, पर जिसके बल पर यह कान स्वयं जाना जाता है — उसी को ब्रह्म जानो; उसे नहीं, जिसकी लोग यहाँ उपासना करते हैं।

devanagari: यत्प्राणेन न प्राणिति येन प्राणः प्रणीयते । / तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥1.9॥
iast: yatprāṇena na prāṇiti yena prāṇaḥ praṇīyate । / tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥1.9॥
sayIt: yat PRAA-nay-na na PRAA-ni-ti YAY-na PRAA-nah pra-NEE-ya-tay / tad AY-va BRAH-ma tvum VID-dhi NAY-dum yad-i-dum-oo-PAA-sa-tay
translation: That which one cannot breathe with the breath, but by which the breath itself is led onward — know that alone as Brahman, not this that people worship here.
source: Kena Upanishad 1.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Sometime today, watch one full breath arrive and leave without your help — what allowed it?

translations.hi: जो प्राण के बल से नहीं जीता, बल्कि जिसके बल पर प्राण स्वयं चलाया जाता है — उसी को ब्रह्म जानो; उसे नहीं, जिसकी लोग यहाँ उपासना करते हैं।

devanagari: यदि मन्यसे सुवेदेति दहरमेवापि / नूनं त्वं वेत्थ ब्रह्मणो रूपम् । / यदस्य त्वं यदस्य देवेष्वथ नु / मीमाँस्येमेव ते मन्ये विदितम् ॥2.1॥
iast: yadi manyase suvedeti daharamevāpi / nūnaṃ tvaṃ vettha brahmaṇo rūpam । / yadasya tvaṃ yadasya deveṣvatha nu / mīmām̐syemeva te manye viditam ॥2.1॥
sayIt: YA-di MUN-ya-say soo-VAY-day-ti DA-ha-ram ay-VAA-pi / NOO-num tvum VAYT-tha BRAH-ma-no ROO-pum / yad US-ya tvum yad US-ya day-VAYSH-va-tha noo / mee-MAAM-syay-MAY-va tay MUN-yay vi-di-TUM
translation: If you think "I know it well," you know only a little of Brahman's form — of what it is in you, of what it is among the gods. It still calls for your inquiry. — "I think it is known."
source: Kena Upanishad 2.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Where in your life has "I already know this" quietly ended your learning?

translations.hi: अगर तुम मानते हो "मैं इसे अच्छी तरह जानता हूँ," तो ब्रह्म के रूप का बस थोड़ा-सा जाना है — जितना वह तुममें है, जितना देवताओं में। इसकी जाँच अभी बाक़ी है। — "मुझे लगता है, अब जाना।"

devanagari: नाहं मन्ये सुवेदेति नो न वेदेति वेद च । / यो नस्तद्वेद तद्वेद नो न वेदेति वेद च ॥2.2॥
iast: nāhaṃ manye suvedeti no na vedeti veda ca । / yo nastadveda tadveda no na vedeti veda ca ॥2.2॥
sayIt: NAA-hum MUN-yay soo-VAY-day-ti NO na VAY-day-ti VAY-da cha / YO nas tad VAY-da tad VAY-da NO na VAY-day-ti VAY-da cha
translation: I do not think I know it well; yet neither do I not know it — I know, and I do not. Whoever among us understands "neither unknown to me, nor fully known" — he truly knows it.
source: Kena Upanishad 2.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Is there something you understand deeply yet cannot honestly claim to "know well"?

translations.hi: मैं नहीं मानता कि मैं इसे अच्छी तरह जानता हूँ; पर ऐसा भी नहीं कि नहीं जानता — जानता भी हूँ, नहीं भी जानता। हममें से जो इस "न अनजाना, न पूरा जाना" को समझ लेता है, वही उसे सचमुच जानता है।

devanagari: यस्यामतं तस्य मतं मतं यस्य न वेद सः । / अविज्ञातं विजानतां विज्ञातमविजानताम् ॥2.3॥
iast: yasyāmataṃ tasya mataṃ mataṃ yasya na veda saḥ । / avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ vijñātamavijānatām ॥2.3॥
sayIt: yas-YAA-ma-tum TUS-ya MA-tum MA-tum YAS-ya na VAY-da sah / a-vig-YAA-tum vi-jaa-na-TAAM vig-YAA-tum a-vi-jaa-na-TAAM
translation: To whom it is not conceived, to him it is known; to whom it is conceived, he does not know it. It is unknown to those who understand it, and understood by those who do not.
source: Kena Upanishad 2.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What would change if you held your surest belief about the divine as a pointer rather than a possession?

translations.hi: जिसकी धारणा में वह नहीं समाया, उसी ने उसे जाना; जिसने धारणा बना ली, वह नहीं जानता। समझने वालों के लिए वह अनजाना है, और न समझने वालों के लिए जाना हुआ।

devanagari: प्रतिबोधविदितं मतममृतत्वं हि विन्दते । / आत्मना विन्दते वीर्यं विद्यया विन्दतेऽमृतम् ॥2.4॥
iast: pratibodhaviditaṃ matamamṛtatvaṃ hi vindate । / ātmanā vindate vīryaṃ vidyayā vindate'mṛtam ॥2.4॥
sayIt: pra-ti-BO-dha-vi-di-tum MA-tum am-ri-TUT-vum hi VIN-da-tay / AAT-ma-naa VIN-da-tay VEER-yum VID-ya-yaa VIN-da-tay-mri-tum
translation: Known in each pulse of awareness, it is truly known — for such knowing wins immortality. Through one's own self one finds strength; through knowledge one finds the deathless.
source: Kena Upanishad 2.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Can you catch, three times today, the quiet awareness present inside an ordinary moment?

translations.hi: जागरूकता की हर कौंध में जाना जाए, तभी वह सचमुच जाना गया — ऐसा जानना ही अमरता दिलाता है। अपने आत्मबल से शक्ति मिलती है, और विद्या से अमृत।

devanagari: इह चेदवेदीदथ सत्यमस्ति / न चेदिहावेदीन्महती विनष्टिः । / भूतेषु भूतेषु विचित्य धीराः / प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥2.5॥
iast: iha cedavedīdatha satyamasti / na cedihāvedīnmahatī vinaṣṭiḥ । / bhūteṣu bhūteṣu vicitya dhīrāḥ / pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ॥2.5॥
sayIt: i-ha chayd a-vay-DEED A-tha SUT-yum US-ti / na chayd i-HAA-vay-deen ma-ha-TEE vi-NASH-tih / BHOO-tay-shoo BHOO-tay-shoo vi-CHIT-ya DHEE-raah / prayt-YAAS-maal lo-KAAD am-ri-TAA bha-VAN-ti
translation: If one has known it here, then there is truth; if one has not known it here, great is the loss. Discerning it in being after being, the wise rise beyond this world and become immortal.
source: Kena Upanishad 2.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Whose eyes will you meet today, and can you recognize the same seeing behind them?

translations.hi: यदि यहीं — इसी जीवन में — उसे जान लिया, तो सत्य हाथ लगा; न जाना, तो हानि बड़ी है। प्राणी-प्राणी में उसे पहचानकर धीर जन इस लोक से ऊपर उठकर अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो / विजये देवा अमहीयन्त ॥3.1॥
iast: brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo / vijaye devā amahīyanta ॥3.1॥
sayIt: BRAH-ma ha day-VAY-bhyo vi-JIG-yay TAS-ya ha BRAH-ma-no / vi-ja-YAY day-VAA a-ma-HEE-yan-ta
translation: Brahman — so the story goes — won a victory for the gods; and in that victory of Brahman the gods grew great.
source: Kena Upanishad 3.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Whose power was really at work in your most recent success?

translations.hi: कहते हैं, ब्रह्म ने देवताओं के लिए विजय जीती; और ब्रह्म की उस विजय में देवता महिमा पा गए।

devanagari: त ऐक्षन्तास्माकमेवायं विजयोऽस्माकमेवायं महिमेति । / तद्धैषां विजज्ञौ तेभ्यो ह प्रादुर्बभूव तन्न व्यजानत / किमिदं यक्षमिति ॥3.2॥
iast: ta aikṣantāsmākamevāyaṃ vijayo'smākamevāyaṃ mahimeti । / taddhaiṣāṃ vijajñau tebhyo ha prādurbabhūva tanna vyajānata / kimidaṃ yakṣamiti ॥3.2॥
sayIt: ta ike-SHAN-taas-MAA-ka-may-VAA-yum vi-ja-YO-smaa-ka-may-VAA-yum ma-hi-MAY-ti / tad-DHIGH-shaam vi-jaj-NYOW TAY-bhyo ha praa-door-ba-BHOO-va TAN-na vya-JAA-na-ta / kim-i-DUM YAK-sham-i-ti
translation: The gods thought: "This victory is ours alone; this greatness is ours alone." Brahman knew what they were thinking and appeared before them — and they could not make it out. "What is this wondrous spirit?" they asked.
source: Kena Upanishad 3.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Where in your life have you quietly added the word "alone" to "this is mine"?

translations.hi: देवताओं ने सोचा: "यह विजय हमारी ही है, यह महिमा हमारी ही है।" ब्रह्म ने उनका यह भाव जान लिया और उनके सामने प्रकट हुआ — पर वे उसे पहचान न सके। पूछने लगे: "यह अद्भुत यक्ष कौन है?"

devanagari: तेऽग्निमब्रुवन् जातवेद एतद्विजानीहि / किमिदं यक्षमिति तथेति ॥3.3॥
iast: te'gnimabruvan jātaveda etadvijānīhi / kimidaṃ yakṣamiti tatheti ॥3.3॥
sayIt: TAY-gni-ma-broo-van JAA-ta-VAY-da ay-tad-vi-jaa-NEE-hi / kim-i-DUM YAK-sham-i-ti ta-THAY-ti
translation: They said to Agni: "Knower of all things born, find out what this spirit is." "So be it," he said.
source: Kena Upanishad 3.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you face something you cannot name, do you send your expertise ahead of your openness?

translations.hi: उन्होंने अग्नि से कहा: "जातवेद! पता लगाओ, यह यक्ष क्या है।" अग्नि बोले: "ठीक है।"

devanagari: तदभ्यद्रवत्तमभ्यवदत्कोऽसीत्यग्निर्वा / अहमस्मीत्यब्रवीज्जातवेदा वा अहमस्मीति ॥3.4॥
iast: tadabhyadravattamabhyavadatko'sītyagnirvā / ahamasmītyabravījjātavedā vā ahamasmīti ॥3.4॥
sayIt: tad-abh-ya-DRA-vat-tam-abh-ya-va-dat-KO-see-tyag-nir-VAA / a-ham-as-MEE-tyab-ra-veej-JAA-ta-VAY-daa vaa a-ham-as-MEE-ti
translation: Agni rushed toward it. The spirit asked him: "Who are you?" "I am Agni," he said, "I am Jātaveda, knower of all that is born."
source: Kena Upanishad 3.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If something asked you "who are you?" and neither your name nor your titles were allowed, what would be left to say?

translations.hi: अग्नि उसकी ओर दौड़े। यक्ष ने पूछा: "तुम कौन हो?" उन्होंने कहा: "मैं अग्नि हूँ, मैं जातवेद हूँ — हर जन्मे हुए का ज्ञाता।"

devanagari: तस्मिँस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमित्यपीदँ सर्वं / दहेयं यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥3.5॥
iast: tasmim̐stvayi kiṃ vīryamityapīdam̐ sarvaṃ / daheyaṃ yadidaṃ pṛthivyāmiti ॥3.5॥
sayIt: tas-MIMS-tva-yi kim VEER-ya-mi-tya-PEE-dum SAR-vum / da-HAY-yum ya-di-DUM pri-thi-VYAA-mi-ti
translation: "What power is there in such a one as you?" "I could burn all this — whatever there is upon the earth."
source: Kena Upanishad 3.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which of your powers do you describe in total terms — "I could handle anything" — and who lent it to you?

translations.hi: "तुम-जैसे में क्या सामर्थ्य है?" "मैं यह सब जला सकता हूँ — पृथ्वी पर जो कुछ भी है।"

devanagari: तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतद्दहेति । / तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाक दग्धुं स तत एव / निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥3.6॥
iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāvetaddaheti । / tadupapreyāya sarvajavena tanna śaśāka dagdhuṃ sa tata eva / nivavṛte naitadaśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yadetadyakṣamiti ॥3.6॥
sayIt: tas-MY TRI-num ni-da-DHAA-vay-tad-da-HAY-ti / tad-oo-pa-PRAY-yaa-ya sar-va-ja-VAY-na TAN-na sha-SHAA-ka DAG-dhum sa ta-ta AY-va / ni-va-VRI-tay nigh-ta-da-SHA-kum vij-NYAA-tum ya-day-tad-YAK-sham-i-ti
translation: The spirit set a blade of grass before him: "Burn this." He went at it with all his speed — and could not burn it. He turned back from there: "I could not find out what this spirit is."
source: Kena Upanishad 3.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What is your blade of grass — the small thing that keeps refusing your full strength?

translations.hi: यक्ष ने उनके सामने एक तिनका रख दिया: "इसे जलाओ।" अग्नि पूरे वेग से उस पर झपटे — पर उसे जला न सके। वहीं से लौट गए: "मैं पता नहीं लगा सका कि यह यक्ष क्या है।"

devanagari: अथ वायुमब्रुवन्वायवेतद्विजानीहि / किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति ॥3.7॥
iast: atha vāyumabruvanvāyavetadvijānīhi / kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti ॥3.7॥
sayIt: a-tha VAA-yoo-mab-roo-van-VAA-ya-vay-tad-vi-jaa-NEE-hi / kim-ay-tad-YAK-sham-i-ti ta-THAY-ti
translation: Then they said to Vāyu: "Vāyu, find out what this spirit is." "So be it," he said.
source: Kena Upanishad 3.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When your first approach fails, do you change the approach or only the person trying it?

translations.hi: फिर उन्होंने वायु से कहा: "वायु! पता लगाओ, यह यक्ष क्या है।" वायु बोले: "ठीक है।"

devanagari: तदभ्यद्रवत्तमभ्यवदत्कोऽसीति वायुर्वा / अहमस्मीत्यब्रवीन्मातरिश्वा वा अहमस्मीति ॥3.8॥
iast: tadabhyadravattamabhyavadatko'sīti vāyurvā / ahamasmītyabravīnmātariśvā vā ahamasmīti ॥3.8॥
sayIt: tad-abh-ya-DRA-vat-tam-abh-ya-va-dat-KO-see-ti vaa-YOOR-vaa / a-ham-as-MEE-tyab-ra-veen-MAA-ta-rish-VAA vaa a-ham-as-MEE-ti
translation: He rushed toward it. It asked him: "Who are you?" "I am Vāyu," he said, "I am Mātariśvan, who moves in the womb of space."
source: Kena Upanishad 3.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Apart from what you do all day, what would you say you are?

translations.hi: वायु उसकी ओर दौड़े। यक्ष ने पूछा: "तुम कौन हो?" उन्होंने कहा: "मैं वायु हूँ, मैं मातरिश्वा हूँ — आकाश की गोद में चलने वाला।"

devanagari: तस्मिँस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमित्यपीदँ / सर्वमाददीय यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥3.9॥
iast: tasmim̐stvayi kiṃ vīryamityapīdam̐ / sarvamādadīya yadidaṃ pṛthivyāmiti ॥3.9॥
sayIt: tas-MIMS-tva-yi kim VEER-ya-mi-tya-PEE-dum / sar-va-MAA-da-DEE-ya ya-di-DUM pri-thi-VYAA-mi-ti
translation: "What power is there in such a one as you?" "I could carry off all this — whatever there is upon the earth."
source: Kena Upanishad 3.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Is there a claim you make about yourself that is true of your role but not of you?

translations.hi: "तुम-जैसे में क्या सामर्थ्य है?" "मैं यह सब उठा ले जा सकता हूँ — पृथ्वी पर जो कुछ भी है।"

devanagari: तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतदादत्स्वेति / तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाकादतुम् | / स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥3.10॥
iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāvetadādatsveti / tadupapreyāya sarvajavena tanna śaśākādatum । / sa tata eva nivavṛte naitadaśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yadetadyakṣamiti ॥3.10॥
sayIt: tas-MY TRI-num ni-da-DHAA-vay-ta-DAA-dat-SVAY-ti / tad-oo-pa-PRAY-yaa-ya sar-va-ja-VAY-na TAN-na sha-SHAA-kaa-da-tum / sa ta-ta AY-va ni-va-VRI-tay nigh-ta-da-SHA-kum vij-NYAA-tum ya-day-tad-YAK-sham-i-ti
translation: It set a blade of grass before him: "Take this up." He went at it with all his speed — and could not lift it. He turned back from there: "I could not find out what this spirit is."
