source: Kena Upanishad 3.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When did you last say, out loud and without excuses, "I could not do it"?

translations.hi: यक्ष ने उनके सामने एक तिनका रख दिया: "इसे उठा लो।" वायु पूरे वेग से उस पर झपटे — पर उसे हिला न सके। वहीं से लौट गए: "मैं पता नहीं लगा सका कि यह यक्ष क्या है।"

devanagari: अथेन्द्रमब्रुवन्मघवन्नेतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति / तदभ्यद्रवत्तस्मात्तिरोदधे ॥3.11॥
iast: athendramabruvanmaghavannetadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti / tadabhyadravattasmāttirodadhe ॥3.11॥
sayIt: a-THAYN-dra-mab-roo-van-MA-gha-van-nay-tad-vi-jaa-NEE-hi kim-ay-tad-YAK-sham-i-ti ta-THAY-ti / tad-abh-ya-DRA-vat-tas-MAAT-ti-ro-da-DHAY
translation: Then they said to Indra: "Maghavan, find out what this spirit is." "So be it," he said, and rushed toward it — and it vanished from before him.
source: Kena Upanishad 3.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When an answer vanishes on you, do you leave with the crowd or stay in the empty sky?

translations.hi: फिर उन्होंने इंद्र से कहा: "मघवन्! पता लगाओ, यह यक्ष क्या है।" "ठीक है" कहकर इंद्र उसकी ओर दौड़े — और यक्ष उनके सामने से अंतर्धान हो गया।

devanagari: स तस्मिन्नेवाकाशे स्त्रियमाजगाम बहुशोभमानामुमाँ / हैमवतीं ताँहोवाच किमेतद्यक्षमिति ॥3.12॥
iast: sa tasminnevākāśe striyamājagāma bahuśobhamānāmumām̐ / haimavatīṃ tām̐hovāca kimetadyakṣamiti ॥3.12॥
sayIt: sa tas-min-nay-VAA-kaa-shay stri-ya-MAA-ja-GAA-ma ba-hoo-sho-bha-MAA-naa-moo-MAAM / high-ma-va-TEEM TAAM-ho-VAA-cha kim-ay-tad-YAK-sham-i-ti
translation: There, in that very sky, he came upon a woman of great radiance — Umā, daughter of the snow mountain. He asked her: "What is this spirit?"
source: Kena Upanishad 3.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When your effort fails and the sky is empty, can you wait there long enough for grace to speak?

translations.hi: उसी आकाश में उन्हें एक परम कांतिमयी स्त्री मिलीं — हिमालय-पुत्री उमा। इंद्र ने उन्हीं से पूछा: "यह यक्ष क्या है?"

devanagari: सा ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद्विजये महीयध्वमिति / ततो हैव विदाञ्चकार ब्रह्मेति ॥4.1॥
iast: sā brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etadvijaye mahīyadhvamiti / tato haiva vidāñcakāra brahmeti ॥4.1॥
sayIt: saa brah-MAY-ti ho-VAA-cha BRAH-ma-no vaa ay-tad-vi-ja-YAY ma-HEE-yadh-va-mi-ti / ta-TO HIGH-va vi-DAAN-cha-KAA-ra brah-MAY-ti
translation: She said: "It is Brahman. In Brahman's victory it is you who are exalted." From that alone Indra knew: it is Brahman.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which "mine" in your vocabulary is most overdue for the correction Umā made?

translations.hi: उमा ने कहा: "वह ब्रह्म है। ब्रह्म की उस विजय में ही तुम सब महिमा पा रहे हो।" उसी वचन से इंद्र ने जान लिया: वह ब्रह्म है।

devanagari: तस्माद्वा एते देवा अतितरामिवान्यान्देवान्यदग्निर्वायुरिन्द्रस्ते / ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्शुस्ते ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदाञ्चकार ब्रह्मेति ॥4.2॥
iast: tasmādvā ete devā atitarāmivānyāndevānyadagnirvāyurindraste / hyenannediṣṭhaṃ pasparśuste hyenatprathamo vidāñcakāra brahmeti ॥4.2॥
sayIt: tas-MAAD-vaa ay-TAY day-VAA a-ti-ta-RAA-mi-VAAN-yaan-day-VAAN-ya-dag-nir-VAA-yoo-rin-dras-tay / hyay-nan-nay-DISH-tum pas-par-SHOOS-tay hyay-nat-pra-tha-MO vi-DAAN-cha-KAA-ra brah-MAY-ti
translation: Therefore these gods — Agni, Vāyu, and Indra — surpass the other gods, as it were; for they touched it nearest, and they first knew it as Brahman.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Has a failure ever brought you nearer to the truth than your successes did?

translations.hi: इसीलिए ये देवता — अग्नि, वायु और इंद्र — मानो दूसरे देवताओं से बढ़कर हैं; क्योंकि उन्होंने ही उसे सबसे निकट से छुआ, और उन्होंने ही सबसे पहले जाना कि वह ब्रह्म है।

devanagari: तस्माद्वा इन्द्रोऽतितरामिवान्यान्देवान् / सह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्श स ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदाञ्चकार ब्रह्मेति ॥4.3॥
iast: tasmādvā indro'titarāmivānyāndevān / sahyenannediṣṭhaṃ pasparśa sa hyenatprathamo vidāñcakāra brahmeti ॥4.3॥
sayIt: tas-MAAD-vaa IN-dro-ti-ta-RAA-mi-VAAN-yaan-day-VAAN / sa-hyay-nan-nay-DISH-tum pas-PAR-sha sa hyay-nat-pra-tha-MO vi-DAAN-cha-KAA-ra brah-MAY-ti
translation: And therefore Indra surpasses the other gods, as it were; for he touched it nearest, and he first knew it as Brahman.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Do you value what you seized more than what you were patiently taught?

translations.hi: और इसीलिए इंद्र मानो दूसरे देवताओं से बढ़कर हैं; क्योंकि उन्होंने ही उसे सबसे निकट से छुआ, और उन्होंने ही सबसे पहले जाना कि वह ब्रह्म है।

devanagari: तस्यैष आदेशो यदेतद्विद्युतो व्यद्युतदा३ / footnoteExtra `aa'kaar is used in the sense of comparison / इतीन् न्यमीमिषदा३ / इत्यधिदैवतम् ॥4.4॥
iast: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yadetadvidyuto vyadyutadā3 / itīn nyamīmiṣadā3 / ityadhidaivatam ॥4.4॥
sayIt: tas-YIGH-sha aa-DAY-sho ya-day-tad-VID-yoo-to vyad-yoo-ta-DAAA / i-TEEN nya-mee-mi-sha-DAAA / i-tya-dhi-DIGH-va-tum
translation: This is its teaching-sign: it is as when lightning flashes forth — ah, like that! — as when the eye blinks — like that! This, with reference to the divine.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Can you catch one lightning-quick moment of pure seeing today before thought closes over it?

translations.hi: उसका संकेत यह है: जैसे बिजली कौंध जाए — बस वैसा! — जैसे पलक झपक जाए — वैसा! यह हुआ देव-जगत की ओर से संकेत।

devanagari: अथाध्यात्मं यद्देतद्गच्छतीव च मनोऽनेन / चैतदुपस्मरत्यभीक्ष्णँ सङ्कल्पः ॥4.5॥
iast: athādhyātmaṃ yaddetadgacchatīva ca mano'nena / caitadupasmaratyabhīkṣṇam̐ saṅkalpaḥ ॥4.5॥
sayIt: a-THAADH-yaat-mum yad-day-tad-gach-cha-TEE-va cha ma-NO-nay-na / chigh-ta-doo-pas-ma-ra-tya-BHEEKSH-num san-KAL-pah
translation: Now with reference to the self: it is what the mind seems to move toward; by the mind one remembers it again and again; and intention keeps returning to it.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Each time your mind darts somewhere today, can you notice what it is that set it moving?

translations.hi: अब भीतर का संकेत: वह वही है जिसकी ओर मन मानो जाता है; मन से ही उसे बार-बार याद किया जाता है; और संकल्प बार-बार उसी की ओर मुड़ता है।

devanagari: तद्ध तद्वनं नाम तद्वनमित्युपासितव्यं स य एतदेवं वेदाभि / हैनँ सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाञ्छन्ति ॥4.6॥
iast: taddha tadvanaṃ nāma tadvanamityupāsitavyaṃ sa ya etadevaṃ vedābhi / hainam̐ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāñchanti ॥4.6॥
sayIt: TAD-dha TAD-va-num NAA-ma TAD-va-na-mi-tyoo-PAA-si-tav-yum sa ya ay-ta-DAY-vum vay-DAA-bhi / HIGH-num SAR-vaa-ni BHOO-taa-ni sam-VAAN-chhan-ti
translation: It is named Tadvanam — "That toward which all longing turns" — and as Tadvanam it should be revered; whoever knows it so, all beings long for him.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What are your longings really longing for, behind the things they land on?

translations.hi: उसका नाम है "तद्वनम्" — वह, जिसकी ओर हर चाह मुड़ती है — और इसी रूप में उसकी उपासना करनी चाहिए; जो उसे ऐसा जानता है, सारे प्राणी उसी को चाहने लगते हैं।

devanagari: उपनिषदं भो ब्रूहीत्युक्ता त उपनिषद्ब्राह्मीं वाव त / उपनिषदमब्रूमेति ॥4.7॥
iast: upaniṣadaṃ bho brūhītyuktā ta upaniṣadbrāhmīṃ vāva ta / upaniṣadamabrūmeti ॥4.7॥
sayIt: oo-pa-ni-sha-DUM bho broo-HEE-tyook-TAA ta oo-pa-ni-shad-BRAAH-meem VAA-va ta / oo-pa-ni-sha-da-mab-ROO-may-ti
translation: "Sir, teach me the Upanishad." "The Upanishad has been told to you: we have told you the Upanishad of Brahman itself."
source: Kena Upanishad 4.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Is there a teaching you already hold that you keep treating as a preview of some fuller one?

translations.hi: "भगवन्, मुझे उपनिषद कहिए।" "उपनिषद तुमसे कही जा चुकी; हमने तुम्हें ब्रह्म-विषयक उपनिषद कह ही दी है।"

devanagari: तसै तपो दमः कर्मेति प्रतिष्ठा वेदाः सर्वाङ्गानि / सत्यमायतनम् ॥4.8॥
iast: tasai tapo damaḥ karmeti pratiṣṭhā vedāḥ sarvāṅgāni / satyamāyatanam ॥4.8॥
sayIt: ta-SIGH TA-po DA-mah KAR-may-ti pra-tish-THAA VAY-daah sar-VAANG-gaa-ni / sat-ya-MAA-ya-ta-num
translation: Austerity, self-restraint, and work are its foundation; the Vedas are all its limbs; truth is its dwelling place.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which of the three supports — austerity, restraint, honest work — is weakest under your practice right now?

translations.hi: तप, संयम और कर्म उसकी नींव हैं; वेद उसके सारे अंग हैं; सत्य उसका घर है।

devanagari: यो वा एतामेवं वेदापहत्य पाप्मानमनन्ते स्वर्गे / लोके ज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति ॥4.9॥
iast: yo vā etāmevaṃ vedāpahatya pāpmānamanante svarge / loke jyeye pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati ॥4.9॥
sayIt: yo vaa ay-TAA-may-vum vay-DAA-pa-HAT-ya paap-MAA-na-ma-NAN-tay SVAR-gay / LO-kay JYAY-yay pra-ti-TISH-tha-ti pra-ti-TISH-tha-ti
translation: Whoever knows it thus, shaking off evil, stands firm at the last in the boundless, unsurpassed world of heaven — stands firm indeed.
source: Kena Upanishad 4.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What would standing firm — in something that cannot be taken from you — look like in your week ahead?

translations.hi: जो इसे ऐसा जानता है, वह पाप को झाड़कर अंत में उस असीम, सर्वोच्च स्वर्ग-लोक में प्रतिष्ठित हो जाता है — सचमुच प्रतिष्ठित हो जाता है।

devanagari: ॐ आप्यायन्तु ममाङ्गानि वाक्प्राणश्चक्षुः / श्रोत्रमथो बलमिन्द्रियाणि च सर्वाणि । / सर्वं ब्रह्मौपनिषदं / माऽहं ब्रह्म निराकुर्यां मा मा ब्रह्म / निराकरोदनिराकरणमस्त्वनिराकरणं मेऽस्तु । / तदात्मनि निरते य / उपनिषत्सु धर्मास्ते मयि सन्तु ते मयि सन्तु । / ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः
iast: oṃ āpyāyantu mamāṅgāni vākprāṇaścakṣuḥ / śrotramatho balamindriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi । / sarvaṃ brahmaupaniṣadaṃ / mā'haṃ brahma nirākuryāṃ mā mā brahma / nirākarodanirākaraṇamastvanirākaraṇaṃ me'stu । / tadātmani nirate ya / upaniṣatsu dharmāste mayi santu te mayi santu । / oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
sayIt: om aap-YAA-yan-too ma-MAAN-gaa-ni vaak-praa-NASH-chuk-shooh / SHRO-tra-ma-tho ba-la-min-dri-YAA-ni cha sar-VAA-ni / SAR-vum brah-MOW-pa-ni-sha-dum / MAA-hum BRAH-ma ni-raa-KOOR-yaam maa maa BRAH-ma / ni-raa-ka-RO-da-ni-raa-KA-ra-na-mas-tva-ni-raa-KA-ra-num MAY-stoo / ta-DAAT-ma-ni ni-ra-TAY ya / oo-pa-ni-SHUT-soo dhar-MAAS-tay MA-yi SUN-too tay MA-yi SUN-too / om SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih
translation: May my limbs grow strong, and my speech, breath, eye, ear, and all my senses gain strength. All this is the Brahman of the Upanishads. May I never deny Brahman; may Brahman never deny me. Let there be no rejection — let there at least be no rejection from my side. May the truths that live in the Upanishads live in me, who delight in the Self. Om, peace, peace, peace.
source: Kena Upanishad, shanti mantra, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Before you learn anything today, what would it mean to ask that you not turn away from the truth — and that it not turn away from you?

translations.hi: मेरे अंग पुष्ट हों — वाणी, प्राण, आँख, कान और सारी इंद्रियाँ बलवती हों। यह सब उपनिषदों का ब्रह्म है। मैं ब्रह्म को कभी अस्वीकार न करूँ, और ब्रह्म मुझे अस्वीकार न करे। अस्वीकार हो ही नहीं — कम से कम मेरी ओर से अस्वीकार न हो। आत्मा में रमे हुए मुझमें उपनिषदों के धर्म बसें — मुझमें बसें। ॐ शांति, शांति, शांति।

devanagari: ओमित्येतदक्षरमिदँसर्वं तस्योपव्याख्यानभूतं भवद् भविष्यदिति सर्वमोङ्कार एव। / यच्चान्यत् त्रिकालातीतं तदप्योङ्कार एव ॥1॥
iast: omityetadakṣaramidam̐sarvaṃ tasyopavyākhyānabhūtaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyaditi sarvamoṅkāra eva। / yaccānyat trikālātītaṃ tadapyoṅkāra eva ॥1॥
sayIt: o-MIT-yay-tad UK-sha-ra-mi-DUM SAR-vum TAS-yo-pa-vyaa-KHYAA-num BHOO-tum BHA-vad bha-VISH-ya-DI-ti SAR-va-MONG-kaa-ra AY-va / yach-CHAAN-yat tri-kaa-LAA-tee-TUM ta-dap-YONG-kaa-ra AY-va
translation: Om — this syllable is all this. Its explanation: what was, what is, and what will be — all of it is simply Om; and whatever else lies beyond the three times, that too is simply Om.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If everything you will meet today is contained in one syllable, what changes when you say it slowly once?

translations.hi: ॐ — यह अक्षर ही यह सब कुछ है। इसकी व्याख्या: जो हो चुका, जो हो रहा है, और जो होगा — वह सब ओंकार ही है; और जो कुछ तीनों कालों के पार है, वह भी ओंकार ही है।

devanagari: सर्वं ह्येतद् ब्रह्मायमात्मा ब्रह्म सोऽयमात्मा चतुष्पात् ॥2॥
iast: sarvaṃ hyetad brahmāyamātmā brahma so'yamātmā catuṣpāt ॥2॥
sayIt: SAR-vum HYAY-tud brah-MAA-ya-MAAT-maa BRAH-ma SO-ya-MAAT-maa cha-toosh-PAAT
translation: All this is indeed Brahman. This self is Brahman. And this same self has four quarters.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you say the word "I", which of the day's many states of yourself do you mean?

translations.hi: यह सब निश्चय ही ब्रह्म है। यह आत्मा ब्रह्म है। और यही आत्मा चार पादों वाला है।

devanagari: जागरितस्थानो बहिःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः स्थूलभुग्वैश्वानरः प्रथमः पादः ॥3॥
iast: jāgaritasthāno bahiḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ sthūlabhugvaiśvānaraḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ ॥3॥
sayIt: JAA-ga-ri-ta-STHAA-no ba-hih-PRAG-yah sap-TAANG-ga ay-KO-na-vim-sha-ti-MOO-khah STHOO-la-bhoog vysh-VAA-na-rah pra-tha-MAH PAA-dah
translation: The first quarter is Vaishvanara — his field the waking state, his awareness turned outward, seven-limbed, nineteen-mouthed, an enjoyer of gross things.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Today, in the middle of being busy and awake, can you remember once that this outward-facing self is only one quarter of you?

translations.hi: पहला पाद वैश्वानर है — उसका क्षेत्र जाग्रत अवस्था, उसकी चेतना बाहर की ओर, सात अंगों और उन्नीस मुखों वाला, स्थूल का भोक्ता।

devanagari: स्वप्नस्थानोऽन्तःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजसो द्वितीयः पादः ॥4॥
iast: svapnasthāno'ntaḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ praviviktabhuktaijaso dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ॥4॥
sayIt: SVAP-na-STHAA-non-tah-PRAG-yah sap-TAANG-ga ay-KO-na-vim-sha-ti-MOO-khah pra-vi-VIK-ta-bhook TIE-ja-so dvi-TEE-yah PAA-dah
translation: The second quarter is Taijasa — his field the dream state, his awareness turned inward, seven-limbed, nineteen-mouthed, an enjoyer of the subtle.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you wake tomorrow, can you notice the exact moment one complete world is exchanged for another?

translations.hi: दूसरा पाद तैजस है — उसका क्षेत्र स्वप्न अवस्था, उसकी चेतना भीतर की ओर, सात अंगों और उन्नीस मुखों वाला, सूक्ष्म का भोक्ता।

devanagari: यत्र सुप्तो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते न कञ्चन स्वप्नं पश्यति तत् सुषुप्तम् । / सुषुप्तस्थान एकीभूतः प्रज्ञानघन एवानन्दमयो ह्यानन्दभुक् चेतोमुखः प्राज्ञस्तृतीयः पादः ॥5॥
iast: yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṃ paśyati tat suṣuptam । / suṣuptasthāna ekībhūtaḥ prajñānaghana evānandamayo hyānandabhuk cetomukhaḥ prājñastṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ ॥5॥
sayIt: YA-tra SOOP-to na KUN-cha-na KAA-mum KAA-ma-ya-tay na KUN-cha-na SVAP-num PASH-ya-ti tat soo-SHOOP-tum / soo-SHOOP-ta-STHAA-na ay-KEE-bhoo-tah prag-YAA-na-gha-na ay-VAA-nun-da-ma-yo HYAA-nun-da-bhook CHAY-to-moo-khah PRAAG-yas tri-TEE-yah PAA-dah
translation: Where the sleeper desires no desire and sees no dream — that is deep sleep. The third quarter is Prajna: his field is deep sleep; in him all is gathered into one; he is a solid mass of knowing, made of bliss, an enjoyer of bliss, with consciousness for his doorway.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What was present last night in your deepest sleep, when nothing else was?

translations.hi: जहाँ सोया हुआ न कोई कामना करता है, न कोई स्वप्न देखता है — वह सुषुप्ति है। तीसरा पाद प्राज्ञ है: उसका क्षेत्र गहरी नींद; उसमें सब कुछ एक हो जाता है; वह प्रज्ञान का ठोस पुंज है, आनन्दमय, आनन्द का भोक्ता, और चेतना ही उसका द्वार है।

devanagari: एष सर्वेश्वर एष सर्वज्ञ एषोऽन्तर्याम्येष योनिः सर्वस्य प्रभवाप्ययौ हि भूतानाम् ॥6॥
iast: eṣa sarveśvara eṣa sarvajña eṣo'ntaryāmyeṣa yoniḥ sarvasya prabhavāpyayau hi bhūtānām ॥6॥
sayIt: AY-sha sar-VAYSH-va-ra AY-sha sar-VAG-ya AY-shon-tar-YAAM-yay-sha YO-nih SAR-vas-ya pra-bha-VAAP-ya-yow hi bhoo-TAA-naam
translation: This is the Lord of all; this is the knower of all; this is the inner controller; this is the womb of all — for it is the origin and the dissolution of beings.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If the same inner controller waits in everyone's sleep, how will you look at the next stranger you pass?

translations.hi: यही सबका ईश्वर है; यही सर्वज्ञ है; यही अन्तर्यामी है; यही सबका उद्गम (योनि) है — क्योंकि प्राणियों की उत्पत्ति और लय इसी में हैं।

devanagari: नान्तःप्रज्ञं न बहिष्प्रज्ञं नोभयतःप्रज्ञं न प्रज्ञानघनं न प्रज्ञं नाप्रज्ञम् । / अदृष्टमव्यवहार्यमग्राह्यमलक्षणं अचिन्त्यमव्यपदेश्यमेकात्मप्रत्ययासारं प्रपञ्चोपशमं शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं चतुर्थं मन्यन्ते स आत्मा स विज्ञेयः ॥7॥
iast: nāntaḥprajñaṃ na bahiṣprajñaṃ nobhayataḥprajñaṃ na prajñānaghanaṃ na prajñaṃ nāprajñam । / adṛṣṭamavyavahāryamagrāhyamalakṣaṇaṃ acintyamavyapadeśyamekātmapratyayāsāraṃ prapañcopaśamaṃ śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ caturthaṃ manyante sa ātmā sa vijñeyaḥ ॥7॥
sayIt: NAAN-tah-PRAG-yum na ba-hish-PRAG-yum NO-bha-ya-tah-PRAG-yum na prag-YAA-na-gha-num na PRAG-yum NAA-prag-yum / a-DRISH-tum av-ya-va-HAAR-yum a-GRAAH-yum a-LUK-sha-num a-CHIN-tyum av-ya-pa-DAYSH-yum ay-KAAT-ma-PRUT-ya-YAA-saa-rum pra-pun-CHO-pa-sha-mum SHAAN-tum shi-VUM ad-VY-tum cha-toor-THUM mun-YUN-tay sa AAT-maa sa vig-YAY-yah
translation: Not inwardly knowing, not outwardly knowing, not knowing both ways; not a mass of knowing, not knowing, not unknowing. Unseen, beyond all dealings, ungraspable, without mark, unthinkable, unnameable; its essence the certainty of the one Self; the stilling of all appearance — peaceful, auspicious, non-dual: that, the wise hold, is the fourth. That is the Self; that is to be known.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Can you rest for one breath today as the one who watches waking, dreaming, and sleeping come and go?

translations.hi: जो न भीतर जानता है, न बाहर, न दोनों ओर; जो न प्रज्ञान-पुंज है, न ज्ञाता, न अज्ञ। अदृष्ट, व्यवहार से परे, अग्राह्य, लक्षण-रहित, अचिन्त्य, अकथनीय; एक आत्मा की प्रतीति ही जिसका सार है; जहाँ सारा प्रपंच थम जाता है — शान्त, शिव, अद्वैत: उसे ही ज्ञानी चौथा मानते हैं। वही आत्मा है; वही जानने योग्य है।

devanagari: सोऽयमात्माध्यक्षरमोङ्करोऽधिमात्रं पादा मात्रा मात्राश्च पादा अकार उकारो मकार इति ॥8॥
iast: so'yamātmādhyakṣaramoṅkaro'dhimātraṃ pādā mātrā mātrāśca pādā akāra ukāro makāra iti ॥8॥
sayIt: SO-ya-MAAT-maa-DHYUK-sha-ra-MONG-ka-RO-dhi-MAA-trum PAA-daa MAA-traa MAA-traash-cha PAA-daa a-KAA-ra oo-KAA-ro ma-KAA-ra I-ti
translation: This same Self, in terms of the syllable, is Om; in terms of its measures, the quarters are the measures and the measures are the quarters — the sound a, the sound u, the sound m.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: The next time you say Om, can you hear the three sounds and the silence after them as four distinct places?

translations.hi: यही आत्मा अक्षर की दृष्टि से ओंकार है; मात्राओं की दृष्टि से पाद ही मात्राएँ हैं और मात्राएँ ही पाद — अकार, उकार, मकार।

devanagari: जागरितस्थानो वैश्वानरोऽकारः प्रथमा मात्राऽऽप्तेरादिमत्त्वाद्वाऽऽप्नोति ह वै सर्वान् कामानादिश्च भवति य एवं वेद ॥9॥
iast: jāgaritasthāno vaiśvānaro'kāraḥ prathamā mātrā''pterādimattvādvā''pnoti ha vai sarvān kāmānādiśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥9॥
sayIt: JAA-ga-ri-ta-STHAA-no vysh-VAA-na-RO-kaa-rah pra-tha-MAA MAA-traap-tay-RAA-di-mut-TVAAD VAAP-no-ti ha vy sar-VAAN kaa-maa-NAA-dish-cha BHA-va-ti ya AY-vum VAY-da
translation: Vaishvanara, whose field is waking, is the sound a, the first measure — from "attaining", or from "being first". One who knows this attains all desires and becomes the first.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: As you begin anything today, can you hear the open a of it — the moment before everything else follows?

translations.hi: जाग्रत क्षेत्र वाला वैश्वानर अकार है, पहली मात्रा — 'आप्ति' (पा लेने, व्याप्ति) से, या 'आदि' (प्रथम) होने से। जो ऐसा जानता है, वह सारी कामनाएँ पा लेता है और प्रथम हो जाता है।

devanagari: स्वप्नस्थानस्तैजस उकारो द्वितीया मात्रोत्कर्षात् उभयत्वाद्वोत्कर्षति ह वै ज्ञानसन्ततिं समानश्च भवति नास्याऽब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति य एवं वेद ॥10॥
iast: svapnasthānastaijasa ukāro dvitīyā mātrotkarṣāt ubhayatvādvotkarṣati ha vai jñānasantatiṃ samānaśca bhavati nāsyā'brahmavitkule bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥10॥
sayIt: SVAP-na-STHAA-nas TIE-ja-sa oo-KAA-ro dvi-TEE-yaa MAA-trot-kar-SHAAT oo-bha-ya-TVAAD vot-KAR-sha-ti ha vy gyaa-na-SUN-ta-tim sa-MAA-nash-cha BHA-va-ti NAAS-yaa-BRAH-ma-vit KOO-lay BHA-va-ti ya AY-vum VAY-da
translation: Taijasa, whose field is dream, is the sound u, the second measure — from "rising higher", or from "being between both". One who knows this raises his stream of knowledge ever higher and becomes equal to all; in his family no one is born who does not know Brahman.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What is your imagination quietly building between your waking hours, and is it raising you or lowering you?

translations.hi: स्वप्न क्षेत्र वाला तैजस उकार है, दूसरी मात्रा — 'उत्कर्ष' (ऊपर उठने) से, या 'उभय' (दोनों के बीच) होने से। जो ऐसा जानता है, उसकी ज्ञान-धारा निरंतर ऊँची होती है और वह सबके लिए समान हो जाता है; उसके कुल में ब्रह्म को न जानने वाला कोई नहीं जन्मता।

devanagari: सुषुप्तस्थानः प्राज्ञो मकारस्तृतीया मात्रा मितेरपीतेर्वा मिनोति ह वा इदं सर्वमपीतिश्च भवति य एवं वेद ॥11॥
iast: suṣuptasthānaḥ prājño makārastṛtīyā mātrā miterapītervā minoti ha vā idaṃ sarvamapītiśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥11॥
sayIt: soo-SHOOP-ta-STHAA-nah PRAAG-yo ma-KAA-ras tri-TEE-yaa MAA-traa MI-tay-ra-PEE-tayr-vaa mi-NO-ti ha vaa i-DUM SAR-va-ma-PEE-tish-cha BHA-va-ti ya AY-vum VAY-da
translation: Prajna, whose field is deep sleep, is the sound m, the third measure — from "measuring", or from "merging". One who knows this measures all this and becomes its place of merging.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: At the end of today, can you let the whole day pour into rest the way sound closes into m?

translations.hi: सुषुप्ति क्षेत्र वाला प्राज्ञ मकार है, तीसरी मात्रा — 'मिति' (मापने) से, या 'अपीति' (लय, समा जाने) से। जो ऐसा जानता है, वह इस सब को माप लेता है और इसका लय-स्थान बन जाता है।

devanagari: अमात्रश्चतुर्थोऽव्यवहार्यः प्रपञ्चोपशमः शिवोऽद्वैत एवमोङ्कार आत्मैव संविशत्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं य एवं वेद ॥12॥
iast: amātraścaturtho'vyavahāryaḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ śivo'dvaita evamoṅkāra ātmaiva saṃviśatyātmanā''tmānaṃ ya evaṃ veda ॥12॥
sayIt: a-MAA-trash cha-toor-THO vya-va-HAAR-yah pra-pun-CHO-pa-sha-mah shi-VO-DVY-ta AY-va-MONG-kaa-ra AAT-my-va sum-vi-SHUT-YAAT-ma-NAAT-maa-num ya AY-vum VAY-da
translation: The fourth is without measure — beyond all dealings, the stilling of appearance, auspicious, non-dual. Thus Om is the Self itself. One who knows this enters the Self by the Self.
source: Mandukya Upanishad 12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: After your next Om, can you stay in the silence one heartbeat longer than feels natural?

translations.hi: चौथा मात्रा-रहित है — व्यवहार से परे, जहाँ सारा प्रपंच थम जाता है, शिव (कल्याणमय), अद्वैत। इस प्रकार ओंकार आत्मा ही है। जो ऐसा जानता है, वह आत्मा के द्वारा ही आत्मा में प्रवेश करता है।

devanagari: ॐ भद्रं कर्णेभिः शृणुयाम देवाः भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः । / स्थिरैरङ्गैस्तुष्टुवाँसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः / स्वस्ति न इन्द्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः । / स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु ॥ / ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥
iast: oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devāḥ bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhiryajatrāḥ । / sthirairaṅgaistuṣṭuvām̐sastanūbhirvyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ / svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ । / svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatirdadhātu ॥ / oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ ॥
sayIt: om BHUD-rum kar-NAY-bhih shri-noo-YAA-ma DAY-vaah BHUD-rum pash-YAY-maak-sha-bhir ya-ja-TRAAH / sthi-RY-rung-GYS toosh-too-VAAM-sas ta-NOO-bhir vya-SHAY-ma day-va-hi-TUM ya-DAA-yooh / SVAS-ti na IN-dro vrid-dha-SHRA-vaah SVAS-ti nah POO-shaa vish-va-VAY-daah / SVAS-ti nas TAARK-shyo a-rish-ta-NAY-mih SVAS-ti no bri-has-PA-tir da-DHAA-too / om SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih
translation: Om. May we hear what is good with our ears, O gods; may we see what is good with our eyes, O you worthy of worship. With steady limbs and sound bodies may we, offering praise, live out the full life the gods have appointed. May Indra of ancient fame be well-being for us; may Pushan the all-knowing be well-being for us; may Tarkshya of the unbroken wheel-rim be well-being for us; may Brihaspati grant us well-being. Om, peace, peace, peace.
source: Mandukya Upanishad, shanti mantra, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Before you take in anything today — news, advice, teaching — can you first ask that your hearing itself be made good?

translations.hi: ॐ। हे देवो, हम कानों से शुभ सुनें; हे यज्ञ-योग्य देवो, आँखों से शुभ देखें। स्थिर अंगों और स्वस्थ शरीरों से स्तुति करते हुए, देवताओं का दिया पूरा आयुष्य जिएँ। पुरानी कीर्ति वाले इन्द्र हमारा कल्याण करें; सर्वज्ञ पूषा हमारा कल्याण करें; अटूट नेमि वाले तार्क्ष्य (गरुड़) हमारा कल्याण करें; बृहस्पति हमें कल्याण दें। ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः।

devanagari: ॐ ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ता / भुवनस्य गोप्ता । / स ब्रह्मविद्यां सर्वविद्याप्रतिष्ठामथर्वाय / ज्येष्ठपुत्राय प्राह ॥1.1.1॥
iast: oṃ brahmā devānāṃ prathamaḥ saṃbabhūva viśvasya kartā / bhuvanasya goptā । / sa brahmavidyāṃ sarvavidyāpratiṣṭhāmatharvāya / jyeṣṭhaputrāya prāha ॥1.1.1॥
sayIt: om brah-MAA day-vaa-NAAM pra-tha-MAH sam-ba-BHOO-va vish-VAS-ya kar-TAA / bhu-va-NAS-ya gop-TAA / sa brah-ma-vid-YAAM sar-va-vid-YAA-pra-tish-THAAM a-thar-VAA-ya / jyaysh-tha-pu-TRAA-ya PRAA-ha
translation: Om. Brahma arose first among the gods — maker of the universe, guardian of the world. He taught the knowledge of Brahman, the foundation of all knowledge, to his eldest son Atharvan.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Who handed you the most valuable thing you know, and what did it cost them to carry it to you?

translations.hi: ॐ। देवताओं में सबसे पहले ब्रह्मा प्रकट हुए — विश्व के रचयिता, भुवन के रक्षक। उन्होंने सब विद्याओं की नींव, ब्रह्मविद्या, अपने ज्येष्ठ पुत्र अथर्वा को कह सुनाई।

devanagari: अथर्वणे यां प्रवदेत ब्रह्माऽथर्वा तं / पुरोवाचाङ्गिरे ब्रह्मविद्याम् । / स भारद्वाजाय सत्यवाहाय प्राह / भारद्वाजोऽङ्गिरसे परावराम् ॥1.1.2॥
iast: atharvaṇe yāṃ pravadeta brahmā'tharvā taṃ / purovācāṅgire brahmavidyām । / sa bhāradvājāya satyavāhāya prāha / bhāradvājo'ṅgirase parāvarām ॥1.1.2॥
sayIt: a-thar-va-NAY yaam pra-va-DAY-ta brah-MAA-thar-VAA tam / pu-ro-VAA-chaan-gi-RAY brah-ma-vid-YAAM / sa bhaa-rad-VAA-jaa-ya sat-ya-VAA-haa-ya PRAA-ha / bhaa-rad-VAA-jon-gi-ra-SAY pa-raa-va-RAAM
translation: The brahmavidya that Brahma declared to Atharvan, Atharvan of old taught to Angir. Angir passed it on to Bharadvaja Satyavaha, and Bharadvaja to Angiras — the knowledge of the higher and the lower.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What have you received carefully enough that you could pass it on undamaged?

translations.hi: जो ब्रह्मविद्या ब्रह्मा ने अथर्वा को कही, वही अथर्वा ने पुराने समय में अंगी को सुनाई। अंगी ने उसे सत्यवह भारद्वाज को दिया, और भारद्वाज ने अंगिरा को — परा और अपरा दोनों को समेटे वह विद्या।

devanagari: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । / कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥1.1.3॥
iast: śaunako ha vai mahāśālo'ṅgirasaṃ vidhivadupasannaḥ papraccha । / kasminnu bhagavo vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti ॥1.1.3॥
sayIt: shau-na-KO ha vai ma-haa-SHAA-lon-gi-ra-sam vi-dhi-vad u-pa-SAN-nah pa-PRACH-chha / kas-MIN-nu BHA-ga-vo vi-GYAA-tay SAR-vam-i-dum vi-GYAA-tum BHA-va-tee-ti
translation: Shaunaka, the great householder, approached Angiras in the proper manner and asked: "Revered one, what is that, knowing which, all this becomes known?"
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If you could truly understand only one thing, what would you choose so that everything else made sense?

translations.hi: महागृहस्थ शौनक ने विधिपूर्वक अंगिरा के पास पहुँचकर पूछा — "भगवन्, वह क्या है, जिसे जान लेने पर यह सब कुछ जाना हुआ हो जाता है?"

devanagari: तस्मै स होवाच । / द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्म / यद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च ॥1.1.4॥
iast: tasmai sa hovāca । / dve vidye veditavye iti ha sma / yadbrahmavido vadanti parā caivāparā ca ॥1.1.4॥
sayIt: TAS-mai sa ho-VAA-cha / dvay VID-yay vay-di-TAV-yay I-ti ha sma / yad brah-ma-VI-do VA-dan-ti pa-RAA chai-VAA-pa-RAA cha
translation: To him he said: "Two kinds of knowledge are to be known — so, indeed, say the knowers of Brahman — the higher and the lower."
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When did you last notice the difference between information you hold and understanding that holds you?

translations.hi: उन्होंने उससे कहा — "दो विद्याएँ जानने योग्य हैं — ऐसा ब्रह्म के ज्ञाता कहते आए हैं — परा और अपरा।"

devanagari: तत्रापरा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः / शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति । / अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते ॥1.1.5॥
iast: tatrāparā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo'tharvavedaḥ / śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣamiti । / atha parā yayā tadakṣaramadhigamyate ॥1.1.5॥
sayIt: ta-TRAA-pa-raa rig-VAY-do ya-jur-VAY-dah saa-ma-VAY-do-thar-va-VAY-dah / SHIK-shaa KAL-po vyaa-ka-ra-NUM ni-RUK-tum CHHAN-do JYO-ti-sham-i-ti / A-tha pa-RAA ya-YAA tad-AK-sha-ram a-dhi-GAM-ya-tay
translation: Of these, the lower is the Rig Veda, Yajur Veda, Sama Veda, and Atharva Veda, with phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, metre, and astronomy. And the higher is that by which the Imperishable is reached.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What do you know about, and what do you know the way you know your own hand?

translations.hi: इनमें अपरा विद्या है — ऋग्वेद, यजुर्वेद, सामवेद, अथर्ववेद, और साथ में शिक्षा, कल्प, व्याकरण, निरुक्त, छन्द और ज्योतिष। और परा वह है जिससे उस अक्षर तक पहुँचा जाता है।

devanagari: यत्तदद्रेश्यमग्राह्यमगोत्रमवर्ण- / मचक्षुःश्रोत्रं तदपाणिपादम् । / नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं / तदव्ययं यद्भूतयोनिं परिपश्यन्ति धीराः ॥1.1.6॥
iast: yattadadreśyamagrāhyamagotramavarṇa- / macakṣuḥśrotraṃ tadapāṇipādam । / nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ / tadavyayaṃ yadbhūtayoniṃ paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ ॥1.1.6॥
sayIt: yat tad ad-RAYSH-yum a-GRAAH-yum a-GO-trum a-VAR-num / a-CHAK-shuh-SHRO-trum tad a-PAA-ni-PAA-dum / NIT-yum vi-BHUM sar-va-ga-TUM su-SOOK-shmum / tad AV-ya-yum yad bhoo-ta-YO-nim pa-ri-PASH-yan-ti DHEE-raah
translation: That which cannot be seen or grasped, without lineage, without colour, without eyes or ears, without hands or feet — eternal, pervading, present everywhere, exceedingly subtle, undecaying — that the wise behold as the womb of all beings.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What would change if you treated the subtlest presence in your day, not the loudest, as the most real?

translations.hi: जो न देखा जा सकता है न पकड़ा, जिसका न गोत्र है न वर्ण, न आँख-कान न हाथ-पैर — जो नित्य है, व्यापक, सर्वगत, अत्यंत सूक्ष्म और अविनाशी — उसी को धीर पुरुष सब प्राणियों की योनि, सबका उद्गम, देखते हैं।

devanagari: यथोर्णनाभिः सृजते गृह्णते च / यथा पृथिव्यामोषधयः संभवन्ति । / यथा सतः पुरुषात् केशलोमानि / तथाऽक्षरात् संभवतीह विश्वम् ॥1.1.7॥
iast: yathorṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhṇate ca / yathā pṛthivyāmoṣadhayaḥ saṃbhavanti । / yathā sataḥ puruṣāt keśalomāni / tathā'kṣarāt saṃbhavatīha viśvam ॥1.1.7॥
sayIt: ya-thor-na-NAA-bhih sri-ja-TAY grih-na-TAY cha / ya-THAA prith-iv-YAAM o-sha-DHA-yah sam-bha-VAN-ti / ya-THAA sa-TAH pu-ru-SHAAT kay-sha-lo-MAA-ni / ta-THAAK-sha-RAAT sam-bha-va-TEE-ha VISH-vum
translation: As a spider sends forth its thread and draws it back, as plants spring from the earth, as hair grows on a living person — so from the Imperishable arises this universe.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What has your life produced as effortlessly as a spider spins — and have you ever stopped to watch it emerging?

translations.hi: जैसे मकड़ी अपना जाला रचती और समेट लेती है, जैसे धरती से वनस्पतियाँ उग आती हैं, जैसे जीते-जागते मनुष्य पर बाल — वैसे ही उस अक्षर से यह सारा विश्व उपजता है।

devanagari: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते । / अन्नात् प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम् ॥1.1.8॥
iast: tapasā cīyate brahma tato'nnamabhijāyate । / annāt prāṇo manaḥ satyaṃ lokāḥ karmasu cāmṛtam ॥1.1.8॥
sayIt: ta-pa-SAA CHEE-ya-tay BRAH-ma ta-TON-num a-bhi-JAA-ya-tay / an-NAAT praa-NO ma-NAH sat-YUM lo-KAAH kar-ma-SU chaam-RI-tum
translation: By tapas Brahman swells; from that, food is born; and from food — life-breath, mind, the real, the worlds, and in works, the deathless fruit.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What in your life is waiting for the slow heat of sustained attention before it can be born?

translations.hi: तप से ब्रह्म बढ़ता है; उससे अन्न जन्म लेता है; और अन्न से — प्राण, मन, सत्य, लोक, और कर्मों में अमृत फल।

devanagari: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्य ज्ञानमयं तापः । / तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपमन्नं च जायाते ॥1.1.9॥
iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavidyasya jñānamayaṃ tāpaḥ । / tasmādetadbrahma nāma rūpamannaṃ ca jāyāte ॥1.1.9॥
sayIt: yah sar-va-GYAH sar-va-vid YAS-ya gyaa-na-ma-YUM TAA-pah / tas-MAAD ay-tad BRAH-ma NAA-ma ROO-pum an-NUM cha jaa-YAA-tay
translation: He who is all-knowing, wise to each thing, whose tapas is made of knowledge itself — from him is born this Brahma: name, form, and food.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.1.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Is there anything you know so thoroughly that the knowing itself has begun to shape what you create?

translations.hi: जो सर्वज्ञ है, जो एक-एक बात का भी ज्ञाता है, जिसका तप ज्ञान से ही बना है — उसी से यह ब्रह्म जन्म लेता है: नाम, रूप और अन्न।

devanagari: तदेतत् सत्यं मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो / यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा संततानि । / तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः / पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके ॥1.2.1॥
iast: tadetat satyaṃ mantreṣu karmāṇi kavayo / yānyapaśyaṃstāni tretāyāṃ bahudhā saṃtatāni । / tānyācaratha niyataṃ satyakāmā eṣa vaḥ / panthāḥ sukṛtasya loke ॥1.2.1॥
sayIt: tad-AY-tat sat-YUM MAN-tray-shu KAR-maa-ni ka-va-YO / yaan-ya-PASH-yams TAA-ni tray-TAA-yaam ba-hu-DHAA san-ta-TAA-ni / taan-YAA-cha-ra-tha ni-ya-TUM sat-ya-KAA-maa AY-sha vah / PAN-thaah su-kri-TAS-ya LO-kay
translation: This is the truth: the rites that the seers saw in the mantras were spread out manifold in the three fires. Perform them constantly, you who desire the true — this is your path to the world of good deeds.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which practice do you keep faithfully, and what do you honestly expect it to carry you toward?

translations.hi: यह सत्य है: ऋषियों ने मंत्रों में जिन कर्मों को देखा, वे त्रेता — तीन अग्नियों — में अनेक रूपों में फैले। हे सत्य की कामना करने वालो, उन्हें नियमपूर्वक करते रहो — सुकृत के लोक तक यही तुम्हारा मार्ग है।

devanagari: यदा लेलायते ह्यर्चिः समिद्धे हव्यवाहने । / तदाऽऽज्यभागावन्तरेणाऽऽहुतीः प्रतिपादयेत् ॥1.2.2॥
iast: yadā lelāyate hyarciḥ samiddhe havyavāhane । / tadā''jyabhāgāvantareṇā''hutīḥ pratipādayet ॥1.2.2॥
sayIt: ya-DAA lay-LAA-ya-tay hyar-CHIH sa-MID-dhay hav-ya-VAA-ha-nay / ta-DAAJ-ya-bhaa-GAAV an-ta-RAY-naa-hu-TEEH pra-ti-PAA-da-yayt
translation: When the flame flickers up, the offering-bearing fire well kindled, then, between the two pourings of ghee, let him place his oblations.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Where in your daily practice does exactness still feel like love, and where has it hardened into worry?

translations.hi: जब हवि ले जाने वाली अग्नि भली प्रकार प्रज्वलित हो और लौ लहराने लगे, तब घी के दो भागों के बीच अपनी आहुतियाँ अर्पित करे।

devanagari: यस्याग्निहोत्रमदर्शमपौर्णमास- / मचातुर्मास्यमनाग्रयणमतिथिवर्जितं च । / अहुतमवैश्वदेवमविधिना हुत- / मासप्तमांस्तस्य लोकान् हिनस्ति ॥1.2.3॥
iast: yasyāgnihotramadarśamapaurṇamāsa- / macāturmāsyamanāgrayaṇamatithivarjitaṃ ca । / ahutamavaiśvadevamavidhinā huta- / māsaptamāṃstasya lokān hinasti ॥1.2.3॥
sayIt: yas-YAAG-ni-ho-trum a-dar-SHUM a-paur-na-MAA-sum / a-chaa-tur-MAAS-yum a-naa-gra-ya-NUM a-ti-thi-var-ji-TUM cha / a-hu-TUM a-vaish-va-DAY-vum a-vi-dhi-NAA hu-TUM / aa-sap-ta-MAAMS TAS-ya lo-KAAN hi-NAS-ti
translation: But if a man's fire offering lacks the new-moon and full-moon rites, the four-month rites and the harvest offering; if it goes unattended by guests and unoffered, without the offering to all beings, or is offered without rule — it destroys his worlds up to the seventh.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Is any duty of yours complete on paper while the people it was meant to feed go missing from it?

translations.hi: पर जिसका अग्निहोत्र दर्श और पौर्णमास से रहित है, चातुर्मास्य और आग्रयण से रहित, अतिथियों से सूना, बिना आहुति का, वैश्वदेव-रहित, या विधि के विरुद्ध किया हुआ — वह उसके सातवें तक के लोकों को नष्ट कर देता है।

devanagari: काली कराली च मनोजवा च / सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । / स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी / लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥1.2.4॥
iast: kālī karālī ca manojavā ca / sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā । / sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī / lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ॥1.2.4॥
sayIt: KAA-lee ka-RAA-lee cha ma-no-ja-VAA cha / su-lo-hi-TAA yaa cha su-dhoom-ra-VAR-naa / sphu-lin-gi-NEE vish-va-ru-CHEE cha DAY-vee / lay-laa-ya-MAA-naa I-ti SAP-ta jih-VAAH
translation: Kali the black, Karali the terrible, Manojava swift as thought, Sulohita the deep red, Sudhumravarna the smoke-hued, Sphulingini the spark-scatterer, and the shining goddess Vishvaruchi — these, ever flickering, are the seven tongues of the fire.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Could you name the seven moods your own inner fire moves through in a single day?

translations.hi: काली, कराली, मन के वेग वाली मनोजवा, गहरी लाल सुलोहिता, धुएँ के रंग वाली सुधूम्रवर्णा, चिनगारियाँ बिखेरती स्फुलिंगिनी, और देदीप्यमान देवी विश्वरुचि — ये लपलपाती हुई अग्नि की सात जिह्वाएँ हैं।

devanagari: एतेषु यश्चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालं / चाहुतयो ह्याददायन् । / तं नयन्त्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र / देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः ॥1.2.5॥
iast: eteṣu yaścarate bhrājamāneṣu yathākālaṃ / cāhutayo hyādadāyan । / taṃ nayantyetāḥ sūryasya raśmayo yatra / devānāṃ patireko'dhivāsaḥ ॥1.2.5॥
sayIt: ay-TAY-shu yash cha-ra-TAY bhraa-ja-MAA-nay-shu ya-thaa-KAA-lum / chaa-hu-ta-YO hyaa-da-DAA-yan / tum na-YAN-tyay-TAAH soor-YAS-ya rash-ma-YO YA-tra / day-VAA-naam pa-ti-RAY-ko dhi-VAA-sah
translation: Whoever performs his rites while these tongues are blazing, at the proper time — him these oblations, taking him up, lead along the rays of the sun to where the one lord of the gods has his dwelling.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If your efforts carried you exactly as far as they deserve and no further, where would you land?

translations.hi: इन जलती जिह्वाओं के बीच जो यथासमय अपने कर्म करता है, उसे ये आहुतियाँ अपने साथ उठाकर सूर्य की किरणों की राह से वहाँ ले जाती हैं, जहाँ देवताओं के एक स्वामी का वास है।

devanagari: एह्येहीति तमाहुतयः सुवर्चसः / सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्यजमानं वहन्ति । / प्रियां वाचमभिवदन्त्योऽर्चयन्त्य / एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोकः ॥1.2.6॥
iast: ehyehīti tamāhutayaḥ suvarcasaḥ / sūryasya raśmibhiryajamānaṃ vahanti । / priyāṃ vācamabhivadantyo'rcayantya / eṣa vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛto brahmalokaḥ ॥1.2.6॥
sayIt: ay-hyay-HEE-ti tum AA-hu-ta-yah su-var-cha-SAH / soor-YAS-ya rash-mi-BHIR ya-ja-MAA-num va-HAN-ti / pri-YAAM VAA-cham a-bhi-va-DANT-yor-cha-YANT-ya / AY-sha vah PUN-yah su-kri-TO brah-ma-lo-KAH
translation: "Come! Come!" say the radiant oblations, and carry the offerer along the rays of the sun, honouring him, speaking sweet words: "This is your holy Brahma-world, won by good deeds."
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which of your rewards flatter you the most, and what do they quietly ask of you in return?

translations.hi: "आओ! आओ!" कहती हुई तेजस्वी आहुतियाँ यजमान को सूर्य की किरणों की राह ले चलती हैं, मीठी वाणी से उसका मान करती हुई — "यह रहा तुम्हारा पुण्य ब्रह्मलोक, तुम्हारे सुकृत से कमाया हुआ।"

devanagari: प्लवा ह्येते अदृढा यज्ञरूपा / अष्टादशोक्तमवरं येषु कर्म । / एतच्छ्रेयो येऽभिनन्दन्ति मूढा / जरामृत्युं ते पुनरेवापि यन्ति ॥1.2.7॥
iast: plavā hyete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā / aṣṭādaśoktamavaraṃ yeṣu karma । / etacchreyo ye'bhinandanti mūḍhā / jarāmṛtyuṃ te punarevāpi yanti ॥1.2.7॥
sayIt: pla-VAA hyay-TAY a-dri-DHAA yag-ya-ROO-paa / ash-TAA-da-SHOK-tum a-va-RUM YAY-shu KAR-ma / ay-tach-CHRAY-yo YAY-bhi-NAN-dan-ti MOO-dhaa / ja-raa-MRIT-yum tay pu-na-RAY-vaa-pi YAN-ti
translation: Unsteady boats, though, are these forms of sacrifice — the eighteen in which only the lower work is taught. The deluded who hail this as the highest good come again and again to old age and death.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which trusted boat of yours was built for the river, and are you now asking it to cross the sea?

translations.hi: पर ये यज्ञ-रूप तो कच्ची, डगमगाती नावें हैं — वे अठारह, जिनमें केवल निचला कर्म कहा गया है। जो मूढ़ इसी को परम श्रेय मानकर सराहते हैं, वे फिर-फिर बुढ़ापे और मृत्यु में लौट आते हैं।

devanagari: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः / स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः । / जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा / अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥1.2.8॥
iast: avidyāyāmantare vartamānāḥ / svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ । / jaṅghanyamānāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā / andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ ॥1.2.8॥
sayIt: a-vid-YAA-yaam an-ta-RAY var-ta-MAA-naah / sva-YUM DHEE-raah pan-di-TUM man-ya-MAA-naah / jan-ghan-ya-MAA-naah pa-ri-YAN-ti MOO-dhaa / an-DHAY-nai-va nee-ya-MAA-naa ya-THAAN-dhaah
translation: Dwelling in the midst of ignorance, wise in their own eyes, thinking themselves learned, the deluded wander, battered again and again — like the blind led by the blind.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: On what subject are you most certain, and when did you last test that certainty against someone who can see?

translations.hi: अविद्या के बीचोबीच रहते हुए, अपनी नज़र में धीर, अपने को पंडित मानते हुए, मूढ़ ठोकरें खाते हुए भटकते फिरते हैं — जैसे अंधे के हाथों चलाए जाते अंधे।

devanagari: अविद्यायां बहुधा वर्तमाना वयं / कृतार्था इत्यभिमन्यन्ति बालाः । / यत् कर्मिणो न प्रवेदयन्ति रागात् / तेनातुराः क्षीणलोकाश्च्यवन्ते ॥1.2.9॥
iast: avidyāyāṃ bahudhā vartamānā vayaṃ / kṛtārthā ityabhimanyanti bālāḥ । / yat karmiṇo na pravedayanti rāgāt / tenāturāḥ kṣīṇalokāścyavante ॥1.2.9॥
sayIt: a-vid-YAA-yaam ba-hu-DHAA var-ta-MAA-naa va-YUM / kri-TAAR-thaa it-ya-bhi-MAN-yan-ti BAA-laah / yat kar-mi-NO na pra-VAY-da-yan-ti raa-GAAT / tay-NAA-tu-raah kshee-na-lo-KAASH chya-VAN-tay
translation: Dwelling in ignorance in many ways, the childish tell themselves, "We have reached the goal." Because those bound to works do not come to know — out of attachment — they sink down, anguished, when their worlds are spent.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Where might comfort, rather than evidence, be what convinces you that you are already done growing?

translations.hi: अनेक तरह से अविद्या में रहते हुए नादान मान बैठते हैं — "हम कृतार्थ हो गए।" कर्मों में बँधे लोग आसक्ति के कारण जान नहीं पाते, इसलिए पुण्य-लोक चुक जाने पर व्याकुल होकर नीचे गिर जाते हैं।

devanagari: इष्टापूर्तं मन्यमाना वरिष्ठं / नान्यच्छ्रेयो वेदयन्ते प्रमूढाः । / नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृतेऽनुभूत्वेमं / लोकं हीनतरं वा विशन्ति ॥1.2.10॥
iast: iṣṭāpūrtaṃ manyamānā variṣṭhaṃ / nānyacchreyo vedayante pramūḍhāḥ । / nākasya pṛṣṭhe te sukṛte'nubhūtvemaṃ / lokaṃ hīnataraṃ vā viśanti ॥1.2.10॥
sayIt: ish-TAA-poor-tum man-ya-MAA-naa va-rish-THUM / NAAN-yach-CHRAY-yo vay-da-YAN-tay pra-MOO-dhaah / naa-KAS-ya prish-THAY tay su-kri-TAY-nu-BHOOT-vay-mum / lo-KUM hee-na-ta-RUM vaa vi-SHAN-ti
translation: Convinced that sacrifice and public works are the highest, the deluded know no better good. Having enjoyed their reward on heaven's high back, won by good deeds, they enter this world again — or one lower still.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you give, are you setting something free, or quietly invoicing the future for a reward?

translations.hi: यज्ञ और लोकोपकार के कामों को ही सर्वोच्च मानते हुए, भटके हुए लोग इससे बेहतर किसी श्रेय को नहीं जानते। स्वर्ग की ऊँचाई पर, सुकृत से मिला अपना फल भोगकर, वे फिर इसी लोक में लौट आते हैं — या इससे भी नीचे उतरते हैं।

devanagari: तपःश्रद्धे ये ह्युपवसन्त्यरण्ये / शान्ता विद्वांसो भैक्ष्यचर्यां चरन्तः । / सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति / यत्रामृतः स पुरुषो ह्यव्ययात्मा ॥1.2.11॥
iast: tapaḥśraddhe ye hyupavasantyaraṇye / śāntā vidvāṃso bhaikṣyacaryāṃ carantaḥ । / sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti / yatrāmṛtaḥ sa puruṣo hyavyayātmā ॥1.2.11॥
sayIt: ta-pah-shrad-DHAY yay hyu-pa-va-SAN-tya-ran-yay / shaan-TAA vid-VAAM-so bhaik-shya-char-YAAM cha-RAN-tah / soor-ya-DVAA-ray-na tay vi-ra-JAAH pra-YAAN-ti / ya-TRAAM-ri-tah sa pu-ru-SHO hyav-ya-YAAT-maa
translation: But those who practise tapas and faith in the forest — tranquil knowers, living on alms — they pass, freed of dust, through the door of the sun, to where that deathless Person is, the imperishable Self.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What could you put down this week that would leave you lighter for the road you actually mean to travel?

translations.hi: पर जो वन में तप और श्रद्धा को साधते हैं — शान्त, ज्ञानी, भिक्षा पर जीते हुए — वे धूल से मुक्त होकर सूर्य-द्वार से वहाँ पहुँचते हैं, जहाँ वह अमृत पुरुष है — अविनाशी आत्मा।

devanagari: परीक्ष्य लोकान् कर्मचितान् ब्राह्मणो / निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन । / तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत् / समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम् ॥1.2.12॥
iast: parīkṣya lokān karmacitān brāhmaṇo / nirvedamāyānnāstyakṛtaḥ kṛtena । / tadvijñānārthaṃ sa gurumevābhigacchet / samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭham ॥1.2.12॥
sayIt: pa-REEK-shya lo-KAAN kar-ma-chi-TAAN braah-ma-NO / nir-VAY-dum aa-YAAN NAAS-tya-kri-TAH kri-TAY-na / tad-vig-yaa-NAAR-thum sa gu-rum-ay-VAA-bhi-gach-chhayt / sa-mit-PAA-nih SHRO-tri-yum brah-ma-nish-THUM
translation: Having examined the worlds that works build up, let a seeker of Brahman grow dispassionate: the uncreated is not reached by the created. To know That, let him go, fuel in hand, to a teacher alone — one learned in the scriptures and established in Brahman.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you last needed real guidance, did you look for someone comfortable or someone qualified?

translations.hi: कर्मों से रचे गए लोकों को परखकर ब्रह्म का जिज्ञासु वैराग्य को प्राप्त हो: जो अकृत है, वह कृत से नहीं मिलता। उसे जानने के लिए वह हाथ में समिधा लिए केवल गुरु के पास जाए — जो श्रोत्रिय हो और ब्रह्म में निष्ठ।

devanagari: तस्मै स विद्वानुपसन्नाय सम्यक् / प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय । / येनाक्षरं पुरुषं वेद सत्यं प्रोवाच / तां तत्वतो ब्रह्मविद्याम् ॥1.2.13॥
iast: tasmai sa vidvānupasannāya samyak / praśāntacittāya śamānvitāya । / yenākṣaraṃ puruṣaṃ veda satyaṃ provāca / tāṃ tatvato brahmavidyām ॥1.2.13॥
sayIt: TAS-mai sa vid-VAAN u-pa-san-NAA-ya sam-YAK / pra-shaan-ta-chit-TAA-ya sha-MAAN-vi-taa-ya / yay-NAAK-sha-rum pu-ru-shum VAY-da sat-YUM pro-VAA-cha / taam tat-va-TO brah-ma-vid-YAAM
translation: To him who had approached rightly, whose mind was at peace, whose senses were stilled, that knower taught, as it truly is, the knowledge of Brahman by which one knows the imperishable Person, the true.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 1.2.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Before you ask your next big question, what would make your mind quiet enough to receive the answer?

translations.hi: जो विधिपूर्वक आया था, जिसका चित्त प्रशान्त और इंद्रियाँ संयत थीं — उस शिष्य को उस ज्ञानी ने वह ब्रह्मविद्या तत्त्वतः कह सुनाई, जिससे मनुष्य उस अक्षर, सत्य पुरुष को जान लेता है।

devanagari: तदेतत् सत्यं / यथा सुदीप्तात् पावकाद्विस्फुलिङ्गाः / सहस्रशः प्रभवन्ते सरूपाः । / तथाऽक्षराद्विविधाः सोम्य भावाः / प्रजायन्ते तत्र चैवापि यन्ति ॥2.1.1॥
iast: tadetat satyaṃ / yathā sudīptāt pāvakādvisphuliṅgāḥ / sahasraśaḥ prabhavante sarūpāḥ । / tathā'kṣarādvividhāḥ somya bhāvāḥ / prajāyante tatra caivāpi yanti ॥2.1.1॥
sayIt: ta-DAY-tat SAT-yum / ya-THAA su-DEEP-taat paa-va-KAAD-vis-phu-LIN-gaah / sa-HAS-ra-shah pra-bha-VAN-tay sa-ROO-paah / ta-THAAK-sha-raad-vi-vi-DHAAH SOM-ya BHAA-vaah / pra-JAA-yan-tay TAT-ra chai-VAA-pi YAN-ti
translation: This is the truth: as from a blazing fire thousands of sparks spring forth, each of the same nature as the fire, so from the Imperishable, dear one, arise beings of every kind — and into it they return.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you feel small and separate today, can you remember what the spark is made of?

translations.hi: यही सत्य है: जैसे धधकती आग से हज़ारों चिंगारियाँ उठती हैं, रूप में उसी आग जैसी, वैसे ही अविनाशी से, प्रिय, नाना प्रकार के जीव उत्पन्न होते हैं — और उसी में लौट जाते हैं।

devanagari: दिव्यो ह्यमूर्तः पुरुषः स बाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्यजः । / अप्राणो ह्यमनाः शुभ्रो ह्यक्षरात् परतः परः ॥2.1.2॥
iast: divyo hyamūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sa bāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ । / aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhro hyakṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ ॥2.1.2॥
sayIt: div-YO hya-MOOR-tah PU-ru-shah sa baa-hyaa-BHYAN-ta-ro HYA-jah / a-PRAA-no hya-ma-NAAH SHUBH-ro hyak-sha-RAAT PA-ra-tah PA-rah
translation: Divine and formless is the Purusha; he is outside and within, unborn — without breath, without mind, radiant — higher even than the imperishable that lies beyond all things.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What happens to your idea of the divine if you gently set down every image you have of it?

translations.hi: वह पुरुष दिव्य है, निराकार; बाहर भी है और भीतर भी, अजन्मा; न प्राण, न मन — शुभ्र, उज्ज्वल; और उस अक्षर से भी परे, जो स्वयं सबसे परे है।

devanagari: एतस्माज्जायते प्रणो मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च । / खं वायुर्ज्योतिरापः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी ॥2.1.3॥
iast: etasmājjāyate praṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca । / khaṃ vāyurjyotirāpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī ॥2.1.3॥
sayIt: ay-tas-maaj-JAA-ya-tay PRA-no MA-nah sar-ven-dri-YAA-ni cha / khum VAA-yur-JYO-ti-RAA-pah pri-thi-VEE VISH-vas-ya DHAA-ri-nee
translation: From this one are born the life-breath, the mind, and all the senses; space, air, fire, water, and the earth that supports all.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Can you treat your next breath as arriving from the same source as the sky?

translations.hi: इसी से जन्म लेते हैं प्राण, मन और सारी इन्द्रियाँ; आकाश, वायु, अग्नि, जल, और सबको धारण करने वाली पृथ्वी।

devanagari: अग्नीर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्रसूर्यौ / दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग् विवृताश्च वेदाः । / वायुः प्रणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां / पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा ॥2.1.4॥
iast: agnīrmūrdhā cakṣuṣī candrasūryau / diśaḥ śrotre vāg vivṛtāśca vedāḥ । / vāyuḥ praṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvamasya padbhyāṃ / pṛthivī hyeṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā ॥2.1.4॥
sayIt: ag-neer-MOOR-dhaa CHAK-shu-shee chan-dra-SOOR-yow / DI-shah SHRO-tray vaag vi-vri-TAASH-cha VAY-daah / VAA-yuh PRA-no HRI-da-yum VISH-va-mas-ya PAD-bhyaam / pri-thi-VEE HYAY-sha sar-va-bhoo-taan-ta-RAAT-maa
translation: Fire is his head; his eyes, the moon and sun; the directions his ears; his speech, the revealed Vedas; air his breath, the whole universe his heart; from his feet came the earth — truly he is the inner self of all beings.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Whose face today will you try to see as a face of the one you are looking for?

translations.hi: अग्नि उसका सिर है; चन्द्र और सूर्य उसकी आँखें; दिशाएँ कान; प्रकट वेद उसकी वाणी; वायु प्राण; समूचा विश्व हृदय; पैरों से पृथ्वी — वही सब प्राणियों का अन्तरात्मा है।

devanagari: तस्मादग्निः समिधो यस्य सूर्यः / सोमात् पर्जन्य ओषधयः पृथिव्याम् । / पुमान् रेतः सिञ्चति योषितायां / बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात् संप्रसूताः ॥2.1.5॥
iast: tasmādagniḥ samidho yasya sūryaḥ / somāt parjanya oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyām । / pumān retaḥ siñcati yoṣitāyāṃ / bahvīḥ prajāḥ puruṣāt saṃprasūtāḥ ॥2.1.5॥
sayIt: tas-MAAD-ag-NIH SA-mi-dho YAS-ya SOOR-yah / so-MAAT par-JAN-ya O-sha-dha-yah pri-thiv-YAAM / pu-MAAN RAY-tah SIN-cha-ti yo-shi-TAA-yaam / bah-VEEH pra-JAAH pu-ru-SHAAT sam-pra-SOO-taah
translation: From him comes the fire whose fuel is the sun; from the moon comes rain, and from rain the plants upon the earth; the man pours seed into the woman — and so the many generations of beings descend, all of them, from the Purusha.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What has been handed down the long chain to you today, and what will you pass forward?

translations.hi: उसी से वह अग्नि है जिसका ईंधन सूर्य है; सोम से मेघ बरसता है, वर्षा से धरती पर वनस्पतियाँ उगती हैं; पुरुष स्त्री में बीज सींचता है — इस तरह अनगिनत संतानें, सबकी सब, उसी पुरुष से चली आई हैं।

devanagari: तस्मादृचः साम यजूंषि दीक्षा / यज्ञाश्च सर्वे क्रतवो दक्षिणाश्च । / संवत्सरश्च यजमानश्च लोकाः / सोमो यत्र पवते यत्र सूर्यः ॥2.1.6॥
iast: tasmādṛcaḥ sāma yajūṃṣi dīkṣā / yajñāśca sarve kratavo dakṣiṇāśca । / saṃvatsaraśca yajamānaśca lokāḥ / somo yatra pavate yatra sūryaḥ ॥2.1.6॥
sayIt: tas-maad-RI-chah SAA-ma ya-JOON-shi DEEK-shaa / yag-YAASH-cha SAR-vay KRA-ta-vo dak-shi-NAASH-cha / sam-vat-sa-RASH-cha ya-ja-MAA-nash-cha LO-kaah / SO-mo YAT-ra PA-va-tay YAT-ra SOOR-yah
translation: From him come the Rig verses, the Saman chants, the Yajus formulas, and initiation; all sacrifices, solemn rites, and the gifts to priests; the year too, and the sacrificer, and the worlds — where the moon shines purifying and where the sun shines.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Does your practice today point beyond itself, or has the ladder quietly become the destination?

translations.hi: उसी से ऋचाएँ, साम-गान और यजुः-मंत्र आए, दीक्षा भी; सारे यज्ञ, अनुष्ठान और दक्षिणाएँ; संवत्सर भी, यजमान भी, और वे लोक भी जहाँ सोम पवित्र करता चमकता है और जहाँ सूर्य तपता है।

devanagari: तस्माच्च देवा बहुधा संप्रसूताः / साध्या मनुष्याः पशवो वयांसि । / प्राणापानौ व्रीहियवौ तपश्च / श्रद्ध सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं विधिश्च ॥2.1.7॥
iast: tasmācca devā bahudhā saṃprasūtāḥ / sādhyā manuṣyāḥ paśavo vayāṃsi । / prāṇāpānau vrīhiyavau tapaśca / śraddha satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidhiśca ॥2.1.7॥
sayIt: tas-MAACH-cha DAY-vaa ba-hu-DHAA sam-pra-SOO-taah / SAADH-yaa ma-NUSH-yaah PA-sha-vo va-YAAN-si / praa-naa-PAA-now vree-hi-ya-VOW TA-pash-cha / SHRAD-dha SAT-yum brah-ma-CHAR-yum vi-DHISH-cha
translation: And from him the gods are begotten, in their many orders; the celestial Sadhyas, humans, beasts, and birds; the in-breath and the out-breath, rice and barley, austerity, faith, truth, the disciplined life, and sacred rule.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which quality you strain after might grow easier if you treated it as already planted in you?

translations.hi: और उसी से देवता अनेक रूपों में उत्पन्न हुए; साध्यगण, मनुष्य, पशु और पक्षी; प्राण और अपान, धान और जौ, तप, श्रद्धा, सत्य, ब्रह्मचर्य और विधि — सब उसी से।

devanagari: सप्त प्राणाः प्रभवन्ति तस्मात् / सप्तार्चिषः समिधः सप्त होमाः । / सप्त इमे लोका येषु चरन्ति प्राणा / गुहाशया निहिताः सप्त सप्त ॥2.1.8॥
iast: sapta prāṇāḥ prabhavanti tasmāt / saptārciṣaḥ samidhaḥ sapta homāḥ । / sapta ime lokā yeṣu caranti prāṇā / guhāśayā nihitāḥ sapta sapta ॥2.1.8॥
sayIt: SAP-ta PRAA-naah pra-BHA-van-ti tas-MAAT / sap-TAAR-chi-shah SA-mi-dhah SAP-ta HO-maah / SAP-ta i-MAY LO-kaa YAY-shu cha-RAN-ti PRAA-naa / gu-HAA-sha-yaa ni-hi-TAAH SAP-ta SAP-ta
translation: From him spring the seven life-breaths, the seven flames and their fuel, the seven oblations; these seven worlds in which the breaths move — laid down in the secret place, seven in every being.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If every glance is an offering poured into fire, what will you choose to look at today?

translations.hi: उसी से सात प्राण उठते हैं, सात लपटें और उनका ईंधन, सात आहुतियाँ; ये सात लोक जिनमें प्राण विचरते हैं — हृदय की गुहा में रखे हुए, हर प्राणी में सात-सात।

devanagari: अतः समुद्रा गिरयश्च सर्वेऽस्मात् / स्यन्दन्ते सिन्धवः सर्वरूपाः । / अतश्च सर्वा ओषधयो रसश्च / येनैष भूतैस्तिष्ठते ह्यन्तरात्मा ॥2.1.9॥
iast: ataḥ samudrā girayaśca sarve'smāt / syandante sindhavaḥ sarvarūpāḥ । / ataśca sarvā oṣadhayo rasaśca / yenaiṣa bhūtaistiṣṭhate hyantarātmā ॥2.1.9॥
sayIt: A-tah sa-mud-RAA gi-ra-YASH-cha sar-VAY-smaat / syan-DAN-tay SIN-dha-vah sar-va-ROO-paah / a-TASH-cha SAR-vaa O-sha-dha-yo RA-sash-cha / yay-NAI-sha bhoo-tais-TISH-tha-tay hyan-ta-RAAT-maa
translation: From him are all the seas and the mountains; from him stream the rivers of every form; from him come all the plants, and the sap by which the inner self stands firm amid the elements that body it.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: At your next meal, can you taste the river, the rain, and what stands behind them both?

translations.hi: उसी से सारे समुद्र और पर्वत हैं; उसी से हर रूप की नदियाँ बहती हैं; उसी से सारी वनस्पतियाँ, और वह रस भी जिसके सहारे यह अन्तरात्मा भूतों के बीच — देह बने तत्वों के घेरे में — टिका रहता है।

devanagari: पुरुष एवेदं विश्वं कर्म तपो ब्रह्म परामृतम् । / एतद्यो वेद निहितं गुहायां / सोऽविद्याग्रन्थिं विकिरतीह सोम्य ॥2.1.10॥
iast: puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam । / etadyo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ / so'vidyāgranthiṃ vikiratīha somya ॥2.1.10॥
sayIt: PU-ru-sha ay-VAY-dum VISH-vum KAR-ma TA-po BRAH-ma pa-RAA-mri-tum / ay-TAD-yo VAY-da NI-hi-tum gu-HAA-yaam / so-vid-yaa-GRAN-thim vi-ki-ra-TEE-ha SOM-ya
translation: The Purusha alone is all this — rite and austerity too. He is Brahman, the highest immortal. Whoever knows this as hidden in the secret cave of the heart, dear one, unties the knot of ignorance here — in this very life.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.1.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which knot in you is waiting not for more effort but for a clearer seeing?

translations.hi: पुरुष ही यह सब कुछ है — कर्म भी, तप भी; वही ब्रह्म है, परम अमृत। प्रिय, जो इसे हृदय की गुहा में छिपा जान लेता है, वह अविद्या की गाँठ यहीं — इसी जीवन में — खोल देता है।

devanagari: आविः संनिहितं गुहाचरं नाम / महत्पदमत्रैतत् समर्पितम् । / एजत्प्राणन्निमिषच्च यदेतज्जानथ / सदसद्वरेण्यं परं विज्ञानाद्यद्वरिष्ठं प्रजानाम् ॥2.2.1॥
iast: āviḥ saṃnihitaṃ guhācaraṃ nāma / mahatpadamatraitat samarpitam । / ejatprāṇannimiṣacca yadetajjānatha / sadasadvareṇyaṃ paraṃ vijñānādyadvariṣṭhaṃ prajānām ॥2.2.1॥
sayIt: AA-vih SAM-ni-hi-tum gu-HAA-cha-rum NAA-ma / ma-HAT-pa-dum a-TRAI-tat sa-MAR-pi-tum / AY-jat-PRAA-nan-ni-mi-SHACH-cha ya-DAY-taj-JAA-na-tha / sa-da-sad-va-RAYN-yum PA-rum vig-yaa-NAAD-yad-va-RISH-thum pra-JAA-naam
translation: It is manifest, it is set close at hand — "the one moving in the secret cave" is its name — the great abode; on it is fixed all this: whatever stirs, breathes, and blinks. Know it as being and non-being at once, the thing worth choosing, beyond ordinary understanding, the highest that creatures can reach.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What would change if you treated the divine as the nearest thing in the room rather than the farthest?

translations.hi: वह प्रकट है, पास ही रखा है — "गुहा में विचरने वाला" उसका नाम है — वही महान आधार है; उसी पर यह सब टिका है: जो कुछ हिलता है, साँस लेता है, पलक झपकाता है। उसे सत् और असत् दोनों जानो — वरण करने योग्य, साधारण समझ से परे, प्रजाओं के लिए सर्वोच्च।

devanagari: यदर्चिमद्यदणुभ्योऽणु च / यस्मिँल्लोका निहिता ��ोकिनश्च । / तदेतदक्षरं ब्रह्म स प्राणस्तदु वाङ्मनः / तदेतत्सत्यं तदमृतं तद्वेद्धव्यं सोम्य विद्धि ॥2.2.2॥
iast: yadarcimadyadaṇubhyo'ṇu ca / yasmim̐llokā nihitā lokinaśca । / tadetadakṣaraṃ brahma sa prāṇastadu vāṅmanaḥ / tadetatsatyaṃ tadamṛtaṃ tadveddhavyaṃ somya viddhi ॥2.2.2॥
sayIt: ya-DAR-chi-mad ya-da-nu-BHYO-nu cha / yas-mil-LO-kaa NI-hi-taa LO-ki-nash-cha / ta-day-ta-DAK-sha-rum BRAH-ma sa PRAA-nas TA-du VAANG-ma-nah / ta-day-tat-SAT-yum ta-dam-RI-tum tad-VAYD-dhav-yum SOM-ya VID-dhi
translation: That which is luminous, subtler than the subtle; that in which the worlds are set, and the dwellers in the worlds — that is this imperishable Brahman. It is breath; it is speech and mind; it is the real, it is the immortal. It is the mark to be pierced, dear one: pierce it.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If knowing were aiming, what is your attention actually pointed at right now?

translations.hi: जो देदीप्यमान है, जो सूक्ष्म से भी सूक्ष्म; जिसमें सारे लोक रखे हैं और लोकवासी भी — वही यह अक्षर ब्रह्म है। वही प्राण है, वही वाणी और मन; वही सत्य है, वही अमृत। प्रिय, वही बेधने योग्य लक्ष्य है — उसे बेध डालो।

devanagari: धनुर्गृहीत्वौपनिषदं महास्त्रं / शरं ह्युपासा निशितं सन्धयीत । / आयम्य तद्भावगतेन चेतसा / लक्ष्यं तदेवाक्षरं सोम्य विद्धि ॥2.2.3॥
iast: dhanurgṛhītvaupaniṣadaṃ mahāstraṃ / śaraṃ hyupāsā niśitaṃ sandhayīta । / āyamya tadbhāvagatena cetasā / lakṣyaṃ tadevākṣaraṃ somya viddhi ॥2.2.3॥
sayIt: dha-nur-gri-hee-TVOW-pa-ni-sha-dum ma-HAAST-rum / SHA-rum hyu-PAA-saa NI-shi-tum san-dha-YEE-ta / AA-yam-ya tad-bhaa-va-ga-TAY-na CHAY-ta-saa / LUCK-shyum ta-day-VAAK-sha-rum SOM-ya VID-dhi
translation: Take up the bow of the Upanishads, that great weapon; fit to it an arrow sharpened by devoted practice. Draw it with a mind absorbed into the being of That, and know, dear one: the target is that very Imperishable — pierce it.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What daily practice is quietly sharpening your arrow, and what is dulling it?

translations.hi: उपनिषदों का धनुष — वह महान अस्त्र — उठाओ; उस पर उपासना से तेज़ किया हुआ बाण चढ़ाओ। उस-मय हुए चित्त से डोरी खींचो, और प्रिय, जान लो: लक्ष्य वही अक्षर है — उसे बेधो।

devanagari: प्रणवो धनुः शारो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । / अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत् तन्मयो भवेत् ॥2.2.4॥
iast: praṇavo dhanuḥ śāro hyātmā brahma tallakṣyamucyate । / apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravat tanmayo bhavet ॥2.2.4॥
sayIt: pra-na-VO DHA-nuh SHAA-ro HYAAT-maa BRAH-ma tal-LUCK-shyum UCH-ya-tay / a-pra-MAT-tay-na VAYD-dhav-yum SHA-ra-vat tan-MA-yo bha-VAYT
translation: Om is the bow, the self is the arrow, and Brahman is called its target. It is to be pierced by one who does not waver — then, like the arrow, become of one substance with the mark.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you sit with Om today, are you launching the arrow or only polishing the bow?

translations.hi: प्रणव (ॐ) धनुष है, आत्मा बाण, और ब्रह्म उसका लक्ष्य कहा गया है। उसे बिना डिगे, पूरे होश में बेधना है — फिर बाण की तरह उसी में तन्मय हो जाना है।

devanagari: यस्मिन् द्यौः पृथिवी चान्तरिक्षमोतं / मनः सह प्राणैश्च सर्वैः । / तमेवैकं जानथ आत्मानमन्या वाचो / विमुञ्चथामृतस्यैष सेतुः ॥2.2.5॥
iast: yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣamotaṃ / manaḥ saha prāṇaiśca sarvaiḥ । / tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānamanyā vāco / vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ ॥2.2.5॥
sayIt: YAS-min dyowh pri-thi-VEE chaan-ta-RIK-sha-MO-tum / MA-nah SA-ha praa-NAISH-cha SAR-vaih / ta-may-VAI-kum JAA-na-tha aat-MAA-nam an-YAA VAA-cho / vi-mun-cha-THAAM-ri-tas-YAI-sha SAY-tuh
translation: In him are woven heaven, the earth, and the space between, the mind too, together with all the breaths. Know him alone as the one Self; let go of other words. This is the bridge to the immortal.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which conversation about the sacred could you set down today in order to actually cross?

translations.hi: उसी में स्वर्ग, पृथ्वी और बीच का अंतरिक्ष बुने हुए हैं, मन भी, सारे प्राणों समेत। उस एक को ही आत्मा जानो; बाक़ी बातें छोड़ दो। अमृत का सेतु यही है।

devanagari: अरा इव रथनाभौ संहता यत्र नाड्यः । / स एषोऽन्तश्चरते बहुधा जायमानः । / ओमित्येवं ध्यायथ आत्मानं स्वस्ति वः / पाराय तमसः परस्तात् ॥2.2.6॥
iast: arā iva rathanābhau saṃhatā yatra nāḍyaḥ । / sa eṣo'ntaścarate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ । / omityevaṃ dhyāyatha ātmānaṃ svasti vaḥ / pārāya tamasaḥ parastāt ॥2.2.6॥
sayIt: a-RAA i-va ra-tha-NAA-bhow SAM-ha-taa YAT-ra NAAD-yah / sa ay-SHON-tash-CHA-ra-tay ba-hu-DHAA jaa-ya-MAA-nah / o-mit-YAY-vum DHYAA-ya-tha aat-MAA-num SVAS-ti vah / paa-RAA-ya TA-ma-sah pa-ras-TAAT
translation: Where the channels of the body come together like spokes at the hub of a chariot wheel, there he moves within, appearing in many ways. Meditate on the Self as Om. May it be well with you in crossing to the far shore beyond darkness.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Who once blessed your journey, and can you travel today as someone accompanied rather than alone?

translations.hi: जहाँ शरीर की नाड़ियाँ ऐसे मिलती हैं जैसे रथ के पहिये की नाभि में अरे, वहीं वह भीतर विचरता है, बहुत रूपों में प्रकट होता हुआ। "ओम्" — इस रूप में आत्मा का ध्यान करो। अंधकार के उस पार, दूर के किनारे तक की यात्रा तुम्हारे लिए मंगलमय हो।

devanagari: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद् यस्यैष महिमा भुवि । / दिव्ये ब्रह्मपुरे ह्येष व्योम्न्यात्मा प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ / मनोमयः प्राणशरीरनेता / प्रतिष्ठितोऽन्ने हृदयं सन्निधाय । / तद् विज्ञानेन परिपश्यन्ति धीरा / आनन्दरूपममृतं यद् विभाति ॥2.2.7॥
iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid yasyaiṣa mahimā bhuvi । / divye brahmapure hyeṣa vyomnyātmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ ॥ / manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīranetā / pratiṣṭhito'nne hṛdayaṃ sannidhāya । / tad vijñānena paripaśyanti dhīrā / ānandarūpamamṛtaṃ yad vibhāti ॥2.2.7॥
sayIt: yah sar-vag-YAH sar-va-VID yas-YAI-sha ma-hi-MAA BHU-vi / div-YAY brah-ma-pu-RAY HYAY-sha vyom-NYAAT-maa pra-TISH-thi-tah / ma-no-MA-yah praa-na-sha-REE-ra-NAY-taa / pra-tish-thi-TON-nay HRI-da-yum san-ni-DHAA-ya / tad vig-yaa-NAY-na pa-ri-PASH-yan-ti DHEE-raa / aa-nan-da-ROO-pum am-RI-tum yad vi-BHAA-ti
translation: He who knows all, who knows each thing in full — his is this glory upon the earth. In the divine city of Brahman, in its inner sky, that Self stands established: known through mind, leader of breath and body, settled into the heart within this food-built frame. Seeing him by clear knowledge, the wise behold everywhere the immortal that shines as bliss.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Can you look for the resident of the city today, not by leaving your body but by listening deeper into it?

translations.hi: जो सर्वज्ञ है, जो हर वस्तु को पूरा जानता है — पृथ्वी पर यह महिमा उसी की है। ब्रह्म की दिव्य नगरी में, उसके भीतरी आकाश में वह आत्मा प्रतिष्ठित है: मन से जाना जाने वाला, प्राण और शरीर का नेता, अन्न से बनी इस देह में हृदय को आसन बनाए हुए। स्पष्ट ज्ञान से देखने पर धीर पुरुष सर्वत्र उसी अमृत को देखते हैं, जो आनंद-रूप होकर चमकता है।

devanagari: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । / क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे ॥2.2.8॥
iast: bhidyate hṛdayagranthiśchidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ । / kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare ॥2.2.8॥
sayIt: BHID-ya-tay hri-da-ya-GRAN-thish-CHHID-yan-tay sar-va-sam-sha-YAAH / KSHEE-yan-tay CHAAS-ya kar-MAA-ni TAS-min DRISH-tay pa-RAA-va-ray
translation: The knot of the heart is split open, all doubts are cut through, and one's karmas wither away — when That is seen, the higher and the lower.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If your doubts are shadows of a knot rather than problems to solve, what is the knot made of?

translations.hi: हृदय की गाँठ खुल जाती है, सारे संशय कट जाते हैं, और संचित कर्म क्षीण हो जाते हैं — जब वह देख लिया जाता है, जो परे भी है और पास भी।

devanagari: हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलम् । / तच्छुभ्रं ज्योतिषं ज्योतिस्तद् यदात्मविदो विदुः ॥2.2.9॥
iast: hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajaṃ brahma niṣkalam । / tacchubhraṃ jyotiṣaṃ jyotistad yadātmavido viduḥ ॥2.2.9॥
sayIt: hi-ran-ma-YAY pa-RAY KO-shay VI-ra-jum BRAH-ma NISH-ka-lum / tach-CHHUBH-rum JYO-ti-shum JYO-tis-tad ya-DAAT-ma-vi-do VI-duh
translation: In the highest golden sheath lies Brahman — stainless, without parts. Pure it is, the light of lights: that is what the knowers of the Self know.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What is the light by which you are reading this sentence, and can you turn toward it for a moment?

translations.hi: सोने जैसे परम कोश में ब्रह्म रखा है — निर्मल, निष्कल, अखंड। वही शुभ्र है, ज्योतियों की भी ज्योति: आत्मा को जानने वाले उसी को जानते हैं।

devanagari: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं / नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । / तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं / तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥2.2.10॥
iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ / nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto'yamagniḥ । / tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ / tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ॥2.2.10॥
sayIt: na TAT-ra SOOR-yo BHAA-ti na chan-dra-TAA-ra-kum / NAY-maa VID-yu-to BHAAN-ti ku-TO-ya-MAG-nih / ta-MAY-va BHAAN-tum a-nu-BHAA-ti SAR-vum / TAS-ya BHAA-saa SAR-va-mi-dum vi-BHAA-ti
translation: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine — how then could this fire? Everything shines only after him who shines; by his light all this becomes light.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
