reflection: Before you name anything you see today, can you notice the seeing it is appearing in?

translations.hi: वहाँ न सूर्य चमकता है, न चन्द्र-तारे; ये बिजलियाँ भी वहाँ नहीं चमकतीं — फिर इस अग्नि की क्या बिसात? सब कुछ उसी के चमकने के पीछे-पीछे चमकता है; उसी के प्रकाश से यह सब प्रकाशित है।

devanagari: ब्रह्मैवेदममृतं पुरस्ताद् ब्रह्म पश्चाद् ब्रह्म दक्षिणतश्चोत्तरेण । / अधश्चोर्ध्वं च प्रसृतं ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमिदं वरिष्ठम् ॥2.2.11॥
iast: brahmaivedamamṛtaṃ purastād brahma paścād brahma dakṣiṇataścottareṇa । / adhaścordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaṃ brahmaivedaṃ viśvamidaṃ variṣṭham ॥2.2.11॥
sayIt: brah-MAI-vay-dum am-RI-tum pu-ras-TAAD BRAH-ma pash-CHAAD BRAH-ma dak-shi-na-tash-CHOT-ta-ray-na / a-dhash-CHORDH-vum cha PRA-sri-tum brah-MAI-vay-dum VISH-va-mi-dum va-RISH-thum
translation: Brahman alone is this immortal: Brahman in front, Brahman behind, Brahman to the right and to the left, Brahman spread below and above. Brahman alone is all this — this whole, the most excellent.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: In which direction do you still assume the sacred is not?

translations.hi: ब्रह्म ही यह अमृत है: आगे ब्रह्म, पीछे ब्रह्म, दाएँ ब्रह्म, बाएँ ब्रह्म; नीचे और ऊपर भी वही फैला है। ब्रह्म ही यह सब है — यही सबसे विशाल, वरिष्ठ पूर्णता।

devanagari: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । / तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति ॥3.1.1॥
iast: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte । / tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti ॥3.1.1॥
sayIt: dvaa su-par-NAA sa-yu-JAA sa-KHAA-yaa sa-MAA-num VRIK-shum pa-ri-shas-va-JAA-tay / ta-yor-AN-yah PIP-pa-lum svaad-VAT-tya-nash-nan-NAN-yo a-bhi-chaa-ka-SHEE-ti
translation: Two birds, close companions, clasp the very same tree. One of them eats the sweet pippala fruit; the other, not eating, simply looks on.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: In the middle of today's most absorbing experience, can you feel the quiet one in you who is only watching?

translations.hi: दो पक्षी, घनिष्ठ साथी, एक ही पेड़ से लिपटे बैठे हैं। उनमें से एक मीठा पीपल-फल चखता है; दूसरा बिना खाए बस देखता रहता है।

devanagari: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽ / नीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । / जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य / महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥3.1.2॥
iast: samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagno' / nīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ । / juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśamasya / mahimānamiti vītaśokaḥ ॥3.1.2॥
sayIt: sa-MAA-nay VRIK-shay PU-ru-sho ni-mag-NO a-nee-sha-YAA SHO-cha-ti muh-ya-MAA-nah / JUSH-tum ya-DAA PASH-yat-yan-yam-EE-sham-as-ya ma-hi-MAA-nam-i-ti vee-ta-SHO-kah
translation: On that same tree a person sits sunk down, grieving, deluded by his own helplessness. But when he sees the other — the beloved Lord — and sees "this glory is his," he becomes free of sorrow.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: When you feel stuck and helpless today, what happens if you pause the tasting and simply look for the companion who watches?

translations.hi: उसी पेड़ पर एक व्यक्ति डूबा बैठा है — अपनी बेबसी से मोहित होकर शोक करता हुआ। पर जब वह दूसरे को — पूजित प्रभु को — देखता है और समझता है कि "यह महिमा उसी की है," तब वह शोक से मुक्त हो जाता है।

devanagari: यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णं / कर्तारमीशं पुरुषं ब्रह्मयोनिम् । / तदा विद्वान् पुण्यपापे विधूय / निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैति ॥3.1.3॥
iast: yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ / kartāramīśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim । / tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya / nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaiti ॥3.1.3॥
sayIt: ya-DAA PASH-yah PASH-ya-tay ruk-ma-VAR-num / kar-TAA-ram-EE-shum PU-ru-shum brah-ma-YO-nim / ta-DAA vid-VAAN pun-ya-PAA-pay vi-DHOO-ya / ni-RAN-ja-nah pa-ra-MUM SAAM-yam-u-PAI-ti
translation: When the seer sees the golden-hued one — the maker, the Lord, the Person, the source of Brahma — then the knower, shaking off merit and sin, stainless, reaches the supreme sameness.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If both your failures and your achievements were set down together, what would remain of you?

translations.hi: जब देखने वाला उस स्वर्ण-वर्ण को देखता है — कर्ता, ईश, पुरुष, ब्रह्मा के भी स्रोत को — तब वह ज्ञानी पुण्य और पाप दोनों झाड़कर, निर्मल होकर, परम साम्य को प्राप्त होता है।

devanagari: प्रणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति / विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । / आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावा- / नेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥3.1.4॥
iast: praṇo hyeṣa yaḥ sarvabhūtairvibhāti / vijānan vidvān bhavate nātivādī । / ātmakrīḍa ātmaratiḥ kriyāvā- / neṣa brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ ॥3.1.4॥
sayIt: praa-NO HYAY-sha yah sar-va-BHOO-tair-vi-BHAA-ti / vi-JAA-nun vid-VAAN BHA-va-tay naa-ti-VAA-dee / aat-ma-KREE-da aat-ma-RA-tih kri-yaa-VAAN / AY-sha brah-ma-vi-DAAM va-RISH-thah
translation: He is truly the life that shines out through all beings. Knowing him, the wise one stops arguing past others. Playing in the Self, delighting in the Self, yet full of action — such a one is the best of the knowers of Brahman.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Is there a truth you defend in argument more often than you rest in it?

translations.hi: वही तो प्राण है जो सब प्राणियों में चमकता है। उसे जानकर ज्ञानी वितंडा करना छोड़ देता है। आत्मा में खेलता, आत्मा में रमता, फिर भी कर्मशील — ऐसा व्यक्ति ब्रह्म को जानने वालों में श्रेष्ठ है।

devanagari: सत्येन लभ्यस्तपसा ह्येष आत्मा / सम्यग्ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् । / अन्तःशरीरे ज्योतिर्मयो हि शुभ्रो / यं पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीणदोषाः ॥3.1.5॥
iast: satyena labhyastapasā hyeṣa ātmā / samyagjñānena brahmacaryeṇa nityam । / antaḥśarīre jyotirmayo hi śubhro / yaṃ paśyanti yatayaḥ kṣīṇadoṣāḥ ॥3.1.5॥
sayIt: sat-YAY-na LAB-hyas-ta-pa-SAA HYAY-sha AAT-maa / sam-yag-GYAA-nay-na brah-ma-char-YAY-na NIT-yum / an-tah-sha-REE-ray jyo-tir-MA-yo hi SHUB-hro / yum PASH-yan-ti ya-TA-yah ksheen-a-DO-shaah
translation: By truth this Self can be won — by tapas, by right knowledge, by constant brahmacharya. Within the body he dwells, made of light, radiant; the strivers whose faults have worn thin see him.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which one fault of yours could daily, unheroic practice begin to thin this week?

translations.hi: सत्य से यह आत्मा पाया जाता है — तप से, सम्यक् ज्ञान से, निरंतर ब्रह्मचर्य से। शरीर के भीतर ही वह है — ज्योतिर्मय, शुभ्र; जिन साधकों के दोष क्षीण हो चुके हैं, वे ही उसे देख पाते हैं।

devanagari: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं / सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । / येनाऽऽक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा / यत्र तत् सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥3.1.6॥
iast: satyameva jayate nānṛtaṃ / satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ । / yenā''kramantyṛṣayo hyāptakāmā / yatra tat satyasya paramaṃ nidhānam ॥3.1.6॥
sayIt: sat-yam-AY-va JA-ya-tay NAAN-ri-tum / sat-YAY-na PAN-thaa vi-ta-TO day-va-YAA-nah / yay-NAAK-ra-mant-yri-sha-yo hyaap-ta-KAA-maa / YAT-ra tat sat-YAS-ya pa-ra-MUM ni-DHAA-num
translation: Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood. By truth is laid the path called the way of the gods, by which the seers whose desires are fulfilled ascend to where truth's supreme treasure lies.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Where in your life are you hoping truth will win eventually, without yet being willing to walk on it today?

translations.hi: सत्य ही जीतता है, असत्य नहीं। सत्य से ही वह देवयान पथ बिछा है, जिस पर आप्तकाम ऋषि चढ़ते हैं — वहाँ तक, जहाँ सत्य का परम निधान है।

devanagari: बृहच्च तद् दिव्यमचिन्त्यरूपं / सूक्ष्माच्च तत् सूक्ष्मतरं विभाति । / दूरात् सुदूरे तदिहान्तिके च / पश्यन्त्विहैव निहितं गुहायाम् ॥3.1.7॥
iast: bṛhacca tad divyamacintyarūpaṃ / sūkṣmācca tat sūkṣmataraṃ vibhāti । / dūrāt sudūre tadihāntike ca / paśyantvihaiva nihitaṃ guhāyām ॥3.1.7॥
sayIt: bri-HUCH-cha tud DIV-yam-a-chin-tya-ROO-pum / sook-SHMAACH-cha tut sook-shma-TA-rum vi-BHAA-ti / doo-RAAT su-DOO-ray tad-i-HAAN-ti-kay cha / pash-YAN-tvi-HAI-va ni-hi-TUM gu-HAA-yaam
translation: Vast is That, divine, of a form beyond thought, and it shines forth subtler than the subtle. It is farther than the farthest, and yet here, close at hand — hidden, right here, in the cave of the heart.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What have you been seeking at a distance that might be waiting in the one place you have not looked — right here?

translations.hi: वह विराट है, दिव्य है, जिसका रूप सोच से परे है; और वह सूक्ष्म से भी सूक्ष्मतर होकर चमकता है। वह दूर से भी सुदूर है, और फिर भी यहीं, पास ही है — यहीं, हृदय की गुहा में छिपा हुआ।

devanagari: न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा / नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मण वा । / ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्व- / स्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं / ध्यायमानः ॥3.1.8॥
iast: na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate nāpi vācā / nānyairdevaistapasā karmaṇa vā । / jñānaprasādena viśuddhasattva- / statastu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ / dhyāyamānaḥ ॥3.1.8॥
sayIt: na chak-shu-SHAA GRIH-ya-tay NAA-pi VAA-chaa / NAAN-yair-day-VAIS-ta-pa-SAA kar-ma-NAA vaa / gyaa-na-pra-SAA-day-na vi-shud-dha-SAT-tvas / ta-TAS-tu tum PASH-ya-tay nish-ka-LUM dhyaa-ya-MAA-nah
translation: He is not grasped by the eye, nor by speech, nor by the other senses, nor by austerity or ritual work. But when one's being has become pure through the clarity of knowledge, then, meditating, one sees him — the indivisible.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What would clear on its own today if you simply stopped stirring it?

translations.hi: वह न आँख से पकड़ में आता है, न वाणी से, न अन्य इंद्रियों से, न तप या कर्मकांड से। पर जब ज्ञान की प्रसन्नता से अंतःकरण शुद्ध हो जाता है, तब ध्यान करता हुआ साधक उस निष्कल — अखंड — को देख लेता है।

devanagari: एषोऽणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यो / यस्मिन् प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश । / प्राणैश्चित्तं सर्वमोतं प्रजानां / यस्मिन् विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा ॥3.1.9॥
iast: eṣo'ṇurātmā cetasā veditavyo / yasmin prāṇaḥ pañcadhā saṃviveśa । / prāṇaiścittaṃ sarvamotaṃ prajānāṃ / yasmin viśuddhe vibhavatyeṣa ātmā ॥3.1.9॥
sayIt: ay-SHO a-nu-RAAT-maa chay-ta-SAA vay-di-TAV-yo / YAS-min PRAA-nah pan-cha-DHAA sam-vi-VAY-sha / praa-naish-CHIT-tum sar-va-MO-tum pra-jaa-NAAM / YAS-min vi-SHUD-dhay vi-bha-VAT-yay-sha AAT-maa
translation: This subtle Self is to be known by awareness — here, where the life-breath has entered fivefold. Every creature's mind is woven through with these breaths; when that mind is purified, this Self shines forth.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If your mind is woven from your breath, what might ten slow breaths do to the weave today?

translations.hi: यह सूक्ष्म आत्मा चेतना से ही जानने योग्य है — यहीं, जहाँ प्राण पाँच रूपों में समाया है। हर प्राणी का चित्त इन्हीं प्राणों से बुना है; जब वह चित्त शुद्ध होता है, तब यह आत्मा प्रकट होकर चमक उठता है।

devanagari: यं यं लोकं मनसा संविभाति / विशुद्धसत्त्वः कामयते यांश्च कामान् । / तं तं लोकं जयते तांश्च कामां- / स्तस्मादात्मज्ञं ह्यर्चयेत् भूतिकामः ॥3.1.10॥
iast: yaṃ yaṃ lokaṃ manasā saṃvibhāti / viśuddhasattvaḥ kāmayate yāṃśca kāmān । / taṃ taṃ lokaṃ jayate tāṃśca kāmāṃ- / stasmādātmajñaṃ hyarcayet bhūtikāmaḥ ॥3.1.10॥
sayIt: yum yum LO-kum ma-na-SAA sam-vi-BHAA-ti / vi-shud-dha-SAT-tvah kaa-ma-YA-tay YAAMSH-cha kaa-MAAN / tum tum LO-kum ja-YA-tay TAAMSH-cha kaa-MAAMS / tas-MAAD aat-ma-GYUM hyar-cha-YAYT bhoo-ti-KAA-mah
translation: Whatever world a person of purified being pictures in the mind, whatever desires he desires — that very world and those desires he wins. Therefore let anyone who longs for well-being honour the knower of the Self.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Whose company reliably clears your mind, and when did you last simply sit near them?

translations.hi: शुद्ध अंतःकरण वाला व्यक्ति मन से जिस लोक की कल्पना करता है, जिन कामनाओं की कामना करता है — वह उसी लोक को और उन्हीं कामनाओं को पा लेता है। इसलिए कल्याण चाहने वाला आत्मा को जानने वाले का आदर करे।

devanagari: स वेदैतत् परमं ब्रह्म धाम / यत्र विश्वं निहितं भाति शुभ्रम् । / उपासते पुरुषं ये ह्यकामास्ते / शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति धीराः ॥3.2.1॥
iast: sa vedaitat paramaṃ brahma dhāma / yatra viśvaṃ nihitaṃ bhāti śubhram । / upāsate puruṣaṃ ye hyakāmāste / śukrametadativartanti dhīrāḥ ॥3.2.1॥
sayIt: sa vay-DAI-tat pa-ra-MUM BRAH-ma DHAA-ma / YAT-ra VISH-vum ni-hi-TUM BHAA-ti SHU-bhrum / u-PAA-sa-tay PU-ru-shum yay hya-kaa-MAAS-tay / SHUK-rum AY-tad a-ti-VAR-tan-ti DHEE-raah
translation: Such a knower knows that supreme Brahman — the abode where the whole world rests, shining pure. The wise who worship the Person free of all desire pass beyond this seed of birth.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What would your reverence look like today if it asked for nothing at all?

translations.hi: ऐसा ज्ञानी उस परम ब्रह्म को जानता है — वह धाम, जिसमें सारा विश्व टिका हुआ निर्मल चमकता है। जो धीर निष्काम होकर उस पुरुष की उपासना करते हैं, वे जन्म के इस बीज के पार निकल जाते हैं।

devanagari: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः / स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र । / पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु / इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ॥3.2.2॥
iast: kāmān yaḥ kāmayate manyamānaḥ / sa kāmabhirjāyate tatra tatra । / paryāptakāmasya kṛtātmanastu / ihaiva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ ॥3.2.2॥
sayIt: kaa-MAAN yah kaa-ma-YA-tay man-ya-MAA-nah / sa KAA-ma-bhir JAA-ya-tay TAT-ra TAT-ra / par-yaap-ta-KAA-mas-ya kri-TAAT-ma-nas-tu / i-HAI-va SAR-vay pra-vi-LEE-yan-ti KAA-maah
translation: Whoever keeps desiring desires, dwelling on them, is born through those very desires, here and there. But for one whose desire is fulfilled, whose self is made whole, all desires dissolve right here.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What is the one want you keep rehearsing, and what would this hour feel like if you were already full?

translations.hi: जो कामनाओं में डूबा उन्हीं की कामना करता रहता है, वह उन्हीं कामनाओं के ज़रिए जहाँ-तहाँ जन्म लेता है। पर जिसकी कामना पूरी हो चुकी, जिसका आत्मा सध गया, उसकी सारी कामनाएँ यहीं — इसी जीवन में — घुल जाती हैं।

devanagari: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो / न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । / यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्य- / स्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम् ॥3.2.3॥
iast: nāyamātmā pravacanena labhyo / na medhayā na bahunā śrutena । / yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhya- / stasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām ॥3.2.3॥
sayIt: naa-ya-MAAT-maa pra-va-cha-NAY-na LABH-yo / na may-dha-YAA na ba-hu-NAA shru-TAY-na / ya-may-VAI-sha vri-NU-tay TAY-na LABH-yas / tas-YAI-sha AAT-maa vi-vri-NU-tay ta-NOOM svaam
translation: This Self is not attained by discourse, nor by intellect, nor by much hearing. Whom this very Self chooses, by him it is attained — to him this Self unveils its own form.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: What would your seeking look like if it were less like studying for an exam and more like waiting for a beloved?

translations.hi: यह आत्मा न प्रवचन से मिलता है, न बुद्धि से, न बहुत सुनने से। जिसे यह स्वयं चुनता है, उसी को मिलता है — उसी के आगे यह आत्मा अपना स्वरूप खोल देता है।

devanagari: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो / न च प्रमादात् तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् । / एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वां- / स्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम ॥3.2.4॥
iast: nāyamātmā balahīnena labhyo / na ca pramādāt tapaso vāpyaliṅgāt । / etairupāyairyatate yastu vidvāṃ- / stasyaiṣa ātmā viśate brahmadhāma ॥3.2.4॥
sayIt: naa-ya-MAAT-maa ba-la-HEE-nay-na LABH-yo / na cha pra-maa-DAAT ta-pa-SO vaap-ya-lin-GAAT / ay-tair-u-PAA-yair ya-ta-TAY YAS-tu vid-VAAMS / tas-YAI-sha AAT-maa vi-sha-TAY brah-ma-DHAA-ma
translation: This Self is not attained by one without strength, nor through carelessness, nor by discipline that lacks its true mark. But the wise one who strives by these means — his self enters the abode of Brahman.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Where is your effort leaking in small ways, and what would gathering it into one careful stream change today?

translations.hi: यह आत्मा न बलहीन को मिलता है, न प्रमाद से, न ऐसे तप से जिसमें सच्चा लक्षण न हो। पर जो ज्ञानी इन उपायों से यत्न करता है, उसका आत्मा ब्रह्म के धाम में प्रवेश करता है।

devanagari: संप्राप्यैनमृषयो ज्ञानतृप्ताः / कृतात्मानो वीतरागाः प्रशान्ताः / ते सर्वगं सर्वतः प्राप्य धीरा / युक्तात्मानः सर्वमेवाविशन्ति ॥3.2.5॥
iast: saṃprāpyainamṛṣayo jñānatṛptāḥ / kṛtātmāno vītarāgāḥ praśāntāḥ / te sarvagaṃ sarvataḥ prāpya dhīrā / yuktātmānaḥ sarvamevāviśanti ॥3.2.5॥
sayIt: sam-praap-YAI-num RI-sha-yo gyaa-na-TRIP-taah / kri-TAAT-maa-no vee-ta-RAA-gaah pra-SHAAN-taah / tay SAR-va-gum sar-va-TAH PRAAP-ya DHEE-raa / yuk-TAAT-maa-nah sar-va-may-VAA-vi-shan-ti
translation: Having attained him, the seers are satisfied with knowledge, their selves made whole, passions gone, deeply calm. Finding the all-pervading everywhere, joined to it in self, the wise enter into the very all.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which is furthest from you right now — satisfied, whole, passion-free, or quiet — and what one small step leans toward it?

translations.hi: उसे पाकर ऋषि ज्ञान से तृप्त हो जाते हैं — सधे हुए आत्मा वाले, राग-मुक्त, प्रशांत। सर्वव्यापी को सब ओर पाकर, आत्मा से उसी में जुड़े हुए, वे धीर स्वयं सर्वस्व में प्रवेश कर जाते हैं।

devanagari: वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः / संन्यासयोगाद् यतयः शुद्धसत्त्वाः । / ते ब्रह्मलोकेषु परान्तकाले / परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वे ॥3.2.6॥
iast: vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ / saṃnyāsayogād yatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ । / te brahmalokeṣu parāntakāle / parāmṛtāḥ parimucyanti sarve ॥3.2.6॥
sayIt: vay-daan-ta-vi-GYAA-na-su-nish-chi-TAAR-thaah / san-nyaa-sa-yo-GAAD ya-ta-YAH shud-dha-SAT-tvaah / tay brah-ma-lo-KAY-shu pa-raan-ta-KAA-lay / pa-raam-ri-TAAH pa-ri-MUCH-yan-ti SAR-vay
translation: Those who have made the truth certain through Vedanta-knowledge, strivers purified in being through the yoga of renunciation — at the final hour, in the worlds of Brahman, beyond death's reach, they are all completely freed.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which of your convictions has actually been tested until certain, and which are borrowed opinions still waiting for the test?

translations.hi: जिन्होंने वेदांत-विज्ञान से सत्य को सुनिश्चित कर लिया, जो संन्यास-योग से शुद्ध अंतःकरण वाले यति हैं — वे अंतिम काल में ब्रह्मलोकों में, परम अमृत होकर, सब के सब पूर्ण मुक्त हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: गताः कलाः पञ्चदश प्रतिष्ठा / देवाश्च सर्वे प्रतिदेवतासु । / कर्माणि विज्ञानमयश्च आत्मा / परेऽव्यये सर्वे एकीभवन्ति ॥3.2.7॥
iast: gatāḥ kalāḥ pañcadaśa pratiṣṭhā / devāśca sarve pratidevatāsu । / karmāṇi vijñānamayaśca ātmā / pare'vyaye sarve ekībhavanti ॥3.2.7॥
sayIt: ga-TAAH ka-LAAH pan-cha-DA-sha pra-tish-THAA / day-VAASH-cha SAR-vay pra-ti-day-va-TAA-su / kar-MAA-ni vi-GYAA-na-ma-yash-cha AAT-maa / pa-RAY AV-ya-yay SAR-vay ay-kee-BHA-van-ti
translation: The fifteen parts go back to their foundations; all the deities of the body return to their presiding gods. Actions, and the self made of understanding — all become one in the supreme Imperishable.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which of the things you call "mine" — breath, body, cleverness — is really on loan, and from where?

translations.hi: पंद्रह कलाएँ अपनी-अपनी प्रतिष्ठाओं में लौट जाती हैं; देह के सारे देव अपने-अपने अधिष्ठाता देवताओं में। कर्म, और विज्ञानमय आत्मा — सब कुछ परम अव्यय में एक हो जाता है।

devanagari: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽ / स्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय । / तथा विद्वान् नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः / परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥3.2.8॥
iast: yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre' / staṃ gacchanti nāmarūpe vihāya । / tathā vidvān nāmarūpādvimuktaḥ / parātparaṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam ॥3.2.8॥
sayIt: ya-THAA NAD-yah syan-da-MAA-naah sa-mud-RAY AS-tum / gach-CHAN-ti naa-ma-ROO-pay vi-HAA-ya / ta-THAA vid-VAAN naa-ma-roo-PAAD vi-MUK-tah / pa-RAAT-pa-rum PU-ru-shum u-PAI-ti DIV-yum
translation: As flowing rivers disappear into the sea, leaving name and form behind, so the knower, freed from name and form, reaches the divine Person beyond the beyond.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If your name and your outline were set down for one minute, what would still be flowing?

translations.hi: जैसे बहती नदियाँ नाम और रूप छोड़कर समुद्र में विलीन हो जाती हैं, वैसे ही ज्ञानी नाम-रूप से छूटकर परात्पर दिव्य पुरुष तक पहुँच जाता है।

devanagari: स यो ह वै तत् परमं ब्रह्म वेद / ब्रह्मैव भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति । / तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानं गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो / विमुक्तोऽमृतो भवति ॥3.2.9॥
iast: sa yo ha vai tat paramaṃ brahma veda / brahmaiva bhavati nāsyābrahmavitkule bhavati । / tarati śokaṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ guhāgranthibhyo / vimukto'mṛto bhavati ॥3.2.9॥
sayIt: sa yo ha vai tat pa-ra-MUM BRAH-ma VAY-da / brah-MAI-va BHA-va-ti naas-yaa-BRAH-ma-vit KU-lay BHA-va-ti / TA-ra-ti SHO-kum TA-ra-ti paap-MAA-num / gu-haa-GRAN-thi-bhyo vi-MUK-to AM-ri-to BHA-va-ti
translation: Truly, whoever knows that supreme Brahman becomes Brahman itself; in his family none is born who does not know Brahman. He crosses beyond sorrow, crosses beyond wrong; freed from the knots of the heart, he becomes immortal.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Which knot in your heart — a grievance worn as identity, a fear dressed as love — is ready to loosen first?

translations.hi: सचमुच, जो उस परम ब्रह्म को जानता है, वह ब्रह्म ही हो जाता है; उसके कुल में कोई ब्रह्म से अनजान नहीं जन्मता। वह शोक के पार चला जाता है, पाप के पार चला जाता है; हृदय की गाँठों से छूटकर अमर हो जाता है।

devanagari: तदेतदृचाऽभ्युक्तम् । / क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रिया ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः / स्वयं जुह्वत एकर्षिं श्रद्धयन्तः । / तेषामेवैतां ब्रह्मविद्यां वदेत / शिरोव्रतं विधिवद् यैस्तु चीर्णम् ॥3.2.10॥
iast: tadetadṛcā'bhyuktam । / kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyā brahmaniṣṭhāḥ / svayaṃ juhvata ekarṣiṃ śraddhayantaḥ । / teṣāmevaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta / śirovrataṃ vidhivad yaistu cīrṇam ॥3.2.10॥
sayIt: ta-day-tad ri-CHAA a-bhyuk-tum / kri-yaa-VAN-tah SHRO-tri-yaa brah-ma-NISH-thaah / sva-YUM JUH-va-ta ay-KAR-shim shrad-dha-YAN-tah / tay-shaa-may-VAI-taam brah-ma-VID-yaam va-DAY-ta / shi-ro-VRA-tum vi-dhi-VAD YAIS-tu CHEER-num
translation: This is declared by the Rig verse: those who perform the rites, learned in the Veda, established in Brahman, who with faith make offerings themselves into the One-Seer fire — to them alone may one teach this knowledge of Brahman, and to those who have duly kept the vow of the head.
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Before asking for the next teaching, what would making your own hearth ready for it actually involve?

translations.hi: यही ऋचा में कहा गया है: जो कर्मपरायण हैं, श्रोत्रिय हैं, ब्रह्मनिष्ठ हैं, जो श्रद्धा से स्वयं एकर्षि अग्नि में आहुति देते हैं — यह ब्रह्मविद्या उन्हीं को कहनी चाहिए, और उन्हें जिन्होंने विधिपूर्वक शिरोव्रत निभाया हो।

devanagari: तदेतत् सत्यमृषिरङ्गिराः / पुरोवाच नैतदचीर्णव्रतोऽधीते । / नमः परमऋषिभ्यो नमः परमऋषिभ्यः ॥3.2.11॥
iast: tadetat satyamṛṣiraṅgirāḥ / purovāca naitadacīrṇavrato'dhīte । / namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyo namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyaḥ ॥3.2.11॥
sayIt: ta-DAY-tat SAT-yum RI-shir an-gi-RAAH / pu-ro-VAA-cha NAI-tad a-cheer-na-vra-TO a-DHEE-tay / NA-mah pa-ra-ma-RI-shi-bhyo NA-mah pa-ra-ma-RI-shi-bhyah
translation: This is the truth. The seer Angiras taught it long ago; one who has not kept the vow does not study it. Salutation to the supreme seers — salutation to the supreme seers!
source: Mundaka Upanishad 3.2.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: Who carried this teaching as far as you, and how do you thank a chain of teachers you will never meet?

translations.hi: यही सत्य है। ऋषि अंगिरा ने इसे बहुत पहले कहा था; जिसने व्रत नहीं निभाया, वह इसे नहीं पढ़ता। परम ऋषियों को नमन — परम ऋषियों को नमन!

devanagari: ॐ भद्रं कर्णेभिः श्रुणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः । / स्थिरैरङ्गैस्तुष्टुवाँसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः । / स्वस्ति न इन्द्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः । / स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु । / ॥ ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः
iast: oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śruṇuyāma devā bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhiryajatrāḥ । / sthirairaṅgaistuṣṭuvām̐sastanūbhirvyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ । / svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ । / svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatirdadhātu । / ॥ oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
sayIt: om bha-DRUM kar-NAY-bhih shru-nu-YAA-ma DAY-vaa bha-DRUM pash-YAY-maak-sha-bhir ya-ja-TRAAH / sthi-rair AN-gais tush-tu-VAAM-sas ta-NOO-bhir vya-SHAY-ma day-va-hi-TUM ya-DAA-yuh / SVAS-ti na IN-dro vrid-dha-SHRA-vaah SVAS-ti nah POO-shaa vish-va-VAY-daah / SVAS-ti nas TAARK-shyo a-rish-ta-NAY-mih SVAS-ti no bri-has-PA-tir da-DHAA-tu / om SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih
translation: Om. May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods; may we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O you worthy of worship. With steady limbs and bodies may we, singing your praise, live out the full span of life the gods have set. May Indra of ancient fame bless us; may the all-knowing Pushan bless us; may Tarkshya of the unbroken wheel bless us; may Brihaspati grant us well-being. Om — peace, peace, peace.
source: Mundaka Upanishad, shanti mantra, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D
reflection: If your ears and eyes let in only what is worth keeping today, what would you refuse at the gate?

translations.hi: ॐ। हे देवो, हम कानों से शुभ सुनें; हे पूजनीय, हम आँखों से शुभ देखें। स्थिर अंगों और स्वस्थ शरीर से आपकी स्तुति करते हुए हम वह पूरी आयु जिएँ जो देवताओं ने हमारे लिए रखी है। पुरानी कीर्ति वाले इन्द्र हमारा कल्याण करें; सब जानने वाले पूषा कल्याण करें; अखंड नेमि वाले तार्क्ष्य कल्याण करें; बृहस्पति हमें मंगल दें। ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः।

devanagari: असतो मा सद्गमय, तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय, मृत्योर्मामृतं गमयेति ।
iast: asato mā sadgamaya, tamaso mā jyotirgamaya, mṛtyormāmṛtaṃ gamayeti ।
sayIt: a-sa-TO maa sud GA-ma-ya / ta-ma-SO maa jyo-TIR GA-ma-ya / mrit-YOR maa AM-ri-tum GA-ma-ya
translation: From the unreal, lead me to the real. From darkness, lead me to light. From death, lead me to immortality.
source: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.3.28, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AC%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%95_%E0%A4%89%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D_1a
reflection: Which of the three — the real, the light, the undying — is the direction you most need to be led toward today?

translations.hi: असत् से मुझे सत् की ओर ले चलो। अंधकार से मुझे प्रकाश की ओर ले चलो। मृत्यु से मुझे अमृत की ओर ले चलो।

devanagari: तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि । / धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥१०॥
iast: tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi । / dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt ॥10॥
sayIt: tut sa-vi-TOOR va-RAYN-yum / BHAR-go DAY-vas-ya DHEE-ma-hi / dhi-YO yo nah pra-cho-da-YAAT
translation: May we hold in our heart that most excellent radiance of the god Savitṛ, the inspirer — may he set our thoughts in motion.
source: Rig Veda 3.62.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%83_%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%82_%E0%A5%A9.%E0%A5%AC%E0%A5%A8
reflection: If your first request of the day were only "let me think clearly," what might change by evening?

translations.hi: हम प्रेरक देव सवितृ के उस श्रेष्ठ तेज को अपने भीतर धारण करें — वे हमारी बुद्धि को प्रेरित करें।

devanagari: त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् । / उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान्मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात् ॥१२॥
iast: tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam । / urvārukamiva bandhanānmṛtyormukṣīya māmṛtāt ॥12॥
sayIt: tryum-BA-kum ya-JAA-ma-hay / soo-GUN-dhim POOSH-ti-var-dha-num / oor-VAA-roo-kum i-va bun-dha-NAAN / mrit-YOR mook-SHEE-ya MAA-mri-taat
translation: We worship the three-eyed one, fragrant, who nourishes all that grows. As a cucumber is released from its stem, may I be released from death — not from immortality.
source: Rig Veda 7.59.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%83_%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%82_%E0%A5%AD.%E0%A5%AB%E0%A5%AF
reflection: What are you holding onto that, like the ripe cucumber, might be ready to let go of you?

translations.hi: हम त्रिनेत्रधारी की उपासना करते हैं — सुगंधित, पुष्टि बढ़ाने वाले। जैसे पकी ककड़ी अपनी बेल के बंधन से सहज छूट जाती है, वैसे ही मैं मृत्यु के बंधन से छूटूँ — अमृत से नहीं।

devanagari: ॐ ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति । / किं कारणं ब्रह्म कुतः स्म जाता जीवाम केन क्व च सम्प्रतिष्ठा । / अधिष्ठिताः केन सुखेतरेषु वर्तामहे ब्रह्मविदो व्यवस्थाम् ॥1.1॥
iast: oṃ brahmavādino vadanti । / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ brahma kutaḥ sma jātā jīvāma kena kva ca sampratiṣṭhā । / adhiṣṭhitāḥ kena sukhetareṣu vartāmahe brahmavido vyavasthām ॥1.1॥
sayIt: om brah-ma-VAA-di-no VA-dun-ti / kim KAA-ra-num BRAH-ma koo-TAH sma JAA-taa jee-VAA-ma KAY-na kva cha sam-pra-TISH-thaa / a-dhish-thi-TAAH KAY-na soo-khay-ta-RAY-shoo var-TAA-ma-hay brah-ma-vi-DO vya-vas-THAAM
translation: Om. Those who inquire into Brahman ask: What is the cause — is it Brahman? From what were we born? By what do we live, and on what are we established? Governed by whom, O knowers of Brahman, do we move through our appointed course of joys and sorrows?
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which of the opening questions — where do I come from, what carries me, who governs my joys and sorrows — is most alive in you today?

translations.hi: ॐ। ब्रह्म की चर्चा करने वाले पूछते हैं: कारण क्या है — क्या ब्रह्म? हम कहाँ से जन्मे हैं? किसके सहारे जीते हैं, और किस पर टिके हैं? हे ब्रह्म के ज्ञाताओं, किसके शासन में हम सुख-दुःख की इस व्यवस्था से गुज़रते हैं?

devanagari: कालः स्वभावो नियतिर्यदृच्छा भूतानि योनिः पुरुष इति चिन्त्यम् । / संयोग एषां न त्वात्मभावादात्माप्यनीशः सुखदुःखहेतोः ॥1.2॥
iast: kālaḥ svabhāvo niyatiryadṛcchā bhūtāni yoniḥ puruṣa iti cintyam । / saṃyoga eṣāṃ na tvātmabhāvādātmāpyanīśaḥ sukhaduḥkhahetoḥ ॥1.2॥
sayIt: KAA-lah sva-BHAA-vo ni-ya-TIR ya-DRICH-chhaa BHOO-taa-ni YO-nih POO-roo-sha I-ti CHIN-tyum / sum-YO-ga AY-shaam na TVAAT-ma-bhaa-VAAD aat-MAAP-ya-NEE-shah soo-kha-DOOH-kha-hay-TOH
translation: Time, inherent nature, necessity, chance, the elements, a womb, a person — these are to be considered. Nor is it a combination of these, since the self exists; yet even the self is no master, for it too is subject to pleasure and pain.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When you explain your life to yourself, which of these six — time, nature, law, luck, matter, willpower — do you lean on most?

translations.hi: काल, स्वभाव, नियति, आकस्मिक संयोग, भूत-तत्त्व, योनि, पुरुष — इन पर विचार करना चाहिए। इनका मेल भी कारण नहीं हो सकता, क्योंकि आत्मा मौजूद है; और आत्मा भी स्वामी नहीं, क्योंकि वह स्वयं सुख-दुःख के अधीन है।

devanagari: ते ध्यानयोगानुगता अपश्यन्देवात्मशक्तिं स्वगुणैर्निगूढाम् । / यः कारणानि निखिलानि तानि कालात्मयुक्तान्यधितिष्ठत्येकः ॥1.3॥
iast: te dhyānayogānugatā apaśyandevātmaśaktiṃ svaguṇairnigūḍhām । / yaḥ kāraṇāni nikhilāni tāni kālātmayuktānyadhitiṣṭhatyekaḥ ॥1.3॥
sayIt: tay dhyaa-na-yo-GAA-noo-ga-taa a-PASH-yun day-VAAT-ma-SHUK-tim sva-goo-NAIR ni-GOO-dhaam / yah kaa-ra-NAA-ni ni-khi-LAA-ni TAA-ni kaa-LAAT-ma-yook-TAAN-ya-dhi-TISH-thut-YAY-kah
translation: Those seekers, absorbed in the yoga of meditation, saw the self-power of God, hidden by its own qualities — the One who alone presides over all those causes, from time to the individual self.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What question in your life have you been trying to argue your way through that might only open in stillness?

translations.hi: ध्यान-योग में डूबे उन जिज्ञासुओं ने देव की अपनी शक्ति को देखा, जो अपने ही गुणों से ढकी हुई है — वह एक, जो काल से लेकर जीवात्मा तक उन सारे कारणों पर अकेला शासन करता है।

devanagari: तमेकनेमिं त्रिवृतं षोडशान्तं शतार्धारं विंशतिप्रत्यराभिः । / अष्टकैः षड्भिर्विश्वरूपैकपाशं त्रिमार्गभेदं द्विनिमित्तैकमोहम् ॥1.4॥
iast: tamekanemiṃ trivṛtaṃ ṣoḍaśāntaṃ śatārdhāraṃ viṃśatipratyarābhiḥ । / aṣṭakaiḥ ṣaḍbhirviśvarūpaikapāśaṃ trimārgabhedaṃ dvinimittaikamoham ॥1.4॥
sayIt: tum ay-ka-NAY-mim tri-VRI-tum sho-da-SHAAN-tum sha-TAAR-dhaa-rum vim-sha-ti-prat-ya-RAA-bhih / ash-ta-KAIH SHUD-bhir vish-va-roo-PAI-ka-PAA-shum tri-MAAR-ga-BHAY-dum dvi-ni-mit-TAI-ka-MO-hum
translation: We meditate on him as the wheel: one rim, threefold, with sixteen end-points, fifty spokes, twenty counter-spokes, and six sets of eight; its one rope of countless forms; its three different paths; its one delusion arising from two causes.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your life does sheer complexity hide the fact that one thing is actually turning everything?

translations.hi: हम उसका ध्यान चक्र के रूप में करते हैं: एक नेमि (घेरा), तीन परतें, सोलह छोर, पचास अरे, बीस प्रति-अरे और आठ-आठ के छह समूह; अनगिनत रूपों वाला उसका एक पाश; उसके तीन अलग-अलग मार्ग; और दो कारणों से उपजा उसका एक मोह।

devanagari: पञ्चस्रोतोम्बुं पञ्चयोन्युग्रवक्त्रां पञ्चप्राणोर्मिं पञ्चबुद्ध्यादिमूलाम् । / पञ्चावर्तां पञ्चदुःखौघवेगां पञ्चाशद्भेदां पञ्चपर्वामधीमः ॥1.5॥
iast: pañcasrotombuṃ pañcayonyugravaktrāṃ pañcaprāṇormiṃ pañcabuddhyādimūlām । / pañcāvartāṃ pañcaduḥkhaughavegāṃ pañcāśadbhedāṃ pañcaparvāmadhīmaḥ ॥1.5॥
sayIt: pun-cha-SRO-tom-boom pun-cha-yon-YOOG-ra-vak-traam pun-cha-praa-NOR-mim pun-cha-bood-DHYAA-di-moo-laam / pun-CHAA-var-taam pun-cha-dooh-KHOW-gha-vay-gaam pun-CHAA-shud-BHAY-daam pun-cha-PAR-vaam a-DHEE-mah
translation: We meditate on it as a river of five streams, fierce and winding from its five sources, whose waves are the five vital breaths, whose first spring is fivefold perception; with five whirlpools, driven by the rushing flood of five sorrows, with fifty divisions and five stages.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which of your five senses is the stream that most often sweeps you off your feet?

translations.hi: हम उसका ध्यान पाँच धाराओं वाली नदी के रूप में करते हैं — पाँच स्रोतों से निकली उग्र और घुमावदार, जिसकी लहरें पाँच प्राण हैं, जिसका पहला सोता पाँच प्रकार का बोध है; जिसमें पाँच भँवर हैं, पाँच दुःखों की तेज़ बाढ़ का वेग है, पचास भेद हैं और पाँच पड़ाव।

devanagari: सर्वाजीवे सर्वसंस्थे बृहन्ते तस्मिन्हंसो भ्राम्यते ब्रह्मचक्रे । / पृथगात्मानं प्रेरितारं च मत्वा जुष्टस्ततस्तेनामृतत्वमेति ॥1.6॥
iast: sarvājīve sarvasaṃsthe bṛhante tasminhaṃso bhrāmyate brahmacakre । / pṛthagātmānaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā juṣṭastatastenāmṛtatvameti ॥1.6॥
sayIt: sar-VAA-jee-vay sar-va-SUM-sthay bri-HUN-tay TUS-min HUM-so BHRAAM-ya-tay brah-ma-CHUK-ray / pri-thug aat-MAA-num pray-ri-TAA-rum cha mut-VAA JOOSH-tus TA-tus tay-NAAM-ri-TUT-vum AY-ti
translation: In that vast wheel of Brahman, in which all things live and all things rest, the swan of the soul is whirled about. When it has known the self and the Mover as distinct, then, blessed by him, it goes to immortality.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Does your life today feel like being whirled by the wheel, or carried by the one who turns it?

translations.hi: उस विशाल ब्रह्म-चक्र में, जिसमें सब कुछ जीता है और सब कुछ ठहरता है, आत्मा रूपी हंस चक्कर खाता रहता है। जब वह अपने-आप को और चलाने वाले (प्रेरक) को अलग-अलग जान लेता है, तब उसकी कृपा पाकर अमरत्व को प्राप्त होता है।

devanagari: उद्गीतमेतत्परमं तु ब्रह्म तस्मिंस्त्रयं सुप्रतिष्ठाऽक्षरं च । / अत्रान्तरं ब्रह्मविदो विदित्वा लीना ब्रह्मणि तत्परा योनिमुक्ताः ॥1.7॥
iast: udgītametatparamaṃ tu brahma tasmiṃstrayaṃ supratiṣṭhā'kṣaraṃ ca । / atrāntaraṃ brahmavido viditvā līnā brahmaṇi tatparā yonimuktāḥ ॥1.7॥
sayIt: ood-GEE-tum AY-tut PA-ra-mum too BRAH-ma TUS-mims TRA-yum soo-pra-TISH-thaak-sha-rum cha / a-TRAAN-ta-rum brah-ma-vi-DO vi-dit-VAA LEE-naa BRAH-ma-ni TUT-pa-raa yo-ni-MOOK-taah
translation: This has been sung as the supreme Brahman: in it stands the triad, and it is the firm foundation, the imperishable. Knowers of Brahman, having known what is within it, are merged in Brahman; intent on it, they are freed from the womb of rebirth.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What would change today if you treated the deepest thing in you as also the most solid thing in you?

translations.hi: यही परम ब्रह्म कहकर गाया गया है: उसमें वह त्रिक प्रतिष्ठित है, और वही सुदृढ़ आधार है, अविनाशी है। ब्रह्म को जानने वाले, उसके भीतर के तत्त्व को जानकर, ब्रह्म में लीन हो जाते हैं; उसी में तत्पर होकर वे जन्म के चक्र से मुक्त हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: संयुक्तमेतत्क्षरमक्षरं च व्यक्ताव्यक्तं भरते विश्वमीशः । / अनीशश्चात्मा बध्यते भोक्तृभावाज्ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥1.8॥
iast: saṃyuktametatkṣaramakṣaraṃ ca vyaktāvyaktaṃ bharate viśvamīśaḥ । / anīśaścātmā badhyate bhoktṛbhāvājjñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ॥1.8॥
sayIt: sum-YOOK-tum AY-tut KSHA-rum a-KSHA-rum cha vyuk-TAAV-yuk-tum BHA-ra-tay VISH-vum EE-shah / a-NEE-shush CHAAT-maa BUDH-ya-tay bhok-tri-BHAA-vaaj gyaat-VAA DAY-vum MOOCH-ya-tay sar-va-PAA-shaih
translation: The Lord carries all this, joined together — the perishable and the imperishable, the manifest and the unmanifest. But the self, no lord, is bound, because it takes the enjoyer's stance; when it knows the God, it is released from every fetter.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which knot in your life is really just the habit of standing before the world as its consumer?

translations.hi: ईश्वर इस सबको धारण करता है — नाशवान और अविनाशी, व्यक्त और अव्यक्त, सब जुड़ा हुआ। पर आत्मा, जो स्वामी नहीं है, भोक्ता का रुख़ अपनाने से बँध जाती है; और जब वह देव को जान लेती है, तो हर पाश से छूट जाती है।

devanagari: ज्ञाज्ञौ द्वावजावीशनीशावजा ह्येका भोक्तृभोग्यार्थयुक्ता । / अनन्तश्चात्मा विश्वरूपो ह्यकर्ता त्रयं यदा विन्दते ब्रह्ममेतत् ॥1.9॥
iast: jñājñau dvāvajāvīśanīśāvajā hyekā bhoktṛbhogyārthayuktā । / anantaścātmā viśvarūpo hyakartā trayaṃ yadā vindate brahmametat ॥1.9॥
sayIt: gyaa-GYOW DVAAV-a-jaav EE-sha-NEE-shaav a-JAA hyay-KAA bhok-tri-bho-GYAAR-tha-yook-TAA / a-NUN-tush CHAAT-maa vish-va-ROO-po hya-KAR-taa TRA-yum ya-DAA VIN-da-tay BRAH-mum AY-tut
translation: Two are unborn — the knower and the unknowing, the lord and the not-lord — and one unborn she is harnessed to the enjoyer and the things enjoyed. And the self is infinite, of universal form, no doer. When one finds this triad, that is Brahman.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When you tell yourself the story of your day, which of the three do you leave out — the world, the soul, or the Lord?

translations.hi: दो अजन्मे हैं — एक ज्ञाता, एक अनजान; एक स्वामी, एक अस्वामी — और एक अजन्मा वह (प्रकृति) है, जो भोक्ता और भोग्य पदार्थों के काम में जुती हुई है। और आत्मा अनंत है, विश्वरूप है, अकर्ता है। जब कोई इस त्रिक को पा लेता है, वही ब्रह्म है।

devanagari: क्षरं प्रधानममृताक्षरं हरः क्षरात्मानावीशते देव एकः । / तस्याभिध्यानाद्योजनात्तत्त्वभावाद्भूयश्चान्ते विश्वमायानिवृत्तिः ॥1.10॥
iast: kṣaraṃ pradhānamamṛtākṣaraṃ haraḥ kṣarātmānāvīśate deva ekaḥ । / tasyābhidhyānādyojanāttattvabhāvādbhūyaścānte viśvamāyānivṛttiḥ ॥1.10॥
sayIt: KSHA-rum pra-DHAA-num am-ri-TAAK-sha-rum HA-rah ksha-RAAT-maa-naav EE-sha-tay DAY-va AY-kah / tus-YAA-bhi-DHYAA-naad yo-ja-NAAT tut-tva-BHAA-vaad BHOO-yush CHAAN-tay vish-va-MAA-yaa-ni-VRIT-tih
translation: Perishable is primal matter; immortal and imperishable is Hara. Over both the perishable and the self rules the one God. By meditating on him, by joining oneself to him, by becoming his reality more and more, at the end all the world's illusion ceases.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What in your life do you already know to be perishable that you are still treating as the imperishable?

translations.hi: नाशवान है प्रधान (मूल प्रकृति); अमर और अविनाशी है हर। नाशवान प्रकृति और आत्मा — दोनों पर उस एक देव का शासन है। उसका ध्यान करने से, अपने को उससे जोड़ने से, अधिकाधिक उसके तत्त्व में होते जाने से, अंत में संसार की सारी माया निवृत्त हो जाती है।

devanagari: ज्ञात्वा देवं सर्वपाशापहानिः क्षीणैः क्लेशेर्जन्ममृत्युप्रहाणिः । / तस्याभिध्यानात्तृतीयं देहभेदे विश्वैश्वर्यं केवल आप्तकामः ॥1.11॥
iast: jñātvā devaṃ sarvapāśāpahāniḥ kṣīṇaiḥ kleśerjanmamṛtyuprahāṇiḥ । / tasyābhidhyānāttṛtīyaṃ dehabhede viśvaiśvaryaṃ kevala āptakāmaḥ ॥1.11॥
sayIt: gyaat-VAA DAY-vum sar-va-paa-SHAA-pa-HAA-nih KSHEE-naih KLAY-shair jun-ma-MRIT-yoo-pra-HAA-nih / tus-YAA-bhi-DHYAA-naat tri-TEE-yum day-ha-BHAY-day vish-VAISH-var-yum KAY-va-la aap-ta-KAA-mah
translation: When the God is known, all fetters fall away; with the afflictions worn thin, birth and death come to an end. By meditating on him there is a third state — at the body's parting, lordship over all; whole in oneself, every longing fulfilled.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If steady attention really is the key that loosens your tightest knots, what will you give it to first each day?

translations.hi: देव को जान लेने पर सारे पाश गिर जाते हैं; क्लेशों के क्षीण होने पर जन्म-मृत्यु का क्रम थम जाता है। उसके ध्यान से एक तीसरी अवस्था मिलती है — देह छूटने पर सर्व-ऐश्वर्य; और केवल (अपने-आप में पूर्ण) होकर मनुष्य आप्तकाम हो जाता है — उसकी हर चाह पूरी।

devanagari: एतज्ज्ञेयं नित्यमेवात्मसंस्थं नातः परं वेदितव्यं हि किञ्चित् । / भोक्ता भोग्यं प्रेरितारं च मत्वा सर्वं प्रोक्तं त्रिविधं ब्रह्ममेतत् ॥1.12॥
iast: etajjñeyaṃ nityamevātmasaṃsthaṃ nātaḥ paraṃ veditavyaṃ hi kiñcit । / bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā sarvaṃ proktaṃ trividhaṃ brahmametat ॥1.12॥
sayIt: AY-tuj GYAY-yum NIT-yum ay-VAAT-ma-sum-sthum NAA-tah PA-rum vay-di-TUV-yum hi KIN-chit / bhok-TAA BHO-gyum pray-ri-TAA-rum cha mut-VAA SAR-vum PROK-tum TRI-vi-dhum BRAH-mum AY-tut
translation: This is what is to be known, dwelling forever in one's own self; beyond this there is nothing further that needs knowing. When one has considered the enjoyer, the enjoyed, and the Mover, all has been said: this is the threefold Brahman.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What are you still searching for at a distance that this verse says has never left your own self?

translations.hi: जानने योग्य यही है — जो सदा अपने ही आत्मा में बसा है; इससे परे और कुछ जानना शेष नहीं। भोक्ता, भोग्य और प्रेरक — इन तीनों पर विचार कर लिया, तो सब कह दिया गया: यही त्रिविध ब्रह्म है।

devanagari: वह्नेर्यथा योनिगतस्य मूर्तिनर्दृश्यते नैव च लिङ्गनाशः । / स भूय एवेन्धनयोनिगृह्यस्तद्वोभयं वै प्रणवेन देहे ॥1.13॥
iast: vahneryathā yonigatasya mūrtinardṛśyate naiva ca liṅganāśaḥ । / sa bhūya evendhanayonigṛhyastadvobhayaṃ vai praṇavena dehe ॥1.13॥
sayIt: VAH-nayr ya-THAA yo-ni-ga-TUS-ya MOOR-tir na DRISH-ya-tay NAI-va cha ling-ga-NAA-shah / sa BHOO-ya ay-VEN-dha-na-yo-ni-GRIH-yus tud VO-bha-yum vai pra-na-VAY-na DAY-hay
translation: As the form of fire resting latent in its kindling wood is not seen, and yet its subtle essence is not lost — for it may be seized again in its source by working the fuel — so indeed are both grasped in the body by means of the praṇava, Om.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What in you feels cold and gone that might only be waiting, like fire in wood, for the right friction?

translations.hi: जैसे अपनी अरणि (काठ) में सोई आग का रूप दिखाई नहीं देता, फिर भी उसका सूक्ष्म तत्त्व नष्ट नहीं होता — मथने पर वह अपने स्रोत से फिर पकड़ में आ जाती है — वैसे ही देह में प्रणव (ॐ) के द्वारा वे दोनों पकड़ में आ जाते हैं।

devanagari: स्वदेहमरणिं कृत्वा प्रणवं चोत्तरारणिम् । / ध्याननिर्मथनाभ्यासाद्देवं पश्यन्निगूढवत् ॥1.14॥
iast: svadehamaraṇiṃ kṛtvā praṇavaṃ cottarāraṇim । / dhyānanirmathanābhyāsāddevaṃ paśyannigūḍhavat ॥1.14॥
sayIt: sva-DAY-hum a-RA-nim krit-VAA PRA-na-vum chot-ta-RAA-ra-nim / dhyaa-na-nir-ma-tha-NAA-bhyaa-saad DAY-vum PASH-yun ni-GOO-dha-vut
translation: Making your own body the lower fire-stick and the praṇava, Om, the upper, by the practice of the churning that is meditation you may see the God — hidden, as fire is hidden in wood.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your day could steady, patient repetition become the friction that warms something hidden back to life?

translations.hi: अपनी देह को नीचे की अरणि बनाकर और प्रणव (ॐ) को ऊपर की, ध्यान रूपी मंथन के अभ्यास से उस देव के दर्शन होते हैं — जो छिपा हुआ है, जैसे लकड़ी में आग।

devanagari: तिलेषु तैलं दधिनीव सर्पिरापः स्रोतःस्वरणीषु चाग्निः । / एवमात्माऽत्मनि गृह्यतेऽसौ सत्येनैनं तपसा योऽनुपश्यति ॥1.15॥
iast: tileṣu tailaṃ dadhinīva sarpirāpaḥ srotaḥsvaraṇīṣu cāgniḥ । / evamātmā'tmani gṛhyate'sau satyenainaṃ tapasā yo'nupaśyati ॥1.15॥
sayIt: ti-LAY-shoo TAI-lum da-dhi-NEE-va SAR-pir AA-pah sro-tus-sva-ra-NEE-shoo CHAAG-nih / AY-vum aat-MAAT-ma-ni GRIH-ya-tay SOW sut-YAY-nai-num ta-pa-SAA YO-noo-PASH-ya-ti
translation: As oil in sesame seeds, as butter in curds, as water in stream-beds, as fire in the kindling sticks — so is that Self grasped within one's own self, by whoever seeks him with truth and with discipline.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: The oil is already in the seed — what daily pressing are you willing to do?

translations.hi: जैसे तिलों में तेल, दही में मक्खन, जल-स्रोतों में पानी और अरणियों में आग — वैसे ही वह आत्मा अपने ही भीतर पकड़ में आता है, उसके लिए जो सत्य और तप के साथ उसे खोजता है।

devanagari: सर्वव्यापिनमात्मानं क्षीरे सर्पिरिवार्पितम् । / आत्मविद्यातपोमूलं तद्ब्रह्मोपनिषत्परं तद्ब्रह्मॊपनिषत्परमिति ॥1.16॥
iast: sarvavyāpinamātmānaṃ kṣīre sarpirivārpitam । / ātmavidyātapomūlaṃ tadbrahmopaniṣatparaṃ tadbrahmopaniṣatparamiti ॥1.16॥
sayIt: sar-va-VYAA-pi-num aat-MAA-num KSHEE-ray SAR-pir i-VAAR-pi-tum / aat-ma-vid-YAA-ta-po-MOO-lum tud brah-MO-pa-ni-shut-PA-rum tud brah-MO-pa-ni-shut-PA-rum I-ti
translation: The Self that pervades all things, as butter lies hidden throughout milk, rooted in self-knowledge and discipline — that is the Brahman, the highest teaching of the Upanishad; that is the Brahman, the highest teaching of the Upanishad.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If the sacred runs through your ordinary life like butter through milk, what churning would let you finally taste it?

translations.hi: वह आत्मा जो सबमें व्याप्त है — जैसे मक्खन दूध के कण-कण में समाया रहता है — जिसकी जड़ें आत्मविद्या और तप हैं; वही ब्रह्म है, उपनिषद का सर्वोच्च रहस्य; वही ब्रह्म है, उपनिषद का सर्वोच्च रहस्य।

devanagari: युञ्जानः प्रथमं मनस्तत्त्वाय सविता धियः । / अग्नेर्ज्योतिर्निचाय्य पृथिव्या अध्याभरत् ॥2.1॥
iast: yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ manastattvāya savitā dhiyaḥ । / agnerjyotirnicāyya pṛthivyā adhyābharat ॥2.1॥
sayIt: yoon-JAA-nah pra-tha-MAM MA-nas tat-TVAA-ya sa-vi-TAA DHI-yah / ag-NAYR JYO-tir ni-CHAAY-ya pri-thiv-YAA a-dhyaa-BHA-rat
translation: Savitṛ, first yoking the mind and stretching his thoughts toward truth, discerned the light of fire and brought it up out of the earth.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Before the day's first demand reaches you, can you pause long enough to point your mind at what is true rather than merely urgent?

translations.hi: सविता ने सबसे पहले मन को जोड़ा और बुद्धि को सत्य की ओर साधा; फिर अग्नि की ज्योति को परखकर उसे पृथ्वी से ऊपर ले आए।

devanagari: युक्तेन मनसा वयं देवस्य सवितुः सवे । / सुवर्गेयाय शक्त्या ॥2.2॥
iast: yuktena manasā vayaṃ devasya savituḥ save । / suvargeyāya śaktyā ॥2.2॥
sayIt: yook-TAY-na MA-na-saa va-YAM day-VAS-ya sa-vi-TOOH sa-VAY / soo-var-gay-YAA-ya SHAK-tyaa
translation: With mind yoked, we stand in the impelling of the god Savitṛ, striving with all our strength for the passage to the heavenly light.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in today's effort could you give your full strength while trusting that the momentum is not yours alone?

translations.hi: मन को जोड़कर हम सविता देव की प्रेरणा में खड़े हैं — स्वर्गिक प्रकाश तक पहुँचने के लिए, अपनी पूरी शक्ति के साथ।

devanagari: युक्त्वाय मनसा देवान् सुवर्यतो धिया दिवम् । / बृहज्ज्योतिः करिष्यतः सविता प्रसुवाति तान् ॥2.3॥
iast: yuktvāya manasā devān suvaryato dhiyā divam । / bṛhajjyotiḥ kariṣyataḥ savitā prasuvāti tān ॥2.3॥
sayIt: yookt-VAA-ya MA-na-saa day-VAAN soo-var-ya-TO dhi-YAA di-VAM / bri-haj-JYO-tih ka-rish-ya-TAH sa-vi-TAA pra-soo-VAA-ti taan
translation: Having yoked with the mind the gods who go by thought to heaven, to the heavenly light — the gods who will make the great radiance blaze — may Savitṛ impel them onward.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which of your senses, yoked to a quieter mind this morning, would most change what you see?

translations.hi: मन से जोड़कर उन देवों को — जो बुद्धि के बल से स्वर्ग की ओर, प्रकाश की ओर जाते हैं और महान ज्योति को प्रकट करेंगे — सविता आगे प्रेरित करें।

devanagari: युञ्जते मन उत युञ्जते धियो विप्रा विप्रस्य बृहतो विपश्चितः । / विहोत्रा दधे वयुनाविदेक इन्मही देवस्य सवितुः परिष्टुतिः ॥2.4॥
iast: yuñjate mana uta yuñjate dhiyo viprā viprasya bṛhato vipaścitaḥ । / vihotrā dadhe vayunāvideka inmahī devasya savituḥ pariṣṭutiḥ ॥2.4॥
sayIt: yoon-JA-tay MA-na oo-ta yoon-JA-tay DHI-yo vip-RAA vip-RAS-ya bri-ha-TO vi-pash-CHI-tah / vi-hot-RAA da-DHAY va-yoo-naa-VID AY-ka in-ma-HEE day-VAS-ya sa-vi-TOOH pa-rish-TOO-tih
translation: The inspired seers of the great inspired Seer yoke their minds and yoke their thoughts; he alone, the knower of the ways, apportions the offerings — great is the praise of the god Savitṛ.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What would you attempt today if you did your part fully and left the ordering of results to one who knows the ways better than you?

translations.hi: उस महान, ज्ञानी, प्रेरणा-पूर्ण देव के प्रेरित ऋषि अपना मन जोड़ते हैं, अपनी बुद्धियाँ जोड़ते हैं; मार्गों का ज्ञाता वह अकेला ही यज्ञ-कर्मों का विधान करता है — महान है सविता देव की स्तुति।

devanagari: युजे वां ब्रह्म पूर्व्यं नमोभिर्विश्लोक एतु पथ्येव सूरेः । / शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्रा आ ये धामानि दिव्यानि तस्थुः ॥2.5॥
iast: yuje vāṃ brahma pūrvyaṃ namobhirviśloka etu pathyeva sūreḥ । / śṛṇvantu viśve amṛtasya putrā ā ye dhāmāni divyāni tasthuḥ ॥2.5॥
sayIt: yoo-JAY vaam BRAH-ma POOR-vyam na-MO-bhir vish-LO-ka AY-too path-YAY-va soo-RAYH / shrin-VAN-too VISH-vay a-mri-TAS-ya poot-RAA aa yay DHAA-maa-ni div-YAA-ni tas-THOOH
translation: For you I yoke the ancient prayer with reverence; let my verse go forth like the sun along its path. Hear it, all you children of immortality — all who have ascended to the heavenly dwellings.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: How would you carry yourself through today if you began it as an heir of immortality rather than a bundle of faults?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे लिए मैं प्रणाम-सहित उस प्राचीन प्रार्थना को जोड़ता हूँ; मेरा श्लोक सूर्य के मार्ग की तरह दूर-दूर तक जाए। सुनो, अमृत के सभी पुत्रो — तुम भी, जो दिव्य धामों तक पहुँच चुके हो।

devanagari: अग्निर्यत्राभिमथ्यते वायुर्यत्राधिरुध्यते । / सोमो यत्रातिरिच्यते तत्र सञ्जायते मनः ॥2.6॥
iast: agniryatrābhimathyate vāyuryatrādhirudhyate । / somo yatrātiricyate tatra sañjāyate manaḥ ॥2.6॥
sayIt: ag-NIR YAT-raa-bhi-MATH-ya-tay vaa-YOOR YAT-raa-dhi-ROODH-ya-tay / SO-mo YAT-raa-ti-RICH-ya-tay TAT-ra san-JAA-ya-tay MA-nah
translation: Where the fire is churned to life, where the wind is brought under rule, where the soma overflows — there the mind is born.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What conditions could you patiently prepare today so that a clearer mind can be born on its own?

translations.hi: जहाँ मंथन से अग्नि जागती है, जहाँ वायु को साधा जाता है, जहाँ सोम छलक उठता है — वहीं मन का जन्म होता है।

devanagari: सवित्रा प्रसवेन जुषेत ब्रह्म पूर्व्यम् । / यत्र योनिं कृणवसे न हि ते पूर्तमक्षिपत् ॥2.7॥
iast: savitrā prasavena juṣeta brahma pūrvyam । / yatra yoniṃ kṛṇavase na hi te pūrtamakṣipat ॥2.7॥
sayIt: sa-vit-RAA pra-sa-VAY-na joo-SHAY-ta BRAH-ma POOR-vyam / YAT-ra YO-nim kri-na-va-SAY na hi tay POOR-tam AK-shi-pat
translation: Impelled by Savitṛ, give yourself gladly to the ancient prayer; make your source and dwelling there — for what has ripened for you in it is never struck away.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What good work have you been anxiously guarding that this verse invites you to consider unlosable?

translations.hi: सविता की प्रेरणा से उस प्राचीन प्रार्थना में रम जाओ; उसी में अपना उद्गम, अपना घर बनाओ — क्योंकि वहाँ जो तुम्हारे लिए पका है, वह कभी छीना नहीं जाता।

devanagari: त्रिरुन्नतं स्थाप्य समं शरीरं हृदीन्द्रियाणि मनसा सन्निवेश्य । / ब्रह्मोडुपेन प्रतरेत विद्वान्स्रोतांसि सर्वाणि भयानकानि ॥2.8॥
iast: trirunnataṃ sthāpya samaṃ śarīraṃ hṛdīndriyāṇi manasā sanniveśya । / brahmoḍupena pratareta vidvānsrotāṃsi sarvāṇi bhayānakāni ॥2.8॥
sayIt: trir OON-na-tam STHAAP-ya SA-mam sha-REE-ram hri-DEEN-dri-YAA-ni MA-na-saa san-ni-VAYSH-ya / brah-MO-doo-PAY-na pra-ta-RAY-ta vid-VAAN sro-TAAM-si sar-VAA-ni bha-yaa-na-KAA-ni
translation: Holding the body steady with its three parts — chest, neck, head — raised in a line, letting the senses and the mind settle into the heart, the wise one crosses on the raft of Brahman all the rivers of fear.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What would sitting steady look like today in the posture of your commitments, not only your spine?

translations.hi: शरीर को स्थिर रखकर, उसके तीन अंग — छाती, गर्दन, सिर — एक सीध में उठाए हुए, इंद्रियों और मन को हृदय में बसाकर, ज्ञानी ब्रह्म की नौका पर भय-भरी सभी नदियों को पार कर जाता है।

devanagari: प्राणान्प्रपीड्येह स युक्तचेष्टः क्षीणे प्राणे नासिकयोच्छ्वसीत । / दुष्टाश्वयुक्तमिव वाहमेनं विद्वान्मनो धारयेताप्रमत्तः ॥2.9॥
iast: prāṇānprapīḍyeha sa yuktaceṣṭaḥ kṣīṇe prāṇe nāsikayocchvasīta । / duṣṭāśvayuktamiva vāhamenaṃ vidvānmano dhārayetāpramattaḥ ॥2.9॥
sayIt: praa-NAAN pra-PEED-yay-ha sa yook-ta-CHAYSH-tah KSHEE-nay praa-NAY naa-si-ka-YOCH-chhva-SEE-ta / doosh-TAASH-va-YOOK-tam i-va VAA-ham AY-nam vid-VAAN MA-no DHAA-ra-yay-taa-pra-MAT-tah
translation: Restraining the breaths here in the body, movements disciplined, let one breathe out gently through the nostrils as the breath grows thin; then let the wise one hold the mind without slack, as a driver holds a chariot yoked to restive horses.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which restive horse of your attention needs a patient driver today rather than a harder whip?

translations.hi: शरीर में प्राणों को साधकर, चेष्टाएँ संयत रखते हुए, जब साँस क्षीण हो तो नासिका से धीरे-से छोड़े; फिर ज्ञानी अपने मन को वैसे ही सँभाले रखे जैसे कोई सारथी बिगड़ैल घोड़ों से जुते रथ को — सजग, बिना ढील दिए।

devanagari: समे शुचौ शर्करावह्निवालुकाविवर्जिते शब्दजलाश्रयादिभिः । / मनोनुकूले न तु चक्षुपीडने गुहानिवाताश्रयणे प्रयोजयेत् ॥2.10॥
iast: same śucau śarkarāvahnivālukāvivarjite śabdajalāśrayādibhiḥ । / manonukūle na tu cakṣupīḍane guhānivātāśrayaṇe prayojayet ॥2.10॥
sayIt: sa-MAY shoo-CHOW shar-ka-RAA-vah-ni-vaa-loo-KAA-vi-VAR-ji-tay SHAB-da-ja-LAASH-ra-YAA-di-bhih / ma-no-noo-KOO-lay na too CHAK-shoo-PEE-da-nay goo-HAA-ni-VAA-taash-ra-ya-nay pra-yo-ja-YAYT
translation: On level, clean ground, free of pebbles, fire, and sand; kindly to the mind in its sounds, its water, its surroundings; with nothing that pains the eye; in a cave or a sheltered place out of the wind — there let practice be joined.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What one small irritation could you remove from the place where you sit, as an act of practice in itself?

translations.hi: समतल, स्वच्छ भूमि पर — जहाँ कंकड़, आग और रेत न हों; जो अपनी ध्वनियों, जल और परिवेश से मन को भाए; जहाँ कुछ भी आँख को न अखरे; किसी गुफा या हवा से बचे आश्रय में — वहीं अभ्यास में जुटना चाहिए।

devanagari: नीहारधूमार्कानिलानलानां खद्योतविद्युत्स्फटिकशशीनाम् । / एतानि रूपाणि पुरःसराणि ब्रह्मण्यभिव्यक्तिकराणि योगे ॥2.11॥
iast: nīhāradhūmārkānilānalānāṃ khadyotavidyutsphaṭikaśaśīnām । / etāni rūpāṇi puraḥsarāṇi brahmaṇyabhivyaktikarāṇi yoge ॥2.11॥
sayIt: nee-HAA-ra-DHOO-maar-kaa-ni-LAA-na-LAA-naam khad-YO-ta-vid-YOOT-spha-ti-ka-sha-SHEE-naam / ay-TAA-ni roo-PAA-ni poo-rah-sa-RAA-ni BRAH-man-ya-bhi-VYAK-ti-ka-RAA-ni YO-gay
translation: Mist, smoke, sun, wind, fire, fireflies, lightning, crystal, moon — these are the forms that go before, the appearances that gradually disclose Brahman in yoga.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When something luminous happens on your way, can you thank it and keep walking instead of pitching a tent there?

translations.hi: कोहरा, धुआँ, सूर्य, वायु, अग्नि, जुगनू, बिजली, स्फटिक, चन्द्रमा — ये आगे-आगे चलने वाले रूप हैं, जो योग में ब्रह्म को क्रमशः प्रकट करते हैं।

devanagari: पृथिव्यप्तेजोऽनिलखे समुत्थिते पञ्चात्मके योगगुणे प्रवृत्ते । / न तस्य रोगो न जरा न मृत्युः प्राप्तस्य योगाग्निमयं शरीरम् ॥2.12॥
iast: pṛthivyaptejo'nilakhe samutthite pañcātmake yogaguṇe pravṛtte । / na tasya rogo na jarā na mṛtyuḥ prāptasya yogāgnimayaṃ śarīram ॥2.12॥
sayIt: pri-thiv-YAP-tay-JO-ni-la-KHAY sa-moot-thi-TAY pan-CHAAT-ma-kay YO-ga-goo-NAY pra-vrit-TAY / na TAS-ya RO-go na ja-RAA na MRIT-yooh praap-TAS-ya yo-GAAG-ni-ma-yam sha-REE-ram
translation: When the fivefold quality of yoga has arisen and is at work — born of earth, water, fire, air, and space — then for one who has won a body made of the fire of yoga there is no sickness, no old age, no death.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If what you identify with truly decides what you fear, what are you identifying with today?

translations.hi: जब पृथ्वी, जल, अग्नि, वायु और आकाश से जन्मा योग का पंचमुखी गुण जाग उठता है और सक्रिय हो जाता है, तब जिसे योगाग्नि से बना शरीर प्राप्त हो गया, उसके लिए न रोग है, न बुढ़ापा, न मृत्यु।

devanagari: लघुत्वमारोग्यमलोलुपत्वं वर्णप्रसादं स्वरसौष्ठवं च । / गन्धः शुभो मूत्रपुरीषमल्पं योगप्रवृत्तिं प्रथमां वदन्ति ॥2.13॥
iast: laghutvamārogyamalolupatvaṃ varṇaprasādaṃ svarasauṣṭhavaṃ ca । / gandhaḥ śubho mūtrapurīṣamalpaṃ yogapravṛttiṃ prathamāṃ vadanti ॥2.13॥
sayIt: la-GHOOT-vam aa-ROG-yam a-lo-loo-PAT-vam var-na-pra-SAA-dam sva-ra-SOWSH-tha-vam cha / GAN-dhah SHOO-bho moot-ra-poo-REE-sham AL-pam yo-ga-pra-VRIT-tim pra-tha-MAAM va-DAN-ti
translation: Lightness, health, an uncraving heart, a clear complexion, beauty of voice, a pleasant scent, and scant bodily waste — these, they say, are the first signs that yoga is at work.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What unglamorous sign — steadier sleep, a lighter appetite, an even temper — might be your truest measure of progress right now?

translations.hi: हल्कापन, आरोग्य, लालसा से मुक्त हृदय, निखरा रंग, सुरीली वाणी, शुभ गंध और अल्प मल-मूत्र — कहते हैं, ये योग के काम करने के पहले लक्षण हैं।

devanagari: यथैव बिम्बं मृदयोपलिप्तं तेजोमयं भ्राजते तत्सुधान्तम् । / तद्वाऽऽत्मतत्त्वं प्रसमीक्ष्य देही एकः कृतार्थो भवते वीतशोकः ॥2.14॥
iast: yathaiva bimbaṃ mṛdayopaliptaṃ tejomayaṃ bhrājate tatsudhāntam । / tadvā''tmatattvaṃ prasamīkṣya dehī ekaḥ kṛtārtho bhavate vītaśokaḥ ॥2.14॥
sayIt: ya-THAI-va BIM-bam mri-da-YO-pa-LIP-tam tay-jo-MA-yam BHRAA-ja-tay tat soo-DHAAN-tam / tad-VAAT-ma-TAT-tvam pra-sa-MEEK-shya day-HEE AY-kah kri-TAAR-tho BHA-va-tay vee-ta-SHO-kah
translation: Just as a disc dulled with clay shines full of light once it is well cleaned, so the embodied one who has beheld the self's true nature becomes single, fulfilled, and freed of sorrow.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What one layer of clay — a habit, a grudge, a hurry — could be gently wiped from your mirror today?

translations.hi: जैसे मिट्टी से सना हुआ धातु का दर्पण अच्छी तरह माँजने पर तेज से दमक उठता है, वैसे ही जो देहधारी आत्मा के असली स्वरूप को देख लेता है, वह एक हो जाता है — कृतार्थ, और शोक से मुक्त।

devanagari: यदात्मतत्त्वेन तु ब्रह्मतत्त्वं दीपोपमेनेह युक्तः प्रपश्येत् । / अजं ध्रुवं सर्वतत्त्वैर्विशुद्धं ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपापैः ॥2.15॥
iast: yadātmatattvena tu brahmatattvaṃ dīpopameneha yuktaḥ prapaśyet । / ajaṃ dhruvaṃ sarvatattvairviśuddhaṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāpaiḥ ॥2.15॥
sayIt: ya-DAAT-ma-tat-TVAY-na too BRAH-ma-TAT-tvam dee-PO-pa-MAY-nay-ha YOOK-tah pra-PASH-yayt / a-JAM dhroo-VAM sar-va-tat-TVAIR vi-SHOOD-dham gyaat-VAA DAY-vam MOOCH-ya-tay sar-va-PAA-paih
translation: When the practitioner, yoked, sees here by the truth of the self — as by a lamp — the truth of Brahman, then, knowing God as unborn, constant, pure beyond every nature, one is released from all sins.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What honest self-knowledge do you already hold that you have not yet used as a lamp?

translations.hi: जब साधक, योग में जुटा हुआ, आत्मा के तत्व को दीपक बनाकर यहीं ब्रह्म के तत्व को देख लेता है, तब उस देव को — अजन्मा, ध्रुव, समस्त तत्वों से परे विशुद्ध — जानकर वह सारे पापों से छूट जाता है।

devanagari: एषो ह देवः प्रदिशोऽनु सर्वाः पूर्वो ह जातः स उ गर्भे अन्तः । / स एव जातः स जनिष्यमाणः प्रत्यङ्जनास्तिष्ठति सर्वतोमुखः ॥2.16॥
iast: eṣo ha devaḥ pradiśo'nu sarvāḥ pūrvo ha jātaḥ sa u garbhe antaḥ । / sa eva jātaḥ sa janiṣyamāṇaḥ pratyaṅjanāstiṣṭhati sarvatomukhaḥ ॥2.16॥
sayIt: AY-sho ha DAY-vah pra-di-SHO-noo SAR-vaah POOR-vo ha JAA-tah sa oo GAR-bhay AN-tah / sa AY-va JAA-tah sa ja-nish-ya-MAA-nah prat-YANG ja-NAAS TISH-tha-ti sar-va-to-MOO-khah
translation: This is the God pervading all the directions: first-born, and yet within the womb; it is he who is born, he who is yet to be born; he stands facing all beings, his face turned every way.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If the same face were looking out at you from every person you meet today, whom would you treat differently?

translations.hi: यही वह देव है जो सारी दिशाओं में व्याप्त है: सबसे पहले जन्मा, और फिर भी गर्भ के भीतर है; जो जन्म चुका वह भी वही, जो जन्म लेने वाला है वह भी वही; वह सब प्राणियों के सम्मुख खड़ा है — हर ओर उसका मुख।

devanagari: यो देवॊऽग्नौ योऽप्सु यो विश्वं भुवनमाविवेश । / य ओषधीषु यो वनस्पतिषु तस्मै देवाय नमो नमः ॥2.17॥
iast: yo devo'gnau yo'psu yo viśvaṃ bhuvanamāviveśa । / ya oṣadhīṣu yo vanaspatiṣu tasmai devāya namo namaḥ ॥2.17॥
sayIt: yo day-VOG-now YOP-soo yo VISH-vam BHOO-va-nam aa-vi-VAY-sha / ya o-sha-DHEE-shoo yo va-nas-PA-ti-shoo TAS-mai day-VAA-ya NA-mo NA-mah
translation: The God who is in fire, who is in water, who has entered the whole world; who is in the herbs, who is in the trees — to that God, homage, homage!
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 2.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which of today's ordinary elements — the flame, the water, the tree outside your window — will you actually pause and bow to?

translations.hi: जो देव अग्नि में है, जो जल में है, जिसने समूचे संसार में प्रवेश किया है; जो औषधियों में है, जो वनस्पतियों में है — उस देव को नमन, बार-बार नमन!

devanagari: य एको जालवानीशत ईशनीभिः सर्वांल्लोकानीशत ईशनीभिः । / य एवैक उद्भवे सम्भवे च य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥3.1॥
iast: ya eko jālavānīśata īśanībhiḥ sarvāṃllokānīśata īśanībhiḥ । / ya evaika udbhave sambhave ca ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥3.1॥
sayIt: ya AY-ko jaa-la-VAAN ee-SHA-ta ee-sha-NEE-bhih sar-vaan-lo-KAAN ee-SHA-ta ee-sha-NEE-bhih / ya ay-VAI-ka ood-BHA-vay sum-BHA-vay cha ya ay-tud-vi-DOOR am-ri-TAAS-tay BHA-van-ti
translation: He who alone, wielding the net, rules by his ruling powers — rules all the worlds by those same powers — he who alone is one in their arising and their unfolding: those who know this become immortal.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Behind the many forces pulling at your day, can you look for the one hand holding the net?

translations.hi: जो अकेला, जाल थामे, अपनी ईशन-शक्तियों से शासन करता है — उन्हीं शक्तियों से सारे लोकों पर शासन करता है — जो जगत के उगने और खिलने में भी एक ही है: जो इसे जानते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: एको हि रुद्रो न द्वितीयाय तस्थुर्य इमांल्लोकानीशत ईशनीभिः । / प्रत्यङ्जनास्तिष्ठति सञ्चुकोचान्तकाले संसृज्य विश्वा भुवनानि गोपाः ॥3.2॥
iast: eko hi rudro na dvitīyāya tasthurya imāṃllokānīśata īśanībhiḥ । / pratyaṅjanāstiṣṭhati sañcukocāntakāle saṃsṛjya viśvā bhuvanāni gopāḥ ॥3.2॥
sayIt: AY-ko hee ROOD-ro na dvi-TEE-yaa-ya TAS-thoor ya i-maan-lo-KAAN ee-SHA-ta ee-sha-NEE-bhih / prat-YUNG ja-NAAS TISH-tha-ti sun-choo-KO-chaan-ta-KAA-lay sum-SRIJ-ya VISH-vaa bhoo-va-NAA-ni GO-paah
translation: There is one Rudra only — they stand by no second — who rules these worlds with his ruling powers. He stands present within every person; having sent forth all the worlds, as their shepherd he draws them together at the end of time.
