source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If the power that set your life in motion is the same one that will gather it home, which of today's fears loosens its grip?

translations.hi: रुद्र एक ही है — जानने वाले किसी दूसरे को जगह नहीं देते — जो इन लोकों पर अपनी ईशन-शक्तियों से शासन करता है। वह हर प्राणी के भीतर विराजमान है; सारे भुवनों को रचकर, उनका रखवाला बनकर, अंत-काल में उन्हें अपने में समेट लेता है।

devanagari: विश्वतश्चक्षुरुत विश्वतोमुखो विश्वतोबाहुरुत विश्वतस्पात् । / सम्बाहुभ्यां धमति सम्पतत्रैर्द्यावाभूमी जनयन्देव एकः ॥3.3॥
iast: viśvataścakṣuruta viśvatomukho viśvatobāhuruta viśvataspāt । / sambāhubhyāṃ dhamati sampatatrairdyāvābhūmī janayandeva ekaḥ ॥3.3॥
sayIt: vish-va-tush-CHUK-shoor oo-ta vish-va-to-MOO-kho vish-va-to-BAA-hoor oo-ta vish-va-tus-PAAT / sum-baa-hoo-BHYAAM DHA-ma-ti sum-pa-tat-RAIR dyaa-vaa-BHOO-mee ja-na-YUN DAY-va AY-kah
translation: Eyes on every side, faces on every side, arms on every side, feet on every side — the one God, bringing heaven and earth to birth, forges them together with his arms, with his wings.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your ordinary day might you catch the making of the world still going on?

translations.hi: हर ओर आँखें, हर ओर मुख, हर ओर भुजाएँ, हर ओर पैर — वह एक देव, आकाश और पृथ्वी को जन्म देते हुए, अपनी भुजाओं और पंखों से उन्हें एक साथ गढ़ता है।

devanagari: यो देवानां प्रभवश्चोद्भवश्च विश्वाधिपो रुद्रो महर्षिः । / हिरण्यगर्भं जनयामास पूर्वं स नो बुद्ध्या शुभया संयुनक्तु ॥3.4॥
iast: yo devānāṃ prabhavaścodbhavaśca viśvādhipo rudro maharṣiḥ । / hiraṇyagarbhaṃ janayāmāsa pūrvaṃ sa no buddhyā śubhayā saṃyunaktu ॥3.4॥
sayIt: yo day-VAA-naam pra-bha-VUSH chod-bha-VUSH cha vish-VAA-dhi-po ROOD-ro ma-HAR-shih / hi-run-ya-GAR-bhum ja-na-YAA-maa-sa POOR-vum sa no BOODH-yaa shoo-bha-YAA sum-yoo-NUK-too
translation: He who is the source and origin of the gods, the ruler of all, Rudra, the great seer, who of old brought Hiranyagarbha to birth — may he join us to a clear and kindly understanding.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If you could ask the source of everything for exactly one thing today, would a clear mind be it?

translations.hi: जो देवताओं का भी उद्गम और मूल है, सबका अधिपति, महर्षि रुद्र, जिसने आदि में हिरण्यगर्भ को जन्म दिया — वह हमें शुभ, निर्मल बुद्धि से जोड़ दे।

devanagari: या ते रुद्रा शिवा तनूरघोराऽपापकाशिनी । / तया नस्तनुवा शन्तमया गिरिशन्ताभिचाकशीहि ॥3.5॥
iast: yā te rudrā śivā tanūraghorā'pāpakāśinī । / tayā nastanuvā śantamayā giriśantābhicākaśīhi ॥3.5॥
sayIt: yaa tay ROOD-raa shi-VAA ta-NOOR a-GHO-raa a-paa-pa-KAA-shi-nee / ta-YAA nus ta-noo-VAA shun-ta-MA-yaa gi-ri-SHUN-taa-bhi-chaa-ka-SHEE-hi
translation: O Rudra, that kindly form of yours — unterrifying, showing nothing of evil — with that most peaceful form, O dweller among the mountains, look upon us.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When you stand before something far more powerful than you today, can you ask to be met by its kind face?

translations.hi: हे रुद्र, तुम्हारा जो कल्याणकारी रूप है — जो डराता नहीं, जिसमें अशुभ की छाया तक नहीं — उसी परम शांत रूप से, हे गिरिवासी, हम पर दृष्टि रखो।

devanagari: यामिषुं गिरिशतं हस्ते बिभर्ष्यस्तवे । / शिवां गिरित्र तां कुरु मा हिंसीः पुरुषं जगत् ॥3.6॥
iast: yāmiṣuṃ giriśataṃ haste bibharṣyastave । / śivāṃ giritra tāṃ kuru mā hiṃsīḥ puruṣaṃ jagat ॥3.6॥
sayIt: yaam I-shoom gi-ri-sha-TUM HUS-tay bi-BHAR-shyus-ta-vay / shi-VAAM gi-RIT-ra taam KOO-roo maa him-SEEH poo-roo-SHUM JA-gut
translation: The arrow you hold in your hand to shoot, O mountain-dweller — make it kindly, O guardian of the mountain; do not harm a person, nor any living, moving thing.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What power in your own hand today could be turned from a threat into a blessing without being put down?

translations.hi: जो बाण तुमने चलाने के लिए हाथ में थामा है, हे गिरिशन्त — उसे कल्याणकारी बना दो, हे गिरित्र; मनुष्य को चोट मत पहुँचाओ, न इस चलते-फिरते जगत को।

devanagari: ततः परं ब्रह्म परं बृहन्तं यथा निकायं सर्वभूतेषु गूढम् । / विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारमीशं तं ज्ञात्वाऽमृता भवन्ति ॥3.7॥
iast: tataḥ paraṃ brahma paraṃ bṛhantaṃ yathā nikāyaṃ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍham । / viśvasyaikaṃ pariveṣṭitāramīśaṃ taṃ jñātvā'mṛtā bhavanti ॥3.7॥
sayIt: ta-TAH PA-rum BRAH-ma PA-rum bri-HUN-tum ya-THAA ni-KAA-yum sar-va-BHOO-tay-shoo GOO-dhum / vish-vas-YAI-kum pa-ri-vesh-ti-TAA-rum EE-shum tum gyaat-VAA am-ri-TAA BHA-van-ti
translation: Higher than that is Brahman — supreme, vast, hidden in all beings, in each body after its kind; the One who encompasses the universe, the Lord — knowing him, they become immortal.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Can you look at the smallest creature you meet today and consider what might be hidden in it?

translations.hi: उससे भी परे है ब्रह्म — परम, विराट, हर प्राणी में उसकी देह के अनुसार छिपा हुआ; जो एक ही सारे विश्व को लपेटे हुए है, वह ईश्वर — उसे जानकर मनुष्य अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् । / तमेव विदित्वातिमृत्युमेति नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय ॥3.8॥
iast: vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntamādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt । / tameva viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate'yanāya ॥3.8॥
sayIt: vay-DAA-ham AY-tum poo-roo-SHUM ma-HAAN-tum aa-dit-ya-VAR-num TA-ma-sah pa-RAS-taat / tum AY-va vi-dit-VAA-ti MRIT-yoom AY-ti NAAN-yah pun-THAA VID-ya-tay a-ya-NAA-ya
translation: I know this great Person, radiant like the sun, beyond darkness. Only in knowing him does one pass beyond death; there is no other path for the journey.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Is there one truth you could speak today from experience — "I know" — rather than from hearsay?

translations.hi: मैं उस महान पुरुष को जानता हूँ — सूर्य के रंग-सा दीप्त, अंधकार से परे। उसे जानकर ही मनुष्य मृत्यु के पार जाता है; जाने के लिए और कोई मार्ग नहीं है।

devanagari: यस्मात्परं नापरमस्ति किंचिद्यस्मान्नणीयो न ज्यायोऽस्ति कश्चित् । / वृक्ष इव स्तब्धो दिवि तिष्ठत्येकस्तेनेदं पूर्णं पुरुषेण सर्वम् ॥3.9॥
iast: yasmātparaṃ nāparamasti kiṃcidyasmānnaṇīyo na jyāyo'sti kaścit । / vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhatyekastenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa sarvam ॥3.9॥
sayIt: yas-MAAT PA-rum NAA-pa-rum US-ti KIM-chid yas-MAAN na-NEE-yo na JYAA-yo US-ti KUSH-chit / VRIK-sha i-va STUB-dho DI-vi TISH-that-YAY-kus tay-NAY-dum POOR-num poo-roo-SHAY-na SAR-vum
translation: Than whom there is nothing at all higher, than whom nothing smaller and nothing greater — like a tree fixed still in heaven the One stands; by that Person this whole world is filled.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What happens to today's loudest worry when you set it beside something that has never moved?

translations.hi: जिससे परे कुछ भी नहीं, जिससे छोटा या बड़ा कुछ भी नहीं; वह एक, आकाश में जड़ जमाए वृक्ष-सा अचल खड़ा है — उसी पुरुष से यह सारा जगत भरा हुआ है।

devanagari: ततो यदुत्तरतरं तदरूपमनामयम् । / य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्त्यथेतरे दुःखमेवापियन्ति ॥3.10॥
iast: tato yaduttarataraṃ tadarūpamanāmayam । / ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavantyathetare duḥkhamevāpiyanti ॥3.10॥
sayIt: ta-TO yud oot-ta-ra-TA-rum tud a-ROO-pum a-NAA-ma-yum / ya ay-tud vi-DOOR am-ri-TAAS-tay BHA-vunt-ya-THAY-ta-ray DOOH-khum ay-VAA-pi-yun-ti
translation: Higher still than that is what has no form and no affliction. Those who know it become immortal; the others go only to sorrow.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Is there something in you that has stayed unwounded through every change your life has taken?

translations.hi: जो उससे भी ऊपर है, वह रूप-रहित है, और रोग-रहित भी। जो इसे जानते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं; बाक़ी दुःख ही पाते हैं।

devanagari: सर्वाननशिरोग्रीवः सर्वभूतगुहाशयः । / सर्वव्यापी स भगवांस्तस्मात्सर्वगतः शिवः ॥3.11॥
iast: sarvānanaśirogrīvaḥ sarvabhūtaguhāśayaḥ । / sarvavyāpī sa bhagavāṃstasmātsarvagataḥ śivaḥ ॥3.11॥
sayIt: sar-VAA-na-na-shi-ro-GREE-vah sar-va-BHOO-ta-goo-HAA-sha-yah / sar-va-VYAA-pee sa BHA-ga-vaans tus-MAAT sar-va-ga-TAH shi-VAH
translation: His faces, heads, and necks are everywhere; he dwells in the heart-cave of every being; the Blessed Lord is all-pervading — therefore he is Shiva, the gracious one, present in all.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What changes if the vastest thing you revere is also seated nearer to you than your own thoughts?

translations.hi: हर ओर उसके मुख, सिर और ग्रीवाएँ हैं; वह हर प्राणी के हृदय की गुफा में बसा है; वह भगवान सर्वव्यापी है — इसीलिए वह शिव है, कल्याणमय, सबमें विद्यमान।

devanagari: महान्प्रभुर्वै पुरुषः सत्वस्यैष प्रवर्तकः । / सुनिर्मलामिमां प्राप्तिमीशानो ज्योतिरव्ययः ॥3.12॥
iast: mahānprabhurvai puruṣaḥ satvasyaiṣa pravartakaḥ । / sunirmalāmimāṃ prāptimīśāno jyotiravyayaḥ ॥3.12॥
sayIt: ma-HAAN pra-BHOOR vai poo-roo-SHAH sut-vas-YAI-sha pra-var-TA-kah / soo-nir-ma-LAAM i-MAAM PRAAP-tim ee-SHAA-no JYO-tir av-ya-YAH
translation: Great indeed is the Person, the Lord — the one who sets the inmost clarity in motion; the Ruler, the imperishable Light, who leads to this utterly stainless attainment.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: The last time your mind turned, unbidden, toward what is good — what do you believe set it moving?

translations.hi: वह पुरुष सचमुच महान प्रभु है — भीतर के सत्त्व को गति देने वाला; वह ईशान, अविनाशी ज्योति, इस परम निर्मल प्राप्ति तक पहुँचाता है।

devanagari: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये सन्निविष्टः । / हृदा मनीषा मनसाभिक्लृप्तो य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥3.13॥
iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye sanniviṣṭaḥ । / hṛdā manīṣā manasābhiklṛpto ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥3.13॥
sayIt: un-GOOSH-tha-MAAT-rah poo-roo-SHO an-ta-RAAT-maa sa-DAA ja-NAA-naam hri-DA-yay sun-ni-VISH-tah / hri-DAA ma-NEE-shaa ma-na-SAA-bhi-KLIP-to ya ay-tud vi-DOOR am-ri-TAAS-tay BHA-van-ti
translation: A Person the measure of a thumb, the inner self, is seated forever in the heart of beings — disclosed by the heart, by insight, by the mind. Those who know this become immortal.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Today, will you look for the immense at the smallest address you own — your own heart?

translations.hi: अँगूठे भर का पुरुष — अंतरात्मा — सदा प्राणियों के हृदय में विराजमान है; वह हृदय से, मनीषा से, मन से ही प्रकट होता है। जो इसे जानते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् । / स भूमिं विश्वतो वृत्वाऽत्यतिष्ठद्दशाङ्गुलम् ॥3.14॥
iast: sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt । / sa bhūmiṃ viśvato vṛtvā'tyatiṣṭhaddaśāṅgulam ॥3.14॥
sayIt: sa-HUS-ra-sheer-shaa poo-roo-SHAH sa-hus-RAAK-shah sa-HUS-ra-paat / sa BHOO-mim vish-va-TO vrit-VAAT-ya-tish-thud da-SHAAN-goo-lum
translation: The Person has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. Enveloping the earth on every side, he stood beyond it by ten fingers' breadth.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What do you claim to know completely — and can you honor the ten fingers of it that will always exceed your grasp?

translations.hi: सहस्र सिरों वाला है वह पुरुष, सहस्र आँखें, सहस्र पैर। पृथ्वी को हर ओर से घेरकर भी वह उससे दस अंगुल ऊपर, परे खड़ा रहा।

devanagari: पुरुष एवेदँसर्वं यद्भूतं यच्च भव्यम् । / उतामृतत्वस्येशानो यदन्नेनातिरोहति ॥3.15॥
iast: puruṣa evedam̐sarvaṃ yadbhūtaṃ yacca bhavyam । / utāmṛtatvasyeśāno yadannenātirohati ॥3.15॥
sayIt: poo-roo-SHA ay-VAY-dum SAR-vum yud BHOO-tum yuch-cha BHAV-yum / oo-TAAM-ri-tut-vas-YAY-shaa-no yud un-NAY-naa-ti-RO-ha-ti
translation: The Person alone is all this — what has been and what is yet to be; and he is the lord of immortality, and of all that grows by food.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Can you treat the part of your life that merely eats and grows — the ordinary, hungry part — as holy too?

translations.hi: जो हो चुका और जो होने वाला है — यह सब वही पुरुष है; वह अमरत्व का भी स्वामी है, और उसका भी जो अन्न से बढ़ता है।

devanagari: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् । / सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥3.16॥
iast: sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham । / sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati ॥3.16॥
sayIt: sar-va-TAH paa-ni-PAA-dum tut sar-va-TO ak-shi-shi-ro-MOO-khum / sar-va-TAH shroo-ti-MUL LO-kay SAR-vum aa-VRIT-ya TISH-tha-ti
translation: With hands and feet on every side, eyes, heads, and faces on every side, ears on every side — it stands in the world, enveloping all.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: How would you act in the next hour if you took seriously that something sees and hears from every side?

translations.hi: हर ओर उसके हाथ-पैर हैं, हर ओर आँखें, सिर और मुख, हर ओर कान — वह जगत में सब कुछ घेरकर खड़ा है।

devanagari: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । / सर्वस्य प्रभुमीशानं सर्वस्य शरणं सुहृत् ॥3.17॥
iast: sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam । / sarvasya prabhumīśānaṃ sarvasya śaraṇaṃ suhṛt ॥3.17॥
sayIt: sar-VEN-dri-ya-goo-NAA-bhaa-sum sar-VEN-dri-ya-vi-VAR-ji-tum / sar-VAS-ya pra-BHOOM ee-SHAA-num sar-VAS-ya sha-ra-NUM soo-HRIT
translation: Shining through the qualities of all the senses, yet itself devoid of every sense; the lord and ruler of all, the refuge of all — the friend.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Do you approach the highest you can imagine as ruler, as refuge, or as friend — and what might change if you tried the third?

translations.hi: सब इन्द्रियों के गुणों में झलकता है, फिर भी स्वयं सब इन्द्रियों से रहित है; वह सबका प्रभु, सबका शासक, सबका आश्रय — और मित्र है।

devanagari: नवद्वारे पुरे देही हंसो लेलायते बहिः । / वशी सर्वस्य लोकस्य स्थावरस्य चरस्य च ॥3.18॥
iast: navadvāre pure dehī haṃso lelāyate bahiḥ । / vaśī sarvasya lokasya sthāvarasya carasya ca ॥3.18॥
sayIt: na-va-DVAA-ray poo-RAY day-HEE HUM-so lay-LAA-ya-tay ba-HIH / va-SHEE sar-VAS-ya lo-KAS-ya sthaa-va-RAS-ya cha-RAS-ya cha
translation: In the city of nine gates the embodied one — the swan — hovers, straying outward; yet he is the master of the whole world, of all that stands still and all that moves.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.18, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When your attention streams out through the nine gates today, who is the one who could call it home?

translations.hi: नौ द्वारों वाले नगर में देही — वह हंस — बाहर की ओर डोलता रहता है; फिर भी वह सारे जगत का, स्थावर और जंगम सबका, स्वामी है।

devanagari: अपाणिपादो जवनो ग्रहीता पश्यत्यचक्षुः स शृणोत्यकर्णः । / स वेत्ति वेद्यं न च तस्यास्ति वेत्ता तमाहुरग्र्यं पुरुषं महान्तम् ॥3.19॥
iast: apāṇipādo javano grahītā paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ । / sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasyāsti vettā tamāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam ॥3.19॥
sayIt: a-PAA-ni-paa-do ja-va-NO gra-HEE-taa PASH-yat-ya-CHUK-shooh sa shri-NOT-ya-KAR-nah / sa VET-ti VAYD-yum na cha tas-YAAS-ti VET-taa tum AA-hoor AG-ryum poo-roo-SHUM ma-HAAN-tum
translation: Without hands or feet, he is swift and he grasps; he sees without eyes, he hears without ears. He knows all that can be known, but of him there is no knower. They call him the primal, great Person.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What do you know today not as an object in front of you but as the very one who is looking?

translations.hi: बिना हाथ-पैर के वह वेगवान है, पकड़ता है; बिना आँखों के देखता है, बिना कानों के सुनता है। वह हर जानने-योग्य को जानता है, पर उसे जानने वाला कोई नहीं। उसे ही आदि, महान पुरुष कहते हैं।

devanagari: अणोरणीयान्महतो महीयानात्मा गुहायां निहितोऽस्य जन्तोः । / तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुः प्रसादान्महिमानमीशम् ॥3.20॥
iast: aṇoraṇīyānmahato mahīyānātmā guhāyāṃ nihito'sya jantoḥ । / tamakratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuḥ prasādānmahimānamīśam ॥3.20॥
sayIt: a-NO-ra-NEE-yaan ma-ha-TO ma-HEE-yaan AAT-maa goo-HAA-yaam ni-hi-TO as-ya jun-TOH / tum-AK-ra-tuh PASH-ya-ti vee-ta-SHO-ko DHAA-tooh pra-SAA-daan ma-hi-MAA-num EE-shum
translation: Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, the Self is lodged in the hidden heart of every creature. One free of willed craving, his grief gone, beholds through the grace of the Ordainer that majesty — the Lord.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.20, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What might you be shown today if you stopped trying to earn the seeing?

translations.hi: सूक्ष्म से सूक्ष्मतर, महान से महत्तर — यह आत्मा हर प्राणी के हृदय की गुफा में बसा है। जो कामना-रहित है, वह विधाता की कृपा से उस महिमा का — उस ईश्वर का — दर्शन करता है, और उसका शोक जाता रहता है।

devanagari: वेदाहमेतमजरं पुराणं सर्वात्मानं सर्वगतं विभुत्वात् । / जन्मनिरोधं प्रवदन्ति यस्य ब्रह्मवादिनो हि प्रवदन्ति नित्यम् ॥3.21॥
iast: vedāhametamajaraṃ purāṇaṃ sarvātmānaṃ sarvagataṃ vibhutvāt । / janmanirodhaṃ pravadanti yasya brahmavādino hi pravadanti nityam ॥3.21॥
sayIt: vay-DAA-ham AY-tum a-ja-RUM poo-RAA-num sar-VAAT-maa-num sar-va-ga-TUM vi-bhoot-VAAT / jun-ma-ni-RO-dhum pra-va-DUN-ti YAS-ya brah-ma-VAA-di-no hee pra-va-DUN-ti NIT-yum
translation: I know him — unaging, ancient, the self of all, present everywhere by his all-pervadingness — of whom the expounders of Brahman proclaim the ceasing of birth; for they proclaim him the eternal.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.21, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: At the end of a long day, what is the one thing you could still honestly say "I know"?

translations.hi: मैं उसे जानता हूँ — अजर, पुरातन, सबकी आत्मा, अपनी व्यापकता से सर्वत्र विद्यमान — जिसे जानने पर, ब्रह्मवादी कहते हैं, जन्म का चक्र थम जाता है; क्योंकि वे उसे नित्य कहते हैं।

devanagari: य एकोऽवर्णो बहुधा शक्तियोगाद्वर्णाननेकान्निहितार्थो दधाति । / विचैति चान्ते विश्वमादौ च देवः स नो बुद्ध्या शुभया संयुनक्तु ॥4.1॥
iast: ya eko'varṇo bahudhā śaktiyogādvarṇānanekānnihitārtho dadhāti । / vicaiti cānte viśvamādau ca devaḥ sa no buddhyā śubhayā saṃyunaktu ॥4.1॥
sayIt: ya AY-ko VAR-no ba-hu-DHAA SHAK-ti-yo-GAAD var-NAAN a-nay-KAAN ni-hi-TAAR-tho da-DHAA-ti / vi-CHAI-ti CHAAN-tay VISH-vum AA-dau cha DAY-vah sa no BUDDH-yaa shu-bha-YAA sum-yu-NAK-tu
translation: The One, himself without color, who by the yoking of his own power deals out many colors with a purpose hidden in them; into whom the universe comes apart at the end, as it unfolded from him at the beginning — may that radiant God join us with a clear understanding.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If you could ask for only one gift today — not success, but a clearer mind — what would that clarity change first?

translations.hi: जो एक है, स्वयं रंगहीन, पर अपनी शक्ति के योग से अनेक रंग गूढ़ प्रयोजन के साथ बाँटता है; जिससे आदि में विश्व खुला और जिसमें अंत में सिमट जाता है — वह देव हमें शुभ बुद्धि से जोड़े।

devanagari: तदेवाग्निस्तदादित्यस्तद्वायुस्तदु चन्द्रमाः । / तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदापस्तत्प्रजापतिः ॥4.2॥
iast: tadevāgnistadādityastadvāyustadu candramāḥ । / tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadāpastatprajāpatiḥ ॥4.2॥
sayIt: ta-DAY-vaag-nis ta-daa-DIT-yas tad-VAA-yus TA-du chan-dra-MAAH / ta-DAY-va SHUK-rum tad-BRAH-ma ta-DAA-pas tat-pra-JAA-pa-tih
translation: That alone is fire; that is the sun; that is the wind, and that too is the moon. That alone is the bright starry heaven; that is Brahman; that is the waters; that is Prajapati, lord of creatures.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which everyday sight — a flame, the wind, the moon — could you let point you to the One behind it today?

translations.hi: वही अग्नि है, वही आदित्य, वही वायु, और वही चंद्रमा भी। वही शुक्र — नक्षत्रों की चमक — है, वही ब्रह्म, वही जल, वही प्रजापति।

devanagari: त्वं स्त्री पुमानसि त्वं कुमार उत वा कुमारी । / त्वं जीर्णो दण्डेन वञ्चसि त्वं जातो भवसि विश्वतोमुखः ॥4.3॥
iast: tvaṃ strī pumānasi tvaṃ kumāra uta vā kumārī । / tvaṃ jīrṇo daṇḍena vañcasi tvaṃ jāto bhavasi viśvatomukhaḥ ॥4.3॥
sayIt: tvum STREE pu-MAAN-a-si tvum ku-MAA-ra u-ta vaa ku-MAA-ree / tvum JEER-no dun-DAY-na VUN-cha-si tvum JAA-to BHA-va-si vish-va-to-MU-khah
translation: You are woman, you are man; you are the boy, and you are the girl too. You are the old one tottering along on a staff; you are born, and you turn your face to every side.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Whose face will you actually look at today, as if the One were looking back?

translations.hi: तुम स्त्री हो, तुम पुरुष हो; तुम कुमार हो और कुमारी भी। तुम्हीं लाठी टेककर चलते वृद्ध हो; तुम्हीं जन्म लेकर हर दिशा में मुख किए खड़े हो।

devanagari: नीलः पतङ्गो हरितो लोहिताक्षस्तडिद्गर्भ ऋतवः समुद्राः । / अनादिमत्त्वं विभुत्वेन वर्तसे यतो जातानि भुवनानि विश्वा ॥4.4॥
iast: nīlaḥ pataṅgo harito lohitākṣastaḍidgarbha ṛtavaḥ samudrāḥ । / anādimattvaṃ vibhutvena vartase yato jātāni bhuvanāni viśvā ॥4.4॥
sayIt: NEE-lah pa-TUN-go HA-ri-to lo-hi-TAAK-shas ta-DID-gar-bha RI-ta-vah sa-mu-DRAAH / a-NAA-di-mat tvum vi-bhu-TVAY-na var-TA-say ya-to JAA-taa-ni bhu-va-NAA-ni VISH-vaa
translation: You are the dark-blue bird and the green one with red eyes; you are the cloud with lightning in its womb, the seasons, and the seas. Beginningless, you abide as the all-pervading one — you, from whom all the worlds are born.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What one exact, particular thing in nature could you really look at today — colors and all — as more than scenery?

translations.hi: तुम नीला पक्षी हो और लाल आँखों वाला हरा (तोता) भी; बिजली को गर्भ में लिए बादल, ऋतुएँ और समुद्र भी तुम्हीं हो। तुम अनादि हो, सर्वव्यापी होकर विराजते हो — तुम्हीं से सारे लोक जन्मे हैं।

devanagari: अजामेकां लोहितशुक्लकृष्णां बह्वीः प्रजाः सृजमानां सरूपाः । / अजो ह्येको जुषमाणोऽनुशेते जहात्येनां भुक्तभोगामजोऽन्यः ॥4.5॥
iast: ajāmekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ sṛjamānāṃ sarūpāḥ । / ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogāmajo'nyaḥ ॥4.5॥
sayIt: a-JAAM ay-KAAM lo-hi-ta-shuk-la-KRISH-naam bah-VEEH pra-JAAH sri-ja-MAA-naam sa-ROO-paah / a-JO hyay-KO ju-sha-MAA-no a-nu-SHAY-tay ja-HAAT-yay-naam bhuk-ta-bho-GAAM a-JO AN-yah
translation: One unborn female — red, white, and black — brings forth many offspring formed just like herself. One unborn male lies beside her, delighting in her; another unborn one leaves her, her enjoyments already enjoyed.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Is there a pleasure in your life that is already finished, even though you are still circling it?

translations.hi: एक अजन्मी — लाल, सफ़ेद और काली — अपने ही जैसी अनेक संतानें रचती जाती है। एक अजन्मा उसमें रमकर उसके साथ लेटा रहता है; दूसरा अजन्मा, उसके भोग भोगे जा चुकने पर, उसे छोड़ देता है।

devanagari: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । / तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्योऽभिचाकशीति ॥4.6॥
iast: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte । / tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo'bhicākaśīti ॥4.6॥
sayIt: dvaa su-par-NAA sa-yu-JAA sa-KHAA-yaa sa-MAA-num VRIK-shum pa-ri-shas-va-JAA-tay / ta-yor-AN-yah PIP-pa-lum svaad-VAT-tya-nash-nan-NAN-yo a-bhi-chaa-ka-SHEE-ti
translation: Two birds, close companions, clasp the very same tree. One of them eats the sweet pippala fruit; the other, not eating, simply looks on.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: The next time today sweeps you up completely, can you sense the friend on the same branch who is only watching?

translations.hi: दो पक्षी, घनिष्ठ साथी, एक ही पेड़ से लिपटे बैठे हैं। उनमें से एक मीठा पीपल-फल चखता है; दूसरा बिना खाए बस देखता रहता है।

devanagari: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । / जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥4.7॥
iast: samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagno'nīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ । / juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśamasya mahimānamiti vītaśokaḥ ॥4.7॥
sayIt: sa-MAA-nay VRIK-shay PU-ru-sho ni-mag-NO a-nee-sha-YAA SHO-cha-ti muh-ya-MAA-nah / JUSH-tum ya-DAA PASH-yat-yan-yam-EE-sham-as-ya ma-hi-MAA-nam-i-ti vee-ta-SHO-kah
translation: On that same tree a person sits sunk down, grieving, deluded by his own helplessness. But when he sees the other — the beloved Lord — and sees "this glory is his," he becomes free of sorrow.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When helplessness next pins you down, what would it take to lift your eyes instead of tightening your grip?

translations.hi: उसी पेड़ पर एक व्यक्ति डूबा बैठा है — अपनी बेबसी से मोहित होकर शोक करता हुआ। पर जब वह दूसरे को — पूजित प्रभु को — देखता है और समझता है कि "यह महिमा उसी की है," तब वह शोक से मुक्त हो जाता है।

devanagari: ऋचो अक्षरे परमे व्योमन्यस्मिन्देवा अधि विश्वे निषेदुः । / यस्तं न वेद किमृचा करिष्यति य इत्तद्विदुस्त इमे समासते ॥4.8॥
iast: ṛco akṣare parame vyomanyasmindevā adhi viśve niṣeduḥ । / yastaṃ na veda kimṛcā kariṣyati ya ittadvidusta ime samāsate ॥4.8॥
sayIt: RI-cho ak-SHA-ray pa-ra-MAY vyo-man-YAS-min DAY-vaa A-dhi VISH-vay ni-SHAY-duh / yas-TUM na VAY-da kim-ri-CHAA ka-rish-YA-ti ya IT tad-vi-DUS ta i-MAY sa-MAA-sa-tay
translation: The hymns rest in the imperishable, in the highest heaven, where all the gods have taken their seat. What will the hymn do for one who does not know That? But those who do know it — they sit here, complete.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Is there a practice you repeat faithfully whose meaning you have not visited in years?

translations.hi: ऋचाएँ उस अक्षर में, परम आकाश में टिकी हैं, जिसमें सब देवता विराजते हैं। जो उस अक्षर को नहीं जानता, ऋचा उसके किस काम की? पर जो उसे जान लेते हैं, वे ही यहाँ तृप्त होकर बैठते हैं।

devanagari: छन्दांसि यज्ञाः क्रतवो व्रतानि भूतं भव्यं यच्च वेदा वदन्ति । / अस्मान्मायी सृजते विश्वमेतत्तस्मिंश्चान्यो मायया सन्निरुद्धः ॥4.9॥
iast: chandāṃsi yajñāḥ kratavo vratāni bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ yacca vedā vadanti । / asmānmāyī sṛjate viśvametattasmiṃścānyo māyayā sanniruddhaḥ ॥4.9॥
sayIt: chun-DAAM-si yuj-NYAAH kra-ta-vo vra-TAA-ni BHOO-tum BHAV-yum yuch-cha VAY-daa va-DUN-ti / as-MAAN maa-YEE sri-ja-TAY vish-vam-AY-tat tas-MINSH-chaan-yo maa-ya-YAA san-ni-RUD-dhah
translation: The meters, the sacrifices, the rites, the vows, what has been and what shall be, and all that the Vedas declare — from this the maker of maya sends forth this universe; and within it the other one is held fast by maya.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which parts of your daily world feel so fixed, so given, that you have never asked who is streaming them forth?

translations.hi: छंद, यज्ञ, क्रतु, व्रत, भूत और भविष्य, और जो कुछ वेद कहते हैं — इसी से मायावी (मायी) यह सारा विश्व रचता है; और उसी में दूसरा माया से जकड़ा हुआ है।

devanagari: मायां तु प्रकृतिं विद्यान्मायिनं च महेश्वरम् । / तस्यवयवभूतैस्तु व्याप्तं सर्वमिदं जगत् ॥4.10॥
iast: māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyānmāyinaṃ ca maheśvaram । / tasyavayavabhūtaistu vyāptaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagat ॥4.10॥
sayIt: MAA-yaam tu pra-KRI-tim vid-YAAN maa-yi-NUM cha ma-HAYSH-va-rum / tas-YAA-va-ya-va-BHOO-tais-tu VYAAP-tum sar-vam-i-DUM JA-gat
translation: Know, then, that maya is prakriti — nature herself — and that the wielder of maya is the great Lord. This whole world is pervaded by what are parts of him.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When the world feels like a trick today, can you look for the hand of the magician instead of staring at the trick?

translations.hi: जान लो कि माया ही प्रकृति है, और माया का स्वामी महेश्वर है। उसी के अंगभूत अंशों से यह सारा जगत व्याप्त है।

devanagari: यो योनिं योनिमधितिष्ठत्येको यस्मिन्निदं सं च विचैति सर्वम् । / तमीशानं वरदं देवमीड्यं निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥4.11॥
iast: yo yoniṃ yonimadhitiṣṭhatyeko yasminnidaṃ saṃ ca vicaiti sarvam । / tamīśānaṃ varadaṃ devamīḍyaṃ nicāyyemāṃ śāntimatyantameti ॥4.11॥
sayIt: yo YO-nim YO-nim a-dhi-TISH-that-YAY-ko YAS-min-ni-dum sum cha vi-CHAI-ti SAR-vum / tam-ee-SHAA-num va-ra-DUM DAY-vam EED-yum ni-CHAAY-yay-maam SHAAN-tim at-YUN-tam AY-ti
translation: The One who presides over every womb, every source, in whom all this comes together and comes apart — perceiving that Lord, the giver of blessings, the God worthy of praise, one comes to this peace that has no end.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What would change if you treated every beginning you meet today as a doorway he is already standing in?

translations.hi: जो एक हर योनि — हर स्रोत — पर अधिष्ठित है, जिसमें यह सब जुड़ता और बिखरता है — उस वरदाता, स्तुति-योग्य ईशान देव का साक्षात् दर्शन कर मनुष्य इस अनंत शांति को पाता है।

devanagari: यो देवानां प्रभवश्चोद्भवश्च विश्वाधिपो रुद्रो महर्षिः । / हिरण्यगर्भं पश्यत जायमानं स नो बुद्ध्या शुभया संयुनक्तु ॥4.12॥
iast: yo devānāṃ prabhavaścodbhavaśca viśvādhipo rudro maharṣiḥ । / hiraṇyagarbhaṃ paśyata jāyamānaṃ sa no buddhyā śubhayā saṃyunaktu ॥4.12॥
sayIt: yo day-VAA-naam pra-bha-VUSH-chod-bha-VUSH-cha vish-VAA-dhi-po RUD-ro ma-har-SHIH / hi-run-ya-GAR-bhum PASH-ya-ta jaa-ya-MAA-num sa no BUDDH-yaa shu-bha-YAA sum-yu-NAK-tu
translation: He who is the source and the unfolding of the gods, the ruler of all, Rudra, the great seer, who beheld the golden germ as it was being born — may he join us with a clear understanding.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What would you do differently today if your one prayer were simply for a clean, bright mind?

translations.hi: जो देवताओं का उद्गम और उदय है, विश्व का अधिपति, रुद्र, महर्षि — जिसने हिरण्यगर्भ को जन्मते देखा — वह हमें शुभ बुद्धि से जोड़े।

devanagari: यो देवानामधिपो यस्मिन्ल्लोका अधिश्रिताः । / य ईशेऽस्य द्विपदश्चतुष्पदः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥4.13॥
iast: yo devānāmadhipo yasminllokā adhiśritāḥ । / ya īśe'sya dvipadaścatuṣpadaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ॥4.13॥
sayIt: yo day-VAA-naam A-dhi-po YAS-min LO-kaa a-dhi-shri-TAAH / ya EE-shay AS-ya dvi-pa-DUSH cha-tush-pa-DUH KAS-mai day-VAA-ya ha-vi-SHAA vi-DHAY-ma
translation: He who is the overlord of the gods, on whom the worlds rest, who rules over every two-footed and four-footed creature here — to which god shall we offer our oblation?
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If you traced where your best energy went this week, what god would the record say you were offering to?

translations.hi: जो देवताओं का अधिपति है, जिसमें लोक आश्रित हैं, जो यहाँ के दो पैरों और चार पैरों वाले हर प्राणी पर शासन करता है — किस देव को हम हवि अर्पित करें?

devanagari: सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मं कलिलस्य मध्ये विश्वस्य स्रष्टारमनेकरूपम् । / विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा शिवं शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥4.14॥
iast: sūkṣmātisūkṣmaṃ kalilasya madhye viśvasya sraṣṭāramanekarūpam । / viśvasyaikaṃ pariveṣṭitāraṃ jñātvā śivaṃ śāntimatyantameti ॥4.14॥
sayIt: sook-SHMAA-ti-SOOK-shmum ka-li-LAS-ya MADH-yay vish-VAS-ya srash-TAA-ram a-nay-ka-ROO-pum / vish-VAS-yai-kum pa-ri-vaysh-ti-TAA-rum gyaat-VAA shi-VUM SHAAN-tim at-YUN-tam AY-ti
translation: Subtler than the subtle, in the very middle of the world's dense tangle, the creator of all, wearing many forms, the one encircler of the universe — knowing him as Shiva, the kind, one comes to peace without end.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Can you look for the kind one today exactly where life is most tangled, instead of waiting for the tangle to clear?

translations.hi: सूक्ष्म से भी सूक्ष्म, संसार की घनी उलझन के ठीक बीच, अनेक रूपों वाला विश्व का रचयिता, सबको घेरे हुए एक — उसे शिव (कल्याणमय) जानकर मनुष्य अनंत शांति पाता है।

devanagari: स एव काले भुवनस्य गोप्ता विश्वाधिपः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः । / यस्मिन्युक्ता ब्रह्मर्षयो देवताश्च तमेवं ज्ञात्वा मृत्युपाशांश्छिनत्ति ॥4.15॥
iast: sa eva kāle bhuvanasya goptā viśvādhipaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ । / yasminyuktā brahmarṣayo devatāśca tamevaṃ jñātvā mṛtyupāśāṃśchinatti ॥4.15॥
sayIt: sa AY-va KAA-lay bhu-va-NAS-ya gop-TAA vish-VAA-dhi-pah sar-va-BHOO-tay-shu GOO-dhah / YAS-min yuk-TAA brah-mar-sha-yo day-va-TAASH-cha tam-AY-vum gyaat-VAA mrit-yu-PAA-shaamsh chi-NAT-ti
translation: He is the guardian of the world in time, the ruler of all, hidden in every being; the seer-sages and the gods are joined with him. Knowing him thus, one cuts the cords of death.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your life do you most need a guardian right now — and can you imagine him already hidden there?

translations.hi: वही समय में जगत का रक्षक है, विश्व का अधिपति, हर प्राणी में छिपा; उसी से ब्रह्मर्षि और देवता जुड़े हैं। उसे इस तरह जानकर मनुष्य मृत्यु के पाश काट देता है।

devanagari: घृतात्परं मण्डमिवातिसूक्ष्मं ज्ञात्वा शिवं सर्वभूतेषु गूढम् । / विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥4.16॥
iast: ghṛtātparaṃ maṇḍamivātisūkṣmaṃ jñātvā śivaṃ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍham । / viśvasyaikaṃ pariveṣṭitāraṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ॥4.16॥
sayIt: ghri-TAAT pa-rum MUN-dum i-VAA-ti-SOOK-shmum gyaat-VAA shi-VUM sar-va-BHOO-tay-shu GOO-dhum / vish-VAS-yai-kum pa-ri-vaysh-ti-TAA-rum gyaat-VAA DAY-vum MUCH-ya-tay sar-va-PAA-shaih
translation: Like the film of cream finer than the ghee it floats on — so subtle is the kind one hidden in every being. Knowing him, the God who alone encircles the universe, one is freed from every fetter.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What ordinary thing in your day deserves a second, finer look for what is floating just on its surface?

translations.hi: घी के ऊपर तैरती उससे भी महीन मलाई की परत जैसा — इतना सूक्ष्म है वह कल्याणमय, हर प्राणी में छिपा। उसे — विश्व को अकेले घेरने वाले देव को — जानकर मनुष्य सारे बंधनों से छूट जाता है।

devanagari: एष देवो विश्वकर्मा महात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये सन्निविष्टः । / हृदा मनीषा मनसाभिक्लृप्तो य एतद् विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥4.17॥
iast: eṣa devo viśvakarmā mahātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye sanniviṣṭaḥ । / hṛdā manīṣā manasābhiklṛpto ya etad viduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥4.17॥
sayIt: AY-sha DAY-vo vish-va-kar-MAA ma-HAAT-maa sa-DAA ja-NAA-naam hri-da-YAY san-ni-VISH-tah / hri-DAA ma-nee-SHAA ma-na-SAA-bhi-KLIP-to ya AY-tad vi-DUR am-ri-TAAS-tay bha-VUN-ti
translation: This God, the maker of all, the great Self, is seated forever in the heart of beings. He is grasped by the heart, by insight, by the mind — those who know this become immortal.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When you go looking for God today, will you check the nearest room first — the one behind your ribs?

translations.hi: यह देव, विश्वकर्मा, महात्मा, सदा प्राणियों के हृदय में विराजा है। वह हृदय से, प्रज्ञा से, मन से जाना जाता है — जो इसे जान लेते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: यदाऽतमस्तन्न दिवा न रात्रिर्न सन्नचासच्छिव एव केवलः । / तदक्षरं तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं प्रज्ञा च तस्मात्प्रसृता पुराणी ॥4.18॥
iast: yadā'tamastanna divā na rātrirna sannacāsacchiva eva kevalaḥ । / tadakṣaraṃ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ prajñā ca tasmātprasṛtā purāṇī ॥4.18॥
sayIt: ya-DAA a-TA-mas tan-na di-VAA na RAAT-rir na SUN-na CHAA-sach chi-VA AY-va KAY-va-lah / tad-ak-SHA-rum tat-sa-vi-TUR va-RAYN-yum pruj-NYAA cha tas-MAAT pra-sri-TAA pu-RAA-nee
translation: When there is no darkness, then there is neither day nor night, neither being nor non-being — only the kind one, alone. That is the imperishable; that is the adorable splendor of Savitri; and from that the ancient wisdom streamed forth.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.18, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which of your daily words — a prayer, a greeting, a name — might open into something vast if you said it slowly, once?

translations.hi: जब अंधकार नहीं, तब न दिन है न रात, न सत् न असत् — केवल शिव (कल्याणमय) अकेला। वही अक्षर है, वही सविता का वरणीय तेज; और उसी से पुरातन प्रज्ञा बही है।

devanagari: नैनमूर्ध्वं न तिर्यञ्चं न मध्ये न परिजग्रभत् । / न तस्य प्रतिमा अस्ति यस्य नाम महद्यशः ॥4.19॥
iast: nainamūrdhvaṃ na tiryañcaṃ na madhye na parijagrabhat । / na tasya pratimā asti yasya nāma mahadyaśaḥ ॥4.19॥
sayIt: NAI-nam OORDH-vum na tir-YUN-chum na MADH-yay na pa-ri-jag-RA-bhat / na TAS-ya pra-ti-MAA AS-ti YAS-ya NAA-ma ma-had YA-shah
translation: Not above, not across, not in the middle has anyone grasped him. There is no likeness of him, whose name is Great Glory.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What picture of God did you inherit — and can you let it stay a window today rather than becoming a wall?

translations.hi: न ऊपर से, न आड़े से, न बीच में — किसी ने उसे पकड़ा नहीं। उसकी कोई प्रतिमा नहीं, जिसका नाम ही है महान यश।

devanagari: न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् । / हृदा हृदिस्थं मनसा य एनमेवं विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥4.20॥
iast: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpamasya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam । / hṛdā hṛdisthaṃ manasā ya enamevaṃ viduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥4.20॥
sayIt: na sum-dri-SHAY TISH-tha-ti ROO-pam AS-ya na chuk-shu-SHAA PASH-ya-ti KUSH-cha-NAI-num / hri-DAA hri-DIS-thum ma-na-SAA ya AY-nam AY-vum vi-DUR am-ri-TAAS-tay bha-VUN-ti
translation: His form does not stand within sight; no one sees him with the eye. Those who know him with the heart and the mind, as dwelling in the heart — they become immortal.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.20, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What if, instead of trying to picture God today, you simply sat with the sense that something kind is already seated in your chest?

translations.hi: उसका रूप दृष्टि के सामने नहीं ठहरता; आँख से उसे कोई नहीं देखता। जो उसे हृदय और मन से, हृदय में बसा हुआ जान लेते हैं — वे अमर हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: अजात इत्येवं कश्चिद्भीरुः प्रपद्यते । / रुद्र यत्ते दक्षिणं मुखं तेन मां पाहि नित्यम् ॥4.21॥
iast: ajāta ityevaṃ kaścidbhīruḥ prapadyate । / rudra yatte dakṣiṇaṃ mukhaṃ tena māṃ pāhi nityam ॥4.21॥
sayIt: a-JAA-ta it-YAY-vum KUSH-chid BHEE-ruh pra-PUD-ya-tay / RUD-ra YUT-tay duk-shi-NUM MU-khum TAY-na maam PAA-hi NIT-yum
translation: "Unborn!" — so crying, someone, afraid, takes refuge. O Rudra, with that face of yours which is gracious, protect me always.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.21, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When fear finds you next, do you already know a face of kindness you can turn toward?

translations.hi: "अजन्मा!" — ऐसा पुकारकर कोई भयभीत शरण में आता है। हे रुद्र, तुम्हारा जो दक्षिण (कृपालु) मुख है, उसी से मेरी सदा रक्षा करो।

devanagari: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयुषि मा नो गोषु मा न अश्वेषु रीरिषः । / वीरान् मा नो रुद्र भामितोऽवधीर्हविष्मन्तः सदामित्त्वा हवामहे ॥4.22॥
iast: mā nastoke tanaye mā na āyuṣi mā no goṣu mā na aśveṣu rīriṣaḥ । / vīrān mā no rudra bhāmito'vadhīrhaviṣmantaḥ sadāmittvā havāmahe ॥4.22॥
sayIt: maa nas TO-kay ta-na-YAY maa na AA-yu-shi maa no GO-shu maa na ASH-vay-shu REE-ri-shah / vee-RAAN maa no RUD-ra BHAA-mi-to a-va-DHEER ha-vish-MUN-tah sa-dam IT tvaa ha-VAA-ma-hay
translation: Harm us not in our child or grandchild, nor in our span of life, nor in our cattle, nor in our horses. Do not, O Rudra, enraged, strike down our strong ones — bearing offerings, we call on you always.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 4.22, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If you let your prayer be completely honest, what small, unglamorous thing in your household would you name first?

translations.hi: हमारे बच्चों को, पोतों को हानि मत पहुँचाओ; न हमारी आयु को, न गायों को, न घोड़ों को। हे रुद्र, क्रोध में हमारे वीरों का वध मत करो — हवि लिए हम सदा तुम्हें ही पुकारते हैं।

devanagari: द्वे अक्षरे ब्रह्मपरे त्वनन्ते विद्याविद्ये निहिते यत्र गूढे । / क्षरं त्वविद्यां ह्यमृतं तु विद्या विद्याविद्ये ईशते यस्तु सोऽन्यः ॥5.1॥
iast: dve akṣare brahmapare tvanante vidyāvidye nihite yatra gūḍhe । / kṣaraṃ tvavidyāṃ hyamṛtaṃ tu vidyā vidyāvidye īśate yastu so'nyaḥ ॥5.1॥
sayIt: dvay ak-SHA-ray brah-ma-PA-ray tvan-AN-tay vid-YAA-vid-yay NI-hi-tay YAT-ra GOO-dhay / KSHA-rum tva-VID-yaam hya-MRI-tum too VID-yaa vid-YAA-vid-yay EE-sha-tay YAS too SON-yah
translation: Two things lie hidden in the imperishable, infinite, supreme Brahman: knowledge and ignorance. The perishable is ignorance; the immortal is knowledge. And the one who rules over both knowledge and ignorance is other than either.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When knowing and not-knowing both crowd your day, can you turn toward the one who holds them both?

translations.hi: अविनाशी, अनंत परब्रह्म में दो चीज़ें छिपी हैं — विद्या और अविद्या। जो नाशवान है वह अविद्या है, और जो अमर है वह विद्या। और जो विद्या-अविद्या दोनों पर शासन करता है, वह इन दोनों से अलग है।

devanagari: यो योनिं योनिमधितिष्ठत्येको विश्वानि रूपाणि योनीश्च सर्वाः । / ऋषिं प्रसूतं कपिलं यस्तमग्रे ज्ञानैर्बिभर्ति जायमानं च पश्येत् ॥5.2॥
iast: yo yoniṃ yonimadhitiṣṭhatyeko viśvāni rūpāṇi yonīśca sarvāḥ । / ṛṣiṃ prasūtaṃ kapilaṃ yastamagre jñānairbibharti jāyamānaṃ ca paśyet ॥5.2॥
sayIt: yo YO-nim YO-nim a-dhi-TISH-tha-tyay-ko vish-VAA-ni roo-PAA-ni yo-NEESH-cha SAR-vaah / RI-shim pra-SOO-tum KA-pi-lum YAS-tum AG-ray gyaa-NAIR BI-bhar-ti jaa-ya-MAA-num cha PASH-yayt
translation: He is the one who alone presides over every single womb, over all forms and all sources; who at the beginning bore the seer Kapila in knowledge, and watched him as he was being born.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What knowledge in you arrived as a gift rather than an achievement?

translations.hi: वही एक है जो हर एक योनि पर — सब रूपों और सब स्रोतों पर — अधिष्ठित है; जिसने आदि में जन्मे ऋषि कपिल को ज्ञान से धारण किया और उन्हें जन्म लेते देखा।

devanagari: एकैकं जालं बहुधा विकुर्वन्नस्मिन्क्षेत्रे संहरत्येष देवः । / भूयः सृष्ट्वा पतयस्तथेशः सर्वाधिपत्यं कुरुते महात्मा ॥5.3॥
iast: ekaikaṃ jālaṃ bahudhā vikurvannasminkṣetre saṃharatyeṣa devaḥ । / bhūyaḥ sṛṣṭvā patayastatheśaḥ sarvādhipatyaṃ kurute mahātmā ॥5.3॥
sayIt: ay-KAI-kum JAA-lum ba-hoo-DHAA vi-KOOR-van AS-min KSHAY-tray sam-HA-ra-tyay-sha DAY-vah / BHOO-yah SRISHT-vaa pa-ta-YAS ta-THAY-shah sar-VAA-dhi-pat-yum koo-ROO-tay ma-HAAT-maa
translation: Spreading one net after another out in many ways across this field of the world, this God gathers them in again; then, creating anew with the powers that rule, the Lord, the great Self, wields sovereignty over all.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your life might a season of contraction be the work of the same hand that once cast the net wide?

translations.hi: इस जगत रूपी क्षेत्र में एक-एक जाल को अनेक रूपों में फैलाकर यह देव उसे फिर समेट लेता है; फिर नई सृष्टि रचकर, अधिपति-शक्तियों समेत, वह ईश — वह महात्मा — सब पर प्रभुत्व करता है।

devanagari: सर्वा दिश ऊर्ध्वमधश्च तिर्यक्प्रकाशयन्भ्राजते यद्वनड्वान् । / एवं स देवो भगवान्वरेण्यो योनिस्वभावानधितिष्ठत्येकः ॥5.4॥
iast: sarvā diśa ūrdhvamadhaśca tiryakprakāśayanbhrājate yadvanaḍvān । / evaṃ sa devo bhagavānvareṇyo yonisvabhāvānadhitiṣṭhatyekaḥ ॥5.4॥
sayIt: SAR-vaa DI-sha OOR-dhvam a-DHASH-cha tir-YAK pra-KAA-sha-yan BHRAA-ja-tay YAD-va-nad-VAAN / AY-vam sa DAY-vo bha-ga-VAAN va-RAYN-yo yo-ni-sva-bhaa-VAAN a-dhi-TISH-tha-tyay-kah
translation: As the sun blazes, lighting all directions — above, below, across — so that one God, glorious and worthy of worship, alone presides over all the natures sprung from the source.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What would change in your dealings today if you treated everyone you meet as standing in the same light?

translations.hi: जैसे सूर्य ऊपर, नीचे और आर-पार — सब दिशाओं को उजालता हुआ दमकता है, वैसे ही वह एक देव — भगवान, वरेण्य — मूल स्रोत से उपजे सब स्वभावों पर अकेला अधिष्ठित है।

devanagari: यच्च स्वभावं पचति विश्वयोनिः पाच्यांश्च सर्वान् परिणामयेद्यः । / सर्वमेतद्विश्वमधितिष्ठत्येको गुणांश्च सर्वान्विनियोजयेद्यः ॥5.5॥
iast: yacca svabhāvaṃ pacati viśvayoniḥ pācyāṃśca sarvān pariṇāmayedyaḥ । / sarvametadviśvamadhitiṣṭhatyeko guṇāṃśca sarvānviniyojayedyaḥ ॥5.5॥
sayIt: YACH-cha sva-BHAA-vum PA-cha-ti vish-va-YO-nih PAACH-yaansh-cha sar-VAAN pa-ri-naa-ma-YAYD yah / SAR-vum ay-TUD VISH-vum a-dhi-TISH-tha-tyay-ko goo-NAANSH-cha sar-VAAN vi-ni-yo-ja-YAYD yah
translation: The womb of the universe ripens each thing's own nature and brings all that can be ripened through its change; he presides, one, over this entire world, and sets all the qualities to their work.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What in your life are you trying to force that may simply still be ripening?

translations.hi: विश्व की योनि — सबका मूल गर्भ — हर वस्तु के स्वभाव को पकाता है और जो-जो पकने योग्य है उसे उसके परिणाम तक पहुँचाता है; इस समूचे विश्व पर वह अकेला अधिष्ठित है, और सारे गुणों को उनके काम पर लगाता है।

devanagari: तद्वेदगुह्योपनिषत्सु गूढं तद्ब्रह्मा वेदते ब्रह्मयोनिम् । / ये पूर्वं देवा ऋषयश्च तद्विदुस्ते तन्मया अमृता वै बभूवुः ॥5.6॥
iast: tadvedaguhyopaniṣatsu gūḍhaṃ tadbrahmā vedate brahmayonim । / ye pūrvaṃ devā ṛṣayaśca tadviduste tanmayā amṛtā vai babhūvuḥ ॥5.6॥
sayIt: tad-VAY-da-goo-hyo-pa-ni-SHAT-soo GOO-dhum tad-BRAH-maa VAY-da-tay brah-ma-YO-nim / yay POOR-vum DAY-vaa RI-sha-yash-cha tad-vi-DOOS-tay tan-ma-YAA a-mri-TAA vai ba-BHOO-vooh
translation: That is what lies hidden in the Upanishads, the secret core of the Vedas; Brahmā knows it as the womb of Brahman. The gods and seers of old who knew it became of its very substance, and became immortal indeed.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When you study, are you collecting information or letting it change what you are made of?

translations.hi: वही है जो वेदों के गूढ़ मर्म — उपनिषदों — में छिपा है; ब्रह्मा उसे ब्रह्म की योनि के रूप में जानते हैं। पुराने देवता और ऋषि जो उसे जान गए, वे तन्मय हो गए — उसी के बने — और सचमुच अमर हुए।

devanagari: गुणान्वयो यः फलकर्मकर्ता कृतस्य तस्यैव स चोपभोक्ता । / स विश्वरूपस्त्रिगुणस्त्रिवर्त्मा प्राणाधिपः सञ्चरति स्वकर्मभिः ॥5.7॥
iast: guṇānvayo yaḥ phalakarmakartā kṛtasya tasyaiva sa copabhoktā । / sa viśvarūpastriguṇastrivartmā prāṇādhipaḥ sañcarati svakarmabhiḥ ॥5.7॥
sayIt: goo-NAAN-va-yo yah pha-la-KAR-ma-kar-taa kri-TAS-ya TAS-yai-va sa cho-pa-BHOK-taa / sa vish-va-ROO-pas tri-goo-NAS tri-VART-maa praa-NAA-dhi-pah san-CHA-ra-ti sva-KAR-ma-bhih
translation: Joined to the qualities of nature, doing works for their fruits, the enjoyer of exactly what he has done — the embodied self, wearing every form, three-stranded, walking three roads, lord of the life-breaths, wanders on by its own actions.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If you are the enjoyer of exactly what you do, what are you preparing to enjoy tomorrow?

translations.hi: गुणों से जुड़ा, फल के लिए कर्म करता, और जो किया है ठीक उसी का भोक्ता — यह देही, हर रूप धरता हुआ, तीन गुणों वाला, तीन राहों का यात्री, प्राणों का अधिपति, अपने ही कर्मों से चलता-फिरता है।

devanagari: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रो रवितुल्यरूपः सङ्कल्पाहङ्कारसमन्वितो यः । / बुद्धेर्गुणेनात्मगुणेन चैव आराग्रमात्रोऽप्यपरोऽपि दृष्टः ॥5.8॥
iast: aṅguṣṭhamātro ravitulyarūpaḥ saṅkalpāhaṅkārasamanvito yaḥ । / buddherguṇenātmaguṇena caiva ārāgramātro'pyaparo'pi dṛṣṭaḥ ॥5.8॥
sayIt: an-goosh-tha-MAAT-ro ra-vi-TOOL-ya-roo-pah san-kal-paa-han-KAA-ra-sa-man-vi-to yah / bood-DHAYR goo-NAY-naat-ma-goo-NAY-na CHAI-va aa-RAAG-ra-maat-ro pya-pa-RO-pi DRISH-tah
translation: The size of a thumb, radiant like the sun, endowed with intention and the sense of "I" — yet through the qualities of intellect and body it is seen as another, smaller even than the point of an awl.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: How much of the smallness you feel today is truly yours, and how much belongs to the instruments you are measuring with?

translations.hi: अँगूठे भर का, सूर्य जैसा दीप्त, संकल्प और अहंकार से जुड़ा — फिर भी बुद्धि और देह के गुणों के कारण वह दूसरा-सा, सुई की नोक से भी सूक्ष्म देखा जाता है।

devanagari: बालाग्रशतभागस्य शतधा कल्पितस्य च । / भागो जीवः स विज्ञेयः स चानन्त्याय कल्पते ॥5.9॥
iast: bālāgraśatabhāgasya śatadhā kalpitasya ca । / bhāgo jīvaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sa cānantyāya kalpate ॥5.9॥
sayIt: baa-LAAG-ra-sha-ta-BHAA-gas-ya sha-ta-DHAA kal-pi-TAS-ya cha / BHAA-go JEE-vah sa vig-YAY-yah sa chaa-nan-TYAA-ya KAL-pa-tay
translation: Take the tip of a hair, divide it a hundred ways, then divide one part a hundred ways again: know the individual soul to be like a part of that — and yet it is capable of infinity.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your life are you letting your apparent size decide what you are capable of?

translations.hi: बाल की नोक को सौ हिस्सों में बाँटिए, फिर उनमें से एक हिस्से को फिर सौ में: जीव को उसका एक भाग जैसा जानिए — और फिर भी वह अनंत का अधिकारी है।

devanagari: नैव स्त्री न पुमानेष न चैवायं नपुंसकः । / यद्यच्छरीरमादत्ते तेने तेने स युज्यते ॥5.10॥
iast: naiva strī na pumāneṣa na caivāyaṃ napuṃsakaḥ । / yadyaccharīramādatte tene tene sa yujyate ॥5.10॥
sayIt: NAI-va stree na poo-MAA-nay-sha na CHAI-vaa-yam na-POOM-sa-kah / yad-yach-cha-REE-ram aa-DAT-tay TAY-nay TAY-nay sa YOOJ-ya-tay
translation: This self is not female, not male, and not neuter either; whatever body it takes up, with that body it is joined.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which labels attached to your body have you mistaken for the one who wears it?

translations.hi: यह आत्मा न स्त्री है, न पुरुष, न ही नपुंसक; जो-जो शरीर वह धारण करती है, उसी-उसी से जुड़ जाती है।

devanagari: सङ्कल्पनस्पर्शनदृष्टिमोहैर्ग्रासांबुवृष्ट्यात्मविवृद्धिजन्म । / कर्मानुगान्यनुक्रमेण देही स्थानेषु रूपाण्यभिसम्प्रपद्यते ॥5.11॥
iast: saṅkalpanasparśanadṛṣṭimohairgrāsāṃbuvṛṣṭyātmavivṛddhijanma । / karmānugānyanukrameṇa dehī sthāneṣu rūpāṇyabhisamprapadyate ॥5.11॥
sayIt: san-kal-pa-na-spar-sha-na-DRISH-ti-mo-hair graa-saam-boo-vrish-tyaat-ma-vi-VRID-dhi-jan-ma / kar-maa-noo-GAAN-ya-noo-kra-MAY-na DAY-hee sthaa-NAY-shoo roo-PAAN-ya-bhi-sam-pra-PAD-ya-tay
translation: Through delusions of intention, touch, and sight, and through the body's birth and growth fed by food and drink poured in like rain, the embodied self follows its own actions and takes on form after form, place after place, in due order.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What are you reaching for so habitually that it has begun to build where you will live?

translations.hi: संकल्प, स्पर्श और दृष्टि के मोहों से, और वर्षा की तरह उतरते अन्न-जल से पलती देह के जन्म और बढ़त से, यह देही अपने ही कर्मों के पीछे-पीछे, क्रम से, स्थान-स्थान में रूप पर रूप धारण करती है।

devanagari: स्थूलानि सूक्ष्माणि बहूनि चैव रूपाणि देही स्वगुणैर्वृणोति । / क्रियागुणैरात्मगुणैश्च तेषां संयोगहेतुरपरोऽपि दृष्टः ॥5.12॥
iast: sthūlāni sūkṣmāṇi bahūni caiva rūpāṇi dehī svaguṇairvṛṇoti । / kriyāguṇairātmaguṇaiśca teṣāṃ saṃyogaheturaparo'pi dṛṣṭaḥ ॥5.12॥
sayIt: sthoo-LAA-ni sook-SHMAA-ni ba-HOO-ni CHAI-va roo-PAA-ni DAY-hee sva-goo-NAIR vri-NO-ti / kri-yaa-goo-NAIR aat-ma-goo-NAISH-cha TAY-shaam sam-YO-ga-hay-toor a-pa-RO-pi DRISH-tah
translation: Gross forms and subtle ones, many of them, the embodied self puts on by its own qualities; but the cause of their joining — through the qualities of its acts and of itself — is seen to be another still.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When you list everything you have worn — roles, moods, bodies of habit — what remains on the far side of the list?

translations.hi: स्थूल और सूक्ष्म, अनेक रूप यह देही अपने ही गुणों से ओढ़ती है; पर कर्म के गुणों और अपने गुणों के द्वारा उन रूपों से जुड़ने का जो कारण है, वह इन सबसे अलग ही देखा गया है।

devanagari: अनाद्यनन्तं कलिलस्य मध्ये विश्वस्य स्रष्टारमनेकरूपम् । / विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥5.13॥
iast: anādyanantaṃ kalilasya madhye viśvasya sraṣṭāramanekarūpam । / viśvasyaikaṃ pariveṣṭitāraṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ॥5.13॥
sayIt: a-naad-ya-NAN-tam ka-li-LAS-ya MAD-hyay vish-VAS-ya srash-TAA-ram a-nay-ka-ROO-pam / vish-VAS-yai-kam pa-ri-vaysh-ti-TAA-ram GYAAT-vaa DAY-vam MOOCH-ya-tay sar-va-PAA-shaih
translation: Without beginning and without end, in the thick of the world's tangle, the creator of all, wearing many forms, the one who wraps the universe round — knowing that God, one is freed from every fetter.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: In the middle of today's tangle, can you look for the one the tangle is wrapped around?

translations.hi: अनादि और अनंत, संसार की घनी उलझन के बीच, सबका रचयिता, अनेक रूपों वाला, विश्व को चारों ओर से घेरे हुए वह एक — उस देव को जान लेने पर मनुष्य सारे पाशों से छूट जाता है।

devanagari: भावग्राह्यमनीडाख्यं भावाभावकरं शिवम् । / कलासर्गकरं देवं ये विदुस्ते जहुस्तनुम् ॥5.14॥
iast: bhāvagrāhyamanīḍākhyaṃ bhāvābhāvakaraṃ śivam । / kalāsargakaraṃ devaṃ ye viduste jahustanum ॥5.14॥
sayIt: bhaa-va-GRAAH-yam a-nee-DAAKH-yam bhaa-VAA-bhaa-va-ka-ram SHI-vam / ka-laa-SAR-ga-ka-ram DAY-vam yay vi-DOOS-tay ja-HOOS ta-noom
translation: Grasped by the heart's disposition, called the nestless one, maker of becoming and unbecoming, gracious — śiva — the God who sends forth the phases of creation: those who know him have left the body behind.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%9E%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What do you know with your heart's disposition that argument alone has never given you?

translations.hi: जो भाव से पकड़ में आता है, जो "अनीड" — बिना घोंसले का, अशरीरी — कहलाता है, जो होने और न-होने दोनों का कर्ता है, जो शिव — कल्याणमय — है, सृष्टि की कलाओं का रचयिता: उस देव को जो जान लेते हैं, वे देह पीछे छोड़ देते हैं।

devanagari: स्वभावमेके कवयो वदन्ति कालं तथान्ये परिमुह्यमानाः । / देवस्यैष महिमा तु लोके येनेदं भ्राम्यते ब्रह्मचक्रम् ॥6.1॥
iast: svabhāvameke kavayo vadanti kālaṃ tathānye parimuhyamānāḥ । / devasyaiṣa mahimā tu loke yenedaṃ bhrāmyate brahmacakram ॥6.1॥
sayIt: sva-BHAA-vum AY-kay ka-va-yo va-DUN-ti KAA-lum ta-THAAN-yay pa-ri-mu-hya-MAA-naah / day-VUS-yai-sha ma-hi-MAA tu LO-kay yay-NAY-dum BHRAAM-ya-tay brah-ma-CHUK-rum
translation: Some seers say it is inherent nature; others, just as bewildered, say time. But it is the greatness of God in the world by which this wheel of Brahman is turned.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: When you explain how your life is going, what do you credit — habit, luck, time — and what would change if you named the wheel-turner instead?

translations.hi: कुछ ज्ञानी कहते हैं — यह सब स्वभाव है; दूसरे, उतने ही भ्रमित, कहते हैं — काल। पर यह तो जगत में ईश्वर की महिमा है, जिससे यह ब्रह्मचक्र घुमाया जा रहा है।

devanagari: येनावृतं नित्यमिदं हि सर्वं ज्ञः कालकारो गुणी सर्वविद्यः । / तेनेशितं कर्म विवर्तते ह पृथिव्यप्तेजोनिलखानि चिन्त्यम् ॥6.2॥
iast: yenāvṛtaṃ nityamidaṃ hi sarvaṃ jñaḥ kālakāro guṇī sarvavidyaḥ । / teneśitaṃ karma vivartate ha pṛthivyaptejonilakhāni cintyam ॥6.2॥
sayIt: yay-NAA-vri-tum NIT-yum-i-dum hi SAR-vum gyah kaa-la-KAA-ro gu-NEE sar-va-VID-yah / tay-NAY-shi-tum KAR-ma vi-VAR-ta-tay ha pri-thi-vyup-TAY-jo-ni-la-KHAA-ni CHINT-yum
translation: By him — the knower, the maker of time, bearer of qualities, knowing all — all this is forever enveloped. Ruled by him, the work of creation keeps unfolding: what is contemplated as earth, water, fire, air, and space.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your day do you treat time as the boss, and what shifts if time itself has a maker?

translations.hi: जिसने — वह ज्ञाता, काल का रचयिता, गुणों का धारक, सर्वज्ञ — इस समस्त जगत को सदा से ढाँप रखा है; उसी के शासन में सृष्टि का कर्म खुलता चलता है — जिसका चिंतन पृथ्वी, जल, अग्नि, वायु और आकाश के रूप में होता है।

devanagari: तत्कर्म कृत्वा विनिवर्त्य भूयस्तत्त्वस्य तत्त्वेन समेत्य योगम् । / एकेन द्वाभ्यां त्रिभिरष्टभिर्वा कालेन चैवात्मगुणैश्च सूक्ष्मैः ॥6.3॥
iast: tatkarma kṛtvā vinivartya bhūyastattvasya tattvena sametya yogam । / ekena dvābhyāṃ tribhiraṣṭabhirvā kālena caivātmaguṇaiśca sūkṣmaiḥ ॥6.3॥
sayIt: tut-KAR-ma krit-VAA vi-ni-VART-ya BHOO-yus tut-TVUS-ya tut-TVAY-na sa-MAYT-ya YO-gum / ay-KAY-na DVAABH-yaam tri-bhir-ush-ta-BHIR-vaa kaa-LAY-na chai-VAAT-ma-gu-NAISH-cha SOOKSH-maih
translation: Having done that work and drawn it in again, he entered into union, principle with principle — with one, with two, with three, or with eight, with time, and with the subtle qualities of the self.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which layer of your own machinery — body, habit, mood, thought — are you currently mistaking for the one operating it?

translations.hi: वह कर्म करके और उसे फिर समेटकर, उसने तत्त्व का तत्त्व से योग साधा — एक से, दो से, तीन से या आठ से, काल से, और आत्मा के सूक्ष्म गुणों से।

devanagari: आरभ्य कर्माणि गुणान्वितानि भावांश्च सर्वान् विनियोजयेद्यः । / तेषामभावे कृतकर्मनाशः कर्मक्षये याति स तत्त्वतोऽन्यः ॥6.4॥
iast: ārabhya karmāṇi guṇānvitāni bhāvāṃśca sarvān viniyojayedyaḥ । / teṣāmabhāve kṛtakarmanāśaḥ karmakṣaye yāti sa tattvato'nyaḥ ॥6.4॥
sayIt: AA-rubh-ya kar-MAA-ni gu-NAAN-vi-TAA-ni BHAA-vaansh-cha sar-VAAN vi-ni-yo-ja-YAYD-yah / tay-SHAAM-a-BHAA-vay kri-ta-kar-ma-NAA-shah kar-mak-SHA-yay YAA-ti sa tut-TVA-to UN-yah
translation: He who sets works in motion, joined with the gunas, and allots all states of being — when those fall away, the work done dissolves; and with the wearing out of karma he goes on, in truth other than it all.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If you are, in essence, other than your work, what are you afraid would be left of you without it?

translations.hi: जो गुणों से जुड़े कर्मों को आरम्भ कर सभी भावों को नियोजित करता है — उनके न रहने पर किया हुआ कर्म नष्ट हो जाता है; और कर्म के क्षय पर वह आगे बढ़ जाता है — तत्त्वतः उन सबसे अन्य।

devanagari: आदिः स संयोगनिमित्तहेतुः परस्त्रिकालादकलोऽपि दृष्टः । / तं विश्वरूपं भवभूतमीड्यं देवं स्वचित्तस्थमुपास्य पूर्वम् ॥6.5॥
iast: ādiḥ sa saṃyoganimittahetuḥ parastrikālādakalo'pi dṛṣṭaḥ । / taṃ viśvarūpaṃ bhavabhūtamīḍyaṃ devaṃ svacittasthamupāsya pūrvam ॥6.5॥
sayIt: AA-dih sa sum-yo-ga-ni-MIT-ta-HAY-tuh pa-rus-tri-kaa-LAAD-a-ka-LO-pi DRISH-tah / tum vish-va-ROO-pum bha-va-BHOO-tum EED-yum DAY-vum sva-chit-tus-THUM u-PAAS-ya POOR-vum
translation: He is the beginning, the cause behind the joining of soul and nature; he is seen as beyond the three times, and as without parts. Worship first that adorable God of every form, the spring of all becoming, who stands within your own heart.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Before you look for the sacred anywhere else today, what would it mean to begin the search in your own heart?

translations.hi: वह आदि है, जीव और प्रकृति के संयोग का निमित्त-कारण; उसे तीनों कालों से परे और अंशरहित देखा गया है। पहले उस पूजनीय, विश्वरूप, भव के मूल देव की उपासना करो, जो तुम्हारे अपने चित्त में विराजा है।

devanagari: स वृक्षकालाकृतिभिः परोऽन्यो यस्मात्प्रपञ्चः परिवर्ततेऽयम् । / धर्मावहं पापनुदं भगेशं ज्ञात्वात्मस्थममृतं विश्वधाम ॥6.6॥
iast: sa vṛkṣakālākṛtibhiḥ paro'nyo yasmātprapañcaḥ parivartate'yam । / dharmāvahaṃ pāpanudaṃ bhageśaṃ jñātvātmasthamamṛtaṃ viśvadhāma ॥6.6॥
sayIt: sa vrik-sha-kaa-LAA-kri-ti-bhih pa-RO-nyo yas-MAAT-pra-PUN-chah pa-ri-VAR-ta-TAY-yum / dhar-MAA-va-hum PAA-pa-nu-dum bha-GAY-shum gyaat-VAAT-mus-thum um-RI-tum vish-va-DHAA-ma
translation: Higher than the world-tree, than time and all forms, is he — the one from whom this whole pageant revolves. Know him — the bringer of dharma, the remover of wrong, the lord of every splendour — as seated in your own self: immortal, the home of all.
