source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where did you see dharma carried in, or a wrong pushed out, in your world today — and did you recognize the hand?

translations.hi: संसार-वृक्ष, काल और आकृतियों से ऊँचा और अन्य है वह — जिससे यह सारा प्रपंच घूमता है। उसे — धर्म को लाने वाले, पाप को हटाने वाले, समस्त ऐश्वर्य के स्वामी को — अपने ही भीतर बसा, अमृत, विश्व का धाम जानो।

devanagari: तमीश्वराणां परमं महेश्वरं तं देवतानां परमं च दैवतम् । / पतिं पतीनां परमं परस्ताद्विदाम देवं भुवनेशमीड्यम् ॥6.7॥
iast: tamīśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ maheśvaraṃ taṃ devatānāṃ paramaṃ ca daivatam । / patiṃ patīnāṃ paramaṃ parastādvidāma devaṃ bhuvaneśamīḍyam ॥6.7॥
sayIt: tum-EESH-va-RAA-naam pa-ra-mum ma-HAYSH-va-rum tum day-va-TAA-naam pa-ra-mum cha DAI-va-tum / pa-TIM pa-TEE-naam pa-ra-mum pa-rus-TAAD vi-DAA-ma DAY-vum bhu-va-NAY-shum EED-yum
translation: Him — the supreme great Lord of lords, the highest deity of deities, the master of masters, supreme, beyond — let us come to know: God, the adorable ruler of the worlds.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Who is in your company of seekers — and if no one is yet, who could be?

translations.hi: उसे — ईश्वरों के परम महेश्वर को, देवताओं के परम दैवत को, पतियों के पति को, परात्पर को — हम जानें: वह देव, भुवनों का पूजनीय स्वामी।

devanagari: न तस्य कार्यं करणं च विद्यते न तत्समश्चाभ्यधिकश्च दृश्यते । / परास्य शक्तिर्विविधैव श्रूयते स्वाभाविकी ज्ञानबलक्रिया च ॥6.8॥
iast: na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca vidyate na tatsamaścābhyadhikaśca dṛśyate । / parāsya śaktirvividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca ॥6.8॥
sayIt: na TAS-ya KAAR-yum KA-ra-num cha VID-ya-tay na tut-sa-mush-CHAABH-ya-dhi-kush-cha DRISH-ya-tay / pa-RAAS-ya SHAK-tir vi-vi-DHAI-va SHROO-ya-tay svaa-BHAA-vi-kee gyaa-na-ba-la-kri-YAA cha
translation: He has no task he must perform and no instrument to perform it with; none is seen equal to him, let alone greater. His supreme power is revealed as manifold indeed — knowledge, strength, and action that are his very nature.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What in your life goes best precisely when you stop straining at it?

translations.hi: उसका न कोई कार्य है, न कोई करण — न करने को कुछ बचा है, न करने का कोई औज़ार; न उसके समान कोई दिखता है, न उससे बड़ा। उसकी परा शक्ति अनेक रूपों में सुनी जाती है — ज्ञान, बल और क्रिया, जो उसका सहज स्वभाव ही हैं।

devanagari: न तस्य कश्चित्पतिरस्ति लोके न चेशिता नैव च तस्य लिङ्गम् । / स कारणं करणाधिपाधिपो न चास्य कश्चिज्जनिता न चाधिपः ॥6.9॥
iast: na tasya kaścitpatirasti loke na ceśitā naiva ca tasya liṅgam । / sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇādhipādhipo na cāsya kaścijjanitā na cādhipaḥ ॥6.9॥
sayIt: na TAS-ya KUSH-chit PA-tir-US-ti LO-kay na CHAY-shi-taa NAI-va cha TAS-ya LIN-gum / sa KAA-ra-num ka-ra-NAA-dhi-PAA-dhi-po na CHAAS-ya kush-chij-ja-ni-TAA na CHAA-dhi-pah
translation: He has no master in this world, no ruler over him, and no mark by which to grasp him. He is the cause — lord over the very lords of the instruments; none begot him, and none stands above him.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which of your labels for God have you quietly begun to mistake for God?

translations.hi: जगत में उसका कोई स्वामी नहीं, उस पर कोई शासक नहीं, और उसका कोई चिह्न भी नहीं जिससे उसे पकड़ा जा सके। वही कारण है — इन्द्रियों के अधिपतियों का भी अधिपति; न उसे किसी ने जन्म दिया, न कोई उसके ऊपर है।

devanagari: यस्तन्तुनाभ इव तन्तुभिः प्रधानजैः स्वभावतः । / देव एकः स्वमावृणोति स नो दधातु ब्रह्माप्ययम् ॥6.10॥
iast: yastantunābha iva tantubhiḥ pradhānajaiḥ svabhāvataḥ । / deva ekaḥ svamāvṛṇoti sa no dadhātu brahmāpyayam ॥6.10॥
sayIt: yus-tun-tu-NAA-bha i-va TUN-tu-bhih pra-DHAA-na-jaih sva-BHAA-va-tah / DAY-va AY-kah svum-aav-ri-NO-ti sa no da-DHAA-tu brah-MAAP-ya-yum
translation: As a spider covers itself with its own threads, so the one God covers himself, by his own nature, with threads born of primal matter — may he grant us entry into Brahman.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Is the busy weave of your world showing you its maker right now, or veiling him — and how would you tell the difference?

translations.hi: जैसे मकड़ी अपने ही तंतुओं से स्वयं को ढक लेती है, वैसे ही वह एक देव प्रधान से उपजे तंतुओं से, अपने ही स्वभाव से, स्वयं को ढाँप लेता है — वह हमें ब्रह्म में प्रवेश प्रदान करे।

devanagari: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा । / कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥6.11॥
iast: eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā । / karmādhyakṣaḥ sarvabhūtādhivāsaḥ sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaśca ॥6.11॥
sayIt: AY-ko DAY-vah sar-va-BHOO-tay-shu GOO-dhah sar-va-VYAA-pee sar-va-bhoo-TAAN-ta-RAAT-maa / kar-MAADH-yuk-shah sar-va-bhoo-TAA-dhi-VAA-sah SAAK-shee CHAY-taa KAY-va-lo nir-gu-NUSH-cha
translation: The one God hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner self of every creature; the overseer of deeds, dwelling in all beings; the witness, pure awareness, alone, and beyond all qualities.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What becomes of an ordinary task the moment you remember it has a witness within?

translations.hi: एक ही देव सब प्राणियों में छिपा है — सर्वव्यापी, हर प्राणी का अन्तरात्मा; कर्मों का अध्यक्ष, सब भूतों का वास-स्थान; साक्षी, चेतयिता, केवल — अकेला — और निर्गुण।

devanagari: एको वशी निष्क्रियाणां बहूनामेकं बीजं बहुधा यः करोति । / तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम् ॥6.12॥
iast: eko vaśī niṣkriyāṇāṃ bahūnāmekaṃ bījaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti । / tamātmasthaṃ ye'nupaśyanti dhīrāsteṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ॥6.12॥
sayIt: AY-ko va-SHEE nish-kri-YAA-naam ba-HOO-naam AY-kum BEE-jum ba-hu-DHAA yah ka-RO-ti / tum-aat-mus-THUM yay-nu-PASH-yun-ti DHEE-raas TAY-shaam SU-khum SHAASH-va-tum NAY-ta-ray-shaam
translation: The one ruler of the many who do not act of themselves, who makes the one seed manifold — the wise who see him abiding in themselves, theirs is lasting happiness; it belongs to no one else.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What motion in you today — effort, love, attention — could you trace back to its lender?

translations.hi: उन अनेकों का एक वशी — एक स्वामी — जो स्वयं क्रिया नहीं कर सकते; जो एक बीज को अनेक कर देता है; जो धीर उसे अपने भीतर बसा देखते हैं, स्थायी सुख उन्हीं का है — औरों का नहीं।

devanagari: नित्यो नित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानामेको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् । / तत्कारणं सांख्ययोगाधिगम्यं ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥6.13॥
iast: nityo nityānāṃ cetanaścetanānāmeko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān । / tatkāraṇaṃ sāṃkhyayogādhigamyaṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ॥6.13॥
sayIt: NIT-yo nit-YAA-naam CHAY-ta-nash-chay-ta-NAA-naam AY-ko ba-HOO-naam yo vi-da-DHAA-ti KAA-maan / tut-KAA-ra-num saankh-ya-yo-GAA-dhi-GUM-yum gyaat-VAA DAY-vum MUCH-ya-tay sar-va-PAA-shaih
translation: The eternal among eternals, the conscious among the conscious, the one among the many who provides for their desires — knowing that cause, reached through discernment and yoga, knowing God, one is freed from every fetter.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which knot in your life have you been trying to cut that might loosen only by knowing?

translations.hi: नित्यों के बीच नित्य, चेतनों के बीच चेतन, अनेकों के बीच वह एक — जो सबकी कामनाएँ पूरी करता है; उस कारण को — जो सांख्य और योग से पाया जाता है — उस देव को जानकर मनुष्य सारे पाशों से छूट जाता है।

devanagari: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । / तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥6.14॥
iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto'yamagniḥ । / tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ॥6.14॥
sayIt: na TAT-ra SOOR-yo BHAA-ti na chan-dra-TAA-ra-kum NAY-maa VID-yu-to BHAAN-ti ku-TO-ya-MAG-nih / ta-MAY-va BHAAN-tum a-nu-BHAA-ti SAR-vum TAS-ya BHAA-saa SAR-va-mi-dum vi-BHAA-ti
translation: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine — how then could this fire? Everything shines only after him who shines; by his light all this becomes light.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What would change if you treated every brightness you meet today — sun, screen, understanding — as borrowed light?

translations.hi: वहाँ न सूर्य चमकता है, न चन्द्र-तारे; ये बिजलियाँ भी वहाँ नहीं चमकतीं — फिर इस अग्नि की क्या बिसात? सब कुछ उसी के चमकने के पीछे-पीछे चमकता है; उसी के प्रकाश से यह सब प्रकाशित है।

devanagari: एको हंसः भुवनस्यास्य मध्ये स एवाग्निः सलिले संनिविष्टः । / तमेव विदित्वातिमृत्युमेति नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय ॥6.15॥
iast: eko haṃsaḥ bhuvanasyāsya madhye sa evāgniḥ salile saṃniviṣṭaḥ । / tameva viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate'yanāya ॥6.15॥
sayIt: AY-ko HUM-sah bhu-va-nus-YAAS-ya MUDH-yay sa ay-VAAG-nih sa-li-LAY sun-ni-VISH-tah / ta-MAY-va vi-dit-VAA-ti-MRIT-yum AY-ti NAAN-yah pun-THAA VID-ya-tay-ya-NAA-ya
translation: One swan alone in the midst of this world — he indeed is the fire seated deep in the waters. Only in knowing him does one pass beyond death; there is no other road for the journey.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What keeps you afloat through your days — and is it something you have, or something you know?

translations.hi: इस भुवन के बीच एक अकेला हंस — वही है जल के भीतर बैठी अग्नि। उसे जानकर ही मनुष्य मृत्यु के पार जाता है; यात्रा के लिए दूसरा कोई मार्ग नहीं।

devanagari: स विश्वकृद् विश्वविदात्मयोनिर्ज्ञः कालकालो गुणी सर्वविद्यः । / प्रधानक्षेत्रज्ञपतिर्गुणेशः संसारमोक्षस्थितिबन्धहेतुः ॥6.16॥
iast: sa viśvakṛd viśvavidātmayonirjñaḥ kālakālo guṇī sarvavidyaḥ । / pradhānakṣetrajñapatirguṇeśaḥ saṃsāramokṣasthitibandhahetuḥ ॥6.16॥
sayIt: sa vish-va-KRID vish-va-vid-AAT-ma-YO-nir gyah kaa-la-KAA-lo gu-NEE sar-va-VID-yah / pra-DHAA-na-KSHAYT-ra-gya-pa-tir gu-NAY-shah sun-SAA-ra-MOKE-sha-sthi-ti-BUN-dha-HAY-tuh
translation: He is the maker of all, the knower of all, his own source; the knower, the time of time, bearer of qualities, knowing everything; master of primal matter and of the knower of the field, lord of the gunas — the cause of the world's bondage, its continuance, and its release.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: If the same hand holds both bondage and release, what are you asking of it today?

translations.hi: वह सबका रचयिता है, सबका ज्ञाता, स्वयं अपना उद्गम; ज्ञाता, काल का भी काल, गुणों का धारक, सर्वज्ञ; प्रधान और क्षेत्रज्ञ का स्वामी, गुणों का ईश — संसार के बंध, स्थिति और मोक्ष का कारण।

devanagari: स तन्मयो ह्यमृत ईशसंस्थो ज्ञः सर्वगो भुवनस्यास्य गोप्ता । / य ईशेऽस्य जगतो नित्यमेव नान्यो हेतुर्विद्यत ईशनाय ॥6.17॥
iast: sa tanmayo hyamṛta īśasaṃstho jñaḥ sarvago bhuvanasyāsya goptā । / ya īśe'sya jagato nityameva nānyo heturvidyata īśanāya ॥6.17॥
sayIt: sa tun-MA-yo hyum-RI-ta EE-sha-suns-tho gyah SAR-va-go bhu-va-nus-YAAS-ya GOP-taa / ya EE-shays-ya JA-ga-to NIT-yum-AY-va NAAN-yo HAY-tur-VID-ya-ta ee-sha-NAA-ya
translation: One with that, immortal, established as the Lord, the knower, present everywhere, the guardian of this world — it is he who rules this world forever; no other cause of sovereignty can be found.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Where in your life are you acting as owner when you were only ever meant to be guardian?

translations.hi: उसी तत्त्व से एक, अमृत, ईश-रूप में स्थित, ज्ञाता, सर्वगत, इस भुवन का रक्षक — वही इस जगत पर सदा शासन करता है; प्रभुता का दूसरा कोई कारण है ही नहीं।

devanagari: यो ब्रह्माणं विदधाति पूर्वं यो वै वेदांश्च प्रहिणोति तस्मै । / तं ह देवमात्मबुद्धिप्रकाशं मुमुक्षुर्वै शरणमहं प्रपद्ये ॥6.18॥
iast: yo brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvaṃ yo vai vedāṃśca prahiṇoti tasmai । / taṃ ha devamātmabuddhiprakāśaṃ mumukṣurvai śaraṇamahaṃ prapadye ॥6.18॥
sayIt: yo brah-MAA-num vi-da-DHAA-ti POOR-vum yo vai VAY-daansh-cha pra-hi-NO-ti TAS-mai / tum ha DAY-vum-AAT-ma-BUD-dhi-pra-KAA-shum mu-MOOK-shur-vai sha-ra-num-a-HUM pra-PUD-yay
translation: He who creates Brahmā in the beginning and delivers the Vedas to him — in that God, who lights the lamp of self-knowledge, I who long for liberation take refuge.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.18, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: In which one matter today could you stop managing the outcome and genuinely take refuge?

translations.hi: जो सृष्टि के आरम्भ में ब्रह्मा को रचता है और उन्हें वेद सौंपता है — उस देव में, जो आत्मबुद्धि को प्रकाशित करता है, मैं मुमुक्षु शरण लेता हूँ।

devanagari: निष्कलं निष्क्रियंशान्तं निरवद्यं निरञ्जनम् । / अमृतस्य परंसेतुं दग्धेन्दनमिवानलम् ॥6.19॥
iast: niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃśāntaṃ niravadyaṃ nirañjanam । / amṛtasya paraṃsetuṃ dagdhendanamivānalam ॥6.19॥
sayIt: nish-KA-lum nish-KRI-yum SHAAN-tum ni-ra-VUD-yum ni-RUN-ja-num / um-RI-tus-ya PA-rum SAY-tum dug-DHEN-dha-num i-VAA-na-lum
translation: Without parts, without action, tranquil; without blemish, without stain — the supreme bridge to immortality — like a fire whose fuel is burnt away.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which fire in you — a grievance, a craving — could you let burn out today simply by not feeding it?

translations.hi: निष्कल — अंशरहित, निष्क्रिय, शान्त; निर्दोष, निरंजन — अमरत्व का परम सेतु — उस अग्नि की तरह जिसका ईंधन जलकर चुक गया हो।

devanagari: यदा चर्मवदाकाशं वेष्टयिष्यन्ति मानवाः । / तदा देवमविज्ञाय दुःखस्यान्तो भविष्यति ॥6.20॥
iast: yadā carmavadākāśaṃ veṣṭayiṣyanti mānavāḥ । / tadā devamavijñāya duḥkhasyānto bhaviṣyati ॥6.20॥
sayIt: ya-DAA char-ma-vud-aa-KAA-shum vaysh-ta-yish-YUN-ti MAA-na-vaah / ta-DAA DAY-vum-a-vig-YAA-ya duh-khus-YAAN-to bha-VISH-ya-ti
translation: When human beings roll up the sky like a piece of leather — then, without knowing God, will sorrow come to an end.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.20, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Which of your current fixes for unhappiness is, honestly, an attempt to roll up the sky?

translations.hi: जब मनुष्य आकाश को चमड़े की तरह लपेट लेंगे — तब ईश्वर को जाने बिना दुःख का अंत हो जाएगा।

devanagari: तपःप्रभावाद् देवप्रसादाच्च ब्रह्म ह श्वेताश्वतरोऽथ विद्वान् । / अत्याश्रमिभ्यः परमं पवित्रं प्रोवाच सम्यगृषिसङ्घजुष्टम् ॥6.21॥
iast: tapaḥprabhāvād devaprasādācca brahma ha śvetāśvataro'tha vidvān । / atyāśramibhyaḥ paramaṃ pavitraṃ provāca samyagṛṣisaṅghajuṣṭam ॥6.21॥
sayIt: ta-pah-pra-bhaa-VAAD day-va-pra-saa-DAACH-cha BRAH-ma ha shvay-TAASH-va-ta-RO-tha vid-VAAN / ut-YAASH-ra-mibh-yah pa-ra-mum pa-VIT-rum pro-VAA-cha sum-yug-ri-shi-SUN-gha-JUSH-tum
translation: By the power of his austerity and by the grace of God, the wise Shvetashvatara rightly declared Brahman — the supreme purifier, cherished by the company of seers — to those furthest along the path of renunciation.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.21, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Looking back at your own path, which has carried you farther — your effort or what was simply given — and have you thanked both?

translations.hi: तप के प्रभाव से और देव के प्रसाद से, विद्वान श्वेताश्वतर ने उस परम पवित्र ब्रह्म को — जो ऋषि-मंडली का प्रिय है — संन्यास-पथ के सबसे परिपक्व साधकों को यथावत् कह सुनाया।

devanagari: वेदान्ते परमं गुह्यं पुराकल्पे प्रचोदितम् । / नाप्रशान्ताय दातव्यं नापुत्रायाशिष्याय वा पुनः ॥6.22॥
iast: vedānte paramaṃ guhyaṃ purākalpe pracoditam । / nāpraśāntāya dātavyaṃ nāputrāyāśiṣyāya vā punaḥ ॥6.22॥
sayIt: vay-DAAN-tay pa-ra-mum GUH-yum pu-raa-KUL-pay pra-CHO-di-tum / naa-pra-SHAAN-taa-ya daa-TUV-yum naa-put-RAA-yaa-shish-YAA-ya vaa pu-NAH
translation: This deepest secret of the Vedanta, declared in an earlier age, is not to be given to one who is unquiet within, nor again to one who is neither a son nor a student.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.22, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: What teaching have you been reaching for lately that might simply be waiting for you to arrive quieter?

translations.hi: वेदान्त का यह परम गुह्य, पूर्व कल्प में कहा गया, उसे न दिया जाए जिसका मन शांत नहीं, और न उसे जो न पुत्र है, न शिष्य।

devanagari: यस्य देवे परा भक्तिः यथा देवे तथा गुरौ । / तस्यैते कथिता ह्यर्थाः प्रकाशन्ते महात्मनः ॥6.23॥
iast: yasya deve parā bhaktiḥ yathā deve tathā gurau । / tasyaite kathitā hyarthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ ॥6.23॥
sayIt: YAS-ya DAY-vay pa-RAA BHAK-tih ya-THAA DAY-vay ta-THAA gu-ROW / tus-YAI-tay ka-thi-TAA hyar-THAAH pra-kaa-SHUN-tay ma-HAAT-ma-nah
translation: Whoever has supreme devotion to God, and to the teacher as to God — for that great soul these truths, exactly as they have been told, shine forth of themselves.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 6.23, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A0%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Who taught you the truths you actually live by — and when did you last honor them the way this verse suggests?

translations.hi: जिसकी देव में परा भक्ति है, और जैसी देव में वैसी ही गुरु में — उस महात्मा के लिए ये कहे हुए अर्थ स्वयं प्रकाशित हो उठते हैं।

devanagari: ॐ सहनाववतु । सह नौ भुनक्तु । सह वीर्यं करवावहै । तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै ॥ / ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥
iast: oṃ sahanāvavatu । saha nau bhunaktu । saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai । tejasvi nāvadhītamastu mā vidviṣāvahai ॥ / oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ ॥
sayIt: om SA-ha NAA-va-va-too / SA-ha now bhoo-NUK-too / SA-ha VEER-yum ka-ra-VAA-va-high / tay-JUS-vi naa-va-DHEE-tum-US-too / maa vid-vi-SHAA-va-high / om SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih SHAAN-tih
translation: Om. May that One protect us both — teacher and student. May it nourish us both. May we work together with vigour; may what we study be radiant with light; may we never resent one another. Om — peace, peace, peace.
source: Shvetashvatara Upanishad, shanti mantra, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%2F%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%83%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83
reflection: Who is learning or working alongside you right now, and what would change if you began by praying for you both?

translations.hi: ॐ। वे हम दोनों — गुरु और शिष्य — की रक्षा करें। हम दोनों का पोषण करें। हम दोनों मिलकर पूरी शक्ति से काम करें। हमारा पढ़ा हुआ तेजस्वी हो। हम आपस में कभी द्वेष न करें। ॐ शान्ति, शान्ति, शान्ति।

devanagari: शिवः शक्त्या युक्तो यदि भवति शक्तः प्रभवितुं / न चेदेवं देवो न खलु कुशलः स्पन्दितुमपि । / अतस्त्वामाराध्यां हरिहरविरिञ्चादिभिरपि / प्रणन्तुं स्तोतुं वा कथमकृतपुण्यः प्रभवति ॥1॥
iast: śivaḥ śaktyā yukto yadi bhavati śaktaḥ prabhavituṃ / na cedevaṃ devo na khalu kuśalaḥ spanditumapi । / atastvāmārādhyāṃ hariharaviriñcādibhirapi / praṇantuṃ stotuṃ vā kathamakṛtapuṇyaḥ prabhavati ॥1॥
sayIt: shi-VAH SHAK-tyaa YOOK-toh YA-di BHA-va-ti SHAK-tah pra-bha-vi-TOOM / na chay-DAY-vum DAY-vo na KHA-loo KOO-sha-lah SPAN-di-toom-A-pi / a-tas-TVAAM-aa-RAAD-hyaam ha-ri-ha-ra-vi-rin-CHAA-di-bhi-RA-pi / pra-NAN-toom STOH-toom vaa ka-tham a-kri-ta-POON-yah pra-BHA-va-ti
translation: Only joined with Shakti is Shiva able to bring anything forth; without her, the god cannot so much as stir. So you, whom Hari, Hara, Virinchi and the rest themselves worship — how could one who has earned no merit dare to bow to you, or to praise you?
source: Soundarya Lahari 1 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where in your life are you trying to act while cut off from the source that actually powers you?

translations.hi: शक्ति से जुड़कर ही शिव कुछ रचने में समर्थ होते हैं; उसके बिना वे देव हिल तक नहीं सकते। तो तुम — जिनकी आराधना स्वयं हरि, हर और विरिञ्चि जैसे देव करते हैं — तुम्हें प्रणाम करने या तुम्हारी स्तुति करने का साहस, बिना पुण्य कमाए, कोई कैसे कर सकता है?

devanagari: तनीयांसं पांसुं तव चरणपङ्केरुहभवं / विरिञ्चिस्सञ्चिन्वन् विरचयति लोकानविकलम् । / वहत्येनं शौरिः कथमपि सहस्रेण शिरसां / हरस्संक्षुद्यैनं भजति भसितोद्धूलनविधिम् ॥2॥
iast: tanīyāṃsaṃ pāṃsuṃ tava caraṇapaṅkeruhabhavaṃ / viriñcissañcinvan viracayati lokānavikalam । / vahatyenaṃ śauriḥ kathamapi sahasreṇa śirasāṃ / harassaṃkṣudyainaṃ bhajati bhasitoddhūlanavidhim ॥2॥
sayIt: ta-NEE-yaam-sum PAAM-soom TA-va cha-ra-na-pun-KAY-roo-ha-bha-vum / vi-RIN-chis-san-CHIN-van vi-ra-CHA-ya-ti lo-KAAN a-vi-ka-lum / va-hat-YAY-num SHOW-rih ka-tha-MA-pi sa-has-RAY-na shi-ra-SAAM / ha-ras-sank-SHOOD-yai-num BHA-ja-ti bha-si-tod-DHOO-la-na-vi-dhim
translation: Gathering one tiniest grain of dust risen from your lotus feet, Virinchi (Brahma) fashions the worlds without a flaw; Shauri (Vishnu) somehow carries that same grain on his thousand heads; and Hara, grinding it fine, performs with it his rite of smearing sacred ash.
source: Soundarya Lahari 2 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What would change in how you work today if you treated your materials — time, people, resources — as something sacred lent to you rather than raw stock?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे चरण-कमलों की धूल का एक नन्हा-सा कण बटोरकर विरिञ्चि (ब्रह्मा) निर्दोष लोकों की रचना कर देते हैं; उसी कण को शौरि (विष्णु) अपने सहस्र सिरों पर किसी तरह धारण करते हैं; और हर उसे पीसकर उसी से अपना भस्म रमाने का विधान पूरा करते हैं।

devanagari: अविद्यानामन्तस्तिमिरमिहिरद्वीपनगरी / जडानां चैतन्यस्तबकमकरन्दस्रुतिझरी । / दरिद्राणां चिन्तामणिगुणनिका जन्मजलधौ / निमग्नानां दंष्ट्रा मुररिपुवराहस्य भवति ॥3॥
iast: avidyānāmantastimiramihiradvīpanagarī / jaḍānāṃ caitanyastabakamakarandasrutijharī । / daridrāṇāṃ cintāmaṇiguṇanikā janmajaladhau / nimagnānāṃ daṃṣṭrā muraripuvarāhasya bhavati ॥3॥
sayIt: a-vid-YAA-naam an-tas-ti-mi-ra-mi-hi-ra-DVEE-pa-na-ga-ree / ja-DAA-naam chai-TAN-ya-sta-ba-ka-ma-ka-RAN-da-sroo-ti-jha-ree / da-rid-RAA-naam chin-TAA-ma-ni-goo-na-ni-kaa jan-ma-ja-la-DHOW / ni-mag-NAA-naam DAMSH-traa moo-ra-ri-poo-va-RAA-has-ya BHA-va-ti
translation: That dust of your feet is, for those lost in ignorance, the island-city of the sun that scatters their inner darkness; for the dull-minded, a cascade streaming nectar from the flower-cluster of awareness; for the destitute, a whole string of wish-granting gems; and for those drowning in the ocean of birth and death, the rescuing tusk of the Boar, Mura's foe.
source: Soundarya Lahari 3 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which of the four seekers are you today — the one in the dark, the one gone numb, the one in want, or the one going under?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे चरणों की वही धूल अज्ञान में डूबे लोगों के लिए भीतर का अँधेरा मिटाने वाले सूर्य की द्वीप-नगरी है; जड़ बुद्धि वालों के लिए चैतन्य के फूल-गुच्छ से झरती मकरन्द की धारा; निर्धनों के लिए चिन्तामणियों की पूरी माला; और जन्म-मृत्यु के सागर में डूबते हुओं के लिए मुरारि के वराह-रूप का उबार लेने वाला दाँत।

devanagari: त्वदन्यः पाणिभ्यामभयवरदो दैवतगणः / त्वमेका नैवासि प्रकटितवराभीत्यभिनया । / भयात् त्रातुं दातुं फलमपि च वाञ्छासमधिकं / शरण्ये लोकानां तव हि चरणावेव निपुणौ ॥4॥
iast: tvadanyaḥ pāṇibhyāmabhayavarado daivatagaṇaḥ / tvamekā naivāsi prakaṭitavarābhītyabhinayā । / bhayāt trātuṃ dātuṃ phalamapi ca vāñchāsamadhikaṃ / śaraṇye lokānāṃ tava hi caraṇāveva nipuṇau ॥4॥
sayIt: tvad-AN-yah PAA-nib-hyaam a-bha-ya-va-ra-DOH dai-va-ta-ga-NAH / tvam-AY-kaa nai-VAA-si pra-ka-ti-ta-va-RAA-bheet-ya-bhi-na-yaa / bha-YAAT TRAA-toom DAA-toom pha-la-MA-pi cha VAAN-chaa-sa-ma-dhi-kum / sha-RAN-yay lo-KAA-naam TA-va hi cha-ra-NAAV-ay-va ni-poo-NOW
translation: Every god but you signals safety and boons with the hands — the mudras of "fear not" and "I grant." You alone make no such gesture; for, O refuge of the worlds, your feet by themselves are skilled at saving from fear and at giving fruit beyond even what was wished for.
source: Soundarya Lahari 4 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What are you still bargaining for that you could simply place at the feet of what you trust most?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे सिवा हर देव-समूह हाथों से अभय और वरदान की मुद्राएँ दिखाता है। एक तुम्हीं हो जो वर और अभय का कोई अभिनय नहीं करतीं; क्योंकि हे लोकों की शरण, तुम्हारे चरण ही भय से बचाने में और माँगे से भी बढ़कर फल देने में स्वयं निपुण हैं।

devanagari: हरिस्त्वामाराध्य प्रणतजनसौभाग्यजननीं / पुरा नारी भूत्वा पुररिपुमपि क्षोभमनयत् । / स्मरोऽपि त्वां नत्वा रतिनयनलेह्येन वपुषा / मुनीनामप्यन्तः प्रभवति हि मोहाय महताम् ॥5॥
iast: haristvāmārādhya praṇatajanasaubhāgyajananīṃ / purā nārī bhūtvā puraripumapi kṣobhamanayat । / smaro'pi tvāṃ natvā ratinayanalehyena vapuṣā / munīnāmapyantaḥ prabhavati hi mohāya mahatām ॥5॥
sayIt: ha-ris-TVAAM-aa-RAAD-hya pra-na-ta-ja-na-sow-BHAAG-ya-ja-na-neem / poo-RAA NAA-ree BHOOT-vaa poo-ra-ri-poo-MA-pi KSHO-bham a-na-yat / sma-RO-pi tvaam NAT-vaa ra-ti-na-ya-na-LAY-hyay-na va-poo-SHAA / moo-NEE-naam ap-YAN-tah pra-BHA-va-ti hi mo-HAA-ya ma-ha-TAAM
translation: Hari once worshipped you — mother of good fortune to all who bow — and, becoming a woman, stirred even the Destroyer of the Cities himself. And Smara, the god of love, having bowed to you, with a body Rati's eyes drink like nectar, is able to bewilder the minds of even the greatest sages.
source: Soundarya Lahari 5 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which of your strengths do you treat as self-made when it is actually a gift flowing through you?

translations.hi: झुकने वालों को सौभाग्य देने वाली माँ, तुम्हारी आराधना करके हरि ने एक बार नारी रूप धारण किया और स्वयं त्रिपुर-विनाशक शिव तक को विचलित कर दिया। और कामदेव, तुम्हें प्रणाम करके, उस देह के बल पर जिसे रति की आँखें अमृत की तरह पीती हैं, बड़े-बड़े मुनियों के मन में भी मोह जगा देता है।

devanagari: धनुः पौष्पं मौर्वी मधुकरमयी पञ्च विशिखाः / वसन्तः सामन्तो मलयमरुदायोधनरथः । / तथाप्येकः सर्वं हिमगिरिसुते कामपि कृपाम् / अपाङ्गात्ते लब्ध्वा जगदिदमनङ्गो विजयते ॥6॥
iast: dhanuḥ pauṣpaṃ maurvī madhukaramayī pañca viśikhāḥ / vasantaḥ sāmanto malayamarudāyodhanarathaḥ । / tathāpyekaḥ sarvaṃ himagirisute kāmapi kṛpām / apāṅgātte labdhvā jagadidamanaṅgo vijayate ॥6॥
sayIt: dha-NOOH POWSH-pum MOWR-vee ma-dhoo-ka-ra-ma-YEE PUN-cha vi-shi-KHAAH / va-SAN-tah saa-MAN-toh ma-la-ya-ma-roo-DAA-yo-dha-na-ra-thah / ta-THAAP-YAY-kah SAR-vum hi-ma-gi-ri-soo-TAY KAAM-a-pi kri-PAAM / a-PAAN-gaat-tay LUB-dhvaa ja-ga-di-dam a-NUN-go vi-ja-ya-TAY
translation: A bow made of flowers, a bowstring of honeybees, exactly five arrows, the spring season for an ally, the sandal-breeze from Malaya for a war-chariot — and yet, O daughter of the snow mountain, with such gear the bodiless Kama single-handedly conquers this whole world, having won one indescribable drop of grace from your side-glance.
source: Soundarya Lahari 6 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where are you waiting for better equipment when what you actually need is to ask for backing?

translations.hi: फूलों का धनुष, भौंरों की प्रत्यंचा, कुल पाँच बाण, सहयोगी के नाम पर वसन्त ऋतु, और युद्ध-रथ की जगह मलय की चन्दन-सुगन्धित हवा — फिर भी, हे हिमगिरि की पुत्री, इतने से साज़ो-सामान के बल पर वह अनंग (कामदेव) अकेला सारे संसार को जीत लेता है, क्योंकि उसे तुम्हारी तिरछी चितवन से कोई अकथनीय कृपा मिल गई है।

devanagari: क्वणत्काञ्चीदामा करिकलभकुम्भस्तननता / परिक्षीणा मध्ये परिणतशरच्चन्द्रवदना । / धनुर्बाणान् पाशं सृणिमपि दधाना करतलैः / पुरस्तादास्तां नः पुरमथितुराहोपुरुषिका ॥7॥
iast: kvaṇatkāñcīdāmā karikalabhakumbhastananatā / parikṣīṇā madhye pariṇataśaraccandravadanā । / dhanurbāṇān pāśaṃ sṛṇimapi dadhānā karatalaiḥ / purastādāstāṃ naḥ puramathiturāhopuruṣikā ॥7॥
sayIt: kva-nat-KAAN-chee-daa-maa ka-ri-ka-la-bha-KOOM-bha-sta-na-na-taa / pa-rik-SHEE-naa MUD-hyay pa-ri-na-ta-sha-rach-CHAN-dra-va-da-naa / dha-noor-BAA-naan PAA-shum sri-ni-MA-pi da-DHAA-naa ka-ra-ta-LAIH / poo-ras-TAAD-AAS-taam nah poo-ra-ma-thi-toor AA-ho-poo-roo-shi-kaa
translation: Her girdle of bells chiming, gently bowed by breasts full as the frontal globes of a young elephant, slender at the waist, her face the ripened autumn moon, bearing in her palms the bow, the arrows, the noose and the goad — may she stand revealed before us, the very pride of the Destroyer of the Cities.
source: Soundarya Lahari 7 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When your confidence rises, do you ever pause to notice where it is actually coming from?

translations.hi: करधनी की घंटियाँ बजती हुई, गजशिशु के मस्तक जैसे भरे उरोजों से तनिक झुकी हुई, क्षीण कटि वाली, पूर्ण शरद-चन्द्र से मुख वाली, हथेलियों में धनुष, बाण, पाश और अंकुश धारण किए हुए — वे देवी, जो त्रिपुर-विनाशक शिव का अपना गर्व हैं, हमारे सामने प्रकट हों।

devanagari: सुधासिन्धोर्मध्ये सुरविटपिवाटीपरिवृते / मणिद्वीपे नीपोपवनवति चिन्तामणिगृहे । / शिवाकारे मञ्चे परमशिवपर्यङ्कनिलयां / भजन्ति त्वां धन्याः कतिचन चिदानन्दलहरीम् ॥8॥
iast: sudhāsindhormadhye suraviṭapivāṭīparivṛte / maṇidvīpe nīpopavanavati cintāmaṇigṛhe । / śivākāre mañce paramaśivaparyaṅkanilayāṃ / bhajanti tvāṃ dhanyāḥ katicana cidānandalaharīm ॥8॥
sayIt: soo-dhaa-SIN-dhor MUD-hyay soo-ra-vi-ta-pi-VAA-tee-pa-ri-vri-tay / ma-ni-DVEE-pay nee-PO-pa-va-na-va-ti chin-TAA-ma-ni-gri-hay / shi-VAA-kaa-ray MUN-chay pa-ra-ma-shi-va-par-YUN-ka-ni-la-yaam / bha-JAN-ti tvaam DHAN-yaah ka-ti-cha-na chid-aa-NAN-da-la-ha-reem
translation: In the midst of the ocean of nectar, on the Isle of Gems ringed by orchards of the gods' wish-trees, in the house built of chintamani stone with its grove of kadamba trees, on a couch whose form is Shiva, resting on the lap of Paramashiva — there a fortunate few worship you, the wave of consciousness and bliss.
source: Soundarya Lahari 8 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When you imagine the most sacred place you can, what sits at its centre — and what does that tell you about what you are really seeking?

translations.hi: अमृत के सागर के बीच, देव-कल्पवृक्षों के उपवनों से घिरे मणिद्वीप में, कदम्ब-वन वाले चिन्तामणि भवन में, शिव-रूप पलंग पर, परमशिव की गोद में विराजमान तुम्हें — चैतन्य और आनन्द की लहर को — कोई गिने-चुने भाग्यशाली ही भज पाते हैं।

devanagari: महीं मूलाधारे कमपि मणिपूरे हुतवहं / स्थितं स्वाधिष्ठाने हृदि मरुतमाकाशमुपरि । / मनोऽपि भ्रूमध्ये सकलमपि भित्वा कुलपथं / सहस्रारे पद्मे सह रहसि पत्या विहरसे ॥9॥
iast: mahīṃ mūlādhāre kamapi maṇipūre hutavahaṃ / sthitaṃ svādhiṣṭhāne hṛdi marutamākāśamupari । / mano'pi bhrūmadhye sakalamapi bhitvā kulapathaṃ / sahasrāre padme saha rahasi patyā viharase ॥9॥
sayIt: ma-HEEM moo-LAA-dhaa-ray ka-MA-pi ma-ni-POO-ray hoo-ta-va-hum / sthi-TUM svaa-dhish-THAA-nay HRI-di ma-roo-tam aa-KAA-sham OO-pa-ri / ma-NO-pi bhroo-MUD-hyay sa-ka-la-MA-pi BHIT-vaa koo-la-pa-thum / sa-has-RAA-ray PUD-may SA-ha RA-ha-si PUT-yaa vi-ha-ra-say
translation: Earth in the muladhara, water in the manipura, fire abiding in the svadhishthana, air in the heart, ether above it, and mind between the brows — piercing the entire kula path, you delight in secret with your Lord in the thousand-petalled lotus.
source: Soundarya Lahari 9 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: If the sacred travels through every layer of you, which layer of yourself have you been treating as too ordinary to matter?

translations.hi: मूलाधार में पृथ्वी, मणिपूर में जल, स्वाधिष्ठान में अग्नि, हृदय में वायु, उसके ऊपर आकाश, और भौंहों के बीच मन — इस पूरे कुल-मार्ग को भेदकर तुम सहस्रार कमल में अपने स्वामी के साथ एकान्त में विहार करती हो।

devanagari: सुधाधारासारैश्चरणयुगलान्तर्विगलितैः / प्रपञ्चं सिञ्चन्ती पुनरपि रसाम्नायमहसः । / अवाप्य स्वां भूमिं भुजगनिभमध्युष्टवलयं / स्वमात्मानं कृत्वा स्वपिषि कुलकुण्डे कुहरिणि ॥10॥
iast: sudhādhārāsāraiścaraṇayugalāntarvigalitaiḥ / prapañcaṃ siñcantī punarapi rasāmnāyamahasaḥ । / avāpya svāṃ bhūmiṃ bhujaganibhamadhyuṣṭavalayaṃ / svamātmānaṃ kṛtvā svapiṣi kulakuṇḍe kuhariṇi ॥10॥
sayIt: soo-dhaa-DHAA-raa-SAA-raish cha-ra-na-yoo-ga-LAAN-tar-vi-ga-li-taih / pra-PUN-chum sin-CHUN-tee poo-nar-A-pi ra-SAAM-naa-ya-ma-ha-sah / a-VAAP-ya svaam BHOO-mim bhoo-ja-ga-NI-bham adh-YOOSH-ta-va-la-yum / svam-aat-MAA-num KRIT-vaa SVA-pi-shi koo-la-KOON-day koo-ha-ri-ni
translation: Showering the whole body-cosmos with torrents of nectar streaming from between your two feet, you descend again from that splendour whose essence is the moon's nectar; reaching your own ground, you make yourself a serpent-like coil of three and a half turns and sleep in the hollow of the kula-kunda.
source: Soundarya Lahari 10 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What in you is not absent but only asleep, waiting to be honoured rather than forced awake?

translations.hi: अपने दोनों चरणों के बीच से झरती अमृत-धाराओं से इस पूरे देह-ब्रह्माण्ड को सींचती हुई, तुम उस अमृतमय चन्द्र-तेज से फिर नीचे उतरती हो; अपनी भूमि पर पहुँचकर, स्वयं को सर्प जैसी साढ़े तीन कुंडलियों में समेटकर, कुलकुण्ड की गुहा में सो जाती हो।

devanagari: चतुर्भिः श्रीकण्ठैः शिवयुवतिभिः पञ्चभिरपि / प्रभिन्नाभिः शम्भोर्नवभिरपि मूलप्रकृतिभिः । / चतुश्चत्वारिंशद्वसुदलकलाश्रत्रिवलय / त्रिरेखाभिः सार्धं तव शरणकोणाः परिणताः ॥11॥
iast: caturbhiḥ śrīkaṇṭhaiḥ śivayuvatibhiḥ pañcabhirapi / prabhinnābhiḥ śambhornavabhirapi mūlaprakṛtibhiḥ । / catuścatvāriṃśadvasudalakalāśratrivalaya / trirekhābhiḥ sārdhaṃ tava śaraṇakoṇāḥ pariṇatāḥ ॥11॥
sayIt: cha-TOOR-bhih shree-KUN-thaih shi-va-yoo-va-ti-BHIH pun-cha-bhi-RA-pi / pra-BHIN-naa-bhih SHUM-bhor na-va-bhi-RA-pi MOO-la-pra-kri-ti-bhih / cha-toosh-chat-VAA-rim-shad va-soo-da-la-ka-LAASH-ra-tri-va-la-ya / tri-RAY-khaa-bhih SAAR-dhum TA-va sha-ra-na-KO-naah pa-ri-na-TAAH
translation: With four Srikanthas (the Shiva triangles) and five Shiva-maidens (the Shakti triangles) standing apart from Shambhu, with the nine root-sources — together with the eight-petalled and sixteen-petalled lotuses, the three circles and the three lines, the corners of your dwelling come to forty-four.
source: Soundarya Lahari 11 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: If your life were drawn as a diagram of what intersects with what, where is its still centre point?

translations.hi: चार श्रीकण्ठों (शिव-त्रिकोणों) और शम्भु से पृथक् पाँच शिव-युवतियों (शक्ति-त्रिकोणों) से — यानी नौ मूल-प्रकृतियों से — तथा आठ और सोलह दलों वाले कमलों, तीन वलयों और तीन रेखाओं समेत, तुम्हारे निवास के कोण चवालीस हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: त्वदीयं सौन्दर्यं तुहिनगिरिकन्ये तुलयितुं / कवीन्द्राः कल्पन्ते कथमपि विरिञ्चिप्रभृतयः । / यदालोकौत्सुक्यादमरललना यान्ति मनसा / तपोभिर्दुष्प्रापामपि गिरिशसायुज्यपदवीम् ॥12॥
iast: tvadīyaṃ saundaryaṃ tuhinagirikanye tulayituṃ / kavīndrāḥ kalpante kathamapi viriñciprabhṛtayaḥ । / yadālokautsukyādamaralalanā yānti manasā / tapobhirduṣprāpāmapi giriśasāyujyapadavīm ॥12॥
sayIt: tva-DEE-yum sown-DUR-yum too-hi-na-gi-ri-KUN-yay too-la-yi-TOOM / ka-VEEN-draah kul-PUN-tay ka-tha-MA-pi vi-RIN-chi-pra-bhri-ta-yah / ya-daa-lo-KOWT-sook-yaad a-ma-ra-la-la-NAA YAAN-ti MA-na-saa / ta-PO-bhir doosh-PRAA-paam A-pi gi-ri-sha-saa-YOOJ-ya-pa-da-veem
translation: To find a match for your beauty, O daughter of the snow mountain, the best of poets — Virinchi and his peers — barely manage at all; so the women of heaven, longing for even a glimpse of it, go by way of the mind to union with Girisha, a state hard to win even by austerities.
source: Soundarya Lahari 12 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What have you been trying to achieve by effort that might open only to wholehearted attention?

translations.hi: हे हिमगिरि की कन्या, तुम्हारे सौन्दर्य की कोई उपमा खोजने में विरिञ्चि जैसे कवि-श्रेष्ठ भी बड़ी मुश्किल से ही कुछ कर पाते हैं। इसीलिए स्वर्ग की स्त्रियाँ, उसकी एक झलक की ललक में, मन-ही-मन गिरीश (शिव) के साथ उस सायुज्य तक जा पहुँचती हैं जो कठोर तप से भी दुर्लभ है।

devanagari: नरं वर्षीयांसं नयनविरसं नर्मसु जडं / तवापाङ्गालोके पतितमनुधावन्ति शतशः । / गलद्वेणीबन्धाः कुचकलशविस्रस्तसिचया / हठात् त्रुट्यत्काञ्च्यो विगलितदुकूला युवतयः ॥13॥
iast: naraṃ varṣīyāṃsaṃ nayanavirasaṃ narmasu jaḍaṃ / tavāpāṅgāloke patitamanudhāvanti śataśaḥ । / galadveṇībandhāḥ kucakalaśavisrastasicayā / haṭhāt truṭyatkāñcyo vigalitadukūlā yuvatayaḥ ॥13॥
sayIt: NA-rum var-SHEE-yaam-sum na-ya-na-vi-RA-sum NUR-ma-soo JA-dum / ta-VAA-paan-GAA-lo-kay PA-ti-tam a-noo-DHAA-van-ti sha-ta-SHAH / ga-lad-VAY-nee-bun-dhaah koo-cha-ka-la-sha-vis-RAS-ta-si-cha-yaa / ha-THAAT troot-yat-KAANCH-yo vi-ga-li-ta-doo-KOO-laa yoo-va-ta-yah
translation: Let a man be far gone in years, unpleasing to the eye, dull at love's play — yet if he falls within the field of your side-glance, young women run after him by the hundreds, braids slipping loose, garments sliding from their jar-round breasts, girdles snapping of themselves, silks falling away.
source: Soundarya Lahari 13 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Have you ever watched grace make someone compelling in a way their résumé could never explain — and what did that teach you about where worth resides?

translations.hi: कोई पुरुष चाहे बहुत बूढ़ा हो, देखने में अप्रिय, प्रेम-विनोद में एकदम फीका — पर तुम्हारी तिरछी दृष्टि के घेरे में आ भर जाए, तो सैकड़ों युवतियाँ उसके पीछे दौड़ पड़ती हैं — चोटियाँ खुलती हुईं, कलश-से उरोजों से वस्त्र सरकते हुए, करधनियाँ अपने-आप टूटती हुईं, रेशम ढलकते हुए।

devanagari: क्षितौ षट्पञ्चाशद् द्विसमधिकपञ्चाशदुदके / हुताशे द्वाषष्टिश्चतुरधिकपञ्चाशदनिले । / दिवि द्विष्षट्.ह्त्रिंशन्मनसि च चतुष्षष्टिरिति ये / मयूखास्तेषामप्युपरि तव पादाम्बुजयुगम् ॥14॥
iast: kṣitau ṣaṭpañcāśad dvisamadhikapañcāśadudake / hutāśe dvāṣaṣṭiścaturadhikapañcāśadanile । / divi dviṣṣaṭtriṃśanmanasi ca catuṣṣaṣṭiriti ye / mayūkhāsteṣāmapyupari tava pādāmbujayugam ॥14॥
sayIt: kshi-TOW shat-pun-CHAA-shad dvi-sa-ma-dhi-ka-pun-CHAA-sha-doo-da-kay / hoo-TAA-shay dvaa-SHASH-tish cha-toor-a-dhi-ka-pun-CHAA-sha-da-ni-lay / DI-vi dvish-SHAT-trim-shan MA-na-si cha cha-toosh-SHASH-ti-ri-ti yay / ma-YOO-khaas TAY-shaam ap-YOO-pa-ri TA-va paa-DAAM-boo-ja-yoo-gum
translation: Fifty-six rays in earth, fifty-two in water, sixty-two in fire, fifty-four in air, seventy-two in ether, and sixty-four in mind — such are the rays that shine; and above them all, every one, stands the pair of your lotus feet.
source: Soundarya Lahari 14 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What is the highest thing you can conceive — and can you practise treating even that as a threshold rather than the summit?

translations.hi: पृथ्वी में छप्पन किरणें, जल में बावन, अग्नि में बासठ, वायु में चौवन, आकाश में बहत्तर, और मन में चौंसठ — ये सब दीप्तिमान किरणें हैं; और इन सबके भी ऊपर विराजते हैं तुम्हारे चरण-कमलों की जोड़ी।

devanagari: शरज्ज्योत्स्नाशुद्धां शशियुतजटाजूटमकुटां / वरत्रासत्राणस्फटिकघटिकापुस्तककराम् । / सकृन्न त्वा नत्वा कथमिव सतां संन्निदधते / मधुक्षीरद्राक्षामधुरिमधुरीणाः भणितयः ॥15॥
iast: śarajjyotsnāśuddhāṃ śaśiyutajaṭājūṭamakuṭāṃ / varatrāsatrāṇasphaṭikaghaṭikāpustakakarām । / sakṛnna tvā natvā kathamiva satāṃ saṃnnidadhate / madhukṣīradrākṣāmadhurimadhurīṇāḥ bhaṇitayaḥ ॥15॥
sayIt: sha-raj-JYOTS-naa-SHOOD-dhaam sha-shi-yoo-ta-ja-TAA-joo-ta-ma-koo-taam / va-ra-TRAA-sa-traa-na-spha-ti-ka-gha-ti-KAA-poos-ta-ka-ka-raam / sa-KRIN-na tvaa NAT-vaa ka-tham-I-va sa-TAAM san-ni-da-dha-tay / ma-dhoo-KSHEE-ra-DRAAK-shaa-ma-dhoo-ri-ma-dhoo-REE-naah bha-ni-ta-yah
translation: Pure white as autumn moonlight, crowned with matted locks that hold the crescent moon, your hands showing the boon and the shelter-from-fear, bearing the crystal rosary and the book — to one who has bowed to you in this form even once, how could utterances laden with the sweetness of honey, milk and grapes fail to come?
source: Soundarya Lahari 15 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Before your next difficult conversation, what would change if you paused to make your words an offering first?

translations.hi: शरद की चाँदनी-सी धवल, चन्द्रकला धारण किए जटाजूट के मुकुट वाली, हाथों में वर और अभय की मुद्राएँ, स्फटिक की माला और पुस्तक लिए हुए — इस रूप में तुम्हें एक बार भी प्रणाम कर लेने वाले सज्जन के पास शहद, दूध और द्राक्षा की मिठास से लदी वाणी भला क्यों न चली आए?

devanagari: फणितयः / कवीन्द्राणां चेतःकमलवनबालातपरुचिं / भजन्ते ये सन्तः कतिचिदरुणामेव भवतीम् । / विरिञ्चिप्रेयस्यास्तरुणतरशृङ्गारलहरी / गभीराभिर्वाग्भिर्विदधति सतां रञ्जनममी ॥16॥
iast: kavīndrāṇāṃ cetaḥkamalavanabālātaparuciṃ / bhajante ye santaḥ katicidaruṇāmeva bhavatīm । / viriñcipreyasyāstaruṇataraśṛṅgāralaharī / gabhīrābhirvāgbhirvidadhati satāṃ rañjanamamī ॥16॥
sayIt: ka-veen-DRAA-naam CHAY-tah-ka-ma-la-va-na-BAA-laa-ta-pa-roo-chim / bha-JAN-tay yay SAN-tah ka-ti-chid a-roo-NAAM-ay-va bha-va-teem / vi-RIN-chi-pray-yas-YAAS ta-roo-na-ta-ra-shrin-GAA-ra-la-ha-ree / ga-BHEE-raa-bhir VAAG-bhir vi-DA-dha-ti sa-TAAM RUN-ja-nam a-mee
translation: Those few blessed ones who worship you as Aruna, "the Crimson One" — dawn-light falling on the lotus-grove of poets' hearts — they delight the assemblies of the good with words deep as the freshest wave of love-poetry from the beloved of Virinchi herself.
source: Soundarya Lahari 16 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Does your speech lately need more light or more warmth — and what are you feeding it?

translations.hi: जो गिने-चुने सन्त तुम्हें "अरुणा" — कवियों के हृदय-कमलवन पर पड़ती भोर की लाली — के रूप में भजते हैं, वे विरिञ्चि की प्रिया (सरस्वती) की नित-नयी शृंगार-लहरी जैसी गहरी वाणी से सत्पुरुषों की सभाओं को रस से भर देते हैं।

devanagari: सवित्रीभिर्वाचां शशिमणिशिलाभङ्गरुचिभिः / वशिन्याद्याभिस्त्वां सह जननि संचिन्तयति यः । / स कर्ता काव्यानां भवति महतां भङ्गिरुचिभिः / वचोभिर्वाग्देवीवदनकमलामोदमधुरैः ॥17॥
iast: savitrībhirvācāṃ śaśimaṇiśilābhaṅgarucibhiḥ / vaśinyādyābhistvāṃ saha janani saṃcintayati yaḥ । / sa kartā kāvyānāṃ bhavati mahatāṃ bhaṅgirucibhiḥ / vacobhirvāgdevīvadanakamalāmodamadhuraiḥ ॥17॥
sayIt: sa-vit-REE-bhir VAA-chaam sha-shi-ma-ni-shi-LAA-bhun-ga-roo-chi-bhih / va-shin-YAAD-yaa-bhis tvaam SA-ha JA-na-ni sun-CHIN-ta-ya-ti yah / sa KUR-taa kaav-YAA-naam BHA-va-ti ma-ha-TAAM BHUN-gi-roo-chi-bhih / va-CHO-bhir vaag-DAY-vee-va-da-na-ka-ma-LAA-mo-da-ma-dhoo-raih
translation: Mother, whoever contemplates you together with Vashini and her sisters — the begetters of speech, lustrous as slivers of freshly cut moonstone — becomes a maker of great poems, in words that charm like the masters' finest turns of phrase, sweet with the fragrance of the lotus-face of the goddess of speech.
source: Soundarya Lahari 17 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: If every word you spoke today were traced back to its source, what would you want that source to be?

translations.hi: हे जननी, जो कोई तुम्हारा चिन्तन वशिनी आदि देवियों के साथ करता है — वाणी को जन्म देने वाली वे देवियाँ, जो ताज़े कटे चन्द्रकान्त मणि की किरचों-सी दमकती हैं — वह महान काव्यों का रचयिता बन जाता है; उसके वचन बड़े कवियों की भंगिमाओं-से मोहक और वाग्देवी के मुख-कमल की सुगन्ध-से मधुर होते हैं।

devanagari: तनुच्छायाभिस्ते तरुणतरणिश्रीसरणिभिः / दिवं सर्वामुर्वीमरुणिमनि मग्नां स्मरति यः । / भवन्त्यस्य त्रस्यद्वनहरिणशालीननयनाः / सहोर्वश्या वश्याः कति कति न गीर्वाणगणिकाः ॥18॥
iast: tanucchāyābhiste taruṇataraṇiśrīsaraṇibhiḥ / divaṃ sarvāmurvīmaruṇimani magnāṃ smarati yaḥ । / bhavantyasya trasyadvanahariṇaśālīnanayanāḥ / sahorvaśyā vaśyāḥ kati kati na gīrvāṇagaṇikāḥ ॥18॥
sayIt: ta-nooch-CHAA-yaa-bhis tay ta-roo-na-ta-ra-ni-SHREE-sa-ra-ni-bhih / DI-vum sar-VAAM oor-VEEM a-roo-NI-ma-ni mug-NAAM SMA-ra-ti yah / bha-VUNT-yas-ya tras-yad-va-na-ha-ri-na-shaa-LEE-na-na-ya-naah / sa-hor-VUSH-yaa VUSH-yaah KA-ti KA-ti na geer-VAA-na-ga-ni-kaah
translation: Whoever holds in mind all heaven and all earth drowned in crimson by the lustre of your body — pathways of the young sun's splendour — before him how many, how many of heaven's dancing beauties, Urvashi herself among them, their eyes shy as startled forest deer, do not bow captive?
source: Soundarya Lahari 18 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What would today look like if you practised seeing every person and place in it as tinted by the same sacred light?

translations.hi: जो कोई यह स्मरण करता है कि सारा आकाश और सारी पृथ्वी तुम्हारी देह-कान्ति में — नवोदित सूर्य की शोभा की राहों में — अरुणिम डूबी हुई है, उसके आगे चकित वन-हिरणी जैसी लजीली आँखों वाली स्वर्ग की कितनी-कितनी अप्सराएँ — स्वयं उर्वशी समेत — वश में नहीं हो जातीं?

devanagari: मुखं बिन्दुं कृत्वा कुचयुगमधस्तस्य तदधो / हरार्धं ध्यायेद्यो हरमहिषि ते मन्मथकलाम् । / स सद्यः संक्षोभं नयति वनिता इत्यतिलघु / त्रिलोकीमप्याशु भ्रमयति रवीन्दुस्तनयुगाम् ॥19॥
iast: mukhaṃ binduṃ kṛtvā kucayugamadhastasya tadadho / harārdhaṃ dhyāyedyo haramahiṣi te manmathakalām । / sa sadyaḥ saṃkṣobhaṃ nayati vanitā ityatilaghu / trilokīmapyāśu bhramayati ravīndustanayugām ॥19॥
sayIt: MOO-khum BIN-doom KRIT-vaa koo-cha-yoo-gam a-DHAS-tas-ya ta-DAD-ho / ha-RAAR-dhum DHYAA-yed yo ha-ra-MA-hi-shi tay mun-ma-tha-ka-LAAM / sa SUD-yah sank-SHO-bhum NA-ya-ti va-ni-TAA it-ya-ti-LA-ghoo / tri-lo-KEEM ap-YAA-shoo BHRA-ma-ya-ti ra-VEEN-doo-sta-na-yoo-gaam
translation: Queen of Hara, whoever meditates on your manmatha-kala — taking the face as the point, the pair of breasts below it, and below that the half of Hara — he at once sets women trembling; but that is a trifle: he soon sets the three worlds themselves whirling, she whose two breasts are the sun and the moon.
source: Soundarya Lahari 19 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which of your goals are actually door prizes — and what would you aim at if you took the biggest prize seriously?

translations.hi: हे हर की महारानी, जो तुम्हारी मन्मथ-कला का ध्यान करता है — मुख को बिन्दु मानकर, उसके नीचे उरोज-युगल, और उसके नीचे हर का अर्ध — वह तत्क्षण स्त्रियों को विकल कर देता है; पर यह तो बहुत छोटी बात है: वह शीघ्र ही उस त्रिलोकी को भी घुमा देता है जिसके दो उरोज सूर्य और चन्द्रमा हैं।

devanagari: किरन्तीमङ्गेभ्यः किरणनिकुरम्बामृतरसं / हृदि त्वामाधत्ते हिमकरशिलामूर्तिमिव यः । / स सर्पाणां दर्पं शमयति शकुन्ताधिप इव / ज्वरप्लुष्टान् दृष्ट्या सुखयति सुधाधारसिरया ॥20॥
iast: kirantīmaṅgebhyaḥ kiraṇanikurambāmṛtarasaṃ / hṛdi tvāmādhatte himakaraśilāmūrtimiva yaḥ । / sa sarpāṇāṃ darpaṃ śamayati śakuntādhipa iva / jvarapluṣṭān dṛṣṭyā sukhayati sudhādhārasirayā ॥20॥
sayIt: ki-run-TEEM un-GAY-bhyah ki-ra-na-ni-koo-rum-BAAM-ri-ta-ra-sum / HRI-di TVAAM-aa-DHUT-tay hi-ma-ka-ra-shi-LAA-moor-tim I-va yah / sa sur-PAA-naam DUR-pum SHA-ma-ya-ti sha-koon-TAA-dhi-pa I-va / jva-ra-PLOOSH-taan DRISHT-yaa SOO-kha-ya-ti soo-dhaa-DHAA-ra-si-ra-yaa
translation: Whoever holds you in his heart — an image as if carved from moonstone, raining the nectar-essence of a host of rays from every limb — he humbles the pride of serpents like the king of birds himself, and with a glance that runs like a channel of streaming nectar he soothes those burning with fever.
source: Soundarya Lahari 20 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Who around you is running a fever of the heart right now, and could your presence be the cool glance this verse describes?

translations.hi: जो तुम्हें हृदय में धारण करता है — मानो चन्द्रकान्त मणि से गढ़ी मूर्ति, जिसके अंग-अंग से किरण-समूह का अमृत-रस बरस रहा हो — वह गरुड़ की तरह सर्पों का दर्प शान्त कर देता है, और अमृत की धार बहाती नाड़ी जैसी अपनी दृष्टि-भर से ज्वर में जलते हुओं को सुख देता है।

devanagari: तटिल्लेखातन्वीं तपनशशिवैश्वानरमयीं / निषण्णां षण्णामप्युपरि कमलानां तव कलाम् । / महापद्माटव्यां मृदितमलमायेन मनसा / महान्तः पश्यन्तो दधति परमाह्लादलहरीम् ॥21॥
iast: taṭillekhātanvīṃ tapanaśaśivaiśvānaramayīṃ / niṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṇṇāmapyupari kamalānāṃ tava kalām । / mahāpadmāṭavyāṃ mṛditamalamāyena manasā / mahāntaḥ paśyanto dadhati paramāhlādalaharīm ॥21॥
sayIt: ta-til-LAY-khaa-tun-veem ta-pa-na-sha-shi-vaish-VAA-na-ra-ma-yeem / ni-SHAN-naam shan-NAAM ap-YOO-pa-ri ka-ma-LAA-naam TA-va ka-LAAM / ma-haa-pud-MAA-tav-yaam mri-di-ta-ma-la-MAA-yay-na MA-na-saa / ma-HAAN-tah push-YUN-toh DA-dha-ti pa-ra-MAAH-laa-da-la-ha-reem
translation: Slender as a streak of lightning, woven of sun, moon and fire, your subtle kala sits enthroned above even the six lotuses, in the forest of the great lotus; the great ones, beholding her there with a mind whose stains and illusions have been ground away, carry within them a wave of supreme gladness.
source: Soundarya Lahari 21 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What habit of mind would have to be worn away before joy of this kind could find room in you?

translations.hi: बिजली की रेखा-सी क्षीण, सूर्य, चन्द्र और अग्नि से बुनी हुई तुम्हारी सूक्ष्म कला छहों कमलों के भी ऊपर, महापद्म-वन में विराजती है; महात्मा जन, जिनके मन के मल और माया मथकर मिटा दिए गए हैं, उसका दर्शन करते हुए अपने भीतर परम आह्लाद की लहर धारण करते हैं।

devanagari: भवानि त्वं दासे मयि वितर दृष्टिं सकरुणा / मिति स्तोतुं वाञ्छन् कथयति भवानि त्वमिति यः । / तदैव त्वं तस्मै दिशसि निजसायुज्यपदवीं / मुकुन्दब्रह्मेन्द्रस्फुटमकुटनीराजितपदाम् ॥22॥
iast: bhavāni tvaṃ dāse mayi vitara dṛṣṭiṃ sakaruṇā / miti stotuṃ vāñchan kathayati bhavāni tvamiti yaḥ । / tadaiva tvaṃ tasmai diśasi nijasāyujyapadavīṃ / mukundabrahmendrasphuṭamakuṭanīrājitapadām ॥22॥
sayIt: bha-VAA-ni tvam DAA-say MA-yi VI-ta-ra DRISH-tim sa-ka-roo-NAAM / I-ti STO-tum VAAN-chhan ka-tha-YA-ti bha-VAA-ni tvam I-ti yah / ta-DAI-va tvam TAS-mai DI-sha-si ni-ja-saa-YOOJ-ya-pa-da-veem / moo-KOON-da-brah-MEN-dra-sphoo-ta-ma-koo-ta-nee-RAA-ji-ta-pa-daam
translation: A devotee means to pray, "Bhavani, turn your compassionate glance on me, your servant" — but the instant he has said "bhavāni tvam," which also means "may I become you," you grant him oneness with yourself: the state whose feet the bright crowns of Mukunda, Brahma and Indra light in worship.
source: Soundarya Lahari 22 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When you ask the divine for something small, are you ready for the far larger answer hiding inside your own words?

translations.hi: भक्त कहना चाहता है — "भवानी, अपने इस दास पर करुणा-भरी दृष्टि डालो"; पर "भवानि त्वम्" कहते ही — जिसका एक अर्थ "मैं तुम हो जाऊँ" भी है — तुम उसे उसी क्षण अपना सायुज्य दे देती हो: वह पद, जिसके चरणों की आरती मुकुन्द, ब्रह्मा और इन्द्र के दमकते मुकुट करते हैं।

devanagari: त्वया हृत्वा वामं वपुरपरितृप्तेन मनसा / शरीरार्धं शम्भोरपरमपि शङ्के हृतमभूत् । / यदेतत्त्वद्रूपं सकलमरुणाभं त्रिनयनं / कुचाभ्यामानम्रं कुटिलशशिचूडालमकुटम् ॥23॥
iast: tvayā hṛtvā vāmaṃ vapuraparitṛptena manasā / śarīrārdhaṃ śambhoraparamapi śaṅke hṛtamabhūt । / yadetattvadrūpaṃ sakalamaruṇābhaṃ trinayanaṃ / kucābhyāmānamraṃ kuṭilaśaśicūḍālamakuṭam ॥23॥
sayIt: tva-YAA hrit-VAA VAA-mum va-POOR a-pa-ri-TRIP-tay-na MA-na-saa / sha-ree-RAAR-dhum SHAM-bhor A-pa-ram A-pi SHAN-kay HRI-tam a-BHOOT / yad AY-tat tvad-ROO-pum SA-ka-lam a-roo-NAA-bhum tri-NA-ya-num / koo-CHAA-bhyaam AA-nam-rum KOO-ti-la-sha-shi-choo-DAA-la-ma-koo-tum
translation: You seized the left half of Shambhu's body — and then, I suspect, your still-unsatisfied heart took the other half too: for this form of yours is dawn-red through and through, carries three eyes, bows a little with the fullness of your breasts, and wears the curved crescent moon in its crown.
source: Soundarya Lahari 23 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where are you still splitting into halves what your own experience keeps telling you is one?

translations.hi: तुमने शम्भु के शरीर का बायाँ आधा भाग ले लिया — और फिर, मुझे लगता है, तुम्हारे अतृप्त मन ने दूसरा आधा भी ले लिया: तभी तो तुम्हारा यह रूप पूरा का पूरा अरुण आभा में रँगा है, इसमें तीन नेत्र हैं, यह वक्ष के भार से तनिक झुका है, और मुकुट में टेढ़ा अर्धचन्द्र धारण किए है।

devanagari: जगत्सूते धाता हरिरवति रुद्रः क्षपयते / तिरस्कुर्वन्नेतत्स्वमपि वपुरीशस्तिरयति । / सदापूर्वः सर्वं तदिदमनुगृह्णाति च शिव / स्तवाज्ञामालम्ब्य क्षणचलितयोर्भ्रूलतिकयोः ॥24॥
iast: jagatsūte dhātā hariravati rudraḥ kṣapayate / tiraskurvannetatsvamapi vapurīśastirayati । / sadāpūrvaḥ sarvaṃ tadidamanugṛhṇāti ca śiva / stavājñāmālambya kṣaṇacalitayorbhrūlatikayoḥ ॥24॥
sayIt: ja-gat SOO-tay DHAA-taa HA-rir A-va-ti ROO-drah ksha-pa-YA-tay / ti-ras-KOOR-van AY-tat SVAM-a-pi VA-poor EE-shas ti-ra-YA-ti / sa-daa-POOR-vah SAR-vum tad-I-dam a-noo-GRIH-naa-ti cha SHI-vas / ta-vaa-GYAAM aa-LAMB-ya KSHA-na-cha-li-ta-yor BHROO-la-ti-ka-yoh
translation: Brahma brings forth the world, Hari protects it, Rudra dissolves it; Isha veils these three, hiding even his own body; and Shiva with "Sadā" before his name — Sadashiva — graces it all back into being. And every one of them leans on your command, given in a moment's flicker of your vine-slender brows.
source: Soundarya Lahari 24 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: If the whole universe runs on a gesture of grace, what are you still trying to run on willpower alone?

translations.hi: धाता (ब्रह्मा) जगत को जन्म देते हैं, हरि उसकी रक्षा करते हैं, रुद्र उसका संहार करते हैं; ईश इन सबको — अपने शरीर सहित — ओझल कर लेते हैं; और नाम के आगे "सदा" धारे शिव — सदाशिव — इस सब पर फिर अनुग्रह करते हैं। और इनमें से हर एक टिका है तुम्हारी आज्ञा पर, जो तुम्हारी लता-सी भौंहों की क्षण-भर की थिरकन से मिलती है।

devanagari: त्रयाणां देवानां त्रिगुणजनितानां तव शिवे / भवेत् पूजा पूजा तव चरणयोर्या विरचिता । / तथा हि त्वत्पादोद्वहनमणिपीठस्य निकटे / स्थिता ह्येते शश्वन्मुकुलितकरोत्तंसमकुटाः ॥25॥
iast: trayāṇāṃ devānāṃ triguṇajanitānāṃ tava śive / bhavet pūjā pūjā tava caraṇayoryā viracitā । / tathā hi tvatpādodvahanamaṇipīṭhasya nikaṭe / sthitā hyete śaśvanmukulitakarottaṃsamakuṭāḥ ॥25॥
sayIt: tra-YAA-naam day-VAA-naam tri-goo-na-ja-ni-TAA-naam TA-va shi-VAY / bha-VAYT POO-jaa POO-jaa TA-va cha-ra-na-YOR yaa vi-ra-chi-TAA / ta-THAA hi tvat-paa-DOD-va-ha-na-ma-ni-PEE-thas-ya ni-ka-TAY / sthi-TAA hyay-TAY SHASH-van moo-koo-li-ta-ka-ROT-tan-sa-ma-koo-taah
translation: O consort of Shiva, worship offered at your two feet becomes worship of all three gods born of your three qualities — and how could it not, when they stand forever beside the jewelled seat that bears your feet, their folded hands held like buds atop their crowns?
source: Soundarya Lahari 25 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Is your devotion scattered across many counters, or offered once at the root that feeds them all?

translations.hi: हे शिवे! तुम्हारे दोनों चरणों में रची गई पूजा अपने-आप उन तीनों देवों की पूजा बन जाती है जो तुम्हारे तीन गुणों से जन्मे हैं — और भला क्यों न बने, जब वे तीनों तुम्हारे चरण धारण करने वाले मणि-जड़े पीठ के पास सदा खड़े रहते हैं, कली-से जुड़े हाथ अपने मुकुटों के ऊपर उठाए?

devanagari: विरिञ्चिः पञ्चत्वं व्रजति हरिराप्नोति विरतिं / विनाशं कीनाशो भजति धनदो याति निधनम् । / वितन्द्री माहेन्द्री विततिरपि संमीलितदृशा / महासंहारेऽस्मिन् विहरति सति त्वत्पतिरसौ ॥26॥
iast: viriñciḥ pañcatvaṃ vrajati harirāpnoti viratiṃ / vināśaṃ kīnāśo bhajati dhanado yāti nidhanam । / vitandrī māhendrī vitatirapi saṃmīlitadṛśā / mahāsaṃhāre'smin viharati sati tvatpatirasau ॥26॥
sayIt: vi-RIN-chih PANCH-at-vum VRA-ja-ti HA-rir AAP-no-ti VI-ra-tim / vi-NAA-shum kee-NAA-sho BHA-ja-ti DHA-na-do YAA-ti NI-dha-num / vi-TAN-dree maa-HAYN-dree VI-ta-tir A-pi sam-MEE-li-ta-dri-SHAA / ma-haa-sam-HAA-ray-smin vi-HA-ra-ti SA-ti tvat-PA-tir a-SAU
translation: Virinchi the creator returns to the five elements; Hari enters his long rest; Yama, death himself, meets destruction; Kubera the wealth-giver comes to his end; even the unsleeping ranks of great Indras close their eyes. Yet in this great dissolution, O Sati, your husband — he alone — goes on playing.
source: Soundarya Lahari 26 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When everything with a name and an office has gone down, what are you joined to that would still be playing?

translations.hi: विरिञ्चि (ब्रह्मा) पाँच तत्त्वों में लौट जाते हैं; हरि दीर्घ विश्राम में चले जाते हैं; स्वयं मृत्यु के देवता यम का विनाश हो जाता है; धन देने वाले कुबेर का अन्त आ जाता है; बड़े-बड़े इन्द्रों की अनथक पंक्तियाँ भी आँखें मूँद लेती हैं। पर इस महासंहार में भी, हे सती, तुम्हारे पति — केवल वे — क्रीड़ा करते रहते हैं।

devanagari: जपो जल्पः शिल्पं सकलमपि मुद्राविरचना / गतिः प्रादक्षिण्यक्रमणमशनाद्याहुतिविधिः । / प्रणामस्संवेशस्सुखमखिलमात्मार्पणदृशा / सपर्यापर्यायस्तव भवतु यन्मे विलसितम् ॥27॥
iast: japo jalpaḥ śilpaṃ sakalamapi mudrāviracanā / gatiḥ prādakṣiṇyakramaṇamaśanādyāhutividhiḥ । / praṇāmassaṃveśassukhamakhilamātmārpaṇadṛśā / saparyāparyāyastava bhavatu yanme vilasitam ॥27॥
sayIt: JA-po JAL-pah SHIL-pum SA-ka-lam A-pi moo-DRAA-vi-ra-cha-naa / GA-tih praa-DAK-shin-ya-kra-ma-nam a-sha-NAA-dyaa-hoo-ti-vi-dhih / pra-NAA-mas sam-VAY-shas SOO-kham A-khi-lam aat-MAAR-pa-na-dri-SHAA / sa-par-YAA-par-YAA-yas TA-va BHA-va-too YAN-may vi-LA-si-tum
translation: Let my chatter be your japa; every craft of my hands, the tracing of your ritual gestures; my walking, circumambulation of you; my food and all the rest, the fire-offering; my lying down, prostration; my every pleasure, seen with the eye of self-offering — let whatever I naturally do become, in the very doing, one more name for your worship.
source: Soundarya Lahari 27 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which one ordinary act will you do today exactly as always, but as an offering?

translations.hi: मेरी बातचीत तुम्हारा जप बन जाए; मेरे हाथों का हर काम तुम्हारी मुद्राओं की रचना; मेरा चलना तुम्हारी प्रदक्षिणा; मेरा भोजन और बाक़ी सब तुम्हारी आहुति; मेरा लेटना तुम्हें प्रणाम; और मेरा हर सुख आत्म-अर्पण की दृष्टि से देखा जाए — जो कुछ मुझसे सहज होता है, वही होते-होते तुम्हारी पूजा का पर्याय बन जाए।

devanagari: सुधामप्यास्वाद्य प्रतिभयजरामृत्युहरिणीं / विपद्यन्ते विश्वे विधिशतमखाद्या दिविषदः । / करालं यत्क्ष्वेलं कबलितवतः कालकलना / न शम्भोस्तन्मूलं तव जननि ताटङ्कमहिमा ॥28॥
iast: sudhāmapyāsvādya pratibhayajarāmṛtyuhariṇīṃ / vipadyante viśve vidhiśatamakhādyā diviṣadaḥ । / karālaṃ yatkṣvelaṃ kabalitavataḥ kālakalanā / na śambhostanmūlaṃ tava janani tāṭaṅkamahimā ॥28॥
sayIt: soo-DHAAM ap-YAAS-vaad-ya pra-ti-bha-ya-ja-raa-MRIT-yoo-ha-ri-neem / vi-pad-YAN-tay VISH-vay vi-dhi-sha-ta-ma-KHAAD-yaa di-vi-SHA-dah / ka-RAA-lum yat KSHVAY-lum ka-ba-li-ta-va-TAH KAA-la-ka-la-naa / na SHAM-bhos tan-MOO-lum TA-va JA-na-ni taa-TAN-ka-ma-hi-maa
translation: Though they sipped the nectar that strips away dreadful old age and death, the dwellers of heaven — Brahma, hundred-sacrifice Indra and all the rest — perish in the end. Yet Shambhu, who swallowed the terrible poison itself, lies beyond Time's counting — and the root of that, O Mother, is the glory of your ear-ornaments.
source: Soundarya Lahari 28 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Is your sense of safety stored in substances and supplies, or in the bonds that actually hold you?

translations.hi: भयानक बुढ़ापे और मृत्यु को हर लेने वाला अमृत चखकर भी स्वर्गवासी — ब्रह्मा, शतमख इन्द्र और बाक़ी सब — अन्ततः नष्ट हो जाते हैं। पर जिन्होंने विकराल विष को ही निगल लिया, उन शम्भु पर काल की गिनती नहीं चलती — और हे जननी, इसकी जड़ है तुम्हारे कर्णफूलों — ताटंकों — की महिमा।

devanagari: किरीटं वैरिञ्चं परिहर पुरः कैटभभिदः / कठोरे कोटीरे स्खलसि जहि जम्भारिमुकुटम् । / प्रणम्रेष्वेतेषु प्रसभमुपयातस्य भवनं / भवस्याभ्युत्थाने तव परिजनोक्तिर्विजयते ॥29॥
iast: kirīṭaṃ vairiñcaṃ parihara puraḥ kaiṭabhabhidaḥ / kaṭhore koṭīre skhalasi jahi jambhārimukuṭam । / praṇamreṣveteṣu prasabhamupayātasya bhavanaṃ / bhavasyābhyutthāne tava parijanoktirvijayate ॥29॥
sayIt: ki-REE-tum vai-RIN-chum PA-ri-ha-ra poo-RAH kai-ta-bha-BHI-dah / ka-THO-ray ko-TEE-ray SKHA-la-si JA-hi jam-BHAA-ri-moo-koo-tum / pra-NAM-ray-shvay-TAY-shoo pra-SA-bham oo-pa-YAA-tas-ya BHA-va-num / bha-vas-YAA-bhyoot-THAA-nay TA-va pa-ri-ja-NOK-tir vi-ja-ya-TAY
translation: "Mind Virinchi's crown there in front! You will stumble on the hard diadem of Kaitabha's slayer — step past the crown of Jambha's foe!" When Bhava arrives home unannounced and you spring up to receive him, this cry of your attendants — picking a path for you through the prostrate gods — carries the day.
source: Soundarya Lahari 29 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Whom do you rise for before thinking — and what does that reflex say about the true order of your heart?

translations.hi: "आगे विरिञ्चि (ब्रह्मा) का किरीट है, बचकर! कैटभ-हन्ता विष्णु के कठोर मुकुट से ठोकर लग जाएगी — जम्भ-शत्रु इन्द्र का मुकुट हटाकर निकलो!" जब भव (शिव) अचानक भवन आ पहुँचते हैं और तुम उनकी अगवानी में झट उठ पड़ती हो, तब साष्टांग लेटे देवताओं के बीच तुम्हारी राह सुझाती परिचारिकाओं की यही पुकार विजय पाती है।

devanagari: स्वदेहोद्भूताभिर्घृणिभिरणिमाद्याभिरभितो / निषेव्ये नित्ये त्वामहमिति सदा भावयति यः । / किमाश्चर्यं तस्य त्रिनयनसमृद्धिं तृणयतो / महासंवर्ताग्निर्विरचयति नीराजनविधिम् ॥30॥
iast: svadehodbhūtābhirghṛṇibhiraṇimādyābhirabhito / niṣevye nitye tvāmahamiti sadā bhāvayati yaḥ । / kimāścaryaṃ tasya trinayanasamṛddhiṃ tṛṇayato / mahāsaṃvartāgnirviracayati nīrājanavidhim ॥30॥
sayIt: sva-day-HOD-bhoo-TAA-bhir GHRI-ni-bhir a-ni-MAA-dyaa-bhir a-bhi-TO / ni-SHAYV-yay NIT-yay TVAAM A-ham I-ti sa-DAA BHAA-va-ya-ti yah / kim AASH-char-yum TAS-ya tri-NA-ya-na-sam-RID-dhim tri-na-ya-TO / ma-haa-sam-var-TAAG-nir vi-RA-cha-ya-ti nee-RAA-ja-na-vi-dhim
translation: O Eternal One, worthy of all service — the powers called aṇimā and the rest surround you like rays risen from your own body. Whoever contemplates you always as "I," as not other than himself, comes to count even three-eyed Shiva's treasury as straw — and is it any wonder that for him the great fire of dissolution performs the waving of the lamps?
source: Soundarya Lahari 30 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: If the deepest "I" in you cannot burn, how many of today's fears would survive that discovery?

translations.hi: हे नित्ये, सेवा के योग्य देवी! अणिमा आदि सिद्धियाँ तुम्हारे ही शरीर से उठी किरणों की तरह तुम्हें चारों ओर से घेरे रहती हैं। जो तुम्हें सदा "मैं" के रूप में — अपने से अभिन्न — भावित करता है, वह त्रिनेत्र शिव के कोष को भी तिनका गिनने लगता है — तो क्या आश्चर्य कि प्रलय की महाअग्नि स्वयं उसकी आरती उतारती है?

devanagari: चतुष्षष्ट्या तन्त्रैः सकलमतिसंधाय भुवनं / स्थितस्तत्तत्सिद्धिप्रसवपरतन्त्रैः पशुपतिः । / पुनस्त्वन्निर्बन्धादखिलपुरुषार्थैकघटना / स्वतन्त्रं ते तन्त्रं क्षितितलमवातीतरदिदम् ॥31॥
iast: catuṣṣaṣṭyā tantraiḥ sakalamatisaṃdhāya bhuvanaṃ / sthitastattatsiddhiprasavaparatantraiḥ paśupatiḥ । / punastvannirbandhādakhilapuruṣārthaikaghaṭanā / svatantraṃ te tantraṃ kṣititalamavātītaradidam ॥31॥
sayIt: cha-toosh-SHASH-tyaa TAN-traih SA-ka-lam a-ti-san-DHAA-ya bhoo-va-num / sthi-TAS tat-tat-SID-dhi-pra-sa-va-pa-ra-TAN-traih pa-shoo-PA-tih / poo-NAS tvan-nir-ban-DHAAD a-khi-la-poo-roo-SHAAR-thai-ka-gha-ta-NAA / sva-TAN-trum tay TAN-trum kshi-ti-ta-lam a-vaa-TEE-ta-rad i-dam
translation: With the sixty-four tantras — each absorbed in yielding its own single attainment — Pashupati beguiled the whole world, and rested. Then, pressed by your insistence, he brought down to this earth your own tantra: the one teaching independently able to accomplish, all together, every aim of human life.
source: Soundarya Lahari 31 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Are you collecting many partial techniques for many partial gains, or walking one path that carries the whole of you?

translations.hi: चौंसठ तन्त्रों से — जिनमें हर एक बस अपनी-अपनी एक सिद्धि देने में डूबा है — पशुपति ने सारे संसार को उलझाए रखा, और स्वयं मौन रहे। फिर तुम्हारे आग्रह पर वे इस धरती पर तुम्हारा अपना तन्त्र उतार लाए: वह एक विद्या जो अकेली ही मनुष्य-जीवन के सारे लक्ष्य — सब एक साथ — सिद्ध कर देती है।

devanagari: शिवः शक्तिः कामः क्षितिरथ रविः शीतकिरणः / स्मरो हंसः शक्रस्तदनु च परामारहरयः । / अमी हृल्लेखाभिस्तिसृभिरवसानेषु घटिता / भजन्ते वर्णास्ते तव जननि नामावयवताम् ॥32॥
iast: śivaḥ śaktiḥ kāmaḥ kṣitiratha raviḥ śītakiraṇaḥ / smaro haṃsaḥ śakrastadanu ca parāmāraharayaḥ । / amī hṛllekhābhistisṛbhiravasāneṣu ghaṭitā / bhajante varṇāste tava janani nāmāvayavatām ॥32॥
sayIt: shi-VAH SHAK-tih KAA-mah KSHI-tir A-tha RA-vih SHEE-ta-ki-ra-nah / sma-RO HAN-sah SHA-kras tad-A-noo cha pa-RAA-maa-ra-ha-ra-yah / a-MEE hril-lay-KHAA-bhis TIS-ri-bhir a-va-SAA-nay-shoo gha-ti-TAA / bha-JAN-tay VAR-naas tay TA-va JA-na-ni NAA-maa-va-ya-va-taam
translation: Shiva, Shakti, Kama, Earth; then Sun, the cool-rayed Moon, Smara, Hamsa, Shakra; and after these, Para, Mara and Hari — these sounds, O Mother, their groups sealed by the three hṛllekhā syllables, become the very limbs of your name.
source: Soundarya Lahari 32 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which of the most precious things in your life were rightly received from a person, and could never have been extracted from a page?

translations.hi: शिव, शक्ति, काम, क्षिति; फिर रवि, शीतल-किरण चन्द्र, स्मर, हंस, शक्र; और उनके बाद परा, मार, हरि — हे जननी! तीन ह्रल्लेखाओं से अपने-अपने खण्ड के अन्त में जुड़कर ये ही वर्ण तुम्हारे नाम के अंग बन जाते हैं।

devanagari: स्मरं योनिं लक्ष्मीं त्रितयमिदमादौ तव मनो / र्निधायैके नित्ये निरवधिमहाभोगरसिकाः । / भजन्ति त्वां चिन्तामणिगुननिबद्धाक्षवलयाः / शिवाग्नौ जुह्वन्तः सुरभिघृतधाराहुतिशतैः ॥33॥
iast: smaraṃ yoniṃ lakṣmīṃ tritayamidamādau tava mano / rnidhāyaike nitye niravadhimahābhogarasikāḥ । / bhajanti tvāṃ cintāmaṇigunanibaddhākṣavalayāḥ / śivāgnau juhvantaḥ surabhighṛtadhārāhutiśataiḥ ॥33॥
sayIt: sma-RUM YO-nim LAKSH-meem TRI-ta-yam I-dam AA-dau TA-va ma-NOR / ni-DHAA-yai-kay NIT-yay ni-ra-va-dhi-ma-haa-BHO-ga-ra-si-kaah / bha-JAN-ti tvaam chin-TAA-ma-ni-goo-na-ni-bad-DHAAK-sha-va-la-yaah / shi-VAAG-nau JOOH-van-tah soo-ra-bhi-ghri-ta-DHAA-raa-hoo-ti-sha-taih
translation: Some, O Eternal One — connoisseurs of boundless great enjoyment — set the triad Smara, Yoni, Lakshmi before your mantra and worship you, rosaries strung on cords of wish-granting gems in their hands, offering into the fire that is Shiva hundreds of oblations poured as unbroken streams of the celestial cow's ghee.
source: Soundarya Lahari 33 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What are your daily offerings of time, money and attention actually feeding?

translations.hi: हे नित्ये! कुछ उपासक — असीम महाभोग के रसिक — तुम्हारे मन्त्र से पहले स्मर, योनि, लक्ष्मी की त्रयी रखकर तुम्हें भजते हैं; हाथों में चिन्तामणियों से गुँथी अक्षमालाएँ, और शिव-रूपी अग्नि में सुरभि गाय के घी की सैकड़ों अटूट धाराओं की आहुतियाँ।

devanagari: शरीरं त्वं शम्भोः शशिमिहिरवक्षोरुहयुगं / तवात्मानं मन्ये भगवति नवात्मानमनघम् । / अतश्शेषश्शेषीत्ययमुभयसाधारणतया / स्थितः संबन्धो वां समरसपरानन्दपरयोः ॥34॥
iast: śarīraṃ tvaṃ śambhoḥ śaśimihiravakṣoruhayugaṃ / tavātmānaṃ manye bhagavati navātmānamanagham । / ataśśeṣaśśeṣītyayamubhayasādhāraṇatayā / sthitaḥ saṃbandho vāṃ samarasaparānandaparayoḥ ॥34॥
sayIt: sha-REE-rum tvam SHAM-bhoh sha-shi-MI-hi-ra-vak-SHO-roo-ha-yoo-gum / ta-VAAT-maa-num MAN-yay BHA-ga-va-ti na-VAAT-maa-nam a-NA-gham / a-tash SHAY-shash SHAY-sheet-ya-yam oo-bha-ya-saa-DHAA-ra-na-ta-yaa / sthi-TAH sam-BAN-dho vaam sa-ma-RA-sa-pa-raa-NAN-da-pa-ra-yoh
translation: You are the very body of Shambhu, sun and moon your paired breasts; and your self, O Bhagavati, I hold to be the flawless nine-fold Shiva. So the relation of bearer and borne stands common to you both, running equally each way — you two, supreme Bliss and the supreme She, poised in a single savour.
source: Soundarya Lahari 34 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: In your closest bond, can you still tell who carries whom — and does the question even need an answer?

translations.hi: तुम शम्भु का साक्षात् शरीर हो — सूर्य और चन्द्र तुम्हारे वक्ष का युगल हैं; और हे भगवती! तुम्हारी आत्मा को मैं निर्दोष नवात्मा शिव मानता हूँ। इसलिए धारक और धार्य का सम्बन्ध तुम दोनों में साझा है, दोनों ओर बराबर बहता हुआ — तुम दोनों, परम आनन्द और परा शक्ति, एक ही रस में ठहरे हुए।

devanagari: मनस्त्वं व्योम त्वं मरुदसि मरुत्सारथिरसि / त्वमापस्त्वं भूमिस्त्वयि परिणतायां न हि परम् । / त्वमेव स्वात्मानं परिणमयितुं विश्ववपुषा / चिदानन्दाकारं शिवयुवति भावेन बिभृषे ॥35॥
iast: manastvaṃ vyoma tvaṃ marudasi marutsārathirasi / tvamāpastvaṃ bhūmistvayi pariṇatāyāṃ na hi param । / tvameva svātmānaṃ pariṇamayituṃ viśvavapuṣā / cidānandākāraṃ śivayuvati bhāvena bibhṛṣe ॥35॥
sayIt: MA-nas tvam VYO-ma tvam MA-rood A-si ma-root-SAA-ra-thir A-si / tvam AA-pas tvam BHOO-mis TVA-yi pa-ri-na-TAA-yaam na hi PA-rum / tvam AY-va SVAAT-maa-num pa-ri-na-ma-yi-TOOM vish-va-va-poo-SHAA / chid-aa-nan-DAA-kaa-rum SHI-va-yoo-va-ti BHAA-vay-na bi-BHRI-shay
translation: You are mind, you are sky; you are wind, and the fire whose charioteer is wind; you are the waters, you are earth — and beyond you, once you have unfolded yourself, nothing else remains. To turn your own self into the body of the world, it is you who wear the form of consciousness-and-bliss as Shiva's young bride.
source: Soundarya Lahari 35 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: If everything you will touch today is one self unfolded, how will you touch it?

translations.hi: मन तुम हो, आकाश तुम; वायु तुम हो, और वह अग्नि भी जिसका सारथी वायु है; जल तुम हो, पृथ्वी तुम — और जब तुम स्वयं को परिणत कर चुकती हो, तो तुमसे परे कुछ शेष नहीं रहता। अपने ही आप को विश्व का शरीर बनाने के लिए तुम्हीं चिदानन्द का आकार धारे, शिव की नवयुवती वधू के भाव में प्रकट होती हो।

devanagari: तवाज्ञाचक्रस्थं तपनशशिकोटिद्युतिधरं / परं शम्भुं वन्दे परिमिलितपार्श्वं परचिता । / यमाराध्यन् भक्त्या रविशशिशुचीनामविषये / निरालोकेऽलोके निवसति हि भालोकभुवने ॥36॥
iast: tavājñācakrasthaṃ tapanaśaśikoṭidyutidharaṃ / paraṃ śambhuṃ vande parimilitapārśvaṃ paracitā । / yamārādhyan bhaktyā raviśaśiśucīnāmaviṣaye / nirāloke'loke nivasati hi bhālokabhuvane ॥36॥
sayIt: ta-vaa-GYAA-cha-kra-sthum TA-pa-na-sha-shi-KO-ti-dyoo-ti-dha-rum / PA-rum SHAM-bhoom VAN-day pa-ri-MI-li-ta-PAARSH-vum pa-ra-chi-TAA / yam aa-RAA-dhyan BHAK-tyaa RA-vi-sha-shi-shoo-CHEE-naam a-vi-sha-YAY / ni-raa-LO-kay LO-kay ni-VA-sa-ti hi BHAA-lo-ka-bhoo-va-nay
translation: I bow to the supreme Shambhu who dwells in your ājñā centre, bearing the brilliance of millions of suns and moons at once, his side joined by you, Supreme Consciousness. Whoever worships him with devotion comes to dwell where sun, moon and fire hold no province — past every lit world, in a homeland made of light itself.
source: Soundarya Lahari 36 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where do you turn for light when every outer lamp has failed you?
