translations.hi: मैं उन परम शम्भु को प्रणाम करता हूँ जो तुम्हारे आज्ञा-चक्र में विराजते हैं — करोड़ों सूर्यों और चन्द्रमाओं की द्युति एक साथ धारे, और जिनके पार्श्व से परा-चित् — स्वयं तुम — मिली हुई हो। जो उन्हें भक्ति से आराधता है, वह वहाँ जा बसता है जहाँ रवि, शशि और अग्नि का कोई अधिकार नहीं — हर प्रकाशित लोक से परे, वह देश जो स्वयं प्रकाश का बना है।

devanagari: विशुद्धौ ते शुद्धस्फटिकविशदं व्योमजनकं / शिवं सेवे देवीमपि शिवसमानव्यवसिताम् । / ययोः कान्त्या यान्त्याः शशिकिरणसारूप्यसरणे / विधूतान्तर्ध्वान्ता विलसति चकोरीव जगती ॥37॥
iast: viśuddhau te śuddhasphaṭikaviśadaṃ vyomajanakaṃ / śivaṃ seve devīmapi śivasamānavyavasitām । / yayoḥ kāntyā yāntyāḥ śaśikiraṇasārūpyasaraṇe / vidhūtāntardhvāntā vilasati cakorīva jagatī ॥37॥
sayIt: vi-SHOOD-dhau tay SHOOD-dha-spha-ti-ka-VI-sha-dum VYO-ma-ja-na-kum / SHI-vum SAY-vay DAY-veem A-pi SHI-va-sa-MAA-na-vya-va-si-taam / ya-YOH KAAN-tyaa YAAN-tyaah sha-shi-KI-ra-na-saa-ROOP-ya-sa-ra-nay / vi-DHOO-taan-tar-DHVAAN-taa vi-LA-sa-ti cha-ko-REE-va ja-ga-TEE
translation: In your viśuddhi centre I serve Shiva, lucid as flawless crystal, the begetter of the sky, and with him the Devi, one with him in resolve. As their radiance streams out like a path of moonbeam-light, the world sheds its inner darkness and delights like the cakorī bird that lives on moonlight.
source: Soundarya Lahari 37 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Whose presence clears your inner weather without a single word — and how often do you stand in it?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे विशुद्धि-चक्र में मैं उन शिव की सेवा करता हूँ जो निर्मल स्फटिक-से स्वच्छ हैं और आकाश के जनक हैं — और उनके साथ उन देवी की भी, जिनका संकल्प शिव के ही समान है। चाँदनी की राह-सी बहती उन दोनों की कान्ति में भीतर का अँधेरा झड़ जाता है, और जगत उस चकोरी की तरह खिल उठता है जो चाँद की किरणों पर जीती है।

devanagari: समुन्मीलत् संवित् कमलमकरन्दैकरसिकं / भजे हंसद्वन्द्वं किमपि महतां मानसचरम् । / यदालापादष्टादशगुणितविद्यापरिणति / र्यदादत्ते दोषाद् गुणमखिलमद्भ्यः पय इव ॥38॥
iast: samunmīlat saṃvit kamalamakarandaikarasikaṃ / bhaje haṃsadvandvaṃ kimapi mahatāṃ mānasacaram । / yadālāpādaṣṭādaśaguṇitavidyāpariṇati / ryadādatte doṣād guṇamakhilamadbhyaḥ paya iva ॥38॥
sayIt: sa-moon-MEE-lat SAM-vit KA-ma-la-ma-ka-ran-DAI-ka-ra-si-kum / bha-JAY han-sa-DVAN-dvum KIM-a-pi ma-ha-TAAM MAA-na-sa-cha-rum / ya-daa-LAA-paad ash-TAA-da-sha-goo-ni-ta-VID-yaa-pa-ri-na-tir / ya-DAA-dat-tay do-SHAAD GOO-nam A-khi-lam ad-BHYAH PA-ya i-va
translation: I worship a pair of swans past all description, who relish one nectar only — the honey of the opening lotus of awareness — and glide on the Mānasa lake of great minds. From their murmured converse unfolds the whole ripening of the eighteen sciences; and from every fault they draw out whatever is excellent, as a swan draws milk from water.
source: Soundarya Lahari 38 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: From today's mixture of praise, blame and noise, can you drink only the milk?

translations.hi: मैं हंसों के उस अवर्णनीय जोड़े की उपासना करता हूँ जो एक ही मकरन्द का रसिक है — खिलते चैतन्य-कमल का मधु — और महान मनों के मानस-सरोवर में विहरता है। उनके आलाप से ही अठारह विद्याओं का सारा विकास फूटता है; और वे हर दोष में से गुण-भर खींच लेते हैं, जैसे हंस पानी में मिले दूध को अलग कर लेता है।

devanagari: तव स्वाधिष्ठाने हुतवहमधिष्ठाय निरतं / तमीडे संवर्तं जननि महतीं तां च समयाम् । / यदालोके लोकान् दहति महति क्रोधकलिते / दयार्द्रा या दृष्टिः शिशिरमुपचारं रचयति ॥39॥
iast: tava svādhiṣṭhāne hutavahamadhiṣṭhāya nirataṃ / tamīḍe saṃvartaṃ janani mahatīṃ tāṃ ca samayām । / yadāloke lokān dahati mahati krodhakalite / dayārdrā yā dṛṣṭiḥ śiśiramupacāraṃ racayati ॥39॥
sayIt: TA-va svaa-dhish-THAA-nay hoo-ta-VA-ham a-dhish-THAA-ya ni-ra-tum / tam EE-day sam-VAR-tum JA-na-ni ma-ha-TEEM taam cha sa-ma-YAAM / ya-daa-LO-kay lo-KAAN DA-ha-ti MA-ha-ti KRO-dha-ka-li-tay / da-YAAR-draa yaa DRISH-tih SHI-shi-ram oo-pa-CHAA-rum RA-cha-ya-ti
translation: I praise, O Mother, the fire of dissolution that abides forever in your svādhiṣṭhāna, and with it the great Samayā herself; for when that fire's glance, thick with rising wrath, sets the worlds alight, it is her gaze, wet with compassion, that works the cool healing rite.
source: Soundarya Lahari 39 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When your own fire rises, whose compassionate gaze — your own or another's — do you let cool it?

translations.hi: हे जननी! मैं तुम्हारे स्वाधिष्ठान में सदा विराजती संवर्त-अग्नि की स्तुति करता हूँ, और साथ में स्वयं महती समया देवी की भी; क्योंकि जब महाक्रोध से भरी उस अग्नि की दृष्टि लोकों को जलाने लगती है, तब करुणा से भीगी उनकी दृष्टि ही शीतल उपचार रचती है।

devanagari: तटित्त्वन्तं शक्त्या तिमिरपरिपन्थिस्फुरणया / स्फुरन्नानारत्नाभरणपरिणद्धेन्द्रधनुषम् । / तव श्यामं मेघं कमपि मणिपूरैकशरणं / निषेवे वर्षन्तं हरमिहिरतप्तं त्रिभुवनम् ॥40॥
iast: taṭittvantaṃ śaktyā timiraparipanthisphuraṇayā / sphurannānāratnābharaṇapariṇaddhendradhanuṣam । / tava śyāmaṃ meghaṃ kamapi maṇipūraikaśaraṇaṃ / niṣeve varṣantaṃ haramihirataptaṃ tribhuvanam ॥40॥
sayIt: ta-TIT-tvan-tum SHAK-tyaa TI-mi-ra-pa-ri-PAN-thi-sphoo-ra-na-yaa / sphoo-ran-NAA-naa-rat-NAA-bha-ra-na-pa-ri-nad-DHAYN-dra-dha-noo-shum / TA-va SHYAA-mum MAY-ghum KAM-a-pi ma-ni-POO-rai-ka-sha-ra-num / ni-SHAY-vay var-SHAN-tum HA-ra-mi-hi-ra-TAP-tum tri-bhoo-va-num
translation: I wait upon a dark rain-cloud beyond all telling, whose one refuge is your maṇipūra centre: Shakti is its lightning, her flashing the sworn enemy of darkness; the sparkle of its many jewelled ornaments bends into a rainbow; and it pours rain on the three worlds scorched by Hara, the sun of dissolution.
source: Soundarya Lahari 40 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which scorched corner of your life are you still refusing to believe rain can reach?

translations.hi: मैं उस अकथनीय श्याम मेघ की उपासना करता हूँ जिसका एकमात्र आश्रय तुम्हारा मणिपूर-चक्र है: शक्ति ही उसकी बिजली है, जिसकी कौंध अँधेरे की जन्म-बैरिन है; उसके नाना रत्नाभूषणों की चमक झुककर इन्द्रधनुष बन जाती है; और वह उन तीनों लोकों पर बरसता है जिन्हें प्रलय-सूर्य बने हर ने तपा डाला है।

devanagari: तवाधारे मूले सह समयया लास्यपरया / नवात्मानं मन्ये नवरसमहाताण्डवनटम् । / उभाभ्यामेताभ्यामुदयविधिमुद्दिश्य दयया / सनाथाभ्यां जज्ञे जनकजननीमज्जगदिदम् ॥41॥
iast: tavādhāre mūle saha samayayā lāsyaparayā / navātmānaṃ manye navarasamahātāṇḍavanaṭam । / ubhābhyāmetābhyāmudayavidhimuddiśya dayayā / sanāthābhyāṃ jajñe janakajananīmajjagadidam ॥41॥
sayIt: ta-vaa-DHAA-ray MOO-lay SA-ha sa-ma-ya-YAA LAAS-ya-pa-ra-yaa / na-VAAT-maa-num MAN-yay NA-va-ra-sa-ma-haa-TAAN-da-va-na-tum / oo-BHAA-bhyaam ay-TAA-bhyaam oo-da-ya-VI-dhim ood-DISH-ya da-ya-YAA / sa-NAA-thaa-bhyaam JAG-yay JA-na-ka-ja-na-nee-muj JA-gad i-dam
translation: In your mūlādhāra centre I contemplate the nine-fold Lord dancing the great tāṇḍava charged with all nine moods, and with him Samayā, absorbed in her graceful lāsya. By these two — who in compassion took each other as lord and lady, intent on the rite of the world's re-arising — this universe came to have a father and a mother.
source: Soundarya Lahari 41 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What changes in how you treat the world once you believe it has parents rather than a manufacturer?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे मूलाधार में मैं उन नवात्मा नटराज का ध्यान करता हूँ जो नौ रसों से भरा महाताण्डव नाचते हैं, और साथ में लास्य में लीन समया देवी का भी। जगत के पुनरुदय के विधान का संकल्प लेकर करुणावश एक-दूजे के स्वामी-स्वामिनी बने इन्हीं दोनों से इस संसार को अपने पिता और माता मिले।

devanagari: सौन्दर्यलहरी / गतैर्माणिक्यत्वं गगनमणिभिः सान्द्रघटितं / किरीटं ते हैमं हिमगिरिसुते कीर्तयति यः । / स नीडेयच्छायाच्छुरणशबलं चन्द्रशकलं / धनुः शौनासीरं किमिति न निबध्नाति धिषणाम् ॥42॥
iast: gatairmāṇikyatvaṃ gaganamaṇibhiḥ sāndraghaṭitaṃ / kirīṭaṃ te haimaṃ himagirisute kīrtayati yaḥ । / sa nīḍeyacchāyācchuraṇaśabalaṃ candraśakalaṃ / dhanuḥ śaunāsīraṃ kimiti na nibadhnāti dhiṣaṇām ॥42॥
sayIt: ga-tair-maa-NIK-yat-vum GA-ga-na-MA-ni-bhih SAAN-dra-GHA-ti-tum / ki-REE-tum tay HAI-mum HI-ma-GI-ri-soo-tay KEER-ta-ya-ti yah / sa NEE-day-yach-CHHAA-yaach-CHHOO-ra-na-SHA-ba-lum CHAN-dra-SHA-ka-lum / dha-NOOH shau-naa-SEE-rum KIM-i-ti na ni-BADH-naa-ti DHI-sha-naam
translation: Whoever tells of your golden crown, O daughter of the snow mountain — thick-set with the sky-jewels, the twelve suns turned into rubies — why would he not come to the firm conviction that the crescent moon upon it, dappled with the glancing sheen of those nested gems, is the rainbow, the bow of Indra?
source: Soundarya Lahari 42 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What would change in how you see the sky today if you took its lights to be ornaments of the divine?

translations.hi: हे हिमगिरि-पुत्री! जो तुम्हारे स्वर्ण-मुकुट का वर्णन करता है — जिसमें आकाश के मणि, यानी बारह सूर्य, माणिक बनकर सघन जड़े हैं — वह क्यों न मान बैठे कि उस पर टिका चन्द्रमा का टुकड़ा, उन जड़े रत्नों की झिलमिल आभा से रँगा हुआ, स्वयं इन्द्रधनुष है?

devanagari: धुनोतु ध्वान्तं नस्तुलितदलितेन्दीवरवनं / घनस्निग्धश्लक्ष्णं चिकुरनिकुरुम्बं तव शिवे । / यदीयं सौरभ्यं सहजमुपलब्धुं सुमनसो / वसन्त्यस्मिन् मन्ये वलमथनवाटीविटपिनाम् ॥43॥
iast: dhunotu dhvāntaṃ nastulitadalitendīvaravanaṃ / ghanasnigdhaślakṣṇaṃ cikuranikurumbaṃ tava śive । / yadīyaṃ saurabhyaṃ sahajamupalabdhuṃ sumanaso / vasantyasmin manye valamathanavāṭīviṭapinām ॥43॥
sayIt: dhoo-NO-too DHVAAN-tum nas-TOO-li-ta-DA-li-ten-DEE-va-ra-va-num / GHA-na-SNIG-dha-SHLAK-shnum CHI-koo-ra-ni-koo-ROOM-bum TA-va shi-VAY / ya-DEE-yum sau-RABH-yum SA-ha-jam-oo-pa-LAB-dhoom soo-MA-na-so / va-SANT-yas-min MAN-yay VA-la-MA-tha-na-VAA-tee-VI-ta-pi-naam
translation: May the massed abundance of your hair, O consort of Shiva — dense, glossy and fine, rivalling a forest of blue lotuses in full bloom — shake the darkness out of us. It is to win the fragrance native to it, I think, that the flowers of the trees in Indra's own garden come and make their home there.
source: Soundarya Lahari 43 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which sweetness in your life have you been offering back to its own source without realizing it?

translations.hi: हे शिवे! तुम्हारा केश-समूह — घना, स्निग्ध और चिकना, खिले हुए नील कमलों के वन-सा — हमारे भीतर का अन्धकार झाड़ दे। मुझे तो लगता है कि इन्द्र के उपवन के वृक्षों के फूल इसी में आ बसे हैं, ताकि इसकी वह सुगन्ध पा सकें जो इसे जन्म से मिली है।

devanagari: तनोतु क्षेमं नस्तव वदनसौन्दर्यलहरी / परीवाहस्रोतःसरणिरिव सीमन्तसरणिः । / वहन्ती सिन्दूरं प्रबलकबरीभारतिमिर / द्विषां वृन्दैर्बन्दीकृतमिव नवीनार्ककिरणम् ॥44॥
iast: tanotu kṣemaṃ nastava vadanasaundaryalaharī / parīvāhasrotaḥsaraṇiriva sīmantasaraṇiḥ । / vahantī sindūraṃ prabalakabarībhāratimira / dviṣāṃ vṛndairbandīkṛtamiva navīnārkakiraṇam ॥44॥
sayIt: ta-NO-too KSHAY-mum nas TA-va VA-da-na-saun-DAR-ya-la-ha-ree / pa-ree-VAA-ha-SRO-tah-SA-ra-nir-i-va SEE-man-ta-SA-ra-nih / va-HAN-tee sin-DOO-rum PRA-ba-la-KA-ba-ree-BHAA-ra-TI-mi-ra / dvi-SHAAM vrin-DAIR ban-DEE-kri-tam-i-va na-VEE-naar-ka-KI-ra-num
translation: May the parting-line of your hair spread wellbeing over us — it looks like the channel dug to carry off the overflowing flood of your face's beauty; and bearing its line of vermilion, it seems a ray of the newly risen sun taken prisoner by the massed ranks of its enemy, the darkness of your heavy braids.
source: Soundarya Lahari 44 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where in your day could one thin line of brightness be enough to hold back the dark?

translations.hi: तुम्हारी माँग की रेखा हम पर कल्याण बरसाए — वह उस नहर-सी लगती है जो तुम्हारे मुख के सौन्दर्य की उमड़ती बाढ़ को बहा ले जाने के लिए बनी हो; और उसमें भरा सिन्दूर ऐसा है मानो नए उगे सूर्य की एक किरण, जिसे तुम्हारे घने केश-भार रूपी अन्धकार की सेनाओं ने बन्दी बना लिया हो।

devanagari: अरालैः स्वाभाव्यादलिकलभसश्रीभिरलकैः / परीतं ते वक्त्रं परिहसति पङ्केरुहरुचिम् । / दरस्मेरे यस्मिन् दशनरुचिकिञ्जल्करुचिरे / सुगन्धौ माद्यन्ति स्मरदहनचक्षुर्मधुलिहः ॥45॥
iast: arālaiḥ svābhāvyādalikalabhasaśrībhiralakaiḥ / parītaṃ te vaktraṃ parihasati paṅkeruharucim । / darasmere yasmin daśanarucikiñjalkarucire / sugandhau mādyanti smaradahanacakṣurmadhulihaḥ ॥45॥
sayIt: a-RAA-laih svaa-BHAAV-yaad A-li-KA-la-bha-sash-REE-bhir A-la-kaih / pa-REE-tum tay VAK-trum PA-ri-HA-sa-ti pun-KAY-roo-ha-ROO-chim / DA-ra-SMAY-ray YAS-min DA-sha-na-ROO-chi-KIN-jal-ka-ROO-chi-ray / soo-GAN-dhau MAAD-yan-ti SMA-ra-DA-ha-na-CHAK-shoor-MA-dhoo-li-hah
translation: Ringed by your locks, curling by their very nature and lovely as a swarm of young black bees, your face outsmiles the beauty of the lotus; and in that face — softly smiling, radiant with teeth like a lotus's filaments, sweet with fragrance — the eyes of Shiva, burner of the god of love, grow drunk like honey-bees.
source: Soundarya Lahari 45 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What have you kept yourself too disciplined to be delighted by?

translations.hi: स्वभाव से ही घुँघराली, तरुण भौंरों के झुण्ड-सी सुन्दर लटों से घिरा तुम्हारा मुख कमल की शोभा का उपहास करता है; और उस मन्द-मुस्कान वाले मुख में — जहाँ दाँतों की आभा कमल के केसर-सी है, जो सुगन्ध से भरा है — कामदेव को भस्म करने वाले शिव के नेत्र मधुमक्खियों की तरह मतवाले हो जाते हैं।

devanagari: ललाटं लावण्यद्युतिविमलमाभाति तव य / द्द्वितीयं तन्मन्ये {मकुट}घटितं चन्द्रशकलम् । / विपर्यासन्यासादुभयमपि संभूय च मिथः / सुधालेपस्यूतिः परिणमति राकाहिमकरः ॥46॥
iast: lalāṭaṃ lāvaṇyadyutivimalamābhāti tava ya / ddvitīyaṃ tanmanye makuṭaghaṭitaṃ candraśakalam । / viparyāsanyāsādubhayamapi saṃbhūya ca mithaḥ / sudhālepasyūtiḥ pariṇamati rākāhimakaraḥ ॥46॥
sayIt: la-LAA-tum LAA-van-ya-DYOO-ti-VI-ma-lam-aa-BHAA-ti TA-va yad / dvi-TEE-yum tan-MAN-yay MA-koo-ta-GHA-ti-tum CHAN-dra-SHA-ka-lum / vi-par-YAA-sa-NYAA-saad oo-BHA-yam-a-pi sam-BHOO-ya cha mi-THAH / soo-dhaa-LAY-pa-SYOO-tih pa-ri-NA-ma-ti RAA-kaa-HI-ma-ka-rah
translation: Your forehead, shining flawless with the radiance of loveliness, I take to be a second crescent of the moon, set into your crown; the two of them, placed the opposite way about and merging with one another, become the full moon of a festival night, its seam sealed with a plaster of nectar.
source: Soundarya Lahari 46 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What broken half of your life might already have its matching piece waiting nearby?

translations.hi: लावण्य की कान्ति से निर्मल दमकता तुम्हारा ललाट मुझे चन्द्रमा का दूसरा अर्ध-खण्ड लगता है, जो मुकुट में जड़ा है; ये दोनों टुकड़े — एक-दूसरे के उलट रखे हुए, आपस में जुड़ते हुए — पूर्णिमा का वह पूरा चाँद बन जाते हैं जिसकी सन्धि अमृत के लेप से सिली गई हो।

devanagari: भ्रुवौ भुग्ने किंचिद्भुवनभयभङ्गव्यसनिनि / त्वदीये नेत्राभ्यां मधुकररुचिभ्यां धृतगुणम् । / धनुर्मन्ये सव्येतरकरगृहीतं रतिपतेः / प्रकोष्ठे मुष्टौ च स्थगयति निगूढान्तरमुमे ॥47॥
iast: bhruvau bhugne kiṃcidbhuvanabhayabhaṅgavyasanini / tvadīye netrābhyāṃ madhukararucibhyāṃ dhṛtaguṇam । / dhanurmanye savyetarakaragṛhītaṃ ratipateḥ / prakoṣṭhe muṣṭau ca sthagayati nigūḍhāntaramume ॥47॥
sayIt: bhroo-VAU bhoog-NAY KIN-chid BHOO-va-na-BHA-ya-BHUN-ga-vya-SA-ni-ni / tva-DEE-yay nay-TRAABH-yaam MA-dhoo-ka-ra-ROO-chibh-yaam DHRI-ta-goo-num / dha-NOOR MAN-yay sav-YAY-ta-ra-KA-ra-gri-HEE-tum RA-ti-pa-tayh / pra-KOSH-thay MOOSH-tau cha STHA-ga-ya-ti ni-GOO-dhaan-ta-ram-oo-may
translation: O Uma, bent on breaking the fear of the worlds — your pair of brows, slightly arched, I take for the bow of the lord of Rati: its string your two eyes with their black-bee sheen, gripped in his right hand, its middle hidden where his fist and forearm cover it.
source: Soundarya Lahari 47 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Whose fear could you make it your settled habit to break?

translations.hi: हे उमा, संसार का भय तोड़ने में लगी रहने वाली! तुम्हारी हल्की-सी झुकी भौंहों की जोड़ी मुझे कामदेव का धनुष लगती है — जिसकी प्रत्यञ्चा भौंरों-सी चमक वाले तुम्हारे दोनों नेत्र हैं, जिसे उसने अपने दाहिने हाथ में थाम रखा है, और जिसका मध्य भाग उसकी मुट्ठी और कलाई से ढका होने के कारण ओझल है।

devanagari: अहः सूते सव्यं तव नयनमर्कात्मकतया / त्रियामां वामं ते सृजति रजनीनायकतया । / तृतीया ते दृष्टिर्दरदलितहेमाम्बुजरुचिः / समाधत्ते संध्यां दिवसनिशयोरन्तरचरीम् ॥48॥
iast: ahaḥ sūte savyaṃ tava nayanamarkātmakatayā / triyāmāṃ vāmaṃ te sṛjati rajanīnāyakatayā । / tṛtīyā te dṛṣṭirdaradalitahemāmbujaruciḥ / samādhatte saṃdhyāṃ divasaniśayorantaracarīm ॥48॥
sayIt: a-HAH SOO-tay SAV-yum TA-va NA-ya-nam ar-KAAT-ma-ka-ta-yaa / tri-YAA-maam VAA-mum tay SRI-ja-ti RA-ja-nee-NAA-ya-ka-ta-yaa / tri-TEE-yaa tay DRISH-tir DA-ra-DA-li-ta-hay-MAAM-boo-ja-ROO-chih / sa-MAA-dhat-tay SAN-dhyaam DI-va-sa-NI-sha-yor AN-ta-ra-cha-reem
translation: Your right eye, having the sun for its nature, gives birth to the day; your left, as the moon, sovereign of night, creates the night of three watches; and your third glance, glowing like a golden lotus just barely open, brings forth the twilight that moves between day and night.
source: Soundarya Lahari 48 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which hour of your day feels most like a threshold, and what would it mean to treat it as sacred?

translations.hi: तुम्हारा दाहिना नेत्र सूर्य-स्वरूप होकर दिन को जन्म देता है; बायाँ नेत्र रात्रि के स्वामी चन्द्रमा के रूप में तीन पहर की रात रचता है; और तुम्हारी तीसरी दृष्टि — अधखिले सुनहरे कमल की आभा वाली — उस सन्ध्या को जन्म देती है जो दिन और रात के बीच आती-जाती है।

devanagari: विशाला कल्याणी स्फुटरुचिरयोध्या कुवलयैः / कृपाधाराधारा किमपि मधुराभोगवतिका । / अवन्ती दृष्टिस्ते बहुनगरविस्तारविजया / ध्रुवं तत्तन्नामव्यवहरणयोग्या विजयते ॥49॥
iast: viśālā kalyāṇī sphuṭarucirayodhyā kuvalayaiḥ / kṛpādhārādhārā kimapi madhurābhogavatikā । / avantī dṛṣṭiste bahunagaravistāravijayā / dhruvaṃ tattannāmavyavaharaṇayogyā vijayate ॥49॥
sayIt: vi-SHAA-laa kal-YAA-nee SPHOO-ta-ROO-chir a-YODH-yaa KOO-va-la-yaih / kri-paa-DHAA-raa-DHAA-raa KIM-a-pi MA-dhoo-RAA-bho-ga-VA-ti-kaa / a-VAN-tee DRISH-tis-tay BA-hoo-NA-ga-ra-vis-TAA-ra-VI-ja-yaa / dhroo-VUM tat-tan-NAA-ma-vya-va-HA-ra-na-YOG-yaa VI-ja-ya-tay
translation: Your glance is wide (Vishala), auspicious (Kalyani), vivid in beauty and unconquerable by the blue lotuses (Ayodhya), the riverbed of streams of compassion (Dhara), sweet beyond telling (Madhura), rich in graceful fullness (Bhogavati), protecting (Avanti), victorious over the sweep of many cities (Vijaya) — surely it has earned every one of those names, and it reigns supreme.
source: Soundarya Lahari 49 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What are you traveling far to find that a moment of grace could hand you where you stand?

translations.hi: तुम्हारी दृष्टि विशाल है (विशाला), मंगलमयी है (कल्याणी), खिली आभा वाली और नील कमलों से अजेय है (अयोध्या), करुणा की धाराओं का आधार है (धारा), किसी अकथ ढंग से मधुर है (मधुरा), लीला-वैभव से भरी है (भोगवती), रक्षा करने वाली है (अवन्ती), अनेक नगरों के विस्तार पर विजयिनी है (विजया) — निश्चय ही वह इन सब नामों से पुकारे जाने योग्य है, और उसी की जय-जयकार है।

devanagari: कवीनां संदर्भस्तबकमकरन्दैकरसिकं / कटाक्षव्याक्षेपभ्रमरकलभौ कर्णयुगलम् । / अमुञ्चन्तौ दृष्ट्वा तव नवरसास्वादतरला / वसूयासंसर्गादलिकनयनं किंचिदरुणम् ॥50॥
iast: kavīnāṃ saṃdarbhastabakamakarandaikarasikaṃ / kaṭākṣavyākṣepabhramarakalabhau karṇayugalam । / amuñcantau dṛṣṭvā tava navarasāsvādataralā / vasūyāsaṃsargādalikanayanaṃ kiṃcidaruṇam ॥50॥
sayIt: ka-VEE-naam san-DAR-bha-STA-ba-ka-MA-ka-RAN-dai-ka-RA-si-kum / ka-TAAK-sha-VYAAK-shay-pa-BHRA-ma-ra-KA-la-bhau KAR-na-YOO-ga-lum / a-moon-CHAN-tau DRISHT-vaa TA-va NA-va-ra-SAAS-vaa-da-TA-ra-laa / va-SOO-yaa-sam-sar-GAAD A-li-ka-NA-ya-num KIN-chid a-ROO-num
translation: Seeing your two eyes — like two young bees flickering with sidelong glances, trembling with eagerness to taste the nine rasas — never leaving your two ears, which alone savour the honey of the clustered blossoms of the poets' compositions, your forehead-eye, touched by jealousy, has turned faintly red.
source: Soundarya Lahari 50 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When did you last make something beautiful purely as an offering, with no audience in mind but the divine?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे दोनों कान ही कवियों की रचनाओं के गुच्छों का मकरन्द चखते हैं; और तुम्हारे दोनों नेत्र — कटाक्षों की चंचल उड़ान वाले दो तरुण भौंरों जैसे, नौ रसों के आस्वाद के लिए आतुर — उन कानों का साथ छोड़ते ही नहीं। यह देखकर तुम्हारा ललाट-नेत्र ईर्ष्या के स्पर्श से हल्का लाल हो उठा है।

devanagari: शिवे शृङ्गारार्द्रा तदितरजने कुत्सनपरा / सरोषा गङ्गायां गिरिशचरिते विस्मयवती । / हराहिभ्यो भीता सरसिरुहसौभाग्यजननी / सखीषु स्मेरा ते मयि जननी दृष्टिः सकरुणा ॥51॥
iast: śive śṛṅgārārdrā taditarajane kutsanaparā / saroṣā gaṅgāyāṃ giriśacarite vismayavatī । / harāhibhyo bhītā sarasiruhasaubhāgyajananī / sakhīṣu smerā te mayi jananī dṛṣṭiḥ sakaruṇā ॥51॥
sayIt: shi-VAY shrin-gaa-RAAR-draa tad-I-ta-ra-JA-nay KOOT-sa-na-pa-raa / sa-RO-shaa gun-GAA-yaam GI-ri-sha-CHA-ri-tay VIS-ma-ya-va-tee / ha-RAA-hibh-yo BHEE-taa SA-ra-si-ROO-ha-sau-BHAAG-ya-JA-na-nee / sa-KHEE-shoo SMAY-raa tay MA-yi JA-na-nee DRISH-tih sa-ka-ROO-naa
translation: Toward Shiva, melting with love; toward everyone else, full of disdain; flashing anger at Ganga; wide with wonder at Girisha's deeds; frightened of Hara's serpents; mother of the lotus's own loveliness; smiling among your friends — and toward me, O Mother, your glance is full of compassion.
source: Soundarya Lahari 51 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: If you trusted that the divine gaze on you is compassion before anything else, what would you stop hiding?

translations.hi: शिव की ओर शृंगार से भीगी; अन्य किसी जन की ओर उपेक्षा-भरी; गंगा पर रोष से तमतमाई; गिरीश की लीलाओं पर विस्मित; हर के सर्पों से सहमी; कमल के सौभाग्य को जन्म देने वाली; सखियों में मुस्कुराती — और मुझ पर, हे जननी, तुम्हारी वही दृष्टि करुणा से छलकती है।

devanagari: गते कर्णाभ्यर्णं गरुत इव पक्ष्माणि दधती / पुरां भेत्तुश्चित्तप्रशमरसविद्रावणफले । / इमे नेत्रे गोत्राधरपतिकुलोत्तंसकलिके / तवाकर्णाकृष्टस्मरशरविलासं कलयतः ॥52॥
iast: gate karṇābhyarṇaṃ garuta iva pakṣmāṇi dadhatī / purāṃ bhettuścittapraśamarasavidrāvaṇaphale । / ime netre gotrādharapatikulottaṃsakalike / tavākarṇākṛṣṭasmaraśaravilāsaṃ kalayataḥ ॥52॥
sayIt: ga-TAY kar-NAABH-yar-num GA-roo-ta i-va PAKSH-maa-ni DA-dha-tee / poo-RAAM BHET-toosh CHIT-ta-pra-SHA-ma-RA-sa-vi-DRAA-va-na-pha-lay / i-MAY NAY-tray go-TRAA-dha-ra-PA-ti-koo-LOT-tam-sa-KA-li-kay / ta-VAA-kar-NAA-krish-ta-SMA-ra-SHA-ra-vi-LAA-sum KA-la-ya-tah
translation: O bud of the crest-garland of the mountain-king's house — these two eyes of yours, reaching to the very edge of your ears and wearing their lashes like an arrow's feathers, their one success the routing of the great city-breaker's hard-won calm, play out the grace of Kama's arrows drawn back to the ear.
source: Soundarya Lahari 52 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What settled calm of yours would you willingly let love disturb?

translations.hi: हे पर्वतराज के कुल-मुकुट की कली! तुम्हारे ये दोनों नेत्र — कानों की सीमा तक पहुँचे हुए, बरौनियों को बाण के पंखों की तरह धारण किए, जिनकी सफलता त्रिपुर-विध्वंसक शिव के चित्त की शान्ति को भगा देना है — कान तक खींचे गए कामदेव के बाणों की लीला रचते हैं।

devanagari: विभक्तत्रैवर्ण्यं व्यतिकरितलीलाञ्जनतया / विभाति त्वन्नेत्रत्रितयमिदमीशानदयिते । / पुनः स्रष्टुं देवान् द्रुहिणहरिरुद्रानुपरतान् / रजः सत्त्वं बिभ्रत्तम इति गुणानां त्रयमिव ॥53॥
iast: vibhaktatraivarṇyaṃ vyatikaritalīlāñjanatayā / vibhāti tvannetratritayamidamīśānadayite । / punaḥ sraṣṭuṃ devān druhiṇaharirudrānuparatān / rajaḥ sattvaṃ bibhrattama iti guṇānāṃ trayamiva ॥53॥
sayIt: vi-BHAK-ta-trai-VARN-yum VYA-ti-KA-ri-ta-LEE-laan-ja-na-ta-yaa / vi-BHAA-ti tvan-NAY-tra-TRI-ta-yam-i-dam ee-SHAA-na-DA-yi-tay / poo-NAH SRASH-toom day-VAAN DROO-hi-na-HA-ri-roo-DRAAN oo-pa-RA-taan / ra-JAH SAT-tvum BIBH-rat TA-ma i-ti goo-NAA-naam TRA-yam-i-va
translation: O beloved of Ishana — this triad of your eyes, its three colours made distinct by the playful touch of collyrium, shines as if bearing the three gunas — rajas, sattva and tamas — in order to create afresh the gods Druhina, Hari and Rudra when they have ceased at dissolution.
source: Soundarya Lahari 53 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which of the three energies — creating, sustaining, or letting dissolve — does this season of your life ask you to honor?

translations.hi: हे ईशान-प्रिये! काजल की लीला-भरी रेखा से जिनके तीन रंग अलग-अलग निखर आए हैं, तुम्हारे नेत्रों की यह त्रयी ऐसी शोभित होती है मानो रजस्, सत्त्व और तमस् — तीनों गुणों को धारण किए हो, ताकि प्रलय में विश्राम पा चुके ब्रह्मा, हरि और रुद्र को फिर से रच सके।

devanagari: पवित्रीकर्तुं नः पशुपतिपराधीनहृदये / दयामित्रैर्नेत्रैररुणधवलश्यामरुचिभिः । / नदः शोणो गङ्गा तपनतनयेति ध्रुवममुं / त्रयाणां तीर्थानामुपनयसि संभेदमनघम् ॥54॥
iast: pavitrīkartuṃ naḥ paśupatiparādhīnahṛdaye / dayāmitrairnetrairaruṇadhavalaśyāmarucibhiḥ । / nadaḥ śoṇo gaṅgā tapanatanayeti dhruvamamuṃ / trayāṇāṃ tīrthānāmupanayasi saṃbhedamanagham ॥54॥
sayIt: pa-vi-TREE-kar-toom nah PA-shoo-PA-ti-pa-RAA-dhee-na-HRI-da-yay / da-YAA-mi-trair NAY-trair a-ROO-na-DHA-va-la-SHYAA-ma-ROO-chi-bhih / na-DAH SHO-no GUN-gaa TA-pa-na-TA-na-YAY-ti DHROO-vam-a-moom / tra-YAA-naam teer-THAA-naam oo-pa-NA-ya-si sam-BHAY-dam a-NA-gham
translation: O you whose heart is given over wholly to Pashupati — with your eyes, friends of compassion, glowing red, white and dark, you surely bring near to us, to make us pure, this sinless meeting-place of three holy rivers: the red Shona, the white Ganga, and the dark Yamuna, daughter of the sun.
source: Soundarya Lahari 54 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where are you making grace a destination when it may already be traveling toward you?

translations.hi: हे पशुपति के प्रति पूर्ण समर्पित हृदय वाली! करुणा के मित्र अपने नेत्रों से — जिनमें अरुण, धवल और श्याम आभा घुली है — तुम निश्चय ही हमें पवित्र करने के लिए तीन तीर्थों का यह निष्पाप संगम हमारे पास ले आती हो: लाल शोण, श्वेत गंगा, और सूर्य-पुत्री साँवली यमुना।

devanagari: निमेषोन्मेषाभ्यां प्रलयमुदयं याति जगती / तवेत्याहुः सन्तो धरणिधरराजन्यतनये । / त्वदुन्मेषाज्जातं जगदिदमशेषं प्रलयतः / परित्रातुं शङ्के परिहृतनिमेषास्तव दृशः ॥55॥
iast: nimeṣonmeṣābhyāṃ pralayamudayaṃ yāti jagatī / tavetyāhuḥ santo dharaṇidhararājanyatanaye । / tvadunmeṣājjātaṃ jagadidamaśeṣaṃ pralayataḥ / paritrātuṃ śaṅke parihṛtanimeṣāstava dṛśaḥ ॥55॥
sayIt: ni-may-shon-MAY-shaabh-yaam PRA-la-yam-OO-da-yum YAA-ti JA-ga-tee / ta-VAYT-yaa-hooh SAN-to DHA-ra-ni-DHA-ra-RAA-jan-ya-TA-na-yay / tva-doon-may-SHAAJ JAA-tum JA-ga-di-dam-a-SHAY-shum PRA-la-ya-tah / pa-ri-TRAA-toom SHUN-kay PA-ri-HRI-ta-ni-MAY-shaas TA-va DRI-shah
translation: The wise say, O daughter of the king of mountains, that with the closing and the opening of your eyes the world goes to dissolution and rises again — and so I suspect it is to save this whole world, born of one opening of your eyes, from ever dissolving, that your eyes have given up blinking altogether.
source: Soundarya Lahari 55 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Who in your life is held steady simply because you refuse to look away?

translations.hi: हे पर्वतराज-पुत्री! सन्त कहते हैं कि तुम्हारी पलकों के मुँदने और खुलने से जगत का प्रलय और उदय होता है। तो मुझे लगता है — तुम्हारे एक ही उन्मेष से जन्मा यह सारा संसार कहीं लय न हो जाए, इसीलिए तुम्हारे नेत्रों ने पलक झपकना ही त्याग दिया है।

devanagari: तवापर्णे कर्णेजपनयनपैशुन्यचकिता / निलीयन्ते तोये नियतमनिमेषाः शफरिकाः । / इयं च श्रीर्बद्धच्छदपुटकवाटं कुवलयम् / जहाति प्रत्यूषे निशि च विघटय्य प्रविशति ॥56॥
iast: tavāparṇe karṇejapanayanapaiśunyacakitā / nilīyante toye niyatamanimeṣāḥ śapharikāḥ । / iyaṃ ca śrīrbaddhacchadapuṭakavāṭaṃ kuvalayam / jahāti pratyūṣe niśi ca vighaṭayya praviśati ॥56॥
sayIt: ta-VAA-par-nay kar-NAY-ja-pa-NA-ya-na-pai-SHOON-ya-CHA-ki-taa / ni-LEE-yan-tay TO-yay NI-ya-tam-a-ni-MAY-shaah SHA-pha-ri-kaah / i-YUM cha SHREER bad-dhach-CHHA-da-POO-ta-ka-VAA-tum KOO-va-la-yum / ja-HAA-ti prat-YOO-shay NI-shi cha vi-gha-TA-yya pra-VI-sha-ti
translation: O Aparna, the little fish surely hide deep in the water, unblinking, terrified that your eyes — those whisperers that reach right to your ears — will tell on them; and Beauty herself quits the blue lotus at dawn, when its petal-doors are bolted shut, and at night pries them open and moves back in.
source: Soundarya Lahari 56 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Is your goodness something you put on and take off with the hours, or a home you never leave?

translations.hi: हे अपर्णा! नन्ही मछलियाँ निश्चय ही पानी में बिना पलक झपकाए जा छिपती हैं — इस डर से कि कानों तक पहुँचे तुम्हारे नेत्र, कानाफूसी करने वाले, कहीं उनकी चुगली न कर दें; और शोभा (श्री) स्वयं भोर होते ही नील कमल को छोड़ देती है, जब उसकी पंखुड़ियों के किवाड़ बन्द हो जाते हैं, और रात में उन्हें खोलकर फिर भीतर बस जाती है।

devanagari: दृशा द्राघीयस्या दरदलितनीलोत्पलरुचा / दवीयांसं दीनं स्नपय कृपया मामपि शिवे । / अनेनायं धन्यो भवति न च ते हानिरियता / वने वा हर्म्ये वा समकरनिपातो हिमकरः ॥57॥
iast: dṛśā drāghīyasyā daradalitanīlotpalarucā / davīyāṃsaṃ dīnaṃ snapaya kṛpayā māmapi śive । / anenāyaṃ dhanyo bhavati na ca te hāniriyatā / vane vā harmye vā samakaranipāto himakaraḥ ॥57॥
sayIt: dri-SHAA draa-GHEE-yas-yaa DA-ra-DA-li-ta-NEE-lot-pa-la-ROO-chaa / da-VEE-yaam-sum DEE-num SNA-pa-ya KRI-pa-yaa MAAM a-pi shi-VAY / a-NAY-naa-yum DHAN-yo BHA-va-ti na cha tay HAA-nir i-ya-taa / va-NAY vaa HARM-yay vaa SA-ma-KA-ra-ni-PAA-to HI-ma-ka-rah
translation: With your glance — long, far-reaching, lustrous as a blue lotus just barely opened — bathe in compassion even me, O Shiva's own, distant and destitute though I am. You will make this man blessed, and it costs you nothing: the moon lets its light fall equally on the forest and on the palace.
source: Soundarya Lahari 57 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What kindness are you withholding that would cost you nothing to give?

translations.hi: अपनी उस दीर्घ, दूर तक पहुँचने वाली दृष्टि से — जो अधखिले नील कमल-सी आभा रखती है — हे शिवे, मुझ जैसे दूर पड़े दीन को भी कृपा से नहला दो। इससे यह जन धन्य हो जाएगा, और तुम्हारी कोई हानि नहीं: चन्द्रमा अपनी चाँदनी वन पर और महल पर एक समान बरसाता है।

devanagari: अरालं ते पालीयुगलमगराजन्यतनये / न केषामाधत्ते कुसुमशरकोदण्डकुतुकम् । / तिरश्चीनो यत्र श्रवणपथमुल्लङ्घ्य विलस / न्नपाङ्गव्यासङ्गो दिशति शरसंधानधिषणाम् ॥58॥
iast: arālaṃ te pālīyugalamagarājanyatanaye / na keṣāmādhatte kusumaśarakodaṇḍakutukam । / tiraścīno yatra śravaṇapathamullaṅghya vilasa / nnapāṅgavyāsaṅgo diśati śarasaṃdhānadhiṣaṇām ॥58॥
sayIt: a-RAA-lum tay PAA-lee-YOO-ga-lam A-ga-RAA-jan-ya-TA-na-yay / na KAY-shaam AA-dhat-tay KOO-soo-ma-SHA-ra-ko-DAN-da-KOO-too-kum / ti-rash-CHEE-no YA-tra SHRA-va-na-PA-tham-ool-LUNG-ghya VI-la-san / na-PAAN-ga-vyaa-SUN-go DI-sha-ti SHA-ra-san-DHAA-na-DHI-sha-naam
translation: O daughter of the king of mountains — that curving pair of ridge-lines between your eyes and ears: in whom does it not stir the fancy of the flower-arrowed god's bow? All the more when your sidelong glance, flashing across aslant and overshooting the pathway of the ear, gives the perfect impression of an arrow being set to the string.
source: Soundarya Lahari 58 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What beauty in your daily view have you stopped actually seeing?

translations.hi: हे पर्वतराज-कन्ये! आँख और कान के बीच की तुम्हारी वह मुड़ी हुई रेखाओं की जोड़ी किसके मन में पुष्पधन्वा कामदेव के धनुष की कल्पना नहीं जगाती? उस पर जब तुम्हारा कटाक्ष तिरछा चमकता हुआ कान के मार्ग को भी लाँघ जाता है, तो पूरा दृश्य ऐसा लगता है मानो प्रत्यञ्चा पर बाण चढ़ाया जा रहा हो।

devanagari: स्फुरद्गण्डाभोगप्रतिफलितताटङ्कयुगलं / चतुश्चक्रं मन्ये तव मुखमिदं मन्मथरथम् । / यमारुह्य द्रुह्यत्यवनिरथमर्केन्दुचरणं / महावीरो मारः प्रमथपतये सज्जितवते ॥59॥
iast: sphuradgaṇḍābhogapratiphalitatāṭaṅkayugalaṃ / catuścakraṃ manye tava mukhamidaṃ manmatharatham । / yamāruhya druhyatyavanirathamarkenducaraṇaṃ / mahāvīro māraḥ pramathapataye sajjitavate ॥59॥
sayIt: sphoo-rad-GUN-daa-BHO-ga-PRA-ti-pha-LI-ta-TAA-tun-ka-YOO-ga-lum / cha-toosh-CHAK-rum MAN-yay TA-va MOO-kha-mi-dum man-MA-tha-RA-thum / yam-aa-ROOH-ya DROOH-yat-ya-VA-ni-RA-tham ar-KEN-doo-CHA-ra-num / ma-haa-VEE-ro MAA-rah PRA-ma-tha-PA-ta-yay SAJ-ji-ta-VA-tay
translation: This face of yours, with the pair of ear-ornaments reflected in the broad gleam of your cheeks, I take to be the four-wheeled chariot of Manmatha; mounted on it, the great hero Mara dares make war on the Lord of the Pramathas, who had readied the earth as his chariot with the sun and moon for wheels.
source: Soundarya Lahari 59 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When has gentleness in your life proved stronger than force?

translations.hi: चमकते कपोलों के विस्तार में झलकते कुण्डलों की जोड़ी समेत तुम्हारा यह मुख मुझे कामदेव का चार पहियों वाला रथ लगता है; इसी पर चढ़कर वह महावीर "मार" उन प्रमथों के स्वामी शिव से भिड़ने चल पड़ता है, जिन्होंने पृथ्वी को रथ और सूर्य-चन्द्र को उसके पहिये बनाकर तैयारी की थी।

devanagari: सरस्वत्याः सूक्तीरमृतलहरीकौशलहरीः / पिबन्त्याः शर्वाणि श्रवणचुलुकाभ्यामविरलम् । / चमत्कारश्लाघाचलितशिरसः कुण्डलगणो / झणत्कारैस्तारैः प्रतिवचनमाचष्ट इव ते ॥60॥
iast: sarasvatyāḥ sūktīramṛtalaharīkauśalaharīḥ / pibantyāḥ śarvāṇi śravaṇaculukābhyāmaviralam । / camatkāraślāghācalitaśirasaḥ kuṇḍalagaṇo / jhaṇatkāraistāraiḥ prativacanamācaṣṭa iva te ॥60॥
sayIt: sa-ras-vat-YAAH SOOK-teer a-MRI-ta-LA-ha-ree-KAU-sha-la-HA-reeh / pi-BANT-yaah shar-VAA-ni SHRA-va-na-CHOO-loo-kaabh-yaam a-VI-ra-lam / cha-mat-KAA-ra-SHLAA-ghaa-CHA-li-ta-SHI-ra-sah KOON-da-la-GA-no / jha-nat-KAA-rais TAA-raih PRA-ti-VA-cha-nam AA-chash-ta i-va tay
translation: O Sharvani — as you drink in Sarasvati's eloquent sayings without pause, using your two ears for cupped palms — sayings that steal the charm of waves of nectar — your head sways in wondering praise, and the cluster of your earrings, with its clear high ringing, seems to be speaking your reply.
source: Soundarya Lahari 60 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When you listen today, can you give the speaker the kind of attention that itself feels like a reply?

translations.hi: हे शर्वाणि! अमृत-लहरियों की मिठास चुरा लेने वाली सरस्वती की सूक्तियों को तुम अपने दोनों कानों की अंजुलि बनाकर अनवरत पीती जाती हो; विस्मय-भरी सराहना में तुम्हारा सिर हिलता है, और तब तुम्हारे कुण्डलों का समूह अपनी खनकती झंकार से मानो तुम्हारी ओर से उत्तर कह देता है।

devanagari: असौ नासावंशस्तुहिनगिरिवंशध्वजपटि / त्वदीयो नेदीयः फलतु फलमस्माकमुचितम् । / वहन्नन्तर्मुक्ताः शिशिरतरनिश्वासगलितं / समृद्ध्या यत्तासां बहिरपि च मुक्तामणिधरः ॥61॥
iast: asau nāsāvaṃśastuhinagirivaṃśadhvajapaṭi / tvadīyo nedīyaḥ phalatu phalamasmākamucitam । / vahannantarmuktāḥ śiśirataraniśvāsagalitaṃ / samṛddhyā yattāsāṃ bahirapi ca muktāmaṇidharaḥ ॥61॥
sayIt: a-SAU NAA-saa-VUM-shas TOO-hi-na-GI-ri-VUM-sha-DHVA-ja-PA-ti / tva-DEE-yo nay-DEE-yah PHA-la-too PHA-lam as-MAA-kam OO-chi-tam / va-HAN-nan-tar MOOK-taah SHI-shi-ra-TA-ra-nish-VAA-sa-GA-li-tum / sam-RIDH-yaa yat-TAA-saam BA-hir a-pi cha MOOK-taa-MA-ni-dha-rah
translation: O banner of the dynasty of the snow mountain — may that bamboo-staff of your nose, standing so near, bear for us the fruit that is fitting. It carries pearls hidden within, and from the sheer abundance of those inside — one having slipped down with your cool out-breath — it wears a pearl-jewel outside as well.
source: Soundarya Lahari 61 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What in you is full enough that it could overflow for someone else today?

translations.hi: हे हिमगिरि-वंश की ध्वजा! तुम्हारी नासिका का यह बाँस, जो इतना निकट है, हमारे लिए उचित फल फले। वह भीतर मोती धारण करता है — और भीतर की उसी समृद्धि के छलकने से, शीतल श्वास के साथ ढुलककर आया एक मोती, वह बाहर भी पहने हुए है।

devanagari: प्रकृत्या रक्तायास्तव सुदति दन्तच्छदरुचेः / प्रवक्ष्ये सादृश्यं जनयतु फलं विद्रुमलता । / न बिम्बं तद्बिम्बप्रतिफलनरागादरुणितं / तुलामध्यारोढुं कथमिव विलज्जेत कलया ॥62॥
iast: prakṛtyā raktāyāstava sudati dantacchadaruceḥ / pravakṣye sādṛśyaṃ janayatu phalaṃ vidrumalatā । / na bimbaṃ tadbimbapratiphalanarāgādaruṇitaṃ / tulāmadhyāroḍhuṃ kathamiva vilajjeta kalayā ॥62॥
sayIt: pra-krit-YAA rak-TAA-yaas TA-va SOO-da-ti dan-tach-CHHA-da-roo-chayh / pra-VAK-shyay saa-DRISH-yum JA-na-ya-too PHA-lum vi-DROO-ma-la-taa / na BIM-bum tad-BIM-ba-PRA-ti-pha-LA-na-RAA-gaad a-ROO-ni-tum / too-LAAM adh-yaa-RO-dhoom KA-tham i-va vi-LAJ-jay-ta KA-la-yaa
translation: O lady of lovely teeth — for the glow of your lips, red by nature itself, I will venture to name a likeness: first let the coral vine bear fruit! As for the bimba fruit — its own red only borrowed, caught from the reflection of their image — how would it not be ashamed to climb onto the scale against even a sixteenth part of them?
source: Soundarya Lahari 62 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which borrowed glow in your life are you mistaking for the source?

translations.hi: हे सुन्दर दाँतों वाली! स्वभाव से ही लाल तुम्हारे अधरों की आभा की कोई उपमा कहूँ — तो पहले मूँगे की लता फल तो दे! रहा बिम्बफल — जिसकी अपनी लालिमा भी उधार की है, तुम्हारे अधरों के प्रतिबिम्ब से रँगी हुई — वह उनके सोलहवें अंश से भी तुलना के तराज़ू पर चढ़ते हुए भला क्यों न लजाएगा?

devanagari: स्मितज्योत्स्नाजालं तव वदनचन्द्रस्य पिबतां / चकोराणामासीदतिरसतया चञ्चुजडिमा । / अतस्ते शीतांशोरमृतलहरीमम्लरुचयः / पिबन्ति स्वच्छन्दं निशि निशि भृशं काञ्जिकधिया ॥63॥
iast: smitajyotsnājālaṃ tava vadanacandrasya pibatāṃ / cakorāṇāmāsīdatirasatayā cañcujaḍimā । / ataste śītāṃśoramṛtalaharīmamlarucayaḥ / pibanti svacchandaṃ niśi niśi bhṛśaṃ kāñjikadhiyā ॥63॥
sayIt: smi-ta-jyot-SNAA-jaa-lum TA-va va-da-na-CHAN-dras-ya pi-ba-TAAM / cha-ko-RAA-naam aa-SEED a-ti-ra-sa-ta-YAA chan-chu-JA-di-maa / a-TAS-tay shee-TAAM-shor am-ri-ta-la-ha-REEM am-la-ru-cha-yah / PI-ban-ti svach-CHHAN-dum NI-shi NI-shi BHRI-shum kaan-ji-ka-dhi-YAA
translation: The cakora birds drank the flood of moonlight that is the smile on your moon-face until their beaks went numb with too much sweetness; so now, craving something sour, night after night they eagerly drink the moon's own nectar-wave, taking it for sour rice-gruel.
source: Soundarya Lahari 63 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What has grown sweet enough in your life that older pleasures have quietly lost their taste?

translations.hi: आपके मुख-चन्द्र की मुस्कान रूपी चाँदनी को पीते-पीते चकोर पक्षियों की चोंच अति-मिठास से जड़ हो गई; इसलिए अब खटाई की चाह में वे रात-दर-रात चन्द्रमा की अमृत-धारा को काँजी समझकर जी भरकर पीते हैं।

devanagari: अविश्रान्तं पत्युर्गुणगणकथाम्रेडनजपा / जपापुष्पच्छाया तव जननि जिह्वा जयति सा । / यदग्रासीनायाः स्फटिकदृषदच्छच्छविमयी / सरस्वत्या मूर्तिः परिणमति माणिक्यवपुषा ॥64॥
iast: aviśrāntaṃ patyurguṇagaṇakathāmreḍanajapā / japāpuṣpacchāyā tava janani jihvā jayati sā । / yadagrāsīnāyāḥ sphaṭikadṛṣadacchacchavimayī / sarasvatyā mūrtiḥ pariṇamati māṇikyavapuṣā ॥64॥
sayIt: a-vish-RAAN-tum PAT-yur gu-na-ga-na-ka-thaam-RAY-da-na-ja-paa / ja-paa-push-pach-CHHAA-yaa TA-va JA-na-ni JIH-vaa JA-ya-ti saa / ya-dag-raa-SEE-naa-yaah spha-ti-ka-dri-shad-ach-chhach-chha-vi-ma-yee / sa-ras-vat-YAA MOOR-tih pa-ri-NA-ma-ti maa-NIK-ya-va-pu-shaa
translation: O Mother, glory to that tongue of yours, hibiscus-red, ceaselessly repeating like japa the tale of your Husband's virtues — so that the form of Sarasvati seated at its tip, once clear as crystal stone, turns into a body of ruby.
source: Soundarya Lahari 64 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What do you repeat so often that it has begun to colour everything else you say?

translations.hi: हे जननी, आपकी वह जिह्वा जयवन्त है जो अपने स्वामी के गुण-समूह की कथा को अनवरत जप की तरह दोहराती है और जपा-पुष्प (गुड़हल) जैसी लाल है — उसकी नोक पर विराजी स्फटिक-सी निर्मल सरस्वती की मूर्ति भी वहाँ माणिक्य-देह हो उठती है।

devanagari: रणे जित्वा दैत्यानपहृतशिरस्त्रैः कवचिभिर् / निवृत्तैश्चण्डांशत्रिपुरहरनिर्माल्यविमुखैः । / विशाखेन्द्रोपेन्द्रैः शशिविशदकर्पूरशकला / विलीयन्ते मातस्तव वदनताम्बूलकबलाः ॥65॥
iast: raṇe jitvā daityānapahṛtaśirastraiḥ kavacibhir / nivṛttaiścaṇḍāṃśatripuraharanirmālyavimukhaiḥ । / viśākhendropendraiḥ śaśiviśadakarpūraśakalā / vilīyante mātastava vadanatāmbūlakabalāḥ ॥65॥
sayIt: RA-nay JIT-vaa dait-YAAN a-pa-hri-ta-shi-RAS-traih ka-va-chi-bhir / ni-VRIT-taish chan-DAAM-sha-tri-pu-ra-ha-ra-nir-MAAL-ya-vi-mu-khaih / vi-shaa-khayn-DRO-payn-draih sha-shi-vi-sha-da-kar-POO-ra-sha-ka-laa / vi-LEE-yan-tay MAA-tas TA-va va-da-na-taam-BOO-la-ka-ba-laah
translation: O Mother, Vishakha, Indra and Upendra, back from conquering the demons in battle — helmets off though still in armour, and turning away from Shiva's offering-remnants, which are Chanda's share — melt in their mouths the morsels of betel from your own mouth, flecked with camphor white as the moon.
source: Soundarya Lahari 65 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where in your life does the freely shared thing mean more than the formally offered one?

translations.hi: हे माता, युद्ध में दैत्यों को जीतकर लौटे विशाख (कार्तिकेय), इन्द्र और उपेन्द्र (विष्णु) — शिरस्त्राण उतारे, पर कवच पहने ही — त्रिपुरहर शिव के निर्माल्य से मुँह फेर लेते हैं, क्योंकि वह चण्ड का भाग है; और आपके मुख का ताम्बूल, जिसमें चन्द्रमा-सा उजला कपूर मिला है, उनके मुँह में घुलता है।

devanagari: विपञ्च्या गायन्ती विविधमपदानं पशुपतेः / त्वयारब्धे वक्तुं चलितशिरसा साधुवचने । / तदीयैर्माधुर्यैरपलपिततन्त्रीकलरवां / निजां वीणां वाणी निचुलयति चोलेन निभृतम् ॥66॥
iast: vipañcyā gāyantī vividhamapadānaṃ paśupateḥ / tvayārabdhe vaktuṃ calitaśirasā sādhuvacane । / tadīyairmādhuryairapalapitatantrīkalaravāṃ / nijāṃ vīṇāṃ vāṇī niculayati colena nibhṛtam ॥66॥
sayIt: vi-panch-YAA gaa-YAN-tee vi-vi-dham a-pa-DAA-num pa-shu-pa-TAYH / tva-YAA-rab-dhay VAK-tum cha-li-ta-shi-ra-SAA saa-dhu-va-cha-nay / ta-DEE-yair maa-DHUR-yair a-pa-la-pi-ta-tan-TREE-ka-la-ra-vaam / ni-JAAM VEE-naam VAA-nee ni-chu-la-ya-ti CHO-lay-na ni-BHRI-tum
translation: When Sarasvati sings to her vina the many exploits of Pashupati and you begin, with a nod of your head, to say "well sung" — the sweetness of those words shames the soft cry of her strings, and she quietly slips her vina into its cloth cover.
source: Soundarya Lahari 66 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Whose ordinary words carry more music for you than any performance, and have you told them so?

translations.hi: जब सरस्वती अपनी वीणा पर पशुपति के अनेक पराक्रम गाती हैं और आप सिर हिलाकर 'साधु, साधु' कहना आरम्भ करती हैं — तो आपके शब्दों की मिठास के आगे वीणा के तारों की कोमल झंकार फीकी पड़ जाती है, और सरस्वती चुपचाप अपनी वीणा को उसके वस्त्र-कोश में सरका देती हैं।

devanagari: कराग्रेण स्पृष्टं तुहिनगिरिणा वत्सलतया / गिरीशेनोदस्तं मुहुरधरपानाकुलतया । / करग्राह्यं शम्भोर्मुखमुकुरवृन्तं गिरिसुते / कथङ्कारं ब्रूमस्तव चिबुकमौपम्यरहितम् ॥67॥
iast: karāgreṇa spṛṣṭaṃ tuhinagiriṇā vatsalatayā / girīśenodastaṃ muhuradharapānākulatayā । / karagrāhyaṃ śambhormukhamukuravṛntaṃ girisute / kathaṅkāraṃ brūmastava cibukamaupamyarahitam ॥67॥
sayIt: ka-RAAG-ray-na SPRISH-tum tu-hi-na-gi-ri-NAA vat-sa-la-ta-yaa / gi-REE-shay-NO-das-tum MU-hur a-dha-ra-PAA-naa-ku-la-ta-yaa / ka-ra-GRAAH-yum SHAM-bhor mu-kha-mu-ku-ra-VRIN-tum gi-ri-su-tay / ka-thang-KAA-rum BROO-mas TA-va chi-bu-kam ow-pam-ya-ra-hi-tum
translation: Touched by the Snow Mountain's fingertips in a father's tenderness, lifted again and again by Girisha in his eagerness for your lips, fit to rest in Shambhu's hand alone — the stem of the mirror that is your face: O daughter of the mountain, how can we describe your chin, which has no comparison at all?
source: Soundarya Lahari 67 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which touch of affection in your own story would you call beyond comparison?

translations.hi: हिम-पर्वत ने पिता के वात्सल्य से जिसे उँगलियों से छुआ, अधर-पान की उत्सुकता में गिरीश ने जिसे बार-बार ऊपर उठाया, जो केवल शम्भु के हाथ में समाने योग्य है — आपके मुख-दर्पण की वह डंडी: हे गिरिसुते, आपकी उस ठोड़ी का वर्णन हम किन शब्दों में करें, जिसकी कोई उपमा ही नहीं?

devanagari: भुजाश्लेषान्नित्यं पुरदमयितुः कण्टकवती / तव ग्रीवा धत्ते मुखकमलनालश्रियमियम् । / स्वतः श्वेता कालागुरुबहुलजम्बालमलिना / मृणालीलालित्यम् वहति यदधो हारलतिका ॥68॥
iast: bhujāśleṣānnityaṃ puradamayituḥ kaṇṭakavatī / tava grīvā dhatte mukhakamalanālaśriyamiyam । / svataḥ śvetā kālāgurubahulajambālamalinā / mṛṇālīlālityam vahati yadadho hāralatikā ॥68॥
sayIt: bhu-jaash-LAY-shaan NIT-yum pu-ra-da-ma-yi-TUH kan-ta-ka-va-tee / TA-va GREE-vaa DHAT-tay mu-kha-ka-ma-la-NAA-la-shri-yam i-yam / sva-TAH SHVAY-taa kaa-laa-gu-ru-ba-hu-la-jam-BAA-la-ma-li-naa / mri-naa-lee-LAA-lit-yum VA-ha-ti ya-da-DHO haa-ra-la-ti-kaa
translation: Your neck, thrilled evermore by the embrace of the arms of the Destroyer of the Cities, bears the beauty of a stalk to your lotus-face; and the vine of pearls below it, white by nature yet darkened by thick black-aloe paste, carries the loveliness of a mud-flecked lotus fibre.
source: Soundarya Lahari 68 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Can you look at one "smudge" on something you love today and see it as part of the beauty rather than a flaw?

translations.hi: त्रिपुर-विजयी शिव की भुजाओं के आलिंगन से सदा पुलकित आपकी ग्रीवा आपके मुख-कमल की नाल की शोभा धारण करती है; और उसके नीचे मोतियों की लड़ — स्वभाव से श्वेत, पर काले अगरु के गाढ़े लेप से साँवली — कीचड़-लगी कोमल मृणाल की छवि पाती है।

devanagari: गले रेखास्तिस्रो गतिगमकगीतैकनिपुणे / विवाहव्यानद्धप्रगुणगुणसंख्याप्रतिभुवः । / विराजन्ते नानाविधमधुररागाकरभुवां / त्रयाणां ग्रामाणां स्थितिनियमसीमान इव ते ॥69॥
iast: gale rekhāstisro gatigamakagītaikanipuṇe / vivāhavyānaddhapraguṇaguṇasaṃkhyāpratibhuvaḥ । / virājante nānāvidhamadhurarāgākarabhuvāṃ / trayāṇāṃ grāmāṇāṃ sthitiniyamasīmāna iva te ॥69॥
sayIt: GA-lay RAY-khaas TIS-ro ga-ti-ga-ma-ka-GEE-tai-ka-ni-pu-nay / vi-vaa-ha-vyaa-NAD-dha-pra-gu-na-gu-na-SANKH-yaa-pra-ti-bhu-vah / vi-RAA-jan-tay naa-naa-vi-dha-ma-dhu-ra-RAA-gaa-ka-ra-bhu-vaam / tra-YAA-naam graa-MAA-naam sthi-ti-ni-ya-ma-SEE-maa-na i-va tay
translation: O mistress of melody, ornament and song! The three lines on your neck, standing as tokens of the number of strands in the thread tied fast at your wedding, shine like the boundary-lines that fix the domains of the three musical scales — the mines from which all the many sweet ragas are born.
source: Soundarya Lahari 69 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What vow in your life has settled in so deeply that it now reads like music rather than obligation?

translations.hi: हे गति, गमक और गीत में अनुपम निपुणा! आपके कण्ठ की तीन रेखाएँ, विवाह में बँधे सुगठित सूत्र के लड़ों की संख्या की साक्षी बनकर, ऐसी सुशोभित हैं मानो तीन ग्रामों — मधुर रागों की खानों — की सीमाएँ निर्धारित करने वाली रेखाएँ हों।

devanagari: मृणालीमृद्वीनां तव भुजलतानां चतसृणां / चतुर्भिः सौन्दर्यं सरसिजभवः स्तौति वदनैः । / नखेभ्यः सन्त्रस्यन् प्रथममथनादन्धकरिपो / श्चतुर्णां शीर्षाणां सममभयहस्तार्पणधिया ॥70॥
iast: mṛṇālīmṛdvīnāṃ tava bhujalatānāṃ catasṛṇāṃ / caturbhiḥ saundaryaṃ sarasijabhavaḥ stauti vadanaiḥ । / nakhebhyaḥ santrasyan prathamamathanādandhakaripo / ścaturṇāṃ śīrṣāṇāṃ samamabhayahastārpaṇadhiyā ॥70॥
sayIt: mri-naa-lee-mrid-VEE-naam TA-va bhu-ja-la-TAA-naam cha-tas-ri-naam / cha-TUR-bhih soun-DAR-yum sa-ra-si-ja-bha-VAH STOW-ti va-da-naih / na-KHAY-bhyah san-TRAS-yan pra-tha-ma-ma-tha-NAAD an-dha-ka-ri-poh / scha-TUR-naam sheer-SHAA-naam SA-mam a-bha-ya-has-TAAR-pa-na-dhi-yaa
translation: Lotus-born Brahma, trembling before the nails of Shiva, foe of Andhaka, ever since one of his own heads was plucked away, praises with all four mouths the beauty of your four arms, tender as lotus-fibre — hoping that four protecting hands will be raised over his four heads at once.
source: Soundarya Lahari 70 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When fear does its arithmetic in you, whose protection do you actually reach for?

translations.hi: कमल से जन्मे ब्रह्मा — जब से अन्धक-शत्रु शिव ने उनका एक सिर नखों से उखाड़ा, तभी से उन नखों से सहमे हुए — अपने चारों मुखों से आपकी मृणाल-सी कोमल चार बाहु-लताओं के सौन्दर्य की स्तुति करते हैं, इस आशा में कि चारों सिरों के लिए एक साथ चार अभय-हस्त उठ जाएँ।

devanagari: नखानामुद्द्योतैर्नवनलिनरागं विहसतां / कराणां ते कान्तिं कथय कथयामः कथमुमे । / कयाचिद्वा साम्यं भजतु कलया हन्त कमलं / यदि क्रीडल्लक्ष्मीचरणतललाक्षारुणदलम् ॥71॥
iast: nakhānāmuddyotairnavanalinarāgaṃ vihasatāṃ / karāṇāṃ te kāntiṃ kathaya kathayāmaḥ kathamume । / kayācidvā sāmyaṃ bhajatu kalayā hanta kamalaṃ / yadi krīḍallakṣmīcaraṇatalalākṣāruṇadalam ॥71॥
sayIt: na-khaa-naam ud-DYO-tair na-va-na-li-na-RAA-gum vi-ha-sa-taam / ka-RAA-naam tay KAAN-tim KA-tha-ya ka-tha-YAA-mah KA-tham u-may / ka-yaa-CHID vaa SAAM-yum BHA-ja-tu ka-la-yaa HAN-ta ka-ma-lum / YA-di kree-dal-laksh-mee-cha-ra-na-ta-la-LAAK-shaa-ru-na-da-lam
translation: Tell us yourself, O Uma — how could we describe the radiance of your hands, whose flashing nails laugh at the blush of a fresh-blown lotus? Perhaps, alas, the lotus might approach some fraction of their likeness — but only if its petals were reddened by lac-dye from the soles of Lakshmi's feet as she plays upon it.
source: Soundarya Lahari 71 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where in your life would admitting "words fail me" be truer praise than any description?

translations.hi: हे उमा, आप ही बताइए — आपके हाथों की उस कान्ति का वर्णन हम कैसे करें, जिनके नखों की चमक ताज़े खिले कमल की ललाई की हँसी उड़ाती है? हाय, कमल शायद उनकी किसी एक कला की बराबरी कर भी ले — पर तभी, जब उस पर क्रीड़ा करती लक्ष्मी के तलवों का महावर उसकी पंखुड़ियों को रँग दे।

devanagari: समं देवि स्कन्दद्विपवदनपीतं स्तनयुगं / तवेदं नः खेदं हरतु सततं प्रस्नुतमुखम् । / यदालोक्याशङ्काकुलितहृदयो हासजनकः / स्वकुम्भौ हेरम्बः परिमृशति हस्तेन झडिति ॥72॥
iast: samaṃ devi skandadvipavadanapītaṃ stanayugaṃ / tavedaṃ naḥ khedaṃ haratu satataṃ prasnutamukham । / yadālokyāśaṅkākulitahṛdayo hāsajanakaḥ / svakumbhau herambaḥ parimṛśati hastena jhaḍiti ॥72॥
sayIt: SA-mum DAY-vi skan-da-dvi-pa-va-da-na-PEE-tum sta-na-yu-gum / ta-VAY-dum nah KHAY-dum HA-ra-tu sa-ta-tum pras-nu-ta-mu-kham / ya-daa-lok-yaa-shang-kaa-ku-li-ta-HRI-da-yo haa-sa-ja-na-kah / sva-KUM-bhow hay-RAM-bah pa-ri-mri-sha-ti HAS-tay-na JHA-di-ti
translation: O Devi, may this breast-pair of yours, from which Skanda and the elephant-faced one drank alike, its tips ever streaming with milk, take away our sorrow — beholding it, little Heramba, his heart flustered with doubt, pats his own frontal globes in haste, and laughter breaks out.
source: Soundarya Lahari 72 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When sorrow visits you, which memory of being cared for still has the power to lighten it?

translations.hi: हे देवी, आपका यह स्तन-युग्म, जिससे स्कन्द और गजमुख (गणेश) ने एक समान दूध पिया और जिसके मुख से सदा दूध झरता है, हमारा दुःख हर ले — जिसे देखकर नन्हे हेरम्ब का हृदय सन्देह से घबरा उठता है और वे झट अपने ही मस्तक के दोनों कुम्भ टटोलने लगते हैं, और हँसी छूट जाती है।

devanagari: अमू ते वक्षोजावमृतरसमाणिक्यकुतुपौ / न संदेहस्पन्दो नगपतिपताके मनसि नः । / पिबन्तौ तौ यस्मादविदितवधूसङ्गरसिकौ / कुमारावद्यापि द्विरदवदनक्रौञ्चदलनौ ॥73॥
iast: amū te vakṣojāvamṛtarasamāṇikyakutupau / na saṃdehaspando nagapatipatāke manasi naḥ । / pibantau tau yasmādaviditavadhūsaṅgarasikau / kumārāvadyāpi dviradavadanakrauñcadalanau ॥73॥
sayIt: a-MOO tay vak-sho-JAAV am-ri-ta-ra-sa-maa-NIK-ya-ku-tu-pow / na san-DAY-ha-span-do na-ga-pa-ti-pa-TAA-kay MA-na-si nah / pi-BAN-tow tow yas-MAAD a-vi-di-ta-va-DHOO-sang-ga-ra-si-kow / ku-maa-RAA-vad-YAA-pi dvi-ra-da-va-da-na-KROWN-cha-da-la-now
translation: These breasts of yours, O banner of the mountain-king's house, are ruby flasks filled with the essence of nectar — of that our mind holds not one tremor of doubt; for having drunk from them, Ganesha of the elephant face and Skanda, splitter of Mount Krauncha, remain boys to this day, strangers to the pleasure of a bride's company.
source: Soundarya Lahari 73 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What has been fed to you — a teaching, a love, a habit — that keeps some part of you permanently young?

translations.hi: हे पर्वतराज-वंश की पताका! आपके ये स्तन अमृत-रस से भरे माणिक्य के कलश हैं — इसमें हमारे मन में सन्देह की एक कँपकँपी तक नहीं; क्योंकि इन्हें पीकर गजमुख गणेश और क्रौञ्च-भेदी कुमार आज भी बालक ही हैं — वधू-संग के सुख से अनजान।

devanagari: वहत्यम्ब स्तम्बेरमदनुजकुम्भप्रकृतिभिः / समारब्धां मुक्तामणिभिरमलां हारलतिकाम् । / कुचाभोगो बिम्बाधररुचिभिरन्तः शबलितां / प्रतापव्यामिश्रां पुरदमयितुः कीर्तिमिव ते ॥74॥
iast: vahatyamba stamberamadanujakumbhaprakṛtibhiḥ / samārabdhāṃ muktāmaṇibhiramalāṃ hāralatikām । / kucābhogo bimbādhararucibhirantaḥ śabalitāṃ / pratāpavyāmiśrāṃ puradamayituḥ kīrtimiva te ॥74॥
sayIt: va-hat-YAM-ba stam-BAY-ra-ma-da-nu-ja-KUM-bha-pra-kri-ti-bhih / sa-maa-RAB-dhaam muk-TAA-ma-ni-bhir a-ma-LAAM haa-ra-la-ti-kaam / ku-CHAA-bho-go bim-BAA-dha-ra-ru-chi-bhir AN-tah sha-ba-li-taam / pra-TAA-pa-vyaa-MISH-raam pu-ra-da-ma-yi-TUH KEER-tim i-va tay
translation: O Mother, the expanse of your bosom wears a flawless vine of pearls harvested from the frontal globes of the elephant demon, its whiteness dappled from within by the glow of your bimba-red lips — as though it wore the fame of the Destroyer of the Cities, shot through with his valour.
source: Soundarya Lahari 74 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Whose glory do you carry close to your heart, and what colour does it take from you?

translations.hi: हे अम्ब, आपका वक्ष-विस्तार गज-दैत्य के कुम्भस्थल से निकले मोतियों की निर्मल लड़ धारण करता है, जिसकी धवलता आपके बिम्ब-फल-से लाल अधरों की आभा से भीतर-ही-भीतर रँग उठी है — मानो वह त्रिपुरहर शिव की कीर्ति हो, जिसमें उनका प्रताप घुला हुआ है।

devanagari: तव स्तन्यं मन्ये धरणिधरकन्ये हृदयतः / पयःपारावारः परिवहति सारस्वतमिव । / दयावत्या दत्तं द्रविडशिशुरास्वाद्य तव यत् / कवीनां प्रौढानामजनि कमनीयः कवयिता ॥75॥
iast: tava stanyaṃ manye dharaṇidharakanye hṛdayataḥ / payaḥpārāvāraḥ parivahati sārasvatamiva । / dayāvatyā dattaṃ draviḍaśiśurāsvādya tava yat / kavīnāṃ prauḍhānāmajani kamanīyaḥ kavayitā ॥75॥
sayIt: TA-va STAN-yum MAN-yay dha-ra-ni-dha-ra-KAN-yay hri-da-ya-tah / pa-yah-paa-raa-VAA-rah pa-ri-VA-ha-ti saa-ras-va-tam i-va / da-yaa-vat-YAA DAT-tum dra-vi-da-shi-shu-RAAS-vaad-ya TA-va yat / ka-VEE-naam prow-DHAA-naam A-ja-ni ka-ma-NEE-yah ka-va-yi-taa
translation: O daughter of the earth-bearing mountain, I hold that your breast-milk is an ocean of milk flowing from your very heart as eloquence itself; for the child of the Dravida land, tasting it as the gift of your compassion, arose as the beloved poet among the master-poets.
source: Soundarya Lahari 75 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which gift flows through you so naturally that you forget it was once fed to you by someone's kindness?

translations.hi: हे धरणीधर पर्वत की पुत्री! मैं मानता हूँ कि आपका स्तन्य आपके हृदय से उमड़ता दूध का सागर है — मानो साक्षात् सारस्वत-रस, वाणी का अमृत; क्योंकि आपकी दया से दिया गया वह दूध चखकर द्रविड़-शिशु प्रौढ़ कवियों के बीच मनोहर कवि होकर उभरा।

devanagari: हरक्रोधज्वालावलिभिरवलीढेन वपुषा / गभीरे ते नाभीसरसि कृतसङ्गो मनसिजः । / समुत्तस्थौ तस्मादचलतनये धूमलतिका / जनस्तां जानीते तव जननि रोमावलिरिति ॥76॥
iast: harakrodhajvālāvalibhiravalīḍhena vapuṣā / gabhīre te nābhīsarasi kṛtasaṅgo manasijaḥ । / samuttasthau tasmādacalatanaye dhūmalatikā / janastāṃ jānīte tava janani romāvaliriti ॥76॥
sayIt: ha-ra-KRO-dha-jvaa-LAA-va-li-bhir a-va-LEE-dhay-na va-pu-shaa / ga-BHEE-ray tay naa-BHEE-sa-ra-si kri-ta-SANG-go ma-na-si-jah / sa-mut-TAS-thow tas-MAAD a-cha-la-ta-na-yay DHOO-ma-la-ti-kaa / ja-nas-TAAM jaa-NEE-tay TA-va JA-na-ni ro-MAA-va-li-ri-ti
translation: O daughter of the unmoving mountain, the mind-born Kama, his body licked over by the rows of flames of Hara's wrath, plunged for refuge into the deep lake of your navel; the creeper of smoke that rose from it, O Mother, is what people know as the slender line of down above your waist.
source: Soundarya Lahari 76 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When something in you has been burned, where do you go to be received rather than judged?

translations.hi: हे अचल-तनया! मन से जन्मे कामदेव, जिनका शरीर हर के क्रोध की लपटों की कतारों से झुलस चुका था, आपकी नाभि के गहरे सरोवर में जा छिपे; उससे जो धुएँ की लता उठी — हे जननी, लोग उसी को आपकी रोमावलि, कमर के ऊपर की वह महीन रेखा, समझते हैं।

devanagari: यदेतत् कालिन्दीतनुतरतरङ्गाकृति शिवे / कृशे मध्ये किंचिज्जननि तव यद्भाति सुधियाम् । / विमर्दादन्योऽन्यं कुचकलशयोरन्तरगतं / तनूभूतं व्योम प्रविशदिव नाभिं कुहरिणीम् ॥77॥
iast: yadetat kālindītanutarataraṅgākṛti śive / kṛśe madhye kiṃcijjanani tava yadbhāti sudhiyām । / vimardādanyo'nyaṃ kucakalaśayorantaragataṃ / tanūbhūtaṃ vyoma praviśadiva nābhiṃ kuhariṇīm ॥77॥
sayIt: ya-DAY-tat kaa-lin-dee-ta-nu-ta-ra-ta-rang-GAA-kri-ti shi-vay / kri-SHAY MADH-yay kin-chij-JA-na-ni TA-va yad BHAA-ti su-dhi-yaam / vi-mar-DAAD an-YON-yum ku-cha-ka-la-sha-yor AN-ta-ra-ga-tum / ta-noo-BHOO-tum VYO-ma pra-vi-shad I-va NAA-bhim ku-ha-ri-neem
translation: O gracious consort of Shiva, O Mother — that slender something on your slim waist, shaped like the Kalindi's thinnest ripple, which gleams for the discerning: it is as if the sky itself, squeezed between your pitcher-like breasts, had grown thin and were slipping down into the hollow of your navel.
source: Soundarya Lahari 77 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What in your daily view might reveal something vast if you looked at it with a more discerning eye?

translations.hi: हे शिवे, हे जननी — आपकी क्षीण कटि पर वह जो कुछ महीन-सा झिलमिलाता है, यमुना की सबसे पतली लहर जैसा, जिसे सुधी जन ही देख पाते हैं: मानो आकाश ही आपके कलश-से उरोजों के परस्पर दबाव में पतला होकर आपकी गहरी नाभि में उतर रहा हो।

devanagari: स्थिरो गङ्गावर्तः स्तनमुकुलरोमावलिलता / कलावालं कुण्डं कुसुमशरतेजोहुतभुजः । / रतेर्लीलागारं किमपि तव नाभिर्गिरिसुते / बिलद्वारं सिद्धेर्गिरिशनयनानां विजयते ॥78॥
iast: sthiro gaṅgāvartaḥ stanamukularomāvalilatā / kalāvālaṃ kuṇḍaṃ kusumaśaratejohutabhujaḥ । / raterlīlāgāraṃ kimapi tava nābhirgirisute / biladvāraṃ siddhergiriśanayanānāṃ vijayate ॥78॥
sayIt: sthi-RO gang-GAA-var-tah sta-na-mu-ku-la-ro-MAA-va-li-la-taa / ka-laa-VAA-lum KUN-dum ku-su-ma-sha-ra-TAY-jo-hu-ta-bhu-jah / ra-tayr-LEE-laa-GAA-rum kim A-pi TA-va NAA-bhir gi-ri-su-tay / bi-la-DVAA-rum sid-DHAYR gi-ri-sha-na-ya-NAA-naam vi-JA-ya-tay
translation: O daughter of the mountain, your navel is a something beyond words — a stilled eddy of the Ganga; the basin that waters the creeper of your hair-line, whose buds are your breasts; the fire-pit for the flame of the flower-arrowed god's splendour; the pleasure-bower of Rati; the mouth of the cave where the eyes of Girisha attain their fulfilment. It reigns victorious.
source: Soundarya Lahari 78 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What depth in someone you love have you only ever been able to call "a something beyond words"?

translations.hi: हे गिरिसुते, आपकी नाभि शब्दों से परे की कोई वस्तु है — गंगा की थमी हुई भँवर; उस रोमावलि-लता का थाला जिसकी कलियाँ आपके उरोज हैं; पुष्पधन्वा कामदेव के तेज की अग्नि का हवन-कुण्ड; रति का क्रीड़ा-भवन; और वह गुफा-द्वार जहाँ गिरीश के नेत्रों की साधना सिद्ध होती है। उसकी जय हो।

devanagari: निसर्गक्षीणस्य स्तनतटभरेण क्लमजुषो / नमन्मूर्तेर्नारीतिलक शनकैस्त्रुट्यत इव । / चिरं ते मध्यस्य त्रुटिततटिनीतीरतरुणा / समावस्थास्थेम्नो भवतु कुशलं शैलतनये ॥79॥
iast: nisargakṣīṇasya stanataṭabhareṇa klamajuṣo / namanmūrternārītilaka śanakaistruṭyata iva । / ciraṃ te madhyasya truṭitataṭinītīrataruṇā / samāvasthāsthemno bhavatu kuśalaṃ śailatanaye ॥79॥
sayIt: ni-sar-ga-KSHEE-nas-ya sta-na-ta-ta-bha-RAY-na kla-ma-ju-sho / na-man-MOOR-tayr NAA-ree-ti-la-ka sha-na-kais-TRUT-ya-ta i-va / chi-RUM tay MADH-yas-ya tru-ti-ta-ta-ti-nee-TEE-ra-ta-ru-naa / sa-MAA-vas-thaa-STHAYM-no BHA-va-tu ku-sha-lum shai-la-ta-na-yay
translation: Slender by nature, wearied by the weight it bears above, its form bowing until it seems slowly on the point of giving way — O crest-jewel among women, daughter of the mountain, may your waist, poised like a tree on a river-bank the current has torn, be safe and well for ever.
source: Soundarya Lahari 79 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Who in your life is strong enough not to need your worry, and might still be touched to receive your blessing?

translations.hi: स्वभाव से क्षीण, ऊपर के भार से थकी, झुकती हुई ऐसी कि लगे धीरे-धीरे अब टूटी — हे नारी-तिलक, हे शैल-तनये! नदी की धार से कटे किनारे पर खड़े वृक्ष-सी अधर में थमी आपकी वह कटि सदा कुशल से रहे।

devanagari: कुचौ सद्यःस्विद्यत्तटघटितकूर्पासभिदुरौ / कषन्तौ दोर्मूले कनककलशाभौ कलयता । / तव त्रातुं भङ्गादलमिति वलग्नं तनुभुवा / त्रिधा नद्धं देवि त्रिवलि लवलीवल्लिभिरिव ॥80॥
iast: kucau sadyaḥsvidyattaṭaghaṭitakūrpāsabhidurau / kaṣantau dormūle kanakakalaśābhau kalayatā । / tava trātuṃ bhaṅgādalamiti valagnaṃ tanubhuvā / tridhā naddhaṃ devi trivali lavalīvallibhiriva ॥80॥
sayIt: ku-CHOW sad-yah-svid-yat-ta-ta-gha-ti-ta-KOOR-paa-sa-bhi-du-row / ka-SHAN-tow dor-MOO-lay ka-na-ka-ka-la-SHAA-bhow ka-la-ya-taa / TA-va TRAA-tum bhang-GAAD a-lam i-ti va-LAG-num ta-nu-bhu-vaa / tri-DHAA NAD-dhum DAY-vi TRI-va-li la-va-lee-VAL-li-bhir i-va
translation: Seeing your breasts gleam like golden pots — their slopes freshly moist, straining the fitted bodice to bursting, chafing at the very joins of your arms — the mind-born god, thinking "this waist must be saved from breaking," bound it three times about, O Devi, with the three folds, as if with cords of lavali vine.
source: Soundarya Lahari 80 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What fragile and beautiful thing in your care deserves a protective binding rather than mere admiration?

translations.hi: आपके स्वर्ण-कलश-से दमकते उरोज — जिनके तट अभी-अभी स्वेद से भीगे हैं, जो कसी हुई कंचुकी को तोड़े देते हैं और बाँहों के मूल तक को कसते हैं — उन्हें देखकर मन से जन्मे कामदेव ने सोचा, 'इस कटि को टूटने से बचाना ही होगा,' और हे देवी, उसे त्रिवली की तीन रेखाओं से ऐसे तीन बार बाँध दिया मानो लवली-लता की डोरियों से।

devanagari: गुरुत्वं विस्तारं क्षितिधरपतिः पार्वति निजा / न्नितम्बादाच्छिद्य त्वयि हरणरूपेण निदधे । / अतस्ते विस्तीर्णो गुरुरयमशेषां वसुमतीं / नितम्बप्राग्भारः स्थगयति लघुत्वं नयति च ॥81॥
iast: gurutvaṃ vistāraṃ kṣitidharapatiḥ pārvati nijā / nnitambādācchidya tvayi haraṇarūpeṇa nidadhe । / ataste vistīrṇo gururayamaśeṣāṃ vasumatīṃ / nitambaprāgbhāraḥ sthagayati laghutvaṃ nayati ca ॥81॥
sayIt: gu-RUT-vum vis-TAA-rum kshi-ti-dha-ra-pa-TIH PAAR-va-ti ni-jaan / ni-tam-BAAD aach-CHHID-ya tva-yi ha-ra-na-ROO-pay-na ni-da-dhay / a-TAS-tay vis-TEER-no gu-rur A-yam a-SHAY-shaam va-su-ma-teem / ni-tam-ba-PRAAG-bhaa-rah stha-GA-ya-ti la-ghut-vum NA-ya-ti cha
translation: O Parvati, the lord of mountains cut heaviness and breadth from his own flanks and settled them upon you as a wedding-gift; that is why this hip-expanse of yours, broad and weighty, eclipses the whole rich earth and makes her light in the scales.
source: Soundarya Lahari 81 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Which steadiness in you is an inheritance, and have you thanked the one it came from?

translations.hi: हे पार्वती! पर्वतों के राजा ने अपने ही नितम्ब — अपने पहाड़ी ढलानों — से भारीपन और विस्तार काटकर विवाह के उपहार-रूप में आप पर धर दिया; इसीलिए आपका यह विशाल, गुरु नितम्ब-भार समूची वसुन्धरा को ढक लेता है और तराज़ू में उसे हल्का कर देता है।

devanagari: करीन्द्राणां शुण्डान् कनककदलीकाण्डपटली / मुभाभ्यामूरुभ्यामुभयमपि निर्जित्य भवती । / सुवृत्ताभ्यां पत्युः प्रणतिकठिनाभ्यां गिरिसुते / विजिग्ये जानुभ्यां विबुधकरिकुम्भद्वयमसि ॥82॥
iast: karīndrāṇāṃ śuṇḍān kanakakadalīkāṇḍapaṭalī / mubhābhyāmūrubhyāmubhayamapi nirjitya bhavatī । / suvṛttābhyāṃ patyuḥ praṇatikaṭhinābhyāṃ girisute / vijigye jānubhyāṃ vibudhakarikumbhadvayamasi ॥82॥
sayIt: ka-REEN-draa-naam SHUN-daan ka-na-ka-ka-da-lee-KAAN-da-pa-ta-leem / u-BHAA-bhyaam oo-RU-bhyaam u-bha-yam a-pi nir-JIT-ya bha-va-tee / su-VRIT-taa-bhyaam PAT-yuh pra-na-ti-ka-thi-NAA-bhyaam gi-ri-su-tay / vi-JIG-yay JAA-nu-bhyaam vi-bu-dha-ka-ri-KUM-bha-dva-ya-ma-si
translation: With your two thighs, lady, you defeat at once the trunks of lordly elephants and clusters of golden banana-stems; and with your two knees, perfectly rounded, hardened by bowing to your Lord, O daughter of the mountain, you conquer even the pair of frontal globes of the celestial elephant.
source: Soundarya Lahari 82 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What mark has your own daily devotion — to a person, a practice, a duty — left on you, and do you wear it with pride?

translations.hi: हे गिरिसुते! अपनी दोनों जंघाओं से आप गजराजों की सूँड़ों और सुनहरे केले के तनों के झुरमुट — दोनों को एक साथ जीत लेती हैं; और अपने सुडौल घुटनों से — जो अपने स्वामी को बार-बार प्रणाम करने से कठोर हो गए हैं — देवराज के ऐरावत हाथी के दोनों कुम्भस्थलों पर भी विजय पा लेती हैं।

devanagari: पराजेतुं रुद्रं द्विगुणशरगर्भौ गिरिसुते / निषङ्गौ जङ्घे ते विषमविशिखो बाढमकृत । / यदग्रे दृश्यन्ते दशशरफलाः पादयुगली / नखाग्रच्छद्मानः सुरमकुटशाणैकनिशिताः ॥83॥
iast: parājetuṃ rudraṃ dviguṇaśaragarbhau girisute / niṣaṅgau jaṅghe te viṣamaviśikho bāḍhamakṛta । / yadagre dṛśyante daśaśaraphalāḥ pādayugalī / nakhāgracchadmānaḥ suramakuṭaśāṇaikaniśitāḥ ॥83॥
sayIt: pa-raa-JAY-toom ROOD-rum dvi-goo-na-sha-ra-GAR-bhau gi-ri-soo-TAY / ni-SHUN-gau JUNG-ghay tay vi-sha-ma-vi-SHI-kho BAA-dham a-KRI-ta / yad-AG-ray DRISH-yan-tay da-sha-sha-ra-pha-LAAH paa-da-yoo-ga-LEE / na-khaag-rach-CHAD-maa-nah soo-ra-ma-koo-ta-SHAA-nai-ka-ni-shi-TAAH
translation: O daughter of the mountain, to conquer Rudra the god of the odd number of arrows surely made your two shanks his quivers, each holding double his five — for at their tips gleam ten arrowheads in the disguise of your toenails, whetted on a single grindstone: the crowns of the bowing gods.
source: Soundarya Lahari 83 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where in your life does the daily act of bowing — showing up in reverence — quietly sharpen the very strength you depend on?

translations.hi: हे गिरिसुते, रुद्र को जीतने के लिए विषम (पाँच) बाणों वाले कामदेव ने तुम्हारी दोनों पिंडलियों को सचमुच अपने तरकश बना लिया, जिनमें उसके बाणों से दुगुने बाण समाएँ — तभी तो उनके सिरों पर दस बाण-फल झलकते हैं: तुम्हारे नखों के वेश में, झुके हुए देवताओं के मुकुटों की एक ही सान पर तीखे किए हुए।

devanagari: श्रुतीनां मूर्धानो दधति तव यौ शेखरतया / ममाप्येतौ मातः शिरसि दयया धेहि चरणौ । / ययोः पाद्यं पाथः पशुपतिजटाजूटतटिनी / ययोर्लाक्षालक्ष्मीररुणहरिचूडामणिरुचिः ॥84॥
iast: śrutīnāṃ mūrdhāno dadhati tava yau śekharatayā / mamāpyetau mātaḥ śirasi dayayā dhehi caraṇau । / yayoḥ pādyaṃ pāthaḥ paśupatijaṭājūṭataṭinī / yayorlākṣālakṣmīraruṇaharicūḍāmaṇiruciḥ ॥84॥
sayIt: shroo-tee-NAAM moor-DHAA-no DA-dha-ti TA-va yau shay-kha-ra-ta-YAA / ma-MAAP-yay-tau MAA-tah shi-RA-si da-ya-YAA DHAY-hi cha-ra-NAU / ya-YOH PAAD-yum PAA-thah pa-shoo-pa-ti-ja-taa-JOO-ta-ta-ti-NEE / ya-yor-laak-shaa-lak-SHMEE-ra-roo-na-ha-ri-choo-daa-MA-ni-roo-chih
translation: The crowns of the Vedas wear your two feet as their crest, Mother — in your mercy set those same feet on my head too: feet whose bathing-water is the river coiled in Pashupati's matted hair, and the red of whose lac-dye is the glow of the ruby crest-jewel on bowing Hari's head.
source: Soundarya Lahari 84 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: What would change about your day if you began it by asking for grace to rest on your head, rather than another achievement to rest on your name?

translations.hi: श्रुतियों के मस्तक — उपनिषदें — तुम्हारे जिन चरणों को अपना मुकुट बनाकर धारण करते हैं, हे माँ, दया करके वे ही चरण मेरे सिर पर भी रख दो: वे चरण जिनका पाद्य-जल पशुपति की जटाओं में बँधी नदी (गंगा) है, और जिनके महावर की लाली झुके हुए हरि की चूड़ामणि की अरुण आभा है।

devanagari: नमोवाकं ब्रूमो नयनरमणीयाय पदयो / स्तवास्मै द्वन्द्वाय स्फुटरुचिरसालक्तकवते । / असूयत्यत्यन्तं यदभिहननाय स्पृहयते / पशूनामीशानः प्रमदवनकङ्केलितरवे ॥85॥
iast: namovākaṃ brūmo nayanaramaṇīyāya padayo / stavāsmai dvandvāya sphuṭarucirasālaktakavate । / asūyatyatyantaṃ yadabhihananāya spṛhayate / paśūnāmīśānaḥ pramadavanakaṅkelitarave ॥85॥
sayIt: na-mo-VAA-kum BROO-mo na-ya-na-ra-ma-NEE-yaa-ya pa-da-YOH / sta-VAAS-mai dvan-DVAA-ya sphoo-ta-roo-chi-ra-saa-lak-ta-ka-va-TAY / a-soo-yat-yat-YUN-tum yad-a-bhi-ha-na-NAA-ya spri-ha-ya-TAY / pa-shoo-NAA-mee-SHAA-nah pra-ma-da-va-na-kun-KAY-li-ta-ra-vay
translation: We speak our word of homage to this pair of your feet, ravishing to the eyes, bright with fresh lac-dye — feet for whose kick the ashoka tree of the pleasure-garden openly longs, and of which longing the Lord of all creatures is deeply, helplessly jealous.
source: Soundarya Lahari 85 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Is there a love in your life that you express only through wit and sideways gestures, which deserves one plain, spoken word of homage today?

translations.hi: आँखों को रमणीय, चटकीले महावर से दमकते तुम्हारे इस चरण-युगल को हम प्रणाम का वचन कहते हैं — वे चरण, जिनकी ठोकर के लिए प्रमद-वन का अशोक (कंकेलि) वृक्ष तरसता है, और उस वृक्ष से पशुपति — समस्त प्राणियों के स्वामी — गहरी ईर्ष्या करते हैं।

devanagari: मृषा कृत्वा गोत्रस्खलनमथ वैलक्ष्यनमितं / ललाटे भर्तारं चरणकमले ताडयति ते । / चिरादन्तःशल्यं दहनकृतमुन्मूलितवता / तुलाकोटिक्वाणैः किलिकिलितमीशानरिपुणा ॥86॥
iast: mṛṣā kṛtvā gotraskhalanamatha vailakṣyanamitaṃ / lalāṭe bhartāraṃ caraṇakamale tāḍayati te । / cirādantaḥśalyaṃ dahanakṛtamunmūlitavatā / tulākoṭikvāṇaiḥ kilikilitamīśānaripuṇā ॥86॥
sayIt: mri-SHAA KRIT-vaa got-ra-SKHA-la-nam A-tha vai-LUK-shya-na-mi-tum / la-LAA-tay bhar-TAA-rum cha-ra-na-ka-ma-LAY TAA-da-ya-ti tay / chi-RAA-dan-tah-SHUL-yum da-ha-na-kri-tam oon-MOO-li-ta-va-taa / too-laa-KO-ti-kvaa-naih ki-li-ki-li-tam ee-SHAA-na-ri-poo-naa
translation: Your husband slips on your name in error, then bows low in embarrassment — and your lotus foot strikes him on the forehead; at that instant Ishana's old enemy, who has at last pulled out the barb of the burning lodged so long within him, shrieks his glee through the jingling of your anklet-bells.
source: Soundarya Lahari 86 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Can you let the sacred come near enough to your ordinary life that even its quarrels end in music?

translations.hi: तुम्हारे पति नाम की चूक कर बैठते हैं और झेंप से झुक जाते हैं — तभी तुम्हारा चरण-कमल उनके माथे पर आघात करता है; और उसी क्षण ईशान का पुराना वैरी — कामदेव — जो जलाए जाने का युगों से भीतर गड़ा काँटा आख़िर उखाड़ चुका है, तुम्हारे नूपुरों की झनकार में किलकारी मार उठता है।

devanagari: हिमानीहन्तव्यं हिमगिरिनिवासैकचतुरौ / निशायां निद्राणं निशि चरमभागे च विशदौ । / वरं लक्ष्मीपात्रं श्रियमतिसृजन्तौ समयिनां / सरोजं त्वत्पादौ जननि जयतश्चित्रमिह किम् ॥87॥
iast: himānīhantavyaṃ himagirinivāsaikacaturau / niśāyāṃ nidrāṇaṃ niśi caramabhāge ca viśadau । / varaṃ lakṣmīpātraṃ śriyamatisṛjantau samayināṃ / sarojaṃ tvatpādau janani jayataścitramiha kim ॥87॥
sayIt: hi-maa-nee-hun-TUV-yum hi-ma-gi-ri-ni-vaa-SAI-ka-cha-too-rau / ni-SHAA-yaam nid-RAA-num NI-shi cha-ra-ma-BHAA-gay cha vi-sha-dau / VA-rum luk-shmee-PAAT-rum shri-ya-ma-ti-sri-JUN-tau sa-ma-yi-NAAM / sa-RO-jum tvat-PAA-dau JA-na-ni JA-ya-tash CHIT-ram i-ha kim
translation: Frost kills the lotus; your feet alone are perfectly at home on the snow mountain. The lotus sleeps the night through; your feet stay bright and awake even in the night's last watch. The lotus at best is Lakshmi's seat; your feet pour out fortune upon your votaries. So, Mother, your feet defeat the lotus — what wonder is there in that?
source: Soundarya Lahari 87 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: Where in your life do you need a kindness that stays awake through the last watch of the night?

translations.hi: पाला कमल को मार डालता है; तुम्हारे चरण अकेले हिम-पर्वत पर बसने में निपुण हैं। कमल रात भर सोता है; तुम्हारे चरण रात में — रात के अन्तिम पहर में भी — उजले जागते रहते हैं। कमल अधिक-से-अधिक लक्ष्मी का आसन है; तुम्हारे चरण अपने व्रतियों पर लक्ष्मी लुटा देते हैं। तो हे जननी, तुम्हारे चरण कमल को जीत लेते हैं — इसमें अचरज ही क्या?

devanagari: पदं ते कीर्तीनां प्रपदमपदं देवि विपदां / कथं नीतं सद्भिः कठिनकमठीकर्परतुलाम् । / कथं वा बाहुभ्यामुपयमनकाले पुरभिदा / यदादाय न्यस्तं दृषदि दयमानेन मनसा ॥88॥
iast: padaṃ te kīrtīnāṃ prapadamapadaṃ devi vipadāṃ / kathaṃ nītaṃ sadbhiḥ kaṭhinakamaṭhīkarparatulām । / kathaṃ vā bāhubhyāmupayamanakāle purabhidā / yadādāya nyastaṃ dṛṣadi dayamānena manasā ॥88॥
sayIt: PA-dum tay keer-tee-NAAM pra-pa-da-ma-pa-DUM DAY-vi vi-pa-DAAM / ka-THUM NEE-tum sud-BHIH ka-thi-na-ka-ma-thee-KAR-pa-ra-too-LAAM / ka-THUM vaa baa-hoob-HYAAM oo-pa-ya-ma-na-KAA-lay poo-ra-bhi-DAA / ya-DAA-daa-ya NYAS-tum dri-sha-di da-ya-MAA-nay-na MA-na-saa
translation: Your forefoot, Devi, is the abode of glories and no abode at all for misfortunes. How, then, could the wise ever liken it to the hard shell of a she-tortoise? And how did the Breaker of the Cities, at the hour of your wedding, take it in his hands and set it down upon the stone — his heart wincing with tenderness?
source: Soundarya Lahari 88 (traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya), sanskritdocuments.org ITRANS file, personal-study terms, https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/soundaryalahari.itx
reflection: When duty asks you to set something tender down on hard stone, can you do it the way this verse imagines — with a heart that refuses to go hard along with the task?

translations.hi: हे देवी, तुम्हारा अगला चरण कीर्तियों का घर है और विपत्तियों के लिए वहाँ कोई ठौर नहीं। फिर सज्जनों (कवियों) ने उसे कठोर कछुई की पीठ की उपमा कैसे दे दी? और त्रिपुर के विजेता शिव ने विवाह की बेला में उसे अपने हाथों में लेकर सिल (पत्थर) पर कैसे रखा होगा — जबकि उनका मन करुणा से पिघला जा रहा था?

devanagari: नखैर्नाकस्त्रीणां करकमलसंकोचशशिभि / स्तरूणां दिव्यानां हसत इव ते चण्डि चरणौ । / फलानि स्वःस्थेभ्यः किसलयकराग्रेण ददतां / दरिद्रेभ्यो भद्रां श्रियमनिशमह्नाय ददतौ ॥89॥
